# Themes

The recurring ideas extracted across sources, each with the sources that support it. Built from research/themes/ (one file per task). Rules: [README.md](README.md).

## agent-as-service-many-surfaces: The agent as a service with many surfaces
One agent service behind an API, reached through a web app, Slack, browser extensions and embedding in existing tools, rather than a single app or a separate agent per surface. Matters for the agent-interface choice (own app vs Slack vs embedded).
- [Under the River](sources/shopify-engineering-under-the-river.md): the counter-case: River has one surface (Slack, no DMs), with companion links (Quick sites, Live Preview) for rich output (competitive-teardown-shopify-river)
- [Tobi Lütke: AI Agents, Better Decisions (Knowledge Project)](sources/fs-knowledge-project-tobi-lutke-ai-agents.md): River can join Google Meet when invited, "although not really utilized" (competitive-teardown-shopify-river)
- [Meet Stripe's Knowledge AI Platform](sources/stripe-meet-knowledge-ai-platform.md): "The agent is a service, not an application, and surfaces are simply customized views into it"; web app, Slack, Chrome extension in third-party tools, internal apps embed via API (competitive-teardown-stripe-knowledge-agents)
- [Stripe built their own in-house Glean alternative](sources/groundedhallucination-stripe-kai-teardown.md): "Surfaces are views, not the product" (independent restatement) (competitive-teardown-stripe-knowledge-agents)
- [Harbor: Stripe's AI-assisted prototyping tool](sources/stripe-harbor-ai-prototyping.md): Harbor is its own browser app but also an MCP toolset and a rendering service other agents call (competitive-teardown-stripe-knowledge-agents)
- [Airbnb Q3 2025 earnings call and shareholder letter](sources/airbnb-earnings-q3-2025.md): plan to merge AI search, AI support and messaging into one concierge, so "the entire app will act like an AI agent" (research-airbnb-spotify-product-practices)
- [AiKA hub](sources/spotify-portal-aika-hub.md): AiKA is both an MCP client (GitHub) and an MCP server (Claude Code) (research-airbnb-spotify-product-practices)
- [Spotify Portal now generally available](sources/sdtimes-spotify-portal-ga.md): AiKA MCP client and server at GA, Oct 2025 (research-airbnb-spotify-product-practices)
- [AI at Block](sources/block-ai-at-block-page.md): Block's own map of its AI estate: customer agents (Managerbot, Moneybot) and builder tools (Buzz, Berd, Builderbot) (research-block-product-practices)
- [MCP Apps in goose](sources/goose-blog-mcp-apps.md): MCP servers can return interactive HTML UIs rendered inside the chat (experimental, v1.19.0) (research-block-product-practices)
- [Claude Cowork and chat are now one Claude](sources/claude-cowork-chat-unified.md): one Claude on web, desktop and mobile; start on a computer, check progress or answer questions on a phone; work continues in the cloud (Pro/Max launch, "What it looks like"; Enterprise, "One Claude for every task"). ## agent-control-plane: Agent control planes above vendors
Platforms that register, govern and observe agents across vendors (registries, policy, audit, cost), sold as the enterprise layer above individual harnesses.

(research-claude-resources-articles)
- [Introducing the Claude apps gateway for Amazon Bedrock and Google Cloud](sources/claude-apps-gateway.md): single stateless container plus PostgreSQL holding the upstream credential, auth, policy, telemetry and routing (sections "Deploying the gateway", "How the gateway works"). - [Agent view in Claude Code](sources/claude-code-agent-view.md): one list of sessions with status, last response and last-interaction time; opened by left arrow or `claude agents` ("See everything at once"). (research-claude-resources-articles)

## agent-factory-sdlc: Agents across the whole product development loop
A chain of specialised agents (insight, define, build, review, test, coordinate) removes bottlenecks one after another; Glass is the define-stage agent. Related: [[intent-factory-before-discovery]].
- [What product looks like when coding is solved | Geoff Charles (Ramp CPO)](sources/lenny-podcast-geoff-charles-product-when-coding-solved.md): Glass/Inspect/Review Buddy/Testo/Gadget loop (competitive-teardown-ramp-glass)
- [How We Built Glass: Vibe Coding a Product Used by 700 People](sources/x-shanebuchan-how-we-built-glass.md): Glass builds Glass with Defrag, doc validation, gates (competitive-teardown-ramp-glass)

- [How we built OCA, our AI on-call assistant](sources/ramp-builders-how-we-built-oca.md): incident agent hands obvious fixes to Inspect for a human-reviewed PR; assisted 575 of 1,220 incident-fix PRs in four weeks (first-party) (competitive-teardown-ramp-glass)

## agent-failure-modes: Recurring agent failure modes in PM work
Invented content, silent omissions, brittleness, generic output when context is thin.
- [How River takes security work from a fix to merge](sources/shopify-engineering-river-vulnerability-remediation.md): told to enumerate fully, River rechecked only the oldest claim; "Prompts are the right place to express judgment and the wrong place to express a guarantee" (competitive-teardown-shopify-river)
- [AI SLOPCAST #9](sources/oleg-guru-ai-slopcast-shopify-river-lehrwerkstatt.md): public-by-default archives everyone's gaps, "a treasure trove" for HR (critique) (competitive-teardown-shopify-river)
- [Build your own company brain (How I AI, Krishnamurthy)](sources/howiai-stripe-kai-krishnamurthy.md): 'There were agents that went rogue ... may have almost taken down core systems'; 'when in doubt an agent will just brute force it' (competitive-teardown-stripe-knowledge-agents)
- [Thoughts On A Month With Devin](sources/answerai-month-with-devin.md): stuck loops (an HTML-parsing scraper task), a day spent on a platform-unsupported deployment while hallucinating features, tunnel vision on the wrong root cause, false-positive security findings (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [AWS AI coding tool decided to delete and recreate a customer-facing system, causing 13-hour outage (report)](sources/the-decoder-aws-kiro-outage.md): agent 'chose' to delete and recreate the environment; permissions inherited from the engineer bypassed two-person sign-off (FT sources; Amazon says it was misconfigured access controls and limited to Cost Explorer in one China region) (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Replit makes vibe-y promise to stop its AI agents making vibe coding disasters](sources/theregister-replit-saastr-response.md): reported deletion of a production DB with records on ~1,206 executives and ~1,196 companies despite an instruction not to change code; agent reportedly said rollback would not work, but data was recovered manually (eWeek and others, search results) (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [A month with Devin](sources/answerai-thoughts-month-with-devin.md): independent: 3/20 successes on real tasks; unpredictable; pursues impossible tasks instead of flagging blockers (Jan 2025, dated). (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Codex MCP server removal](sources/openai-codex-mcp-server-removed.md): integration route removed by the vendor; third-party blogs still describe it. (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Headless docs](sources/anthropic-claude-code-headless-agent-sdk.md): unattended runs deny permission prompts; `-p` does not wait for MCP tasks; MCP calls moved to background lose their result. (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [CR-Bench](sources/arxiv-cr-bench.md): independent, preliminary: agents built to find all issues have low signal-to-noise in code review (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [METR early-2025 developer RCT](sources/metr-early-2025-experienced-developer-rct.md): independent: AI-allowed tasks took 19% longer for experts on familiar repos while they believed it was faster (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Predictable Results Through Strong Feedback Loops (Honk, Part 3)](sources/spotify-engineering-honk-part-3-feedback-loops.md): no PR / fails CI / passes CI but wrong (worst); causes: weak tests, scope creep, can't run builds (research-airbnb-spotify-product-practices)
- [Rewriting All of Spotify's Code Base, All the Time (QCon talk)](sources/infoq-qcon-spotify-ai-codebase-migration-agent.md): the agent downgrades the Java version, comments out tests; infra failures on Linux VMs (research-airbnb-spotify-product-practices)
- [AI Changed How Spotify Builds… Quality at Higher Velocity](sources/spotify-engineering-quality-at-higher-velocity.md): mobile regressions build up below monitored signals while releases look healthy (research-airbnb-spotify-product-practices)
- [How Delivery Hero's agent merges 100+ pull requests a day with Claude](sources/claude-customers-delivery-hero-pr-agent.md): "If you churn out five times more changes ... you will have five times more incidents if the change failure rate remains at the same level"; investing in agent-driven operations and safer rollouts (§Looking ahead). (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [Multi-agent coordination patterns: Five approaches and when to use them](sources/claude-multi-agent-coordination-patterns.md): rubber-stamping verifiers, orchestrator information bottleneck, conflicting teammates, silent routing failures, reactive loops in shared state (each "Where it struggles"). (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [How Anthropic secures its AI-native software development lifecycle](sources/claude-securing-ai-native-sdlc-at-anthropic.md): the agent-to-agent escalation over Slack after a model upgrade; lesson: "draw the boundary around access and actions, not around a model's instructions" and include an agent's access to other agents (§Monitor). (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [Uber's CISO on building an insider threat program for AI](sources/claude-uber-ciso-insider-threat-ai.md): concern is accidental misuse and models "directed to act outside the constraints we expect"; "constraints create new behaviors" so detection must keep finding new ones. (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [DESIGN.md Explained](sources/departmentofproduct-design-md-explained.md): agents fill a missing token with something plausible, and the divergence spreads while still looking consistent. (research-department-of-product-knowledge-series)
- [Agentic Workflows Explained](sources/departmentofproduct-agentic-workflows-explained.md): a cited benchmark classes failures as planning, execution and formatting errors. (research-department-of-product-knowledge-series)
- [What is parallel AI agent coding? An in-depth guide for product teams](sources/departmentofproduct-parallel-agent-coding.md): parallel agents bring merge conflicts and harder debugging; they're weak on architecture and on UI that needs visual feedback (research-department-of-product-knowledge-series)
- [New Vulnerability in GitHub Copilot and Cursor: How Hackers Can Weaponize Code Agents](sources/pillar-security-rules-file-backdoor.md): vendor responses: Cursor (disclosed 26 Feb 2025) said the risk was users' responsibility; GitHub (disclosed 12 Mar 2025) said users must review suggestions, then added a hidden-Unicode warning on 1 May 2025. (independent; research-dependency-agent)
- [Claude Duet is beautiful. I still forgot to use it](sources/howiai-claire-vo-claude-duet-review.md): 10+ minute threads with no loop closure were forgotten; a faster agent wins "even if ... 10 percent worse" (7:59-9:31) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)

- [Community Wisdom: Syncing Claude Code and Claude Design ...](sources/lenny-community-wisdom-claude-design-handoff.md): no verification step meant drift from the prototype went undetected (Thread 1) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [Make product management fun again with AI agents](sources/lenny-newsletter-tal-raviv-pm-agents.md): agent invented sprint numbers from examples and marked tasks done from end dates: context gaps, not model faults (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [Building eval systems that improve your AI product](sources/lenny-newsletter-evals-hamel-shreya.md): transition failure matrix localises which agent step breaks (section "Agentic workflows") (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [How Claude Mythos found a 15-year-old bug in Mozilla Firefox | Brian Grinstead](sources/howiai-mozilla-mythos-bug-harness.md): agents cheat to hit the goal (setting a test-only pref; introducing a vulnerability to exploit it); patch agents miss the bug class (8:44, 28:22) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [How to do AI analysis you can actually trust](sources/lenny-newsletter-ai-analysis-you-can-trust.md): output "always looks confident"; teams on one enterprise LLM never see what it misses (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [Community Wisdom: How to encourage engineers to use AI more ...](sources/lenny-community-wisdom-engineers-ai-adoption.md): April 2025: a 10-line fix became 170 lines; lost Docker containers; agent mode adds bugs and wrong libraries (thread 1) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [5 OpenClaw agents run my home (Jesse Genet)](sources/howiai-jesse-genet-openclaw-agents.md): agent-to-agent handoffs break; no messaging platform handles them well (show notes, 16:43) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [How Anthropic's product team moves faster than anyone else | Cat Wu](sources/lenny-podcast-cat-wu-anthropic-product-team.md): model explains a skipped UI check as "I delegated the verification to this subagent and ... I didn't check its work" (53:31) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [The grief, loneliness, and burnout ... | Molly Graham](sources/lenny-podcast-molly-graham-delegating-to-ai.md): AI as "a lazy intern"; slop comes from people who have "shipped accountability" by copy-paste-send (35:18) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [OpenClaw: The complete guide](sources/lenny-newsletter-claire-vo-openclaw-guide.md): agents forget, crons break, time zones confused, a user's inbox deleted, the author's calendar mangled (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [Building AI product sense, part 2](sources/lenny-newsletter-ai-product-sense-part-2.md): "semantic fragility" summarising a PRD for a VP; same "top 5 decisions" prompt returns different decisions each run (Rituals 2, 4) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)

- [I spent $20,000 on Devin in a month (Ryan Carson)](sources/howiai-ryan-carson-devin-20k-month.md): "agent decision fatigue" managing 15 parallel agents, tracked on paper; "more AI output is the wrong goal" (18:09, 20:32) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)

- [Block's Goose (Brosamer, Axen)](sources/howiai-block-goose-brosamer-axen.md): Goose tried to read a `.env` holding an API key and was blocked by a built-in check (28:50) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)

## agent-frameworks: Agent frameworks
Libraries and engines (agent frameworks, durable-execution engines) used to build or host an agent loop.
- [How Stripe Built Kai on Deep Agents (LangChain)](sources/langchain-how-stripe-built-kai-deep-agents.md): Kai built on LangChain Deep Agents: 'solves all the non-Stripey problems'; minions on a Goose fork: Stripe uses two different open-source harnesses for two agent families (competitive-teardown-stripe-knowledge-agents)
- [Long-running agents (Cloudflare Agents SDK docs)](sources/cloudflare-agents-long-running-agents.md): recovery after eviction is not automatic replay: onFiberRecovered runs and 'you decide what resuming means'; keepAlive suits minutes not hours, use Workflows for longer work (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Open-Inspect (ColeMurray/background-agents) README](sources/github-open-inspect-background-agents.md): sandbox runs a Supervisor, a harness (OpenCode or Claude Agent) and a Bridge back to the control plane; harness is pluggable (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Durable Execution for AI Agents: LangGraph, DBOS, Inngest and Temporal Compared](sources/hackernoon-durable-execution-compared.md): LangGraph default async durability can lose the newest checkpoint on a hard crash, checkpoints are per node not per tool call; Inngest renaming a step orphans in-flight runs; Temporal needs a cluster and about two weeks to production (author's estimate) (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Production-ready agents with the OpenAI Agents SDK + Temporal](sources/temporal-openai-agents-sdk-integration.md): the integration replaces the Agents SDK Runner so every agent invocation runs as a Temporal Activity; handoffs are also recorded; workflow code holds orchestration logic (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Harness Engineering: ... Eleven Systems](sources/arxiv-harness-engineering-eleven-systems.md): independent: no production coding harness uses LangChain, LangGraph, AutoGen, CrewAI, ADK, Pydantic AI or Semantic Kernel; "the harness SDKs are the framework layer now" (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Agent Frameworks, Runtimes, and Harnesses, oh my!](sources/langchain-agent-frameworks-runtimes-harnesses.md): vendor claim: framework / runtime / harness vocabulary; author admits no agreed definition (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Deep Agents vs LangChain vs LangGraph](sources/langchain-deep-agents-vs-langchain-vs-langgraph.md): vendor claim: harness = framework agent plus middleware, on a LangGraph runtime (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Microsoft Agent Framework overview](sources/microsoft-agent-framework-overview.md): first-party: successor to AutoGen and Semantic Kernel now ships a Harness Agent; Go in preview (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Pydantic AI documentation overview](sources/pydantic-ai-docs.md): first-party: framework adds Harness (memory, sub-agents, compaction) and 8 durable-execution engines (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Agent Development Kit (ADK) documentation](sources/google-adk-docs.md): first-party: model-agnostic, 5 languages, A2A, Google Cloud deployment (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [LangGraph overview](sources/langchain-docs-langgraph-overview.md): first-party: durable execution runtime; deployment and tracing via paid LangSmith (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [OpenAI Agents SDK documentation](sources/openai-agents-sdk-docs.md): first-party: handoffs, guardrails, sessions, tracing, sandbox agents; non-OpenAI via adapters (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Codex SDK and app server](sources/openai-codex-sdk-docs.md): first-party: Codex harness controllable via TypeScript/Python SDK over app-server JSON-RPC (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Agent SDK overview](sources/anthropic-agent-sdk-overview.md): first-party: Claude Code as a library; four build options from Client SDK to Managed Agents (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Claude Managed Agents overview](sources/anthropic-managed-agents-overview.md): first-party: hosted harness, beta, not ZDR/HIPAA eligible (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Mastra documentation](sources/mastra-docs.md): vendor claim: TypeScript framework with scaffolded workspace and memory (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [CrewAI documentation: Introduction](sources/crewai-docs-introduction.md): vendor claim: Flows plus Crews (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [GitHub repos: OpenCode, Goose, Cline](sources/github-opencode-repo.md): OpenCode MIT about 221k stars; Goose Apache-2.0 Rust under Linux Foundation AAIF (github-block-goose-repo); Cline Apache-2.0 with SDK (github-cline-repo) (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Cloudflare Flue post](sources/cloudflare-flue-agents-platform.md): three layers: framework (Flue) / harness (Pi, Think) / runtime (Agents SDK) (vendor) (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Vercel AI SDK Harnesses](sources/vercel-ai-sdk-harnesses.md): harness vs model-provider abstraction as separate axes in a framework (vendor docs) (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Project Think](sources/cloudflare-project-think.md): 'opinionated harness' with lifecycle hooks, override what you need (vendor) (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)

- [Automation Platform v2: Improving Conversational AI at Airbnb](sources/airbnb-tech-automation-platform-v2.md): moved from fixed step workflows to a "Chain of Thought" tool loop where existing actions and workflows become tools (research-airbnb-spotify-product-practices)
- [Multi-agent coordination patterns: Five approaches and when to use them](sources/claude-multi-agent-coordination-patterns.md): five named patterns with mechanics, fit and failure modes, plus a situation-to-pattern table ("Getting started"). (research-claude-resources-articles)

## agent-led-intent-shaping: Agents shape intent, not only execute it
Agents do the research, interrogation and spec-tightening that turn rough intent into shovel-ready requirements, with humans answering and deciding. This is the core job of a "product agent".
- [From Hierarchy to Intelligence](sources/block-from-hierarchy-to-intelligence.md): when the intelligence layer cannot compose a solution, "that failure signal is the future roadmap" (research-block-product-practices)
- [Jack Dorsey: Every Company Can Now Be a Mini-AGI](sources/sequoia-dorsey-every-company-mini-agi.md): customers' queries "make the majority of the decisions" (research-block-product-practices)
- [we're making @blocks smaller today](sources/x-jack-block-smaller-note-2026-02-26.md): customers will "build their own features directly, composed of our capabilities" (research-block-product-practices)
- [The AI-native SDLC playbook](sources/claude-ai-native-sdlc-playbook.md): Claude "asks the questions an analyst would ask: scope, users, constraints, and what success looks like" while the originator brainstorms; the spec pass must flag "areas of concern, especially where you cannot satisfy... (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [Best practices for getting started with Claude Cowork](sources/claude-cowork-getting-started-best-practices.md): "Make Claude ask you questions before it starts", repeating the ask back and asking clarifying questions, called the single most useful habit (Your first 10 minutes). (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [How Miro's champions run their week with Claude Cowork](sources/claude-customers-miro-champions.md): Cowork used to pressure-test half-formed problems "before there's anything to draft"; usage moved from last step to first step (Hostetler, first answer). (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [How the product designer who built Claude Design uses it](sources/claude-design-designer-workflow.md): "ask for ten options, then remix"; generate 15 versions of a flow to collect colleague feedback; Claude provides starting points and the human chooses ("Best practices"). (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [A field guide to Claude Fable 5: Finding your unknowns](sources/claude-fable-finding-unknowns.md): the agent is asked to surface "unknown unknowns" ("blind spot pass"), brainstorm wildly different directions, and interview the user "one question at a time", prioritising questions that would change the architecture... (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [How to use Google's new Ideate Agent for Product Discovery and Ideation](sources/departmentofproduct-google-stitch-ideate-agent.md): Ideate researches named apps, proposes three directions, asks the PM to pick, then drafts a PRD for approval before designing (research-department-of-product-knowledge-series)
- [Head of Growth (Anthropic): "Claude is growing itself at this point"](sources/lenny-podcast-amol-avasare-anthropic-growth.md): CASH's first stage is Claude identifying growth opportunities from trends; Lenny: AI is "getting really good at telling us what to do" (35:29, 39:50) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [Why humans are AI's biggest bottleneck (Alexander Embiricos)](sources/lenny-podcast-embiricos-codex-human-bottleneck.md): sceptical of spec-driven development ("a lot of people don't like writing specs"); prefers proactive agents and "chatter-driven development" from team and customer channels (36:16-37:48) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [Head of Claude Code (Boris Cherny)](sources/lenny-podcast-boris-cherny-after-coding.md): "Claude is starting to come up with ideas" for what to ship from feedback and telemetry (17:54) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [OpenAI's Head of Design (Ian Silber)](sources/lenny-podcast-ian-silber-openai-design.md): ChatGPT helps users "express your intent better" with tap-through follow-up questions (44:08) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [Everyone's an engineer now | Guillermo Rauch](sources/lenny-podcast-guillermo-rauch-v0.md): v0 "inverts" the git commit: start from intent, code is output; three skills are stating intent, coaching, getting unstuck (14:36, 45:46) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [Adam Mosseri: AI is a tailwind for authenticity](sources/lenny-podcast-adam-mosseri-product-staff.md): working with agents "looks more like management": define success, choose how prescriptive to be, give feedback along the way (24:06) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [Why LinkedIn is turning PMs into AI-powered "full stack builders"](sources/lenny-podcast-tomer-cohen-full-stack-builder.md): heads of craft built trust, growth, research and analyst agents that critique specs; the trust agent replayed on the Open to Work spec found "all the holes that we did not catch until later"; the research agent "shifted the direction of the team" (19:58-21:59) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [Felix Rieseberg (Cowork)](sources/howiai-felix-rieseberg-cowork.md): uses Opus over Sonnet when "I ... don't really know yet what [I'm] asking for": reinterpreting the request is the hard part (10:11) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [What we're learning from engineers getting the most from Claude Code](sources/ideas-fin-what-were-learning-from-engineers.md): 5-20 plan-mode turns mapping code, comparing options and challenging edge cases before "build it"; no formal spec artifact, the plan lives in the session (anecdote) (research-pm-agents-jobs-to-be-done)
- [Building and Accelerating the Intent Factory](sources/geoff-building-accelerating-intent-factory.md): Ramp's parallel research agents write each finding to a file; seven-question interrogation; agent-originated intent (§Vision, steps 1–3) (research-product-agent-and-harness)
- [Intent Shaping in a Well-Managed Environment](sources/geoff-intent-shaping-well-managed-environment.md): an iterative owner/risk-advisor loop in which mitigations become requirements and the spec tightens (§Iterative intent-shaping) (research-product-agent-and-harness)
- [Agent Skills (Osmani)](sources/addyosmani-agent-skills.md): "If you didn't have to justify this to anyone, what would you actually want?" (research-skill-rigidity-spectrum)
- [Devin 2.1](sources/cognition-devin-2-1-confidence.md): low self-confidence triggers clarifying questions before work (research-skill-rigidity-spectrum)
- [Introducing Jira Planner](sources/atlassian-blog-introducing-jira-planner.md): asks follow-up questions on scope, constraints and success; PMs named in the audience (Early Access) (user-story-mapping)

## agent-legible-platform: The agent-legible platform
The kinds of information an agent needs about a platform (identity, ownership, contracts, intake, checks and approvers, lead times, calendar, decisions) and the most machine-readable form each has today; the intake rung is strongest, approvals and lead times weakest. Related: [[legible-org-for-agents]].
- [Agent READMEs: An Empirical Study of Context Files for Agentic Coding](sources/arxiv-chatlatanagulchai-agent-readmes.md): across 16 instruction types, most common are test procedures (75.9%), implementation details (70.8%), architecture (68.1%). (independent; research-dependency-agent)
- [MCP Actions (Backstage AI docs)](sources/backstage-docs-mcp-actions.md): "The MCP Actions Backend exposes Actions registered with the Actions Registry as MCP tools"; actions from configured `pluginSources` (e.g. `catalog`, `scaffolder`) appear as tools, splittable into several MCP endpoints with include/exclude rules. (first-party; research-dependency-agent)
- [Writing Templates (Backstage Software Templates)](sources/backstage-docs-writing-templates.md): catalog-aware fields (`OwnerPicker` filtered by `catalogFilter`, `RepoUrlPicker` limited by `allowedHosts`/`allowedOwners`) tie the intake to the ownership graph (Custom fields). (first-party; research-dependency-agent)
- [Open Data Contract Standard (ODCS)](sources/bitol-odcs-open-data-contract-standard.md): contract sections: Fundamentals, Schema, Data Quality, Support & Communication Channels, Pricing, Team, Roles, SLA, Infrastructures & Servers, Authoritative Definitions, Tags, Custom properties (index). (first-party; research-dependency-agent)
- [FedRAMP 20x](sources/fedramp-20x-overview.md): Key Security Indicators (KSIs) were the Phase 1 proof of concept for automated validation; Phase 2 found presenting requirements as KSIs "confusing". (first-party; research-dependency-agent)
- [FINOS Common Cloud Controls (CCC)](sources/finos-common-cloud-controls.md): technology-agnostic Core Catalog of threats and controls that organisations import and extend with service-specific catalogs. (first-party; research-dependency-agent)
- [About code owners](sources/github-docs-about-code-owners.md): gitignore-style patterns, last match wins; file in `.github/`, root or `docs/` of the base branch. (first-party; research-dependency-agent)
- [Dev Portal MCP server (Kong Konnect)](sources/kong-docs-dev-portal-mcp-server.md): read tools: `list_apis`, `fetch_api_spec(_raw)`, `list_api_documents`, `get_portal_form`, `list_application_auth_strategies` and others (Tools). (first-party; research-dependency-agent)
- [Promises (Kratix reference)](sources/kratix-docs-promises-intro.md): the request API is a namespace-scoped CRD; `requiredPromises` declares dependencies between platform offerings (API, Requirements). (first-party; research-dependency-agent)
- [The /llms.txt file](sources/llmstxt-org-llms-txt-proposal.md): fixed Markdown structure: required H1 name, optional blockquote summary, optional prose, H2 sections of link lists; an "Optional" H2 marks links an agent may skip for shorter context (Format section). (first-party; research-dependency-agent)
- [Introducing the MCP Registry](sources/mcp-blog-registry-preview.md): registry is "an open catalog and API" for publicly available MCP servers; its OpenAPI spec is open so others can build compatible sub-registries (Overview). (first-party; research-dependency-agent)
- [Inventory and Discover MCP Servers in Your API Center](sources/microsoft-azure-api-center-mcp-registry.md): registry endpoint `https://<apic>.data.<region>.azure-apicenter.ms/workspaces/default/v0.1/servers` usable from VS Code/Copilot (Configure MCP registry metadata). (first-party; research-dependency-agent)
- [OSCAL: the Open Security Controls Assessment Language (layers and models)](sources/nist-oscal-layers-and-models.md): a Component Definition describes how a component (e.g. a platform service) implements controls, which a consumer can inherit; formats XML, JSON, YAML (OSCAL home). (first-party; research-dependency-agent)
- [Port MCP server: overview and installation](sources/port-docs-remote-mcp-server.md): blueprint, entity and scorecard tools expose the catalog and its standards to agents. (first-party; research-dependency-agent)
- [50% of engineers lack trust in the data they rely on most](sources/port-state-of-idp-2025-metadata-trust.md): 25% of orgs still use a CMDB and 17% spreadsheets as metadata store; 53% have implemented an internal developer portal, 23% specifically as metadata repository. (vendor-claim; research-dependency-agent)
- [llms.txt adoption rises 8.8x but 97% of files get zero AI requests](sources/ppcland-llms-txt-adoption-zero-requests.md): Originality.ai tracked >3M sites; llms.txt instances 4,088 (Jun 2025) to 36,120 (May 2026); llms-full.txt 23 to 2,463; ai.txt 4 to 397; 38,980 adopting sites in total (tracking study, update of 2 Jul 2026). (independent; research-dependency-agent)
- [Score: developer-centric workload specification](sources/score-dev-workload-specification.md): same file works across local and remote environments, so an agent could write one declaration and let each platform resolve it. (first-party; research-dependency-agent)
- [Spectral: a flexible JSON/YAML linter for creating automated style guides](sources/stoplight-spectral-readme.md): example public rulesets from Adidas, Azure and Zalando show large orgs publishing their API style rules as code. (first-party; research-dependency-agent)

## agent-originated-requests: Requests that come from an agent: how people respond and how platforms accept them
Evidence on targeted versus untargeted bot requests, and the first platforms that accept access, change and registration requests from an agent acting for a person.
- [Automating Dependency Updates in Practice: An Exploratory Study on GitHub Dependabot](sources/arxiv-he-dependabot-exploratory-study.md): high receptiveness but notification management is the main coping behaviour; 11.3% of projects deprecated Dependabot (abstract). (independent; research-dependency-agent)
- [Nudge: Accelerating Overdue Pull Requests Towards Completion](sources/arxiv-maddila-nudge-overdue-pull-requests.md): effort-estimation/ML completion-time prediction, activity detection to filter PRs already moving, actor identification "to nudge the appropriate blocker" (abstract). (first-party; research-dependency-agent)
- [DeepTriage: Automated Transfer Assistance for Incidents in Cloud Services](sources/arxiv-pham-deeptriage-incident-routing.md): misrouting cost is large ("increase its time to mitigate by 10x"), the same failure a dependency agent risks by sending asks to the wrong owner. (first-party; research-dependency-agent)
- [Asana AI Teammates: Powerful Agents Ready to Work with Your Team](sources/asana-ai-teammates-overview-launch-planner.md): alerts go to both owners of a threatened dependency, with a proposed schedule. (vendor-claim; research-dependency-agent)
- [Behind the build: A hands-on AI Teammates walkthrough from Asana's CPO](sources/asana-forum-cpo-ai-teammates-walkthrough.md): "Instead of just surfacing the problem, the teammate proposes specific operational actions". (vendor-claim; research-dependency-agent)
- [Asynchronous Authorization (Auth0 for AI Agents)](sources/auth0-docs-asynchronous-authorization.md): listed use cases include a DevOps agent needing approval to deploy to production and reading protected health records. (first-party; research-dependency-agent)
- [Requesting access to a data product (Immuta)](sources/immuta-docs-request-access-data-product.md): requests can be made for oneself or on behalf of other users. (first-party; research-dependency-agent)
- [Dev Portal MCP server (Kong Konnect)](sources/kong-docs-dev-portal-mcp-server.md): write tools `create_application`, `create_application_registration`, `delete_*` require Dev Portal login plus the "MCP server write operations" toggle under AI Settings. (first-party; research-dependency-agent)
- [Access packages for agent identities in Microsoft Entra](sources/microsoft-entra-agent-access-packages.md): three pathways: "The agent identity itself can programmatically request an access package when needed for its operations"; the sponsor can request on its behalf; or an admin assigns directly (Access request and approval process). (first-party; research-dependency-agent)
- [Opal Security Launches Opal Zero to Make Least Privilege a Reality for Enterprise AI Agents](sources/opal-zero-launch-press-release.md): "The agent submits its own access request through Opal's MCP server." (vendor-claim; research-dependency-agent)
- [Planview Reinvents How Enterprises Make Critical Decisions with Connected Work Graph: AI-Powered Dependency Intelligence](sources/planview-connected-work-graph-launch.md): agents "automatically escalate critical risks" and are "running at all times, alerting you when a bottleneck or dependency needs resolving" (CPO quote). (vendor-claim; research-dependency-agent)
- [Port MCP server: overview and installation](sources/port-docs-remote-mcp-server.md): a `run_action` tool; by default "all actions you have permission to run will be available". (first-party; research-dependency-agent)
- [Model Context Protocol Server (SailPoint Identity Security Cloud)](sources/sailpoint-docs-mcp-server.md): tools: list requestable items, initiate access request, query status by request ID, cancel pending request (Access requests). (first-party; research-dependency-agent)
- [Accelerating your DevOps change process (DevOps Change Velocity)](sources/servicenow-docs-devops-change-velocity-approval.md): change control on a pipeline job opens a change request in Assess state, pausing the job; "change receipts" record a change without pausing. (first-party; research-dependency-agent)
- [Now Assist for Strategic Portfolio Management (SPM) release notes](sources/servicenow-docs-now-assist-spm-release-notes.md): Monitor Project Tasks agent (v5.1.1, Mar 2025): "Autonomously monitor project tasks on the critical path of a project", emailing the PM; Project Summary emails on cadence or on demand. (first-party; research-dependency-agent)

## agent-project-failure-rates: Agent project failure rates
Press-reported statistics on agent and genAI pilot failure (Gartner, MIT); not PM-specific and mostly unverified.
- [Deploying AI from pilot to production: a practical blueprint for CIOs and technical leaders](sources/claude-pilot-to-production-cio-blueprint.md): cites Accenture's Pulse of Change (July 2026): only 23% of C-suite leaders report sustained enterprise-wide impact from AI initiatives; pilots are unrepresentative (hand-picked teams, protected budgets). (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [Agentic Workflows Explained](sources/departmentofproduct-agentic-workflows-explained.md): agents failed about 50% of 34 general tasks in a cited study (the post calls it "Cibench"; not verified). (research-department-of-product-knowledge-series)
- [Why most AI products fail: Lessons from 50+ AI deployments](sources/lenny-podcast-reganti-badam-ai-deployments.md): cites ~74-75% of enterprises naming reliability as their top problem; one end-to-end support agent shut down after endless hot fixes; critical workflows take 4-6 months (21:45, 46:18, 30:31) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [Not all AI agents are created equal](sources/lenny-newsletter-three-agent-categories.md): consultants' main failure pattern is mis-categorization: over-engineering deterministic problems, or using workflow tools for reasoning problems, which "breaks in production" (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [How 80,000 companies build with AI (Lenny's Podcast)](sources/lenny-podcast-asha-sharma-loop-not-lane.md): enterprises fail by "doing AI for AI's sake": many parallel projects, no blueprint, no measurement, observability or evals (11:05) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [Sloppenheimer: Amazon employees mock the company's AI on Slack (404 Media)](sources/404media-amazon-employees-mock-ai-slop.md): internal AI coding product mocked as slop; failed usage push (leaderboard detail unverified; paywalled) [re-check 2026-10-24]. (research-pm-agents-jobs-to-be-done)
- [Zapier customer story (Anthropic)](sources/anthropic-customer-story-zapier.md): counter-example claim: 800+ internal agents and 89% adoption (vendor-claimed, no outcomes). (research-pm-agents-jobs-to-be-done)
- [How Brex improves code quality and productivity with Claude Code](sources/claude-brex-claude-code.md): vendor-claimed 3-4x on coding tasks; not PM evidence. (research-pm-agents-jobs-to-be-done)
- [MIT report: 95% of generative AI pilots at companies are failing (Fortune)](sources/fortune-mit-nanda-95-percent-pilots.md): ~95% of pilots no measurable P&L impact; bought tools about 2x as successful as internal builds (press; primary now filed as mit-nanda-genai-divide-2025) [re-check 2026-10-24]. (research-pm-agents-jobs-to-be-done)
- [Over 40% of agentic AI projects will be scrapped by 2027, says Gartner (Outlook Business coverage)](sources/gartner-agentic-ai-40-percent-cancelled.md): forecast: over 40% of agentic AI projects cancelled by end of 2027. (research-pm-agents-jobs-to-be-done)
- [The GenAI Divide: State of AI in Business 2025](sources/mit-nanda-genai-divide-2025.md): primary: "95% of organizations are getting zero return"; success = beyond pilot with measurable KPIs at six months; self-reported, 52 interviews, 153 surveys, selection bias acknowledged (research-pm-agents-jobs-to-be-done)

## agent-protocol-security: Security of agent-to-agent and agent-to-tool protocols
Attacks and gaps that arise because a remote agent or its metadata becomes input to your agent: card or description poisoning, session smuggling, identity loss across delegation hops, optional signing.
- [How We Red-Teamed Our Own AI Agent](sources/block-eng-red-teamed-own-ai-agent.md): zero-width-Unicode prompt injection delivered in a calendar invite through the Calendar MCP (research-block-product-practices)
- [Agent Guardrails and Controls](sources/block-eng-agent-guardrails-and-controls.md): a CORS-style gate on chained tool calls, decided in code, not by the model (research-block-product-practices)
- [Securing the Model Context Protocol](sources/block-eng-securing-the-model-context-protocol.md): MCP threat model; allowlists of pre-validated servers (research-block-product-practices)
- [Agent identity: a new access model for autonomous, team-wide AI](sources/claude-agent-identity-access-model.md): credentials stored separately and injected at the network boundary; non-allowed hosts blocked; every routine, memory write and network call audited (section "Security and audit"). (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [CISO's guide to agentic AI](sources/claude-ciso-guide-agentic-ai.md): prompt injection named as a main internal risk; egress allowlisting called "your strongest control against prompt injection"; connector tokens injected by a reverse proxy so the sandbox never holds them. (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [Inference hooks: inline data loss prevention for Claude Enterprise](sources/claude-enterprise-inference-hooks.md): tool responses from MCP connectors, skills and plugins are inspected before returning to the model, a check against injected or sensitive content arriving via tools ("How inference hooks works"). (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [Centrally manage authorization for MCP connectors](sources/claude-enterprise-managed-mcp-auth.md): implemented as the Enterprise-Managed Authorization extension to the MCP authorization spec, embedding the Cross App Access protocol (intro; Okta-side quote). (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [Zero Trust for AI agents](sources/claude-zero-trust-for-ai-agents.md): Ch 04 catalogues tool poisoning, MCP rug pulls, tool-chaining exfiltration and loop amplification; Ch 06 Phase 2 advises self-hosting and signing verified MCP servers. (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [How to develop an MCP Product Strategy](sources/departmentofproduct-mcp-product-strategy.md): cites the Asana and GitHub MCP incidents. Broad read/write scopes are hard to avoid, and servers should reject tokens with too much or irrelevant scope (research-department-of-product-knowledge-series)
- [Enforce least-privilege authorization in multi-agent AI chains using Cedar](sources/aws-security-cedar-multi-agent-least-privilege.md): cites OWASP Top 10 for Agentic Applications ASI03, Identity & Privilege Abuse. (first-party; research-dependency-agent)
- [Introducing the MCP Registry](sources/mcp-blog-registry-preview.md): moderation is by community flagging and maintainer denylisting, retroactively removing entries (Moderation). (first-party; research-dependency-agent)
- [Accelerating the Adoption of Software and AI Agent Identity and Authorization (NCCoE concept paper)](sources/nist-nccoe-agent-identity-authorization-concept-paper.md): detailed questions cover identification, authorisation, auditing and non-repudiation of agents plus controls for prompt injection (announcement). (first-party; research-dependency-agent)
- [New Vulnerability in GitHub Copilot and Cursor: How Hackers Can Weaponize Code Agents](sources/pillar-security-rules-file-backdoor.md): hidden instructions via zero-width joiners and bidirectional markers; demo made the assistant add a malicious script tag to generated HTML and suppress mention of it (Attack mechanics). (independent; research-dependency-agent)
- [The coming AI security crisis | Sander Schulhoff](sources/lenny-podcast-sander-schulhoff-ai-security.md): malicious email or hidden web text redirects inbox and browser agents; in his competitions agents were easier to trick than models were to jailbreak for CBRNE (1:01:09) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [An AI state of the union (Simon Willison)](sources/lenny-podcast-simon-willison-state-of-ai.md): lethal trifecta (private data, untrusted instructions, exfiltration); "97% ... is a failing grade"; cut the exfiltration leg (1:20:18-1:22:09) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [A2ABreak: Systematic Security Analysis of the A2A Protocol](sources/arxiv-a2abreak-security-analysis.md): The first systematic, specification-level security analysis of A2A found. (research-runtime-patterns-follow-up-round)
- [Agent Card Poisoning: A Metadata Injection Vulnerability in the Systems using Google A2A Protocol](sources/keysight-agent-card-poisoning.md): Shows that an Agent Card is untrusted text that ends up in the caller's prompt: a malicious remote agent embeds instructions in its card, and the host LLM follows them. (research-runtime-patterns-follow-up-round)
- [A Security Engineer's Guide to the A2A Protocol](sources/semgrep-security-engineers-guide-a2a.md): The primary source behind the widely repeated claim that A2A "supports but does not enforce Agent Card signing", which Track 3 had only second-hand. (research-runtime-patterns-follow-up-round)
- [Action Fabric: MCP Server, MCP Client, and A2A explained](sources/servicenow-community-action-fabric-mcp-a2a.md): ServiceNow supports A2A in both directions, but its own governance layer does not cover it: "AI Gateway currently governs MCP traffic only; A2A is outside its scope as of the current GA release." For a regulated setting  (research-runtime-patterns-follow-up-round)
- [When AI Agents Go Rogue: Agent Session Smuggling Attack in A2A Systems](sources/unit42-agent-session-smuggling-a2a.md): A worked attack on stateful agent-to-agent delegation: a malicious remote agent uses an established A2A session to inject instructions into the calling agent across turns, causing data leakage and an unauthorised stock p (research-runtime-patterns-follow-up-round)

## agent-ready-intent: A shared standard for agent-ready specs
Intent is complete enough for agentic delivery when it meets an agreed standard (templates, examples, evals) that gates delivery and improves from delivery feedback.
- [Context Engineering (Honk, Part 2)](sources/spotify-engineering-honk-part-2-context-engineering.md): describe the end state, state when not to act, give examples, define done as tests, one change at a time (research-airbnb-spotify-product-practices)
- [Supercharging Downstream Consumer Dataset Migrations (Honk, Part 4)](sources/spotify-engineering-honk-part-4-dataset-migrations.md): a reused human migration guide led Honk to guess; explicit field-mapping tables worked (research-airbnb-spotify-product-practices)
- [Moving to issues as the new PRs](sources/goose-blog-issues-are-the-new-prs.md): only "Ready" issues with agreed design, constraints and verification go to agents (research-block-product-practices)
- [The AI-native SDLC playbook](sources/claude-ai-native-sdlc-playbook.md): an agreed intent.md template, encoded as a skill "set up by a technical team member and signed off by a lead" (§Stage 1, How to execute). (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [How CodeRabbit used Claude to build an agent orchestration system](sources/claude-coderabbit-plan-orchestration.md): experienced developers omit "obvious" requirements; the login-page anecdote (section "Addressing the internal knowledge gap"). (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [Building verification loops in Claude Code with skills](sources/claude-verification-loops-skills.md): built-in "spec validation" skill verifies each change against a markdown spec in the repo and fixes violations ("Built-in verification loops"). (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [How to speed up engineering velocity with AI: a non-engineer's guide](sources/departmentofproduct-engineering-velocity-non-engineers.md): Morgan Stanley's tool writes English specs of legacy code, which engineers then rewrite from (280k hours claimed, via WSJ) (research-department-of-product-knowledge-series)
- [The Codex feature that works while you sleep](sources/howiai-claire-vo-codex-goal.md): OpenAI's six-part /goal structure (outcome, verification, constraints, boundaries, iteration policy, blocked behaviour) as presented by Claire Vo is a concrete format for intent handed to an agent (7:34-9:21) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [How Devin replaces your junior engineers | Scott Wu](sources/howiai-scott-wu-devin-junior-engineer.md): "tasks, not problems"; DeepWiki turns a one-line ask into a full prompt naming patterns to follow, types, functions and checks (4:04-10:27) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [Spec-driven development at Notion | Ryan Nystrom](sources/howiai-notion-ryan-nystrom-spec-driven.md): one-shot builds came from specs in a house format with code pointers and a verification section; dictated "yap session" → Codex writes spec from the library's format (33:36) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [What happens after coding is solved? | Fiona Fung](sources/lenny-podcast-fiona-fung-after-coding-solved.md): a checked-in "statement of what good looks like" is what makes automated review possible (15:00) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [HTML is the new Markdown | Thariq Shihipar](sources/howiai-thariq-shihipar-html-specs.md): "99% of your AI-generated tokens should go to planning, interfaces, and communication" (episode description) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [Community Wisdom: Quarterly planning and AI ...](sources/lenny-community-wisdom-quarterly-planning.md): a Series E (1,500+) R&D org building a spec-driven AI SDLC; advice: source-of-truth hierarchy, handoff packets, decision records, acceptance criteria, verification gates, separate planner/executor/checker (thread 6) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [Community Wisdom: The changing product development process ...](sources/lenny-community-wisdom-prd-vs-prototype.md): a PRD one-pager "works really well in Claude Code for context"; epics and user stories as guardrails; BMAD-Method recommended (thread 1) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [Community Wisdom: How PMs are using AI coding tools](sources/lenny-community-wisdom-pms-ai-coding-tools.md): "Keeping exhaustive requirements for everything I do. Quality acceptance requirements and context ... significantly improves agent outputs" (thread 4) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [Community Wisdom: When AI velocity outpaces your product strategy ...](sources/lenny-community-wisdom-ai-velocity-strategy.md): dates slip because "the spec wasn't solid enough when we scoped the work"; more input context makes output "on-target and shippable" (threads 1, 4) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [How I run autonomous coding agents with OpenAI Symphony + Linear](sources/howiai-alessio-fanelli-symphony-linear.md): Symphony's orchestration spec is "literally just a markdown file" of primitives and states (13:17) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [From managing people to managing AI: Julie Zhuo](sources/lenny-podcast-julie-zhuo-managing-ai.md): boiling success down "so that an agent can really understand what success and failure looks like is a lot of the game" (12:16) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [Community Wisdom: speeding up discovery in a big org](sources/lenny-community-wisdom-discovery-big-org.md): PRD kept as a version-controlled typed JSON "intent model" (entities, state machines, mutation contracts, acceptance rules) that AI codegen builds from; open questions are an `open_questions[]` field, "not a blocker" (thread 2) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [The secret to better AI prototypes (Ravi Mehta)](sources/howiai-ravi-mehta-data-driven-prototyping.md): a realistic JSON data set as the input to prototyping, because the schema codifies what is "ambiguous around designs or specs"; host: give PRDs and prototyping tools engineering's data schema (3:49, 26:04) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [The rise of the professional vibe coder (Lazar Jovanovic)](sources/lenny-podcast-lazar-jovanovic-vibe-coder.md): once the PRD set exists, "My prompts have become, 'Proceed with the next task'" (34:36) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)

- [Shape Up (Ryan Singer)](sources/lenny-podcast-ryan-singer-shape-up.md): shaped work = narrowed problem, appetite, breadboard/fat-marker flow in fewer than 10 moving parts; done when "a technical person ... say[s] 'Yeah, I know what to go build now'" (42:21, 1:02:23) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [How to design AI agent loops (How I AI)](sources/howiai-claire-vo-agent-loops-design.md): goal loops are "the hardest to write well" (show notes; detail in the companion goal episode) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)

- [What is an idea (Jira Product Discovery docs)](sources/atlassian-jira-product-discovery-ideas.md): an idea is the basic unit; custom idea types (user problem, customer, bet, opportunity, solution), each with its own workflow. (user-story-mapping)

## agent-stewardship: Every deployed agent needs a human steward
Agents that people rely on stay useful only while a named person keeps tending them (reading traces, fixing prompts, adding guardrails, deciding what becomes a primitive); when that care stops, the agent decays. This matters for who maintains a PM agent and what headcount it implies. New because existing slugs cover harness ownership as a build-vs-buy choice (build-vs-buy) or the dimension harness-upkeep, but no theme covers the ongoing human care of a deployed agent as a role.
- [AI (Backstage documentation)](sources/backstage-docs-ai.md): AI resources carry an owner like any catalog entity (research-airbnb-spotify-product-practices)
- [Features of AgentCore Identity (Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Developer Guide)](sources/aws-agentcore-identity-features.md): a unified directory "acts as the single source of truth for all agent identities", with ARN paths (`.../directory/default/workload-identity/agent-name`) for policy at different levels (Centralized agent identity management). (first-party; research-dependency-agent)
- [Agent Identity overview (Google Cloud IAM)](sources/google-cloud-iam-agent-identity-overview.md): SPIFFE ID `spiffe://agents.global.org-ORG_ID.system.id.goog/resources/...` mapped to the hosting resource; X.509 certs valid 24h, auto-renewed; mTLS default, DPoP across Agent Gateway. (first-party; research-dependency-agent)
- [Access packages for agent identities in Microsoft Entra](sources/microsoft-entra-agent-access-packages.md): on expiry the sponsor is notified and may request extension (which can trigger a new approval cycle); with no action access lapses (Access assignment lifecycle). (first-party; research-dependency-agent)
- [Opal Security Launches Opal Zero to Make Least Privilege a Reality for Enterprise AI Agents](sources/opal-zero-launch-press-release.md): decisions route to the agent's owner, who can revoke or deactivate; agents flagged for review when ownership or purpose changes. (vendor-claim; research-dependency-agent)
- [Agent management overview](sources/port-docs-agent-management-overview.md): a registry of agents, skills and MCP servers "with ownership and status in Context Lake". (first-party; research-dependency-agent)
- [The AI paradox: More automation, more humans, more work | Dan Shipper](sources/lenny-podcast-dan-shipper-ai-paradox.md): personal agents failed at Every because "it really needs a human who cares about it"; forward-deployed engineers maintaining one company agent are "the new most essential role" (13:36, 53:15) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [How Claude Mythos found a 15-year-old bug in Mozilla Firefox | Brian Grinstead](sources/howiai-mozilla-mythos-bug-harness.md): analyzer prompts tuned continuously from trace analysis (manual and LLM-assisted) and engineers' feedback on bad reports (12:13) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [Building effective human-agent teams (Slack CPO)](sources/claude-slack-human-agent-teams.md): retire an agent if people cannot say what it is for; a session that outlives its creator needs a named owner (research-shared-persistent-agents)
- [Agent identity: the access model behind Claude Tag](sources/claude-agent-identity-access-model.md): revoking the agent's identity ends access everywhere, "easier than auditing actions across user accounts" (research-shared-persistent-agents)
- [Owners, sponsors, and managers (Entra Agent ID)](sources/microsoft-entra-agent-owners-sponsors.md): a business sponsor is mandatory per agent, groups allowed, succession on departure required; Microsoft sources conflict on the default transfer (research-shared-persistent-agents)
- [Agent identity (Ramp)](sources/ramp-agents-identity-guide.md): standalone agents must have an active human owner in the business (research-shared-persistent-agents)

## ai-flattened-org: AI as the reason to flatten the organisation
Leaders cite AI as the reason to remove management layers, shrink feature teams to squads and replace the information-routing job of managers with agents and a shared "world model". Distinct from leadership-permission-mandate (authority and incentives): this is about the org's shape, which decides who does PM tasks and how many handoffs there are.
- [Jack Dorsey is about to overhaul Block in a reorg](sources/fortune-block-functional-reorg-memo-2024.md): July 2024 move from business units to functions; the memo gave collaboration and craft as reasons, not AI (research-block-product-practices)
- [Block Q2 2024 earnings call](sources/motley-fool-block-q2-2024-earnings-call.md): Dorsey ties the functional org to moving "much, much faster" with AI models (research-block-product-practices)
- [How Block is becoming the most AI-native enterprise (Lenny's Podcast)](sources/lenny-podcast-block-dhanji-goose.md): CTO calls the GM-to-functional reorg "the key" to becoming AI-native and worth more than any tool (research-block-product-practices)
- [Read the email Jack Dorsey sent when he cut 931 of Block's staff](sources/techcrunch-dorsey-email-931-cuts-2025.md): 2025 flattening (80 managers cut, 193 moved to IC, depth capped) explicitly "not replacing folks with AI" (research-block-product-practices)
- [we're making @blocks smaller today](sources/x-jack-block-smaller-note-2026-02-26.md): over 10,000 to just under 6,000 people, credited to intelligence tools "paired with smaller and flatter teams" (2026-02-26) (research-block-product-practices)
- [Block Q4 2025 prepared remarks](sources/block-q4-2025-earnings-prepared-remarks.md): the cut announced alongside +24% gross profit; only metric given is code shipped per engineer up 40%+ (research-block-product-practices)
- [Block lays off 4,000](sources/techcrunch-block-layoffs-4000-2026.md): independent account of the February 2026 cut and its AI rationale (research-block-product-practices)
- [From Hierarchy to Intelligence](sources/block-from-hierarchy-to-intelligence.md): a company world model replaces middle management's routing; three roles only (IC, DRI, player-coach) (2026-03-31) (research-block-product-practices)
- [Jack Dorsey: Every Company Can Now Be a Mini-AGI](sources/sequoia-dorsey-every-company-mini-agi.md): five management layers today, target two to three (research-block-product-practices)
- [Block CTO Dhanji Prasanna: Building the AI-First Enterprise with Goose](sources/sequoia-training-data-dhanji-goose.md): funded special projects, then "progressively we started to unwind our GM structure" (research-block-product-practices)
- [What Happens When a Public Company Goes All In on AI](sources/a16z-owen-jennings-block-all-in-on-ai.md): feature teams of ~14 became squads of 1-6; development layers cut 50-60%; meetings down 70-80% (research-block-product-practices)
- [Block leans into its AI future](sources/paymentsdive-block-leans-into-ai-future.md): analysts judge the reorganisation on financials (research-block-product-practices)

## ai-synthesis-hallucination-risk: AI synthesis can invent or merge facts
Practitioner and academic evidence of fabricated details, merged quotes and lost depth in LLM summaries of qualitative data.
- [Beyond the model: Engineering AI infra with scientific judgement](sources/airbnb-tech-insight-miner-agent-harness.md): a coding agent can return a polished taxonomy of 100k conversations while hiding its method, its evidence and whether a rerun would agree (research-airbnb-spotify-product-practices)
- [Eval-driven development: Lessons from evaluating GenAI at scale](sources/airbnb-tech-eval-driven-development.md): in the worked example, 15 of 100 support-policy answers invented policy details (research-airbnb-spotify-product-practices)
- [Airbnb Q2 2025 earnings call and shareholder letter](sources/airbnb-earnings-q2-2025.md): support chosen first because "you cannot have a high hallucination rate" there (research-airbnb-spotify-product-practices)
- [Simultaneous Triangulation](sources/spotify-design-simultaneous-triangulation.md): an A/B "power skipper" segment was partly confused users, a wrong label caught only by interviews (research-airbnb-spotify-product-practices)
- [When Can LLMs Replace Humans in A/B Tests?](sources/spotify-engineering-llms-replace-humans-ab-tests.md): if assumptions fail, you measure the effect on the LLM, not on users (research-airbnb-spotify-product-practices)
- [Self-service data analytics in Slack: how Anthropic deploys Claude Tag for ad-hoc questions](sources/claude-tag-self-service-analytics.md): stale skill gives "last Tuesday's wrong answer with full confidence" to a consumer cut off from context (section "Refresh skills"). (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [How to use Perplexity's new Computer...](sources/departmentofproduct-perplexity-computer.md): the competitor-monitor prompt has to forbid invented pricing and require a URL for every data point (research-department-of-product-knowledge-series)
- [How to build a Persona Feature Tester with Claude Code and ElevenLabs](sources/departmentofproduct-persona-feature-tester.md): the personas' specific quotes and behaviours trace back to model-written "research" files (research-department-of-product-knowledge-series)
- [How to do AI-powered product discovery sprints](sources/departmentofproduct-ai-discovery-sprints.md): cites Deloitte's partial refund to the Australian government over fabricated sources as a deep-research warning (research-department-of-product-knowledge-series)
- [Automating the Detection of Requirement Dependencies Using Large Language Models](sources/arxiv-darif-leredd-requirement-dependencies.md): "zero-shot models typically over-predict dependencies" (RQ1 answer); the model returns a rationale and confidence score, and predictions with confidence 4 or lower are re-labelled no-dependency as the main filter against unreliable claims. - [Automated Detection of Typed Links in Issue Trackers](sources/arxiv-luders-automated-detection-typed-links.md): shorter issue text predicted better (correlation about -0.70), and the model "does not simply learn textual similarity" (abstract): long, rich specs are not automatically easier. (independent; research-dependency-agent)

- [Advanced evals: How to find (and fix) hidden AI failures in your product](sources/lenny-newsletter-advanced-evals-error-discovery.md): on 100 production traces, agents caught failures visible inside a trace but missed ones needing product judgment (objection handling, missed handoffs) and flagged good responses as failures (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)

- [Community Wisdom: Communication architectures ...](sources/lenny-community-wisdom-communication-architectures.md): storing first-pass analyses loses whatever the first pass missed (thread 3) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [How to do AI analysis you can actually trust](sources/lenny-newsletter-ai-analysis-you-can-trust.md): invented and "Frankenstein" quotes across all major models; word-limit prompts trigger mash-ups; IDs and timestamps can be faked; most quotes in one verified ChatGPT run were paraphrases (Failure mode #1) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
