- [Resources (MCP specification 2025-06-18)](sources/mcp-spec-resources.md): resource = uri, name, title, description, mimeType, size, plus annotations `audience` [user|assistant], `priority` 0-1, `lastModified` ISO-8601; resource templates via RFC 6570 URI templates; `resources/list`, `resources/read`, `r (user-story-mapping)
- [Snowflake-managed MCP server (Snowflake docs)](sources/snowflake-managed-mcp-server-docs.md): supports only tool capabilities, not MCP resources or prompts; response truncation at 250 KB; max 50 tools; recursion depth 10. (user-story-mapping)
- [Descriptor Format of Catalog Entities (Backstage)](sources/backstage-descriptor-format.md): Kubernetes-style envelope (`apiVersion`, `kind`, `metadata` name/title/description/tags/links/labels/annotations, `spec`); relations are generated, not hand-written. (user-story-mapping)
- [Descriptor Format of Catalog Entities (Backstage)](sources/backstage-descriptor-format.md): required fields include `spec.owner` and `spec.lifecycle` (experimental, production, deprecated, extensible); System groups components, Domain groups systems (a built-in grouping hierarchy). (user-story-mapping)
- [MADR: Markdown Architectural Decision Records](sources/adr-madr-template.md): location `docs/decisions/`, name `NNNN-title-with-dashes.md`; frontmatter `status` (proposed, accepted, rejected, deprecated, superseded), `date`, `decision-makers`, `consulted`, `informed`. (user-story-mapping)
- [Diátaxis: a systematic approach to technical documentation](sources/diataxis-framework.md): four types matched to user needs; organises content, style and architecture; the site claims adoption in hundreds of projects (vendor/self-reported). (user-story-mapping)
- [Gherkin Reference (Cucumber)](sources/cucumber-gherkin-reference.md): one Feature per `.feature` file; keywords Feature, Rule, Example/Scenario, Given/When/Then, Background, Scenario Outline; examples double as tests via step definitions. (user-story-mapping)
- [PROV-Overview (W3C)](sources/w3c-prov-overview.md): provenance defined as information about entities, activities and people producing a thing; PROV-DM conceptual model with PROV-O/N/XML serialisations. (user-story-mapping)
- [C2PA and Content Credentials Explainer](sources/c2pa-explainer.md): assertions are grouped into a signed claim, bundled into a manifest bound to the asset by hash; each edit adds a manifest referencing the previous one. (user-story-mapping)
- [PRD template (Confluence)](sources/atlassian-confluence-prd-template.md): named sections: basics and roles, objective, success metrics, assumptions, options (requirement, user story, importance, Jira issues), supporting docs, open questions with answer date, out of scope. (user-story-mapping)
- [Project poster template (Confluence)](sources/atlassian-confluence-project-poster-template.md): Team Playbook project poster: problem space, what we know vs still need to answer, solution and scope, reference links; a living page upstream of the PRD. (user-story-mapping)
- [DACI decision template (Confluence)](sources/atlassian-confluence-daci-decision-template.md): decision record fields: status, impact, DACI roles, due date, background, options with pros/cons/cost, action items, outcome. (user-story-mapping)

## autonomy-alignment-placement: Where autonomy sits in the org
Which level sets intent (team, VP, executive) and how alignment is carried down. It decides where an agent should get the "what and why".
- [Scaling Agile @ Spotify with Tribes, Squads, Chapters & Guilds](sources/kniberg-ivarsson-scaling-agile-spotify.md): in 2012 autonomy sat with the squad "mini-startup"; the product owner owns "what", the chapter lead "how" (pp.2-13) (research-airbnb-spotify-product-practices)
- [Spotify Engineering Culture - Part 1](sources/kniberg-spotify-engineering-culture-part-1.md): "aligned autonomy": leaders say what problem and why, squads decide how; low alignment makes the product "a Frankenstein" (~3:00-4:40) (research-airbnb-spotify-product-practices)
- [Spotify's Failed #SquadGoals](sources/jeremiahlee-failed-squad-goals.md): an ex-PM says autonomy without shared process or accountability hurt cross-team work; the alignment part of the model "was never written" (research-airbnb-spotify-product-practices)
- [Don't Copy the Spotify Model](sources/infoq-dont-copy-spotify-model.md): a 2016 chapter lead says autonomy fails without shared direction; squads led by a product, technology and process triad (research-airbnb-spotify-product-practices)
- [Top 3 Points from the Spotify Engineering Culture Videos](sources/bai-jason-yip-spotify-engineering-culture-points.md): "alignment … around intent, autonomy … towards actions" (Spotify coach, 2022) (research-airbnb-spotify-product-practices)
- [An Update on January 2023 Organizational Changes](sources/spotify-newsroom-january-2023-org-changes.md): most product and engineering centralised under Söderström because teams spent "far too much time syncing on slightly different strategies" (research-airbnb-spotify-product-practices)
- [Lessons from scaling Spotify (Gustav Söderström)](sources/lenny-podcast-gustav-soderstrom-scaling-spotify.md): Spotify moved away from squads; autonomy at the leaves "produces heat", so it now sits at VP level; teams 2-3x larger (28:51-35:45) (research-airbnb-spotify-product-practices)
- [How Spotify Thinks (Invest Like the Best EP.424)](sources/colossus-ilb-gustav-soderstrom-how-spotify-thinks.md): bottom-up VP pitches plus top-down sync; the company is "completely synchronized for good and bad" (~26:50) (research-airbnb-spotify-product-practices)
- [Ek becomes Executive Chairman; Söderström and Norström named co-CEOs](sources/spotify-newsroom-ek-executive-chairman.md): co-CEOs from 2026 formalise the product/tech vs business split used since 2023 (research-airbnb-spotify-product-practices)
- [The Platform PM role at Spotify (DX ep. 50)](sources/dx-podcast-nils-loodin-platform-pm-spotify.md): leadership sets strategy in objectives, strategy docs and roadmaps; teams are "autonomous with how" (research-airbnb-spotify-product-practices)

## bets-and-planning-cadence: Bets and planning cadence
A stack-ranked list of bets on a fixed cadence is the company's unit of commitment, so it anchors plan-stage artifacts. Close to leadership-review-cadence; a later consolidation pass may merge them.
- [Spotify Rhythm: How we create focus](sources/kniberg-spotify-rhythm.md): company bets re-ranked quarterly; product bets every 6 weeks; Now/Next/Later boards; one stack rank, with High-Medium-Low called "broken" (slides 10-19) (research-airbnb-spotify-product-practices)
- [Don't Copy the Spotify Model](sources/infoq-dont-copy-spotify-model.md): DIBBs and a company-wide visible bets board in 2016 (research-airbnb-spotify-product-practices)
- [Lessons from scaling Spotify (Gustav Söderström)](sources/lenny-podcast-gustav-soderstrom-scaling-spotify.md): six-month increments with about two weeks of planning (1:02:46) (research-airbnb-spotify-product-practices)
- [How Spotify Thinks (Invest Like the Best EP.424)](sources/colossus-ilb-gustav-soderstrom-how-spotify-thinks.md): ~14 VPs pitch "as if … a VC"; the co-presidents stack-rank 44 bets (30-50 typical); teams staff from the top down (~16:26) (research-airbnb-spotify-product-practices)
- [Ek memo on the December 2023 layoffs](sources/spotify-ek-memo-december-2023-layoffs.md): fewer, more focused "bold bets" under a lean mandate (research-airbnb-spotify-product-practices)
- [Spotify Q3 2026 Earnings Call](sources/spotify-q3-2026-earnings-call.md): "We decide what we are going to do for six months, then we build it"; the last cycle showed "very significant acceleration" (research-airbnb-spotify-product-practices)

## build-vs-buy: Own the agent harness as a moat
Reasons to build internally: moat, speed of fixes, learning for the external product.
- [We Built Every Employee at Ramp Their Own AI Coworker](sources/x-sebgoddijn-glass-article.md): three reasons (competitive-teardown-ramp-glass)
- [Eric Glyman April 2026 posts on Glass and AI adoption](sources/x-eglyman-april-glass-posts.md): "we decided to own it" (competitive-teardown-ramp-glass)
- [How We Built Glass: Vibe Coding a Product Used by 700 People](sources/x-shanebuchan-how-we-built-glass.md): a 3-person team, vibe-coded (competitive-teardown-ramp-glass)
- [Introducing Glass: Learn Things Once.](sources/x-eglyman-introducing-glass-learn-things-once.md): "as is often the case at Ramp, a small team built something"; now sold externally as a product, so the build also became a revenue line (vendor claim) (competitive-teardown-ramp-glass)
- [How to get your company AI pilled](sources/x-geoffintech-ai-pilled-article.md): "our own version of Claude Code's Cowork, built on Anthropic's Claude Agent SDK"; "a team of four built it in under three months" (competitive-teardown-ramp-glass)
- [Ramp built an AI agent harness in six weeks](sources/thenewstack-ramp-laminar-agent-harness.md): Ramp replaced vendor SDKs with its own harness Laminar (six-week V1, now under Glass and Inspect) after testing Claude Agent SDK, Claude Managed Agents, OpenAI Agents SDK, OpenCode, LangChain, Sierra; no cost comparison published (competitive-teardown-ramp-glass)
- [Building Laminar: Ramp's Managed Agents Platform](sources/ramp-builders-building-laminar.md): Ramp built its own harness (~May 2026, v1 in six weeks) after trying vendor SDKs, managed-agent APIs and frameworks; 'you still need good engineers to be on-call' (competitive-teardown-ramp-glass)
- [Meet Stripe's Knowledge AI Platform](sources/stripe-meet-knowledge-ai-platform.md): built after a no-code agent builder and coding agents for non-engineers both failed (quality sprawl; security and support burden); core primitives shared with Stripe's customer-facing agents (competitive-teardown-stripe-knowledge-agents)
- [Build your own company brain (How I AI, Krishnamurthy)](sources/howiai-stripe-kai-krishnamurthy.md): 'it's not about providing AI it's about providing the correct governance structures'; v0 by 1.5 people in two weeks; core team under 10 (competitive-teardown-stripe-knowledge-agents)
- [Emily Glassberg Sands on Latent Space](sources/latentspace-emily-sands-stripe.md): Sands: build-vs-buy is 'sequential': built GoLLM when no safe vendor existed, then replaced it with open-source LibreChat; buys via RFP 'spotlight' (Braintrust for evals) (competitive-teardown-stripe-knowledge-agents)
- [Ramp Inspect Architecture 2026: How Background Coding Agents Scale Safely](sources/wavect-ramp-inspect-architecture.md): buy commodity sandbox infrastructure; build or heavily customise base images, harness, context, permissions and evals (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Harness Engineering: ... Eleven Systems](sources/arxiv-harness-engineering-eleven-systems.md): independent: 0 of 11 production coding harnesses import a general agent framework; recommends raw SDK calls or a harness SDK, and starting with a bash-only linear loop (scope: coding harnesses) (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Agent Design Is Still Hard](sources/lucumr-agent-design-is-still-hard.md): independent practitioner (anecdote): would not again use a framework SDK for provider abstraction; expects to need own abstraction (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Minions: Stripe's one-shot coding agents](sources/stripe-minions-one-shot-coding-agents.md): first-party: Stripe forked Goose rather than building from scratch or using a framework; reasons are codebase specificity and existing human-dev tooling (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Context Engineering for AI Agents: Lessons from Building Manus](sources/manus-context-engineering-lessons.md): first-party: Manus rebuilt its agent framework four times (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [What I learned building an opinionated and minimal coding agent](sources/mariozechner-pi-minimal-coding-agent.md): anecdote: build for context control; cost is maintaining provider abstraction and TUI (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Anthropic cracks down on unauthorized Claude usage by third-party harnesses](sources/venturebeat-anthropic-third-party-harness-crackdown.md): independent: platform risk, subscription access limited to official clients (Jan 2026) (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Hosting the Agent SDK](sources/anthropic-agent-sdk-hosting.md): first-party: even with the loop bought, the builder owns sandboxing, session storage, tenant isolation, scaling, observability (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Building effective agents](sources/anthropic-building-effective-agents.md): first-party: start with raw API calls; frameworks add abstraction that obscures prompts (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [microsoft/autogen repository](sources/github-microsoft-autogen-archive-notice.md): first-party: AutoGen archived with no fixes; framework churn risk (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [HN Cloudflare OS thread](sources/hn-cloudflare-os-thread.md): 'smells like lock-in' vs 'you can fork it'; open source but contingent on Cloudflare's PaaS (anecdote) (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Vibe Kanban shutdown](sources/vibekanban-shutdown.md): dependency risk of adopting a small vendor's orchestration tool (first-party) (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Cloudflare OS rollout post](sources/cloudflare-how-we-rethink-work-with-cloudflare-os.md): second internal-platform build-then-open-source account (v1 May 2026, v2 open sourced 2026-08-05), self-reported (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Open Source AI Won. Now What?](sources/medium-al-dahle-open-source-ai-won.md): models and agent scaffolding are commoditising; what lasts is proprietary data, workflow integration and taste (research-airbnb-spotify-product-practices)
- [Airbnb Q4 2023 earnings call and shareholder letter](sources/airbnb-earnings-q4-2023.md): models are "infrastructure"; Airbnb will win the "application layer" (research-airbnb-spotify-product-practices)
- [Airbnb Q4 2025 earnings call and shareholder letter](sources/airbnb-earnings-q4-2025.md): "we're not building models"; post-train available models on Airbnb data (research-airbnb-spotify-product-practices)
- [Airbnb Q2 2025 earnings call and shareholder letter](sources/airbnb-earnings-q2-2025.md): the best model isn't enough; tune it and build a custom interface (research-airbnb-spotify-product-practices)
- [Chesky says OpenAI tools not ready for ChatGPT tie-up with Airbnb app](sources/fortune-chesky-openai-not-ready-qwen.md): own agent on many vendors' models rather than living inside ChatGPT (research-airbnb-spotify-product-practices)
- [Airbnb Q4 2024 earnings call](sources/airbnb-earnings-q4-2024.md): models "getting commoditized"; value goes to platforms (research-airbnb-spotify-product-practices)
- [Spotify Q3 2026 Earnings Call](sources/spotify-q3-2026-earnings-call.md): selling internal agentic dev tools is "mostly … option value" to spread costs over "our few thousand developers" (research-airbnb-spotify-product-practices)
- [Introducing: Spotify Technology](sources/spotify-engineering-introducing-spotify-technology.md): every product sold runs first on Spotify's own production (research-airbnb-spotify-product-practices)
- [Q2 2026 Shareholder Letter](sources/block-q2-2026-shareholder-letter.md): "the models are interchangeable"; the harness, data and distribution are Block's (research-block-product-practices)
- [Block rolls out Builderbot](sources/block-builderbot-rollout.md): built a goose-based orchestration layer because no bought tool spanned the whole codebase (research-block-product-practices)
- [The 2026 State of AI Agents Report](sources/claude-2026-state-of-ai-agents.md): 47% both buy off-the-shelf and build in-house, 21% primarily buy, 20% build with APIs/toolkits; enterprises 54% hybrid (ch. 2). (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [How Cresta turned CX expertise into an agent builder on the Claude Agent SDK](sources/claude-cresta-agent-builder-evals.md): Cresta "drew a hard line" between its own conversation data and CX expertise and what it took from the Agent SDK, "and refused to build anything on the wrong side of it" (best-practices box). (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [How Asana built AI Teammates on Claude Opus 4.6](sources/claude-customers-asana-ai-teammates.md): Managed Agents "removed a lot of the undifferentiated heavy lifting" so Asana's team focused on Work Graph integration; Agent Skills cut development time for SharePoint/OneDrive document editing. (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [How Blank Metal, a lean professional services firm, runs on Claude Cowork](sources/claude-customers-blank-metal-cowork.md): the firm watches what comes "off the shelf from Claude" and customises only where needed; Cowork for internal work, Claude Code for ~90% of engineering, the API for client implementations ("How do you keep up"). (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [Carvana turns Slack alerts into production fixes with Claude Tag](sources/claude-customers-carvana-claude-tag.md): two homegrown Slackbots retired; maintenance "required time and resources"; one team refused to adopt the homegrown tools over support uncertainty (section "The challenge"). (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [Cyera on making Claude Cowork the front door to 40 tools](sources/claude-customers-cyera-cowork-front-door.md): considered building its own wrapper around Claude Code pushed to laptops and surveyed open-source harnesses; rejected them as built for people who already know what a cron job is (case study, "The solution"; Q&A). (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [How Sentry built end-to-end bug fixing with Claude Managed Agents](sources/claude-customers-sentry-bug-fixing-agents.md): building a coding agent meant sandboxing, lifecycle management and a runtime, "a significant detour"; Managed Agents let a single engineer ship the initial integration "in weeks instead of months" and removed ongoing infra... (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [Stripe deploys Claude Code to 1,370 engineers with zero-configuration enterprise rollout](sources/claude-customers-stripe-claude-code-rollout.md): six coding assistants enabled for different personas (infra engineers prefer CLI, product engineers in-editor); "going broad", no consolidation yet. (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [A Twilio PM on building a self-learning development platform with Claude Code](sources/claude-customers-twilio-pm-platform.md): built local memory and dreaming himself to be "a good evaluator" of Managed Agents; multi-tenant memory with audit trails is "an infrastructure problem" (Q&A, memory answer). (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [Memory for Claude Managed Agents: agents that learn across sessions](sources/claude-managed-agents-memory.md): Ando and Wisedocs say the feature replaced memory infrastructure they would otherwise build (section "What teams are building", quotes). (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [Claude Marketplace: plugins and connectors, products and agents, and service partners](sources/claude-marketplace.md): customers can apply "a portion of" committed Anthropic spend to buy Claude-powered software (CrowdStrike, Cursor, Harvey, Legora, Lovable, Snowflake, Hebbia), shortening procurement ("For customers"; partner quotes). (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [Are Agent Harnesses the new "secret sauce" for Product Teams?](sources/departmentofproduct-agent-harnesses-secret-sauce.md): Square's head of product calls context management and progressive tool disclosure "at the harness layer" Managerbot's secret sauce; harness as "agentic moat" (second-hand via VentureBeat) (research-department-of-product-knowledge-series)
- [How to build an AI Agent](sources/departmentofproduct-how-to-build-an-ai-agent.md): early three-way choice (framework / from scratch / no-code), from before "extend a vendor harness" was an option (research-department-of-product-knowledge-series)
- [What a harness is and how to build one with Claude Agent SDK](sources/howiai-claire-vo-agent-sdk-harness.md): "When to build a harness versus ... a general-purpose tool like Claude Code or Codex" for a repetitive, structured workflow (03:19, 06:00) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [Why LinkedIn is turning PMs into AI-powered "full stack builders"](sources/lenny-podcast-tomer-cohen-full-stack-builder.md): started from Copilot Enterprise and ChatGPT Enterprise, but own customisation and orchestrator gave "the biggest gains"; trust agent "something you cannot bring off the shelf" (20:25, 23:31) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [How Amplitude built an internal AI tool](sources/howiai-amplitude-wade-chambers-moda.md): built Moda in "3 to 4 weeks of engineers' spare time" after a build-vs-buy decision (show notes only) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [Block's Goose (Brosamer, Axen)](sources/howiai-block-goose-brosamer-axen.md): Block built and open-sourced Goose so it isn't tied to vendor tools that "can only use like that kind of models" (6:40) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [The GenAI Divide: State of AI in Business 2025](sources/mit-nanda-genai-divide-2025.md): counter-evidence: external partnerships reached deployment ~67% vs ~33% for internal builds; report says correlation, not causation (research-pm-agents-jobs-to-be-done)

## capability-packaging-layers: Choosing the layer a capability lives in
Block deliberately packages capability at four layers (MCP server, skill, recipe, platform service) and moves capabilities between them; the rule it states is that scripts and platforms own what must be consistent, skills and recipes own the procedure. Matters for how a PM agent's capabilities would be packaged, versioned and governed.
- [From Localhost to Launched](sources/block-eng-app-kit-localhost-to-launched.md): the internal app-publishing capability moved from an MCP server (BlockCell) to a distributed skill plus a fixed stack (research-block-product-practices)
- [3 Principles for Designing Agent Skills](sources/block-eng-3-principles-agent-skills.md): "know what the agent should not decide": deterministic scripts inside skills for anything that must reproduce (research-block-product-practices)
- [Recipes, Recipe Reference and Shareable Recipes (goose docs)](sources/goose-docs-recipes.md): recipe = instructions, typed parameters, extensions, model, sub-recipes, response schema and shell-checked retries (research-block-product-practices)
- [Block's Playbook for Designing MCP Servers](sources/block-eng-playbook-designing-mcp-servers.md): MCP servers designed around workflows, not APIs (Linear from 30+ tools to 2) (research-block-product-practices)
- [Block rolls out Builderbot](sources/block-builderbot-rollout.md): the shared coding capability became a platform service on goose, not a per-user recipe (research-block-product-practices)

## certified-metrics-layer: Certified metrics layer
One governed, code-reviewed set of metric definitions serves analytics, experiments and executive reports. It is the grounding a metrics or experiment agent needs.
- [How Airbnb achieved metric consistency at scale (Minerva)](sources/airbnb-tech-minerva-metric-consistency.md): 12,000+ metrics, 4,000 dimensions, 200+ producers in one GitHub-defined, code-reviewed layer feeding experiments (ERF), dashboards and executive reports (Apr 2021) (research-airbnb-spotify-product-practices)
- [Designing Experimentation Guardrails](sources/airbnb-tech-designing-experimentation-guardrails.md): protected guardrail metrics in three classes; more guardrails mean more false alarms (92% for 50 metrics in an A/A test) (research-airbnb-spotify-product-practices)

## checklist-implementation-fidelity: Checklists work through the behaviour they force
A checklist's effect depends on whether the team actually does what it demands; mandated or ticked-off checklists show little effect.
- [A surgical safety checklist to reduce morbidity and mortality](sources/nejm-haynes-surgical-safety-checklist.md): deaths 1.5% to 0.8% and complications 11.0% to 7.0% across 8 hospitals (before/after) (research-skill-rigidity-spectrum)
- [Introduction of surgical safety checklists in Ontario](sources/nejm-urbach-ontario-surgical-checklists.md): mandated adoption in 101 hospitals, about 215k procedures, no significant change in mortality or complications (research-skill-rigidity-spectrum)
- [Multiple interacting factors influence adherence](sources/plosone-gagliardi-checklist-adherence.md): checklists "often inaccurately documented as complete" and modified until key interactions vanished (research-skill-rigidity-spectrum)
- [Do explicit review strategies improve code review performance?](sources/emse-goncalves-explicit-review-strategies.md): checklist and guided-checklist effects on code review were weak and task-dependent (research-skill-rigidity-spectrum)
- [A systematic review of validity evidence for checklists versus global rating scales](sources/medu-ilgen-checklists-vs-global-rating-scales.md): "each task requires a separate checklist" while a rating scale spans tasks (research-skill-rigidity-spectrum)
- [Human Factors of Flight-Deck Checklists](sources/nasa-degani-wiener-flight-deck-checklists.md): non-use and improper use cited as probable cause in accidents; production pressure degrades use (research-skill-rigidity-spectrum)

## cognitive-load-and-platforms: Cognitive load and platforms
Team Topologies' framing: platforms exist to reduce stream-aligned teams' cognitive load, and badly built platforms add to it.
- [Atlassian research: AI adoption is rising, but friction persists (State of Developer Experience 2025)](sources/atlassian-state-of-devex-2025.md): adapting to new technology and context switching between tools are the next two time-wasters. (vendor-claim; research-dependency-agent)
- [CNCF Platforms White Paper](sources/cncf-tag-app-delivery-platforms-white-paper.md): the first stated purpose of platforms is to reduce cognitive load on product teams (Why platforms). (independent; research-dependency-agent)
- [Capabilities: Platform engineering](sources/dora-capability-platform-engineering.md): platform engineers should "shift down" complexity into the platform rather than expecting developers to become experts in it (Cognitive load section). (independent; research-dependency-agent)
- [2025 State of Internal Developer Portals](sources/port-state-of-internal-developer-portals-2025.md): 75% lose 6-15 hours weekly to tool sprawl; average 7.4 tools for everyday operational tasks. (vendor-claim; research-dependency-agent)
- [Platform as a Product in a 300-Year-Old Bank](sources/syntasso-natwest-platform-as-product-300-year-old-bank.md): high cognitive load on developers and duplicated effort across teams named as the starting problem. (vendor-claim; research-dependency-agent)
- [Google DORA issues platform engineering caveats](sources/techtarget-pariseau-dora-2024-platform-engineering-caveats.md): the report's caveat that the gains "do not come without some drawbacks". (independent; research-dependency-agent)
- [A decade of cloud native at ING: lessons learned and what comes next](sources/techzine-nardiello-ing-decade-cloud-native.md): "Suddenly, thirty solid interfaces feel like thirty different products." (first-party; research-dependency-agent)

## compounding-context-repo: Context that compounds with each shipped feature
A shared, agent-readable, harness-agnostic store of product context ("evidence, not yet fact", with domain owners), which every spec writes back to. This is the harness's memory layer.
- [Under the River](sources/shopify-engineering-under-the-river.md): monorepo World holds code, skills, conventions, intent documents, runbooks, AGENTS.md and zone knowledge; sessions leave "a pebble, a skill update, an AGENTS.md diff" (competitive-teardown-shopify-river)
- [River's reaction to the Shop floor post](sources/x-tobi-river-reaction-to-shop-floor-post.md): "AGENTS.md files are mirror surfaces": writing them forces teams to find they "didn't quite agree with each other" (competitive-teardown-shopify-river)
- [Shopify's River: The AI Agent as Organizational Memory](sources/aienabledpm-shopify-river-organizational-memory.md): agent failures as context, permission and taste gaps, fixed by making knowledge explicit (competitive-teardown-shopify-river)
- [Scaling Knowledge at Airbnb (Knowledge Repo)](sources/airbnb-tech-scaling-knowledge-knowledge-repo.md): built to move insight "across teams and across time" (research-airbnb-spotify-product-practices)

## coordination-cost-and-waiting: Coordination cost: elapsed time is waiting on other parties
Evidence on how much elapsed time in cross-team work is waiting, chasing and finding rather than working; it matters because this is the cost a dependency agent is meant to cut and the number nobody publishes.
- [Dependency Management in Large-Scale Agile: A Case Study of DevOps Teams](sources/aisel-stray-moe-aasheim-dependency-management-devops-teams.md): dependencies between and within teams must be managed at both project and team levels in large-scale agile (Abstract). (independent; research-dependency-agent)
- [The difficulties of cascading OKRs](sources/allankelly-difficulties-cascading-okrs.md): each level waits for the level above, and setting OKRs takes reflection and iteration, so three layers can take a week or more: "you have a delay built into the system". (anecdote; research-dependency-agent)
- [Automating Low-Risk Code Review at Meta: RADAR, Risk Calibration, and Review Efficiency](sources/arxiv-adams-meta-radar-low-risk-review.md): median time to close down "by over 330%" (the paper's phrasing) and median review wall time down 35%; lines per landed diff +105.9% YoY and per-developer diff volume +51%. (first-party; research-dependency-agent)
- [Coordinating Knowledge Work in Multi-Team Programs: Findings from a Large-Scale Agile Development Program](sources/arxiv-dingsoyr-coordinating-multi-team-programs.md): "In the business project, much of the work concentrated on managing dependencies, 'there were dependencies throughout the program'" (§Group mode); separate meetings were held "to identify dependencies in tasks before work was assigned to teams". (independent; research-dependency-agent)
- [Nudge: Accelerating Overdue Pull Requests Towards Completion](sources/arxiv-maddila-nudge-overdue-pull-requests.md): 60% reduction in PR resolution time in the randomised trial. (first-party; research-dependency-agent)
- [Challenges of Adopting SAFe in the Banking Industry – A Study Two Years after its Introduction](sources/arxiv-tengstrand-safe-banking-challenges.md): related-work summary (§3.1) reports that an American bank found "it was difficult for teams to deliver independently because of dependencies outside of the teams"; Nordea's teams in one ART were frustrated because "delivery streams were not in unison", with PI planning reported as the unifying fix. (independent; research-dependency-agent)
- [Identifying Critical Dependencies in Large-Scale Continuous Software Engineering](sources/arxiv-tkalich-critical-dependencies-cse.md): the framing is delay and bottleneck, not effort: the cost of a dependency is waiting time at a function outside the team. (independent; research-dependency-agent)
- [Atlassian research: AI adoption is rising, but friction persists (State of Developer Experience 2025)](sources/atlassian-state-of-devex-2025.md): 50% of developers lose 10+ hours a week to organisational inefficiencies; 90% lose 6+ hours (blog body). Evidence: vendor survey. (vendor-claim; research-dependency-agent)
- [Black Swan Farming using Cost of Delay](sources/blackswanfarming-maersk-cost-of-delay.md): 82 hours of develop-and-test in 46 weeks end to end, "over 38 weeks" of waiting, 29 weeks in the fuzzy front end (value stream map). By calculation (not in the paper) active time is roughly 4% of elapsed time. (vendor-claim; research-dependency-agent)
- [Coordination Breakdowns and Their Impact on Development Productivity and Software Failures](sources/cataldo-herbsleb-coordination-breakdowns.md): "higher levels of congruence are associated with improved development productivity" (Abstract), measured as resolution time of modification requests (section 7). (independent; research-dependency-agent)
- [DORA Report 2024 (Accelerate State of DevOps)](sources/dora-accelerate-state-of-devops-2024.md): platforms can decrease throughput and change stability (findings list); see techtarget-pariseau-dora-2024-platform-engineering-caveats for the figures (-8% throughput, -14% stability). (independent; research-dependency-agent)
- [Capabilities: Platform engineering](sources/dora-capability-platform-engineering.md): 2024 finding that developer independence, the ability to complete tasks without relying on an enabling team, was linked to a 5% productivity improvement at team and individual levels (Key findings). (independent; research-dependency-agent)
- [Capabilities: Streamlining change approval](sources/dora-capability-streamlining-change-approval.md): suggested metrics include "time changes spend waiting for external or local approval" and the proportion of changes requiring external approval by risk profile (Measuring). (independent; research-dependency-agent)
- [Accelerate: State of DevOps 2019](sources/dora-state-of-devops-2019.md): complexity in change management comes from "the need for coordination between teams, and requirements of regulatory control, particularly in financial services, healthcare, and government" (p. 48); "In our work with large organizations, change management is consistently one of the biggest constraints" (p. 52). (independent; research-dependency-agent)
- [Escape ticketing hell with a shift to self-service platforms](sources/equalexperts-smith-escape-ticketing-hell.md): handoffs to DBAs for schema changes, change managers for approvals, operations for deployments; tickets move through triage, prioritised, blocked. (anecdote; research-dependency-agent)
- [Implementing technology change](sources/fca-implementing-technology-change.md): The UK FCA's multi-firm review of over 1 million production changes made in 2019 by 23 banks, wholesale firms and insurers found that the single most consistent risk factor for a failed change was "a project ... (first-party; research-dependency-agent)
- [Decision: Remark and administrative fine, Swedbank AB (FI Ref. 22-18430)](sources/fi-swedbank-change-management-sanction.md): the bank "did not inform the third-party supplier that had developed the system ... despite the supplier at an earlier stage having expressed at least uncertainty about the intended change" (2.1.2, p. 5). (first-party; research-dependency-agent)
- [The SPACE of Developer Productivity: There's more to it than you think](sources/forsgren-space-of-developer-productivity.md): the Efficiency and flow dimension lists "number of handoffs in a process; number of handoffs across different teams" and "time measures through a system: total time, value-added time, wait time" as example metrics (Efficiency and flow section). (independent; research-dependency-agent)
- [What I Talk About When I Talk About Platforms](sources/fowler-bottcher-what-i-talk-about-platforms.md): "The tasks that had to wait for another team were 10-12x slower in elapsed time" (section on backlog coupling). Evidence: a consultant reporting colleagues' study at one client; no method given. (anecdote; research-dependency-agent)
- [Cloud Security: Federal Authorization Program Usage Increasing, but Challenges Need to Be Fully Addressed (GAO-24-106591)](sources/gao-cloud-security-fedramp-challenges-2024.md): challenge "Receiving timely responses from stakeholders"; "Finding an agency sponsor" (Highlights: What GAO Found). (independent; research-dependency-agent)
- [Report: Developers lose a full day per week due to inefficiencies](sources/getdx-dx-atlassian-developers-lose-a-day.md): "69% of developers lose 8 or more hours each week to inefficiencies" (summary). Evidence: vendor survey, self-reported. (vendor-claim; research-dependency-agent)
- [Splitting the Organization and Integrating the Code: Conway's Law Revisited](sources/herbsleb-grinter-conways-law-revisited.md): questions to the other site often had to "wait at least until the next business day" (section 4.2). (independent; research-dependency-agent)
- [An Empirical Study of Speed and Communication in Globally Distributed Software Development](sources/herbsleb-mockus-speed-communication-distributed-development.md): "the number of people involved is strongly related to the calendar time to complete a work item" (Abstract). (independent; research-dependency-agent)
- [HealthCare.gov: Case Study of CMS Management of the Federal Marketplace (OEI-06-14-00350)](sources/hhs-oig-healthcare-gov-case-study.md): "CMS was never able to complete full end-to-end testing that identifies problems in how the pieces work together, because the component pieces arrived too late"; issuers complained of "unavailable testing environments" (Final Countdown chapter, p. 27). (independent; research-dependency-agent)
- [Why Software Fails](sources/ieee-spectrum-charette-why-software-fails.md): large projects are increasingly "systems of systems"; integration "has stymied many developers"; no one fully understands or can test all the interactions (body). (independent; research-dependency-agent)
- [CBA pushing to production more often, with fewer incidents](sources/itnews-cba-production-more-often-fewer-incidents.md): "In just a year we have doubled the number of changes delivered to production"; customer-impacting incidents fell proportionally more than changes rose; "our time to resolve incidents has reduced to half". (first-party; research-dependency-agent)
- [Accounting Versus Physics – Rewiring Organizations for Improvement](sources/itrevolution-prugh-accounting-versus-physics.md): "every single dependency chain or additional handoff cuts the chance of on-time delivery in half"; "More coordination equals more delays"; overloaded people context-switch and lengthen queues ("wait time presenteeism") (body). (anecdote; research-dependency-agent)
- [Challenges and success factors for large-scale agile transformations: A systematic literature review](sources/jss-dikert-large-scale-agile-transformations.md): "The roll-out of agile had not removed dependencies, and the dependencies made managing development difficult"; Scrum-of-Scrums "worked for up to five teams, but did not scale to a global level" (4.2.4). (independent; research-dependency-agent)
- [Coordination & Integration (LeSS framework)](sources/less-coordination-and-integration.md): on Scrum of Scrums, "it is recommended to not do this in LeSS"; the urge to hold one "can be a sign of unnecessary dependency or coordination problems caused by single-function groups and component teams". (independent; research-dependency-agent)
- [Entangled: Solving the Hairy Problem of Team Dependencies](sources/magennis-entangled-team-dependencies.md): "Delays are NOT CAUSED by the item being delayed, its caused by other factors that are unknowable (and unquantifiable) in advance. It's the start time we struggle to compute" (slide 31). (anecdote; research-dependency-agent)
- [ING's agile transformation](sources/mckinsey-ing-agile-transformation.md): agility is "about minimizing handovers and bureaucracy"; the old organisation had "managers controlling the handovers and slowing down collaboration" (Jacobs, Schlatmann). (first-party; research-dependency-agent)
- [Coordination in Large-Scale Software Development: Helpful and Unhelpful Behaviors](sources/microsoft-research-coordination-large-scale-development.md): "I need to ping the people I depend on for status": 49% frequently or more; "My dependencies proactively communicate their status to me": 34%; "I need to maintain constant contact with my dependent team in order to get what I want": 78% agree (Table 2). (independent; research-dependency-agent)
- [Framework to review programmes (Update April 2021)](sources/nao-framework-to-review-programmes.md): Crossrail example: from 2015 the programme ran on "an aspirational plan designed to improve progress by suppliers"; the plan did not reflect interdependencies, "consequently there was a gap in the understanding of delivery risks"; the sharp cost increase "suddenly became apparent in late 2018" (examples section). (independent; research-dependency-agent)
- [DevEx: What Actually Drives Productivity](sources/noda-devex-what-actually-drives-productivity.md): developers "may wait for approval from code reviewers, which blocks their ability to make progress"; slow feedback loops lead developers to "wait or decide to switch tasks" (Feedback loops section). (independent; research-dependency-agent)
- [Change Advisory Boards Don't Work](sources/octopus-change-advisory-boards-dont-work.md): a change that takes an hour to write can wait 40 business hours (168 clock hours) for a weekly CAB. (anecdote; research-dependency-agent)
- [2023 Project to Product State of the Industry Report](sources/planview-project-to-product-state-of-industry-2023.md): "87% of respondents are impacted by technical, process, and skill dependencies or are delayed by handoffs and coordination with shared services" (p. 17; 58% "dependencies slow down most deliveries", 29% "some self-service but others still require handoffs"). (vendor-claim; research-dependency-agent)
- [Pulse of the Profession 2018: Success in Disruptive Times](sources/pmi-pulse-of-the-profession-2018.md): 52% of projects completed in the past 12 months experienced scope creep, up from 43% five years earlier; projects of high complexity rose from 35% in 2013 to 41% (Control Scope section). (vendor-claim; research-dependency-agent)
- [2025 State of Internal Developer Portals](sources/port-state-of-internal-developer-portals-2025.md): 78% of engineering teams wait a day or more for SRE/DevOps assistance; 16% report a maximum wait of a week or more; 22% say issues are resolved within a day on average (30% with a portal). Evidence: vendor survey. (vendor-claim; research-dependency-agent)
- [SAFe® Program Dependency Board Retrospective – PI Planning and Execution](sources/scaledagile-yeret-program-dependency-board-retrospective.md): "too much red yarn means too many dependencies" and "Too many dependencies mean our Value Stream network isn't configured well" (body). (anecdote; research-dependency-agent)
- [Soon time for one of Europe's largest PI planning events](sources/sebgroup-europes-largest-pi-planning.md): if tribe A depends on tribe B and B plans ten weeks later, A may miss deliveries; shrinking the gap from ten weeks to one week (target two days) reduces that risk (body). (first-party; research-dependency-agent)
- [A taxonomy of inter-team coordination mechanisms in large-scale agile](sources/sintef-berntzen-inter-team-coordination-taxonomy.md): the related thesis work reports negative effects on team autonomy from coordination (limited feature choice, enforced refinement) (search summary of the thesis). (independent; research-dependency-agent)
- [2024 Stack Overflow Developer Survey: Professional Developers](sources/stackoverflow-dev-survey-2024-professional-developers.md): "Waiting on answers to questions often causes interruptions and disrupts my workflow": 53.0% agree or strongly agree (all respondents, n=28,747) (§6.1, ability to find knowledge). (independent; research-dependency-agent)
- [The Developer Coefficient: Software engineering efficiency and its $3 trillion impact on global GDP](sources/stripe-developer-coefficient-2018.md): "the average developer spends more than 17 hours a week dealing with maintenance issues"; about four hours a week on "bad code" (page 5). Evidence: vendor-sponsored, self-reported survey. (vendor-claim; research-dependency-agent)
- [When DORA metrics meet governance in banking - Expert View](sources/teamtopologies-dora-metrics-governance-banking.md): A practitioner round-up on change governance in banks: a large bank still approving production releases through CAB meetings after a decade of DevOps, a Morgan Stanley engineer's count of "3 different Jiras, a change ticket, and 81 individual steps" to get one line of code through paperwork and approval, and Deutsche Bank's experience running DORA surveys across a global engineering organisation. (anecdote; research-dependency-agent)
- [Key Concepts (Team Topologies)](sources/teamtopologies-key-concepts.md): the "Eliminate Team Dependencies" principle: one team waiting on another "kills productivity"; "Fix the handoffs, not just the teams"; stream-aligned teams should have no handoffs to other teams "for any purpose". (independent; research-dependency-agent)
- [Banking at scale: a blueprint for delivery transformation using Team Topologies](sources/teamtopologies-pujar-banking-at-scale.md): central release coordination before the change had heavy decision overhead and no business context. (anecdote; research-dependency-agent)
- [Google DORA issues platform engineering caveats](sources/techtarget-pariseau-dora-2024-platform-engineering-caveats.md): throughput fell 8% for platform users; the report notes platforms usually add "handoffs" between systems and teams (article body). (independent; research-dependency-agent)
- [Mapping out Agile transformation at TBC Bank](sources/thoughtworks-tbc-bank-agile-transformation.md): "high interdependence among our 140 squads" led to "prolonged time-to-market for products spread across various business units" (interview). (vendor-claim; research-dependency-agent)
- [Coordination Challenges in Large-Scale Software Development: A Case Study of Planning Misalignment in Hybrid Settings](sources/tse-bick-planning-misalignment-dependency-awareness.md): dependency awareness is lost through misaligned planning activities, "specification, prioritization, estimation and allocation between agile team and traditional inter-team levels" (abstract). (independent; research-dependency-agent)
- [How a Typical Day of Program Manager Looks Like](sources/zalando-pmo-typical-day-program-manager.md): hours 4-5 should go to updating the program plan, risk register and dashboards, but "more common" is handling ad hoc requests, priority shifts and change requests, then holding extra meetings. (anecdote; research-dependency-agent)

## cost-control-routing: Cost metering and model routing built into the harness
Open access to frontier models blew budgets; Ramp added per-project meters, limits and a router that picks the model.
- [Introducing Glass: Learn Things Once.](sources/x-eglyman-introducing-glass-learn-things-once.md): $1.5M week, taxi meter, Ramp Router, 30% drop claimed (competitive-teardown-ramp-glass)
- [Ramp: Lessons from Building a New AI Product - The Pragmatic Summit](sources/pragmatic-engineer-ramp-lessons-new-ai-product.md): LLM proxy with per-team cost tracing and config-only model swaps (competitive-teardown-ramp-glass)
- [Introducing Glass. Make your entire company smarter](sources/ramp-introducing-glass.md): budget blown in weeks; users default to frontier models (competitive-teardown-ramp-glass)
- [How to get your company AI pilled](sources/x-geoffintech-ai-pilled-article.md): the opposite stance in April: "Kill token limits and access restrictions", "treat AI usage as an infinite learning budget"; metering came later with Router/Glass (competitive-teardown-ramp-glass)
- [Ramp Router launch posts (Jul 20, 2026)](sources/x-ramp-router-launch-posts.md): the 30% bill cut is a Router claim from July 2026, 'without any performance degradation' (Zaks); no published data (competitive-teardown-ramp-glass)
- [Ramp built an AI agent harness in six weeks](sources/thenewstack-ramp-laminar-agent-harness.md): independent data point on in-harness routing, LangChain Open SWE -64% median cost/thread, no significant quality change (competitive-teardown-ramp-glass)
- [Building Laminar: Ramp's Managed Agents Platform](sources/ramp-builders-building-laminar.md): Ramp Router sits in the harness as the LLM gateway; model choice per cost/latency/performance (competitive-teardown-ramp-glass)
- [Building an agentic harness that outlasts the model](sources/shopify-engineering-agentic-harness-outlasts-model.md): full scan $50–300, diff scan $5–50; partitions sized to 20–30% of the context window (competitive-teardown-shopify-river)
- [Small Models, Massive Wins (Beyond the Pilot)](sources/venturebeat-beyond-the-pilot-farhan-thawar.md): no token limits but "circuit breakers"; token leaderboard replaced by a usage dashboard where anyone sees their own spend (competitive-teardown-shopify-river)
- [How Shopify built an AI stack that doesn't care which models survive](sources/venturebeat-shopify-ai-stack-model-agnostic.md): the proxy auto-moved users to Opus or GPT 5.5 when "Claude Fable 5 shut down" (competitive-teardown-shopify-river)
- [From Memo to Movement](sources/firstround-shopify-ai-culture.md): in 2025 a token-spend leaderboard was "a cool proxy for value"; by 2026 it was removed (competitive-teardown-shopify-river)
- [Build your own company brain (How I AI, Krishnamurthy)](sources/howiai-stripe-kai-krishnamurthy.md): Kai projects set the default model and can block expensive models for a workflow (competitive-teardown-stripe-knowledge-agents)
- [Production-grade AI agents for financial compliance: Lessons from Stripe](sources/aws-stripe-compliance-agents.md): all LLM calls go through an LLM Proxy (noisy-neighbour limits, fallbacks, usage tracking by privacy class); prompt caching cut cost 60% (competitive-teardown-stripe-knowledge-agents)
- [Use Claude Code in the cloud (Claude Code on the web docs)](sources/anthropic-claude-code-cloud-sessions.md): no separate VM charge; cloud sessions share the account's rate limits, so parallel tasks consume limits proportionately (Limitations) (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Automate work with scheduled tasks (Claude Code routines docs)](sources/anthropic-claude-code-scheduled-tasks.md): hourly caps (100 scheduled runs/hr per account, 30/hr per task for run-now and API fires) and subscription usage draw-down, no overage by default (Usage and limits) (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [The $47K agent loop: why logging, monitoring and max_tokens all failed to stop it](sources/devto-47k-agent-loop.md): claims four LangChain agents on A2A looped (Verifier requesting, Analyzer producing) with no termination condition or budget cap; 'They had logging. They had monitoring. They did not have a hard limit.' (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Durable Execution for AI Agents: LangGraph, DBOS, Inngest and Temporal Compared](sources/hackernoon-durable-execution-compared.md): payloads must stay in network rules out Inngest unless self-hosted (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [How Ramp built a full-context background coding agent on Modal](sources/modal-ramp-inspect-background-agent.md): sessions start in seconds from a filesystem snapshot refreshed by a cron every 30 minutes (repos cloned, dependencies installed, build run); startup speed framed as the adoption driver (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Oz Cloud Agents & Orchestration (Warp docs)](sources/warp-oz-cloud-agents.md): runs incur platform plus compute plus inference charges; personal BYOK not supported for cloud runs; team-managed inference on Business/Enterprise (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Ramp Inspect Architecture 2026: How Background Coding Agents Scale Safely](sources/wavect-ramp-inspect-architecture.md): measure accepted changes per unit of review effort and incident risk, not PRs per day; review capacity and CI become the bottleneck (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Hosting the Agent SDK](sources/anthropic-agent-sdk-hosting.md): first-party: token cost dominates container cost by an order of magnitude; per-session cost tracking available (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Harness design for long-running application development](sources/anthropic-harness-design-long-running-apps.md): first-party: 20x cost for the full harness on one task (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Context Engineering for AI Agents: Lessons from Building Manus](sources/manus-context-engineering-lessons.md): first-party: KV-cache hit rate is the key production metric (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)

- [Omnigent contextual policies](sources/databricks-omnigent-contextual-policies.md): soft/hard session cost caps that force a cheaper model; per-user daily caps (vendor claim) (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)

- [Chesky says OpenAI tools not ready for ChatGPT tie-up with Airbnb app](sources/fortune-chesky-openai-not-ready-qwen.md): support agent on 13 models, relying heavily on Qwen as "fast and cheap" (research-airbnb-spotify-product-practices)
- [Airbnb Q2 2025 earnings call and shareholder letter](sources/airbnb-earnings-q2-2025.md): one custom agent on 13 models tuned on tens of thousands of conversations (research-airbnb-spotify-product-practices)
- [Airbnb (ABNB) Q2 2026 earnings call transcript and shareholder letter](sources/airbnb-earnings-q2-2026.md): inference cost "de minimis" against booking value; CFO guides to a material rise in AI spend while margins grow (research-airbnb-spotify-product-practices)
- [Spotify Q3 2026 Earnings Call](sources/spotify-q3-2026-earnings-call.md): routes work between models, including open-source, and invests in cost controls (research-airbnb-spotify-product-practices)
