## decision-rationale-records: Decision rationale records
Artifacts that keep the "why" behind a commitment (bet briefs, opportunity trees, RFCs and ADRs) so context survives reorgs and handoffs.
- [Spotify Rhythm: How we create focus](sources/kniberg-spotify-rhythm.md): each bet needs a 2-page brief with DIBB, sponsor, road manager, stakeholders, success metrics and related bets (slide 14) (research-airbnb-spotify-product-practices)
- [When Should I Write an Architecture Decision Record](sources/spotify-engineering-when-to-write-adr.md): RFC, then ADR; ADRs keep context through ownership handovers after reorgs; "a handful of teams" used them in 2020 (research-airbnb-spotify-product-practices)
- [From Gut to Plan: The Thoughtful Execution Framework](sources/spotify-design-thoughtful-execution-framework.md): the only mandatory step is to "document their Thoughtful Execution tree", used to say "what … and why" (research-airbnb-spotify-product-practices)
- [How Spotify Thinks (Invest Like the Best EP.424)](sources/colossus-ilb-gustav-soderstrom-how-spotify-thinks.md): weekly 3-hour E-Team; nobody blocked more than ~2.5 days; VPs must explain details themselves (~23:20) (research-airbnb-spotify-product-practices)
- [OSCAL: the Open Security Controls Assessment Language (layers and models)](sources/nist-oscal-layers-and-models.md): Assessment Results and POA&M record findings and remediation commitments as data. (first-party; research-dependency-agent)
- [Model Context Protocol Server (SailPoint Identity Security Cloud)](sources/sailpoint-docs-mcp-server.md): audit comments "Requested by AI on behalf of <identity>"; cancellations recorded likewise; searchable. (first-party; research-dependency-agent)
- [Accelerating your DevOps change process (DevOps Change Velocity)](sources/servicenow-docs-devops-change-velocity-approval.md): the change links commits, work items, artifact versions, test, quality and security summaries; up to 5 KB of task execution log per step goes to work notes. (first-party; research-dependency-agent)
- [Documenting Architecture Decisions](sources/nygard-documenting-architecture-decisions.md): original ADR format and supersede-never-edit rule (research-skill-rigidity-spectrum)
- [Design Docs at Google](sources/industrialempathy-design-docs-at-google.md): "alternatives considered" called one of the most important sections (research-skill-rigidity-spectrum)
- [Stale docs are prompt injection you wrote yourself](sources/codeminer42-stale-docs-prompt-injection.md): index generated from frontmatter, leaves out superseded records; CI warns above 800 words (research-skill-rigidity-spectrum)

## decision-rights-for-agents: Decision-rights schemes applied to agents
RAPID, DACI and risk-owner schemes place agents as recommenders, inputs or performers, with a named human as decider.
- [Open Data Contract Standard (ODCS)](sources/bitol-odcs-open-data-contract-standard.md): Roles section: `role` (IAM role giving access), `access` (read/write), `firstLevelApprovers`, `secondLevelApprovers`, `description` (Roles page). (first-party; research-dependency-agent)
- [Building the future of finance in the age of AI](sources/fca-rusu-building-future-finance-age-ai.md): firms need "clear accountability, risk-based controls, human oversight, escalation triggers", with senior managers personally accountable. (first-party; research-dependency-agent)
- [About code owners](sources/github-docs-about-code-owners.md): owners are auto-requested on PRs; with the branch-protection or ruleset requirement, approval from any one listed owner satisfies the gate (Requiring review). (first-party; research-dependency-agent)
- [OAuth 2.0 Extension: On-Behalf-Of User Authorization for AI Agents (draft-oauth-ai-agents-on-behalf-of-user-02)](sources/ietf-draft-oauth-ai-agents-on-behalf-of-user.md): a resource server can trigger the flow with 401/403 and `WWW-Authenticate`, prompting fresh consent for the agent. (first-party; research-dependency-agent)
- [Accelerating the Adoption of Software and AI Agent Identity and Authorization (NCCoE concept paper)](sources/nist-nccoe-agent-identity-authorization-concept-paper.md): the framing is agents acting autonomously "on data and tools", requiring identification and authorisation controls to manage access risk. (first-party; research-dependency-agent)
- [Understanding Cross App Access with Okta for AI Agents](sources/okta-support-cross-app-access-ai-agents.md): "Okta moves complex Open Authorization (OAuth) consent flows away from end users and into the Admin Console"; admins define which apps can access which. (first-party; research-dependency-agent)
- [Set self-service actions RBAC (Port)](sources/port-docs-self-service-action-rbac.md): access can be granted to the entity's owners based on its Team property, linking decision rights to catalog ownership. (first-party; research-dependency-agent)
- [Change Success Score (Gamification)](sources/servicenow-community-change-success-score.md): implemented as a Flow Designer action ("Check Change Success Score") in approval flows, i.e. a policy hook, not a model decision. (first-party; research-dependency-agent)
- [RAPID Decision Making](sources/bain-rapid-decision-making.md): one decider, one recommender; Agree is not a veto; no evidence offered (research-skill-rigidity-spectrum)
- [The Four Big Risks](sources/svpg-four-big-risks.md): each risk has a named human owner, which gives a risk register its owner column (research-skill-rigidity-spectrum)
- [Why Do Multi-Agent LLM Systems Fail?](sources/arxiv-why-multi-agent-llm-systems-fail.md): clearer role specs (including the CEO agent's final say) gave +9.4% task success in ChatDev (research-skill-rigidity-spectrum)
- [Claude Code permission modes](sources/anthropic-claude-code-permission-modes-docs.md): six modes; auto mode substitutes a classifier for the human; deny rules bind in every mode; admins lock modes via managed settings; auto is now the interactive default (research-skill-rigidity-spectrum)
- [VS Code agent approvals](sources/vscode-copilot-agent-approvals-and-permissions.md): Manual, LLM-judge Assisted, Allow all; approvals scoped to use, session, workspace or global; sandbox independent of level (research-skill-rigidity-spectrum)
- [People + AI Guidebook: User Needs](sources/pair-guidebook-user-needs-automate-vs-augment.md): automate what people want to delegate, augment what they want to keep; preview, edit, undo even when automating (research-skill-rigidity-spectrum)
- [When combinations of humans and AI are useful](sources/arxiv-vaccaro-when-human-ai-combinations-are-useful.md): give the decision to whichever party is better alone; blend only on creation tasks (research-skill-rigidity-spectrum)
- [The bar raiser program](sources/metaview-bar-raiser-program.md): the reviewer's authority comes from not owning the deadline; objections and overrides are recorded (research-skill-rigidity-spectrum)

## dependency-detection-automation: Automatic dependency detection: what research and vendors can do
Accuracy of link-type prediction in issue trackers, requirement-dependency extraction with language models, and what shipped planning agents actually do with dependencies (read declared ones, alert, propose re-plans).
- [A Taxonomy of Dependencies in Agile Software Development](sources/aisel-strode-huff-dependency-taxonomy-agile.md): the taxonomy is a classification target an agent could label asks against; the paper itself is qualitative. (independent; research-dependency-agent)
- [Automating the Detection of Requirement Dependencies Using Large Language Models](sources/arxiv-darif-leredd-requirement-dependencies.md): zero-shot GPT-5.4 overall F1 0.78, but only 0.29 average F1 on specific dependency types; LEREDD with six retrieved examples per type reaches Requires F1 0.86 in the pilot, about 86% F1 and 87% accuracy overall, with only a 2.27% drop when moved to a new system (RQ1-RQ5). (independent; research-dependency-agent)
- [Automated Detection of Typed Links in Issue Trackers](sources/arxiv-luders-automated-detection-typed-links.md): BERT on linked-issue text, 15 public Jira repositories, average macro F1 0.64 across 9 popular link types (weighted F1 0.73); Subtask 0.89, Epic 0.97 (abstract). (independent; research-dependency-agent)
- [Beyond Duplicates: Towards Understanding and Predicting Link Types in Issue Tracking Systems](sources/arxiv-luders-beyond-duplicates-link-types.md): two state-of-the-art duplicate detectors confused Duplication with other link types in nearly all repositories; accuracy dropped about 6% and 12%; adding other link types to training partly mitigated it (abstract). (independent; research-dependency-agent)
- [In Search of Socio-Technical Congruence: A Large-Scale Longitudinal Study](sources/arxiv-mauerer-socio-technical-congruence.md): STC computes coordination requirements from task assignments and file/logical dependencies; this study's motif-based variant (STMC) counts how often developers working on the same or related files need to communicate. (independent; research-dependency-agent)
- [Asana AI Teammates: Powerful Agents Ready to Work with Your Team](sources/asana-ai-teammates-overview-launch-planner.md): "maps the entire multi-departmental ecosystem"; addresses launches that "miss deadlines or fail due to invisible dependencies". (vendor-claim; research-dependency-agent)
- [Behind the build: A hands-on AI Teammates walkthrough from Asana's CPO](sources/asana-forum-cpo-ai-teammates-walkthrough.md): reasoning across the Work Graph, "connecting signals across projects, meeting notes, and team capacity". (vendor-claim; research-dependency-agent)
- [Dependency and Risk Mapper (AI agent template)](sources/monday-dependency-and-risk-mapper-agent.md): "Reads items, dependencies, owners, dates, and status from the board"; "Trace the critical path and find blocked chains"; no statement that it infers undeclared links. (first-party; research-dependency-agent)
- [Planview Reinvents How Enterprises Make Critical Decisions with Connected Work Graph: AI-Powered Dependency Intelligence](sources/planview-connected-work-graph-launch.md): "surfacing critical path risks and bottlenecks before they impact delivery"; the release implies inference ("analyze work patterns to uncover blockers") without saying how. (vendor-claim; research-dependency-agent)
- [Explain the risk of a change request by using Now Assist for IT Service Management (ITSM)](sources/servicenow-docs-explain-change-risk.md): "similar change requests and the incidents they caused" is a historical change-to-incident link the explanation surfaces. (first-party; research-dependency-agent)
- [Now Assist for Strategic Portfolio Management (SPM) release notes](sources/servicenow-docs-now-assist-spm-release-notes.md): Project Insights v9.4.0 (May 2026) added "dependency issues, and critical path changes"; Project Q&A "now supports questions about work notes and dependencies"; the notes describe no standalone dependency analysis skill. (first-party; research-dependency-agent)

## dependency-knowledge-carriers: The people who carry dependency knowledge
Technical programme managers, programme managers, architects, platform product managers, release and change managers and 'the person who knows' hold most dependency knowledge, and their time is the scarce resource an agent competes for or relieves. Related: [[tacit-knowledge-capture]].
- [Dependency Management in Large-Scale Agile: A Case Study of DevOps Teams](sources/aisel-stray-moe-aasheim-dependency-management-devops-teams.md): supporting teams (two in the study) are part of the dependency web DevOps teams rely on. (independent; research-dependency-agent)
- [Sr. Technical Program Manager (Ring, Blink, & Amazon Key)](sources/amazon-jobs-sr-tpm-ring-blink-key.md): "plan for dependencies, budget for and secure resources to ensure the meeting of agreed upon deliverables and timelines"; "anticipating bottlenecks, providing escalation management and communicating status broadly across all levels" (description). (first-party; research-dependency-agent)
- [Coordinating Knowledge Work in Multi-Team Programs: Findings from a Large-Scale Agile Development Program](sources/arxiv-dingsoyr-coordinating-multi-team-programs.md): the matrix gave each feature team a technical architect (50% design, 50% development) and a functional architect who also served the architecture and business projects (Table 2, §Case); "management by walking around" and project managers who said "this problem I know was addressed by another team two iterations ago, let us get Ola over here" (§Results, Individual mode). (independent; research-dependency-agent)
- [Atlassian research: AI adoption is rising, but friction persists (State of Developer Experience 2025)](sources/atlassian-state-of-devex-2025.md): the top-ranked time-waster is finding information about services, docs and APIs (blog body). (vendor-claim; research-dependency-agent)
- [How JPMorgan Chase built a data mesh architecture to drive significant value to enhance their enterprise data platform](sources/aws-jpmc-data-mesh-enterprise-data-platform.md): before the mesh, data exchanges were system-to-system or via queues with no central, automated record of flows, so owners could not see where their data went. (first-party; research-dependency-agent)
- [Nine things a (technical) program manager does](sources/balter-nine-things-technical-program-manager.md): the TPM is "the 'catch all' for any problem, task, or deliverable that doesn't have another logical owner", including tedious manual spreadsheet updates and repackaged status reports (item 9). (anecdote; research-dependency-agent)
- [Coordination Breakdowns and Their Impact on Development Productivity and Software Failures](sources/cataldo-herbsleb-coordination-breakdowns.md): "the gaps between coordination requirements and the actual coordination activities carried out by the developers significantly increased software failures" (Abstract). (independent; research-dependency-agent)
- [Final Report on EBA Guidelines on outsourcing arrangements (EBA/GL/2019/02)](sources/eba-guidelines-outsourcing-arrangements.md): para 52: "maintain an updated register of information on all outsourcing arrangements"; para 54-55 list minimum fields, adding for critical functions items such as alternative providers, whether the function is time-critical, and "the estimated annual budget cost" (Section 11, pp. 36-38). (first-party; research-dependency-agent)
- [DORA Dry Run exercise: summary report (ESA 2024 35)](sources/esas-dora-dry-run-register-of-information.md): "The most frequent failed data quality check was related to missing mandatory information (86% of all data errors). Another frequent failed check was related to the use of unique identifiers for the financial entities and ICT third-party service providers" (p. 4). (first-party; research-dependency-agent)
- [Regulation (EU) 2022/2554 on digital operational resilience for the financial sector (DORA)](sources/eu-dora-regulation-ict-risk-third-party.md): Art. 8(1): firms must "identify, classify and adequately document all ICT supported business functions", with their roles and responsibilities, the information and ICT assets supporting them and how those relate to ICT risk, reviewing the classification "at least yearly" (paraphrase plus short excerpts); Art. 8(4): firms "shall map the configuration of the information assets and ICT assets" and "the links and inte... (first-party; research-dependency-agent)
- [Implementing technology change](sources/fca-implementing-technology-change.md): / coordination-cost-and-waiting: the most consistent risk factor was when "a project is dependent on other projects delivering their objectives", requiring tight coordination and changes completed in tandem; projects on new technology, changing legacy systems, or relying heavily on third parties were also high risk; being classed "major" was a less consistent factor (Findings: high-risk projects). (first-party; research-dependency-agent)
- [Interagency Guidance on Third-Party Relationships: Risk Management](sources/fed-fdic-occ-third-party-risk-guidance-2023.md): expected documentation includes "A current inventory of all third-party relationships (and, as appropriate to the risk presented, related subcontractors) that clearly identifies those relationships associated with higher-risk activities, including critical activities", and board reporting on "dependency on a single provider for multiple activities" (Section D.3). (first-party; research-dependency-agent)
- [Supervisory Guidance on Model Risk Management (SR 11-7, attachment)](sources/federalreserve-sr-11-7-model-risk-guidance.md): / stale-records-mislead-agents: banks "should maintain a comprehensive set of information for models implemented for use, under development for implementation, or recently retired"; a specific party should maintain "a firm-wide inventory of all models"; the inventory should list "the type and source of inputs used by a given model and underlying components" (Model Inventory, p. 20). (first-party; research-dependency-agent)
- [Consumer-Driven Contracts: A Service Evolution Pattern](sources/fowler-robinson-consumer-driven-contracts.md): without them the provider "cannot see how consumers actually use its contract"; with them providers can deprecate elements while targeting specific consumers. (anecdote; research-dependency-agent)
- [Splitting the Organization and Integrating the Code: Conway's Law Revisited](sources/herbsleb-grinter-conways-law-revisited.md): architects "were known to have a very broad knowledge of the system and who was doing what" and became the routing service; returning visitors became "contact people" or "liaisons" (section 4.2.2). (independent; research-dependency-agent)
- [An Empirical Study of Speed and Communication in Globally Distributed Software Development](sources/herbsleb-mockus-speed-communication-distributed-development.md): survey results on distributed social networks: less awareness of who is doing what at the other site, linked to delay (Survey sections). (independent; research-dependency-agent)
- [The IIA's Three Lines Model: An update of the Three Lines of Defense](sources/iia-three-lines-model-2020.md): "There is a need for collaboration and communication across both the first and second line roles" (Relationships between roles). (first-party; research-dependency-agent)
- [Challenges and success factors for large-scale agile transformations: A systematic literature review](sources/jss-dikert-large-scale-agile-transformations.md): "even allowing teams to have different Sprint durations created delays in delivery" (4.2.4); groups that had committed to long-term plans had to adjust to incremental delivery (4.2.9). (independent; research-dependency-agent)
- [Coordination & Integration (LeSS framework)](sources/less-coordination-and-integration.md): a component mentor is "a teacher and steward of the component, not a gate" and "doesn't review code for approval before it's committed". (independent; research-dependency-agent)
- [SS1/23 – Model risk management principles for banks](sources/pra-ss1-23-model-risk-management-principles.md): Principle 1.2: "A comprehensive model inventory should be maintained to enable firms to: identify the sources of model risk; provide the management information needed for reporting model risk; and help to identify model inter-dependencies"; firms "should maintain a firm-wide model inventory which would help to identify all direct and indirect model inter-dependencies" (p. 11). (first-party; research-dependency-agent)
- [The Scrum@Scale Guide](sources/scrumatscale-guide-scrum-of-scrums.md): the Scrum of Scrums Master pays particular attention to cross-team dependencies and facilitates their removal (§Scrum of Scrums Master). (independent; research-dependency-agent)
- [How We Use Golden Paths to Solve Fragmentation in Our Software Ecosystem](sources/spotify-engineering-golden-paths.md): content ownership is spread across many teams, which created coordination gaps the team was still addressing. (first-party; research-dependency-agent)
- [2024 Stack Overflow Developer Survey: Professional Developers](sources/stackoverflow-dev-survey-2024-professional-developers.md): time spent answering questions per day is higher for people managers: 70.6% of managers spend over 30 minutes (chart values; the text says 61%) versus 43.6% of individual contributors (§6.1, time spent answering). (independent; research-dependency-agent)
- [Lloyds Bank reviews tech and engineering personnel in reorg](sources/theregister-lloyds-tech-engineering-reorg.md): support roles rationalised; business analysts eliminated or moved to Customer Journey Manager roles; some roles keep titles but get new definitions (body). (independent; research-dependency-agent)
- [How a Typical Day of Program Manager Looks Like](sources/zalando-pmo-typical-day-program-manager.md): hours 6-7 are for resolving cross-team dependencies and unblocking: "Primary thing is to get alignment (Persuasion skills will be used here)", then scheduling, then tracking, because one team's delay hits connected work. (anecdote; research-dependency-agent)

## dependency-types-and-practices: What a dependency is and how large organisations manage dependencies today
The kinds of dependency product and programme work carries (team, system, data, process and governance gate, approval, vendor, funding, people, sequencing, knowledge) and the practices, tools and records used to manage them without agents. It matters because a dependency agent inherits these practices and their records.
- [A Taxonomy of Dependencies in Agile Software Development](sources/aisel-strode-huff-dependency-taxonomy-agile.md): three top-level categories, task, resource and knowledge (abstract); offered to practitioners "as a prompt to identify hindering dependencies early" (abstract). (independent; research-dependency-agent)
- [The difficulties of cascading OKRs](sources/allankelly-difficulties-cascading-okrs.md): cascading ties objectives together; if a middle-management objective needs three teams' deliveries, one team's miss sinks the objective; "the OKRs become fragile and a dependency nightmare" (body). (anecdote; research-dependency-agent)
- [Sr. Technical Program Manager (Ring, Blink, & Amazon Key)](sources/amazon-jobs-sr-tpm-ring-blink-key.md): "Create mechanisms to drive timely, accurate, and comprehensive project execution"; "define processes that improve teamwork, communication, collaboration, and commitment across multiple disparate groups"; required experience "building processes and coordinating release schedules" (description and qualifications). (first-party; research-dependency-agent)
- [Coordinating Knowledge Work in Multi-Team Programs: Findings from a Large-Scale Agile Development Program](sources/arxiv-dingsoyr-coordinating-multi-team-programs.md): uses Malone and Crowston's definition of coordination as "management of interdependencies between activities" and Van de Ven's three modes (impersonal, personal individual, personal group) (§Background, Table 1); finds 19 mechanisms across those modes (Table 3). (independent; research-dependency-agent)
- [Beyond Duplicates: Towards Understanding and Predicting Link Types in Issue Tracking Systems](sources/arxiv-luders-beyond-duplicates-link-types.md): 75 link types grouped into General Relation, Duplication, Composition, Temporal/Causal and Workflow (abstract); dependency-like links sit in Temporal/Causal. (independent; research-dependency-agent)
- [Challenges of Adopting SAFe in the Banking Industry – A Study Two Years after its Introduction](sources/arxiv-tengstrand-safe-banking-challenges.md): system dependencies are named as a distinct challenge category: "F2. Complexity and interdependencies between legacy systems are hard to deal with" (Table 1, §5); "Dependencies between systems and having many systems are all impediments for the SAFe transformation" (§5, Systems architecture). (independent; research-dependency-agent)
- [Identifying Critical Dependencies in Large-Scale Continuous Software Engineering](sources/arxiv-tkalich-critical-dependencies-cse.md): preliminary findings name dependencies between software teams and support functions, and between teams and external entities, as the main sources of delays and bottlenecks (abstract). (independent; research-dependency-agent)
- [Define dependencies between work with plans in Jira](sources/atlassian-jira-plans-dependencies-lesson.md): dependencies are directional ("The dependent work item must be scheduled later than the required work item"); link types depend on site configuration (blocks / is blocked by; causes / is caused by; depends on / is depended on by) (lesson body). (vendor-claim; research-dependency-agent)
- [Descriptor Format of Catalog Entities (Backstage)](sources/backstage-descriptor-format.md): the descriptor carries declared dependency edges (`spec.dependsOn`, `providesApis`, `consumesApis` on components), so system-to-system dependencies are only as current as the YAML their owners maintain. (first-party; research-dependency-agent)
- [System Model (Backstage Software Catalog)](sources/backstage-system-model.md): "APIs are the boundaries between different components"; components "implement APIs for other components to consume", "consume APIs implemented by other components", and may "directly depend on components or resources that are attached to it at runtime" (§Core entities). (first-party; research-dependency-agent)
- [Nine things a (technical) program manager does](sources/balter-nine-things-technical-program-manager.md): item 2, "capture and track the work": scope, timing, ordering, owners and external dependencies, then tracking each workstream and deliverable's status; plan and reality must stay in sync. Item 3 reframes the work as "risks and mitigations" rather than problems and solutions. (anecdote; research-dependency-agent)
- [How to manage dependencies with Jira Align](sources/eficode-manage-dependencies-jira-align.md): "One team will send a dependency to another team inclusive of ask date (date, sprint or PI), description and other metadata"; the receiver can accept ownership, propose new due dates, link it to a feature, capability or epic, and comment (body). (vendor-claim; research-dependency-agent)
- [Accounting Versus Physics – Rewiring Organizations for Improvement](sources/itrevolution-prugh-accounting-versus-physics.md): the remedies are structural: modularise along business domains, move to platform teams, embed capabilities in cross-functional product teams, deliver incrementally, maximise cohesion (body). (anecdote; research-dependency-agent)
- [Spotify's Failed #SquadGoals](sources/jeremiahlee-failed-squad-goals.md): "Every responsibility a team cedes to increase its focus becomes a new cross-team dependency"; with no common cross-team process, disputes needed three or more engineering managers then a director to resolve. (independent; research-dependency-agent)
- [Coordination & Integration (LeSS framework)](sources/less-coordination-and-integration.md): seven practices: Just Talk ("You do not need a formal, official, usually slow coordination mechanism in order to coordinate"), Communicate in Code (shared mainline, no branches), Scouts (a member monitors another team or interface for a Sprint), component communities and mentors, multi-team meetings, Travelers (scarce experts rotate), Leading Team (one feature team leads a large feature). (independent; research-dependency-agent)
- [3.10 – RAID Log (Overview & Template Guide)](sources/lga-raid-log-guidance-sds.md): taxonomy (§4): "Risk (uncertain future event), Assumption (believed condition), Issue (happening now), Dependency (external reliance)"; cross-authority engagement, MoUs, evidence commissioning and data sharing are each named as sources of dependencies (§2). (first-party; research-dependency-agent)
- [Track dependencies in Delivery Plans - Azure Boards](sources/microsoft-azure-devops-track-dependencies-delivery-plans.md): tracking supports only the Predecessor/Successor link type; "Dependency conflicts occur when a successor work item is scheduled to complete before its predecessor" (§Resolve dependency conflicts). (vendor-claim; research-dependency-agent)
- [All-in-One PI Planning Template](sources/miro-humana-coach-all-in-one-pi-planning-template.md): Solution Board "manages cross-ART dependencies" with a swimlane per ART listing capabilities and dependencies; Program Board shows team-level features and dependencies, where teams "add their features and dependencies and link to each other" (template description). (anecdote; research-dependency-agent)
- [Framework to review programmes (Update April 2021)](sources/nao-framework-to-review-programmes.md): Key audit question 2, "Portfolio management and dependencies", asks: "Is it clear how programmes within the portfolio interact with each other, and that these interdependencies are recognised and managed?" and "Is there an effective strategy in place to manage interdependencies between different policies, teams and organisations?" (Question 2 sub-questions, p.8 of 36). (independent; research-dependency-agent)
- [SAP LeanIX Application Portfolio Management](sources/sap-leanix-application-portfolio-management.md): APM maps "how applications, interfaces, and IT components connect across your IT landscape" (product page). Search summaries of LeanIX docs describe interfaces as fact sheets that "transfer Data Objects and are implemented via IT Components", with provided and consumed interfaces showing data flows and dependencies (secondary, not read in the docs). (vendor-claim; research-dependency-agent)
- [SAFe® Program Dependency Board Retrospective – PI Planning and Execution](sources/scaledagile-yeret-program-dependency-board-retrospective.md): the program board (also "program dependency board") is "a key artifact used in PI Planning and execution"; red yarn marks dependencies between features and teams (opening). (anecdote; research-dependency-agent)
- [The Scrum@Scale Guide](sources/scrumatscale-guide-scrum-of-scrums.md): the Scaled Daily Scrum asks whether "new dependencies between the teams or a way to resolve an existing dependency [has] been discovered?"; cross-team coordination aims to "mitigate cross-team dependencies to ensure they do not become impediments" (§Scrum of Scrums). (independent; research-dependency-agent)
- [Soon time for one of Europe's largest PI planning events](sources/sebgroup-europes-largest-pi-planning.md): PI planning is "a way of jointly synchronising product planning between business, IT and support functions", producing "a handshake and a realistic plan" (quotes from the domain lead and the head of the Lean Agile Center of Excellence). (first-party; research-dependency-agent)
- [CMDB Health KPIs and metrics](sources/servicenow-cmdb-health-kpis-metrics.md): the CMDB records system dependencies as typed parent-child relationships; health metrics flag duplicate relationships and orphan relationships "missing either a parent CI, a child CI, or both" (§Relationships). (vendor-claim; research-dependency-agent)
- [Add details to demands (Demand Management)](sources/servicenow-demand-management-add-details.md): demand managers work with business relationship managers to identify stakeholders and gather requirements and risks, link requirements to project tasks and track them; demands link to RIDAC records (risks, issues, decisions, actions, change requests). (vendor-claim; research-dependency-agent)
- [A taxonomy of inter-team coordination mechanisms in large-scale agile](sources/sintef-berntzen-inter-team-coordination-taxonomy.md): 27 mechanisms in three categories: coordination meetings (communities of practice, inter-team stand-ups, retrospectives), coordination roles (program architects, the platform team), coordination tools and artefacts (Slack, JIRA, inter-team task boards, backlogs, roadmaps). (independent; research-dependency-agent)
- [Key Concepts (Team Topologies)](sources/teamtopologies-key-concepts.md): three interaction modes, collaboration (time-boxed discovery), X-as-a-Service, facilitation; relationships "WILL change as new goals are set", so any team-interaction map is a snapshot in time. (independent; research-dependency-agent)
- [Your service catalog is already wrong](sources/thereliabilityengineering-service-catalog-already-wrong.md): proposes dependencies from the observed call graph, ownership from deploy history and contributor activity, readiness from SLOs, alerts and incidents, blast radius from live topology. (anecdote; research-dependency-agent)
- [Coordination Challenges in Large-Scale Software Development: A Case Study of Planning Misalignment in Hybrid Settings](sources/tse-bick-planning-misalignment-dependency-awareness.md): the key explanation of ineffective coordination is "a lack of dependency awareness across development teams" (abstract). (independent; research-dependency-agent)

## dependency-value-evidence: What good dependency management is worth: the evidence and its labels
Figures on the payoff of flow, self-service onboarding, portals and catalogues, each with who measured it and how; mostly first-party or vendor, with the independent evidence on the cost side.
- [Black Swan Farming using Cost of Delay](sources/blackswanfarming-maersk-cost-of-delay.md): cost of delay for the example feature about $210,000 per week, so roughly $8 million over 38 weeks of waiting; the top 25% of requirements were worth about 1,000 times the bottom 25% (power-law distribution). (vendor-claim; research-dependency-agent)
- [Infosys insurance customer case study (Backstage developer portal)](sources/cncf-infosys-insurance-backstage.md): "Deployment frequency (DF) increased by 35%"; "Time from code commit to production is faster by 20%"; "products got to market faster by 25-30%" (Impact). (vendor-claim; research-dependency-agent)
- [Two data-backed ways to resolve incidents faster](sources/firehydrant-two-ways-resolve-incidents-faster.md): incidents with services attached showed a "36% decrease in MTTR" across severities versus incidents without (Incident Benchmark Report summary). (vendor-claim; research-dependency-agent)
- [Why Your IT Project May Be Riskier Than You Think](sources/flyvbjerg-budzier-it-project-riskier.md): smart managers "break big projects down into ones of limited size, complexity, and duration" (Avoiding Black Swans). The Emirates NBD core-banking replacement, doubled in size by a merger and launched "big bang" across branches, ATMs, online and call centres, finished 7% late and 18% over budget; steps included resisting scope change and "Broke the project into discrete modules" (inset). (independent; research-dependency-agent)
- [The SPACE of Developer Productivity: There's more to it than you think](sources/forsgren-space-of-developer-productivity.md): the Communication and collaboration dimension lists "discoverability of documentation and expertise", "how quickly work is integrated", network metrics and "onboarding time for and experience of new members" (Communication and collaboration section). (independent; research-dependency-agent)
- [Episode 3: The Quest for Accelerated Delivery (DevOps Enterprise Summit 2016)](sources/itrevolution-nationwide-does16-accelerated-delivery.md): speed to market "months to hours" for Java applications; large app releases down 80%; presentation-tier deploys up to 150 a month (results slide). (first-party; research-dependency-agent)
- [Entangled: Solving the Hairy Problem of Team Dependencies](sources/magennis-entangled-team-dependencies.md): "1 in 2n" (2 to the n) chance all dependencies are on time; "7 dependencies: 1 chance in 128" (slides 28-29); take-away: "Every dependency removed double your chance of on-time delivery" (slide 61). (anecdote; research-dependency-agent)
- [Delivering large-scale IT projects on time, on budget, and on value](sources/mckinsey-delivering-large-scale-it-projects.md): a bank's transformation where "its finance department became involved only a few months before the system was due to go live", leading to changes that "delayed the launch by more than three months, at a cost of more than $8 million" (Managing strategy and stakeholders). (vendor-claim; research-dependency-agent)
- [Developer Velocity: How software excellence fuels business performance](sources/mckinsey-developer-velocity.md): top-quartile Developer Velocity Index scores "correlate with 2014-18 revenue growth that is four to five times faster than bottom-quartile"; 60% higher total shareholder returns; 20% higher operating margins (What really does account for business success). Correlation, self-rated. (vendor-claim; research-dependency-agent)
- [ING's agile transformation](sources/mckinsey-ing-agile-transformation.md): in the QBR "each tribe writes down what it achieved ... and, in that context, which other tribe or squad it will need to link up with"; QBR documents are open to all tribes (Schlatmann). (first-party; research-dependency-agent)
- [Coordination in Large-Scale Software Development: Helpful and Unhelpful Behaviors](sources/microsoft-research-coordination-large-scale-development.md): "It is difficult to work with dependent teams because our commitments are not aligned": 60% agree; "I find it difficult to get a team I depend on to implement a change I require": 25% frequently or more (Table 2); "tool support for dependency management is currently limited" and no tool was used universally to communicate status (section 4.2). (independent; research-dependency-agent)
- [The challenges in implementing digital change](sources/nao-challenges-implementing-digital-change.md): "Failure to understand the complexity and dependencies associated with replacing legacy IT has undermined government's attempts to move away from legacy systems" (para 2.17); Figure 1 marks programmes by "Integration with legacy and other systems" and "Managing interdependencies" alongside their missed dates (e.g. e-Borders, 2011 target, cancelled). (independent; research-dependency-agent)
- [2023 Project to Product State of the Industry Report](sources/planview-project-to-product-state-of-industry-2023.md): "the second most important factor in achieving a product-oriented model is the approach to managing dependencies"; "When all internally consumed capabilities are available as self-service, organizations are more likely to operationalize a product model" (p. 17; five factors found by regression, p. 16). (vendor-claim; research-dependency-agent)
- [Why Dependencies Kill Your Deadlines](sources/quantify-why-dependencies-kill-deadlines.md): at 3 dependencies "the real number across organizations was closer to 50-80%" versus 12.5% predicted; 2 dependencies cost 5-15 points; 5 dependencies lose "roughly a third" of independent work's on-time chance; 10 dependencies: roughly half miss target; 30+: "single-digit on-time rates in some organizations" (body). (vendor-claim; research-dependency-agent)
- [How Spotify measures the value of Backstage](sources/spotify-backstage-measuring-backstage-roi.md): frequent users had "2.3x more developer activity in GitHub" over the following six months than the least-active users; over 2x more code changes; 17% less cycle time; deploy to production 2x as often; software stays deployed 3x as long; 5% more likely to still be at Spotify 12 months later (body). (first-party; research-dependency-agent)
- [How Backstage Made Our Developers More Effective — And How It Can Help Yours, Too](sources/spotify-engineering-backstage-made-developers-more-effective.md): positions a single catalog of services, owners and docs as the fix for discovery cost. (first-party; research-dependency-agent)

## deterministic-scaffold-model-nodes: Deterministic scaffold, model-judged nodes
Rigid and loose parts are combined by nesting: code fixes the sequence and hard checks while the model works inside bounded nodes, or the reverse, with code islands inside a model-chosen flow. It matters because a PM skill can fix the parts that must hold (required sections, sign-offs) without scripting the parts that need judgment.
- [Minions: Stripe's one-shot, end-to-end coding agents, Part 2](sources/stripe-minions-part-2.md): blueprints mix deterministic nodes (lint, push; "don't invoke an LLM at all") with agentic nodes ("Implement task", "Fix CI failures"); "putting LLMs into contained boxes" (research-skill-rigidity-spectrum)
- [Design topics as mini-agents (Copilot Studio)](sources/microsoft-copilot-studio-topics-as-mini-agents.md): "keep deterministic logic inside the topic and leave user communication to the orchestration layer" (research-skill-rigidity-spectrum)
- [Agent orchestration (OpenAI Agents SDK)](sources/openai-agents-sdk-multi-agent-orchestration.md): code patterns are route-on-structured-output, chain (research → outline → draft → critique → revise), evaluator loop, parallel (research-skill-rigidity-spectrum)
- [12-Factor Agents, factor 8](sources/humanlayer-12-factor-agents-own-your-control-flow.md): the model returns the next-step intent, a code switch decides whether to execute and loop or break for human approval (research-skill-rigidity-spectrum)
- [Writing effective tools for agents](sources/anthropic-writing-tools-for-agents.md): consolidate multi-step procedures into one tool (`schedule_event`); tools are "a contract between deterministic systems and non-deterministic agents" (research-skill-rigidity-spectrum)
- [Of course you can build dynamic AI agents with Temporal](sources/temporal-dynamic-ai-agents.md): orchestration deterministic, the plan and tool calls "completely non-deterministic"; the model's choices are replayed from history (research-skill-rigidity-spectrum)
- [Agent Development Kit (ADK) documentation](sources/google-adk-docs.md): workflow agents run sub-agents "without consulting an AI model"; ADK 2.0 graphs combine "AI reasoning with deterministic code logic" (research-skill-rigidity-spectrum)
- [Interrupts (LangGraph)](sources/langchain-langgraph-interrupts.md): the human gate is a code-placed `interrupt()` node over a durable checkpoint (research-skill-rigidity-spectrum)

## enterprise-admin-controls: Enterprise admin controls across harnesses
The identity, audit, policy, data-retention and cost controls a harness gives an org admin, and on which surfaces they are enforced. It is the baseline a regulated owner compares any build or layer against.
- [goose Extension Allowlist (docs)](sources/goose-docs-extension-allowlist.md): an env-var URL to a YAML list of allowed install commands, enforced on the client (research-block-product-practices)

(research-claude-resources-articles)

## evals-autonomy-trust: Evals, autonomy sliders and earned trust
Start agents as suggestions, measure against ground truth, then let users raise autonomy. Related: [[risk-sloped-review]].
- [Ramp: Lessons from Building a New AI Product - The Pragmatic Summit](sources/pragmatic-engineer-ramp-lessons-new-ai-product.md): Policy Agent suggestions -> auto-approve slider; weekly labeling; evals from five examples (competitive-teardown-ramp-glass)

- [How Anthropic enables self-service data analytics with Claude](sources/claude-anthropic-self-service-analytics.md): offline Q/A evals pinned to snapshot dates, results stored as telemetry (skill version, git SHA, model ID), per-domain launch gate at ~90%, ablation per PR (Validation). - [Lessons from Anthropic on building effective human-agent teams](sources/claude-building-effective-human-agent-teams.md): Lesson 4: autonomy granted "in proportion to demonstrated reliability", tracked per task type; Doer-Verifier pairs; rubrics and style guides as verifiers for non-code work. - [How Cresta turned CX expertise into an agent builder on the Claude Agent SDK](sources/claude-cresta-agent-builder-evals.md): build tasks (new agent, write a test case, change an existing agent, root-cause analysis) scored on outcome, execution path, quality vs curated reference, and resource use; rerun on each new Claude model or framework update... - [A Twilio PM on building a self-learning development platform with Claude Code](sources/claude-customers-twilio-pm-platform.md): day one had approval gates after each phase (six interruptions per feature); headless by day 45 after 23 design decisions; stall/oscillation/idle detection, safety floors on budgets, sandbox mode and phase retry added in turn;... - [How the Claude Code team does code review](sources/claude-dev-claude-code-team-code-review.md): past incident-causing PRs, confirmed by engineers, form an eval the reviewer runs against daily; every reviewer change is scored on it; noise is measured by how authors respond to comments (§How we make the reviewer better). - [Building agents: When to fold subagents into your main agent loop](sources/claude-fold-subagents-into-main-loop.md): one shared end-to-end eval set owned centrally plus per-skill evals owned by each team; start with 10 golden examples; check which tasks flipped and run each more than once (section "Task-completion evals"; "Folding subagents"). - [New in Claude Managed Agents: dreaming, outcomes, and multiagent orchestration](sources/claude-managed-agents-dreaming-outcomes.md): outcomes: write a rubric, a separate grader evaluates "in its own context window, so it isn't influenced by the agent's reasoning", and the agent iterates; up to 10 points better task success than a standard prompting loop;... - [How to Manage AI Agents Effectively](sources/departmentofproduct-managing-ai-agents.md): DoorDash went from about 1 human review a day to 2,000 LLM-judge-graded sessions daily (claimed +8 quality points, regression testing cut from 6h to 20m); Airbnb calibrates its judges to 80-90% agreement with humans. - [How to use /loops, /goals and other Powerful Slash Commands as a Non-Engineer](sources/departmentofproduct-loops-goals-slash-commands.md): a good goal states the end state, how it's verified and what must be kept; the agent marks "cause unclear" rather than inferring (research-department-of-product-knowledge-series)
- [How to build an AI Agent](sources/departmentofproduct-how-to-build-an-ai-agent.md): three autonomy levels: supervised predefined tasks, conditional autonomy with escalation, full independence (research-department-of-product-knowledge-series)

- [AI's third era: the rise of persistent AI coworkers](sources/lenny-podcast-tara-seshan-persistent-coworkers.md): code is output-verifiable by tests; knowledge work is not, so the agent must show in-progress work, citations and inputs to be believed (1:05:08) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)

- [Inside Devin](sources/lenny-podcast-scott-wu-inside-devin.md): "give Devin tasks, not problems"; best on well-defined, easy-to-verify work; start with one-point tickets and scale (47:55, 1:09:31) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [Community Wisdom: Syncing Claude Code and Claude Design ...](sources/lenny-community-wisdom-claude-design-handoff.md): buyers trust AI-built software when it is tested and evaluated against stated product intent and runs on their own data, not on process stories (Thread 2) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [Advanced evals: How to find (and fix) hidden AI failures in your product](sources/lenny-newsletter-advanced-evals-error-discovery.md): error discovery (humans read traces until the definition of good stabilises) must precede metrics; cited results: Shopify workflow builder 2.2x faster and 68% cheaper, Ramp receipt matching 35% to 83%, Cursor routing costs down 41% (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [How we restructured Airtable's entire org for AI | Howie Liu](sources/lenny-podcast-howie-liu-airtable-reorg.md): contrarian: for novel capabilities start with "vibes", write evals only once the form factor and use-case cluster have converged (1:03:50) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [The coming AI security crisis | Sander Schulhoff](sources/lenny-podcast-sander-schulhoff-ai-security.md): log every input and output as standard practice for review and improvement, though it is no security defence (56:19) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [Building eval systems that improve your AI product](sources/lenny-newsletter-evals-hamel-shreya.md): error analysis on ~100 traces → <10 failure modes → code checks plus LLM judges validated by TPR/TNR on a held-out human-labelled set; CI golden set plus production discovery loop (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [What happens after coding is solved? | Fiona Fung](sources/lenny-podcast-fiona-fung-after-coding-solved.md): "bad vs sad" quality framework set per team, plus a swear-word dashboard for frustration evals miss; verifying the intended experience is "still a hard one to crack" (44:46-47:39, 1:10:44) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [Make product management fun again with AI agents](sources/lenny-newsletter-tal-raviv-pm-agents.md): "Trust is gained in drops": widen agent scope only after several good cycles (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [Anthropic's first technical PM ... | Dianne Penn](sources/lenny-podcast-dianne-penn-evals-prds.md): capabilities jump discontinuously, so "unless you have the evals ... these jumps might actually happen and you don't know"; evals matter for any product at the intersection of model, harness and context (17:53, 46:54) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [How Claude Mythos found a 15-year-old bug in Mozilla Firefox | Brian Grinstead](sources/howiai-mozilla-mythos-bug-harness.md): Mozilla's loop works because of "a very crystal clear task verification signal" (an AddressSanitizer build); host says articulating success and failure cases crisply is now a hard skill, including for design (23:32, 24:22) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [OpenAI's CPO on how AI changes must-have skills (Kevin Weil)](sources/lenny-podcast-kevin-weil-openai-cpo.md): whether a model is right 60%, 95% or 99.5% of the time decides what product to build; AI products are capped by eval quality (17:50-24:22) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [Head of Claude Code (Boris Cherny)](sources/lenny-podcast-boris-cherny-after-coding.md): a PM used Lenny's 50 non-technical Claude Code uses as a pre-launch Cowork eval; 48/50 passed (1:23:27) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)

- [How top PMs increase their leverage with AI](sources/lenny-newsletter-pm-leverage-ladders.md): PM work as rubric loops: a YAML rubric with structural and binary-LLM checks, one subagent grader per check, iterate until all pass, then schedule; "only two or three loops for most PM tasks" (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [Anthropic's CPO on what comes next (Mike Krieger)](sources/lenny-podcast-mike-krieger-anthropic-cpo.md): best builders keep "a repeatable way to evaluate" each new model: A/B tests, internal evals, rerunning captured traces; customers' own "Cursor bench" beats public benchmarks (52:25) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [Engineers are becoming sorcerers (Sherwin Wu, OpenAI)](sources/lenny-podcast-sherwin-wu-openai-codex.md): engineers' "bar of trust" rises over time; multi-hour tasks will need mid-run feedback products (5:26, 50:34) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [Code with Claude: The 5 biggest updates explained](sources/howiai-code-with-claude-updates.md): "Outcomes" = rubric-based grading of managed-agent work (show notes only) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [Microsoft CPO (Aparna Chennapragada)](sources/lenny-podcast-aparna-chennapragada-microsoft.md): agents defined by autonomy as a spectrum, complexity and natural interaction; editable plans and calibrated "show the work" as trust UI (14:18-19:44) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [Community Wisdom: Top Contributors Summer 2026 (product engineers pilot)](sources/lenny-community-wisdom-product-engineers-pilot.md): LLM features evaluated with curated golden sets plus human sampling, then at scale (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [Why your AI product needs a different development lifecycle (CC/CD)](sources/lenny-newsletter-cc-cd-ai-lifecycle.md): version by agency not features; "Every time you give an AI system more agency, you give up some control"; climb rungs (route, suggest, auto-resolve) as calibration stops surprising (sections 2, CD 1) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [Community Wisdom: PRDs for agents](sources/lenny-community-wisdom-prds-for-agents.md): eval rubric drafted in the PRD, revised as traces reveal unanticipated failures (thread 3) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [Prerna Kaul: FDA submissions](sources/howiai-prerna-kaul-fda-submissions.md): product leaders own "my 100 things I want to know that the model does well on when it comes to safety", online monitoring and rollback (42:49) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [How AI is reshaping the product role (Udezue)](sources/lenny-podcast-udezue-ai-reshaping-pm-role.md): PMs must write evals to verify output "hasn't hallucinated" (19:30) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [How Warp ships 2,000 PRs a month with AI factories (How I AI)](sources/howiai-warp-zach-lloyd-software-factory.md): LLM judge scores sampled runs (e.g. redundant tests); observer agent reads 20-25 failed runs and proposes edits to factory agent definitions (20:20-23:27) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [Why AI evals are the hottest new skill (Lenny's Podcast)](sources/lenny-podcast-hamel-shreya-evals.md): criteria drift: even experts "can't figure out your rubrics upfront"; people burned by Likert judges turned "anti evals" (1:03:35, 1:10:19) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [25 proven tactics to accelerate AI adoption](sources/lenny-newsletter-25-ai-adoption-tactics.md): four questions for any AI demo, including ground-truth dataset and evals and how you prepared for model failure (section 5) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [How 80,000 companies build with AI (Lenny's Podcast)](sources/lenny-podcast-asha-sharma-loop-not-lane.md): reviewing thousands of agents needs "self-healing observability, really good evals"; device and policy management are solved problems to borrow (24:40) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [AI hallucination (Product Talk glossary)](sources/producttalk-ai-hallucination-glossary.md): eval method for synthesis: verbatim-quote check in code plus LLM-as-judge fact checker [re-check 2026-10-24]. (research-pm-agents-jobs-to-be-done)
- [Why not just ship it?](sources/ideas-fin-why-not-just-ship-it.md): every Fin change passes backtests on a few thousand replayed conversations graded by calibrated LLM-judge ensembles, then a pre-registered A/B test, then a 0% dark launch and ramp (2026-08-28) (research-pm-agents-jobs-to-be-done)
- [Webinar Q&A: How Fin 3x'd R&D output in 16 months](sources/ideas-fin-webinar-qa-3x-rd-output.md): the PR-review agent's evals are a human-curated set of historical PRs with confirmed issues, re-run on prompt changes for precision/recall (2026-05-22) (research-pm-agents-jobs-to-be-done)
- [Working with a Black Box (Fin Insights)](sources/ideas-fin-working-with-a-black-box-fin-insights.md): CX Score shipped only after an expert-labelled reference dataset and evaluation pipeline; one score reason dropped for missing the bar (research-pm-agents-jobs-to-be-done)

- [Demystifying evals for AI agents](sources/anthropic-demystifying-evals-ai-agents.md): capability evals "graduate" into regression suites at a near-100% pass rate (research-skill-rigidity-spectrum)

- [Devin 2.1](sources/cognition-devin-2-1-confidence.md): green/yellow/red self-rating; clarifying questions below green; vendor claims green doubles merged-PR odds (research-skill-rigidity-spectrum)

## experiment-decision-rules: Experiment decision rules
Pre-agreed rules, encoded in the platform, that map measurement results to ship, abort or iterate, making "operate and learn" a structured, explainable record.
- [Risk-Aware Product Decisions in A/B Tests with Multiple Metrics](sources/spotify-engineering-risk-aware-product-decisions.md): default ship rule (success metric up, guardrails non-inferior, no deterioration, quality checks pass), encoded in Confidence since 2020 (research-airbnb-spotify-product-practices)
- [Beyond Winning: Spotify's Experiments with Learning Framework](sources/spotify-engineering-experiments-with-learning.md): ~64% learning rate vs ~12% win rate; every experiment classified ship, abort or iterate (Sep 2025) (research-airbnb-spotify-product-practices)
- [Lessons from scaling Spotify (Gustav Söderström)](sources/lenny-podcast-gustav-soderstrom-scaling-spotify.md): Home redesign judged on quant data, research and feedback; new-user cohorts separate "habit broken" from "worse" (44:10-1:01:14) (research-airbnb-spotify-product-practices)

## feedback-triage-agents: Feedback and research triage/synthesis as an agent job
Clustering and routing customer feedback, calls and tickets is the best-evidenced PM-agent job, but needs checks against invented or merged quotes.
- [Beyond the model: Engineering AI infra with scientific judgement](sources/airbnb-tech-insight-miner-agent-harness.md): built to map the taxonomy and prevalence of support situations, including rare risky ones, before the 2025 AI support launch; rerun for each new language and country (research-airbnb-spotify-product-practices)
- [Airbnb Q1 2024 earnings call](sources/airbnb-earnings-q1-2024.md): Chesky names customer service as generative AI's first and biggest near-term use (research-airbnb-spotify-product-practices)
- [Agents you can coach: how Asana builds human-agent teams with Claude](sources/claude-asana-agents-you-can-coach.md): Slack product questions become Asana tasks; agent answers from approved guidance with links, files product gaps to the product intake project, and raises enablement tasks when a question repeats ("Three jobs"). (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [Carvana turns Slack alerts into production fixes with Claude Tag](sources/claude-customers-carvana-claude-tag.md): alert channels monitored; agent finds owning team, tags them, posts root cause in the team's format, opens PR on request (section "From alert to merged fix"). (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [Gumroad's customer support team ships code with Claude](sources/claude-customers-gumroad-support-ships-code.md): "Our customer support team uses Claude to triage and often fix issues, reducing the load on our engineering team" (Claude improves customer support). (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [Inside Rakuten's plan to turn every employee into a builder with Claude Managed Agents](sources/claude-customers-rakuten-every-employee-builder.md): user-interviewing agent that creates tickets for agent or human triage (task system answer). (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [Sourcegraph streamlines product and community insights with Claude](sources/claude-customers-sourcegraph-product-insights.md): weekly community feedback reports for the product team generated from multiple sources (section "Choosing Claude"). (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [How Anthropic employees use Claude Tag](sources/claude-how-anthropic-uses-claude-tag.md): ~20 search variants across Slack to find every rep who asked for a feature (~24 accounts in ~26 min); a week of enterprise issues condensed from ~120 raw findings to 23 open and 14 resolved, then 15 more on a self-check... - [Loop engineering: Getting started with loops](sources/claude-loop-engineering.md): bug reports and issue triage named as the best fit for proactive loops. (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [How Warp builds self-improving agents on Claude](sources/claude-warp-self-improving-agents.md): issue-triage agent fired by a GitHub Action labels issues, assesses complexity and suggests a fix direction; maintainer feedback on a missed "ready to spec" label became a skill PR (section "The loop in action"). - [What happens after coding is solved? | Fiona Fung](sources/lenny-podcast-fiona-fung-after-coding-solved.md): a morning Claude routine reads all feedback channels, finds themes and opens PRs for review (12:39, 36:20) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)

- [Build your personal AI copilot](sources/lenny-newsletter-tal-raviv-ai-copilot.md): event-driven automations: cross-search Slack, HubSpot, Gong on each feature request; flag "product confusion" support closures (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
