## gate-judge-separation: Where a gate fires vs who judges it
The enforcement point of a check (a fixed hook event, tripwire or graph node, fail-open or fail-closed) is a separate choice from its judge (script, model, human). It matters because "make it a hook" settles that the check runs, not how it decides.
- [Supervisory Guidance on Model Risk Management (SR 11-7, attachment)](sources/federalreserve-sr-11-7-model-risk-guidance.md): "effective challenge" is "critical analysis by objective, informed parties"; incentives are stronger "when there is greater separation of that challenge from the model development process" (p. 4). (first-party; research-dependency-agent)
- [The IIA's Three Lines Model: An update of the Three Lines of Defense](sources/iia-three-lines-model-2020.md): "Some second line roles may be assigned to specialists to provide complementary expertise, support, monitoring, and challenge to those with first line roles" (Principle 3); third line independence from management is a separate principle (Principle 5). (first-party; research-dependency-agent)
- [Open Policy Agent documentation (Introduction)](sources/openpolicyagent-docs-overview.md): OPA decides; the caller (Kubernetes admission, Envoy, CI, Terraform plan check) enforces. (first-party; research-dependency-agent)
- [SS1/23 – Model risk management principles for banks](sources/pra-ss1-23-model-risk-management-principles.md): the validation function "should operate independently from the model development process and from model owners", provides "recommendations on model approvals to the appropriate model approval authority", and needs standing to give "effective challenge" (Principle 4.1, p. 25). (first-party; research-dependency-agent)
- [Automate actions with hooks (Claude Code)](sources/anthropic-claude-code-hooks-guide.md): command hooks give "deterministic control"; prompt and agent hooks hand the decision to a model at the same lifecycle point; a Stop hook asks "are all tasks complete?" (research-skill-rigidity-spectrum)
- [Hooks reference (Claude Code)](sources/anthropic-claude-code-hooks-reference.md): decisions allow/deny/ask/defer; only `exit 2` blocks; fail-open unless `onFailure: block` (research-skill-rigidity-spectrum)
- [Configure permissions (Claude Agent SDK)](sources/anthropic-agent-sdk-permissions.md): ordered stack hooks → deny → ask → mode (incl. model-classifier auto) → allow → `canUseTool` callback (research-skill-rigidity-spectrum)
- [Guardrails (OpenAI Agents SDK)](sources/openai-agents-sdk-guardrails.md): the same tripwire can be driven by a cheap agent, a classifier or a function; parallel by default, blocking opt-in (research-skill-rigidity-spectrum)
- [Demystifying evals for AI agents](sources/anthropic-demystifying-evals-ai-agents.md): code graders "where possible", model "where necessary", human "sparingly for validation"; grade the outcome, not the path (research-skill-rigidity-spectrum)
- [Graders (OpenAI)](sources/openai-graders-guide.md): string check → similarity → Python → model judge "when code falls short"; calibrate against experts; watch for grader hacking (research-skill-rigidity-spectrum)
- [Define outcomes (Claude Managed Agents)](sources/anthropic-managed-agents-define-outcomes.md): the harness sets up a grader in a separate context; per-criterion markdown rubric; iterate to `satisfied` or `max_iterations` (research-skill-rigidity-spectrum)
- [Design topics as mini-agents (Copilot Studio)](sources/microsoft-copilot-studio-topics-as-mini-agents.md): Power Fx and entity validation "as reliable as code, so business rules and compliance constraints are respected even when the rest of the plan is generated" (research-skill-rigidity-spectrum)
- [LLM Evaluators Recognize and Favor Their Own Generations](sources/arxiv-llm-evaluators-favor-own-generations.md): the drafting model should not be the judging model (research-skill-rigidity-spectrum)
- [Define success criteria and build evaluations](sources/claude-platform-define-success-and-evaluations.md): code-based "fastest and most reliable", human "avoid if possible", LLM "test to ensure reliability first, then scale" (research-skill-rigidity-spectrum)
- [Claude Code permission modes](sources/anthropic-claude-code-permission-modes-docs.md): auto-mode classifier sees user messages, tool calls and CLAUDE.md but not tool results; pauses after 3 consecutive or 20 total blocks (research-skill-rigidity-spectrum)
- [VS Code agent approvals](sources/vscode-copilot-agent-approvals-and-permissions.md): Assisted permissions LLM judge "can make mistakes in its risk assessment"; terminal auto-approval "not a security boundary" (research-skill-rigidity-spectrum)

## governance-as-code: Governance as code: gates and evidence as data
Policy as code, pipeline-driven change approval, machine-readable control catalogues and authorisation evidence, regulatory registers; where governance already has a machine-readable intake and where it does not. Related: [[gate-judge-separation]].
- [Enforce least-privilege authorization in multi-agent AI chains using Cedar](sources/aws-security-cedar-multi-agent-least-privilege.md): three Cedar layers evaluated in order, first deny wins: L1 agent-to-tool (trust score 1-5, namespace, lifecycle stage); L2 delegation (max five hops, requested task must be a subset of the target agent's registered capabilities); L3 originating user (role, MFA, allowed delegation depth). (first-party; research-dependency-agent)
- [Capabilities: Streamlining change approval](sources/dora-capability-streamlining-change-approval.md): shift validations into the development platform and implement security controls at platform and infrastructure layers rather than manual review (Recommended practices). (independent; research-dependency-agent)
- [Accelerate: State of DevOps 2019](sources/dora-state-of-devops-2019.md): version control as the source of truth makes "the review and submit process highly auditable" (p. 49). (independent; research-dependency-agent)
- [DORA Dry Run exercise: summary report (ESA 2024 35)](sources/esas-dora-dry-run-register-of-information.md): the ESAs provided "templates for the registers, draft data point model, draft reporting taxonomy, examples and instructions for filling data fields, and a tool for converting Excel files into plain-csv files which is the format used by the ESAs for the RoI reporting" (p. 3). (first-party; research-dependency-agent)
- [Building the future of finance in the age of AI](sources/fca-rusu-building-future-finance-age-ai.md): FCA plans a Handbook API for machine-readable rules and machine-readable data collection; AI tools to supervise ~60,000 AML firms joining its remit in 2028 and an AI "market first responder" agent for ~9,000 small wholesale reporting firms. (first-party; research-dependency-agent)
- [FedRAMP 20x](sources/fedramp-20x-overview.md): providers' security status "should be validated automatically whenever possible"; Phase 2 lessons cite consistent machine-readable schemas, validations that fit existing provider tools, and assessor review of validation code (Goals, Phase 2 lessons). (first-party; research-dependency-agent)
- [FINOS Common Cloud Controls (CCC)](sources/finos-common-cloud-controls.md): each control carries assessment requirements that can become scans, code analyses or behavioural checks, runnable as pipeline gates that block non-compliant resources (Verification section). (first-party; research-dependency-agent)
- [CBA pushing to production more often, with fewer incidents](sources/itnews-cba-production-more-often-fewer-incidents.md): "We used to perform assurance of around 2500 controls attributes per year ... we are doing more than 12,000 per month"; similar improvement in monitoring compliance with controls. (first-party; research-dependency-agent)
- [NAB uses CAST to keep its cloud apps in check](sources/itnews-nab-cast-cloud-controls.md): "So if you want to do a change, there's no form to fill in, there's no change board ... There are approvals that need to go through ... but they are all automated"; CAST lets the bank "programmatically define how we run our workloads in the cloud"; a Lambda function checks new instances against controls. (first-party; research-dependency-agent)
- [Speed to Market (D) Working Group, Virtual Meeting, April 23, 2026 (draft minutes, Attachment 1)](sources/naic-speed-to-market-wg-minutes-april-2026.md): Clara "learns individual rules through language, examples, and test cases. Rules are grouped into rule groups that function as checklists, with a many-to-many relationship allowing reuse across product types and review cycles" (item 3). (first-party; research-dependency-agent)
- [OSCAL: the Open Security Controls Assessment Language (layers and models)](sources/nist-oscal-layers-and-models.md): three layers: Control (Catalog, Profile, Control Mapping), Implementation (Component Definition, System Security Plan), Assessment (Assessment Plan, Assessment Results, POA&M); all released (layer page). (first-party; research-dependency-agent)
- [Opal Security Launches Opal Zero to Make Least Privilege a Reality for Enterprise AI Agents](sources/opal-zero-launch-press-release.md): Gateway Sync writes each decision as policy specifying what the agent can reach, how long, whose approval, and when it ends; enforced by Databricks Unity Gateway and AWS AgentCore Gateway at launch. (vendor-claim; research-dependency-agent)
- [Open Policy Agent documentation (Introduction)](sources/openpolicyagent-docs-overview.md): software sends structured input, OPA evaluates it against Rego policies and data, and returns a decision that "can be arbitrary structured data", not just allow/deny (Overview). (first-party; research-dependency-agent)
- [Accelerating your DevOps change process (DevOps Change Velocity)](sources/servicenow-docs-devops-change-velocity-approval.md): (default posture): the manual approval flow is enabled by default and the automated flows apply only to automatically created changes (or with receipts disabled); the "DevOps risk" condition using a committer risk score is inactive by default; docs recommend only one DevOps flow active at a time (DE-language docs page t~YvqQkg2oQX4L7ySrpyuQ, read 2026-10-28). (first-party; research-dependency-agent)
- [Spectral: a flexible JSON/YAML linter for creating automated style guides](sources/stoplight-spectral-readme.md): rules in JSON/YAML/JS with built-in functions (pattern, length, required keys, ordering) and custom JS/TS functions; extends predefined OpenAPI, AsyncAPI and Arazzo rulesets (README). (first-party; research-dependency-agent)
- [When DORA metrics meet governance in banking - Expert View](sources/teamtopologies-dora-metrics-governance-banking.md): code review, security checks, change approvals, audit reporting and deployment gates are mostly human-driven; evidence gathering is manual and audits find gaps that create more remediation paperwork, a "doom loop". (anecdote; research-dependency-agent)
- [The all-in-one trust management platform (Enterprise)](sources/vanta-enterprise-trust-management.md): "Automate audit prep and evidence collection"; continuous controls monitoring via automated tests; "Automatically pull data from 400+ tools". (vendor-claim; research-dependency-agent)

## harness-over-model: The harness, not the model, limits real-world value
Ramp found models were good enough; the preconfigured environment (integrations, skills, memory, UX) decided whether non-experts got value. Central to what a "product agent and harness" is. Related: [[compounding-context-repo]].
- [We Built Every Employee at Ramp Their Own AI Coworker](sources/x-sebgoddijn-glass-article.md): "The Models are Good Enough, The Harness Isn't"; 99% adoption but most stuck (§intro) (competitive-teardown-ramp-glass)
- [How to get your company AI pilled](sources/x-geoffintech-ai-pilled-article.md): same finding framed as lesson 6, "the harness wasn't" (competitive-teardown-ramp-glass)
- [Ramp built an AI agent harness in six weeks](sources/thenewstack-ramp-laminar-agent-harness.md): the harness (sessions, sandboxes, connectors, observability, routing) is what Ramp chose to own; models stay swappable (competitive-teardown-ramp-glass)
- [Building Laminar: Ramp's Managed Agents Platform](sources/ramp-builders-building-laminar.md): the harness's 15 responsibilities listed; provider-agnostic; own trace-debug UI (competitive-teardown-ramp-glass)
- [Building an agentic harness that outlasts the model](sources/shopify-engineering-agentic-harness-outlasts-model.md): better models gave more noise; all 30+ candidates in one audit were downgraded; the harness is the durable asset (competitive-teardown-shopify-river)
- [Introducing Roast](sources/shopify-engineering-introducing-roast.md): "Non-determinism is the enemy of reliability"; YAML + markdown steps interleaved with a Claude Code CodingAgent (competitive-teardown-shopify-river)
- [Learning on the Shop floor](sources/x-tobi-learning-on-the-shop-floor.md): 36%→77% merge rate "did not retrain a model... did not switch models" (self-reported) (competitive-teardown-shopify-river)
- [Stripe's AI minions ship 1,300 PRs weekly from a Slack emoji (How I AI)](sources/howiai-stripe-minions-kaliski.md): minions succeed because of years of devex: hosted devboxes, CI, docs, a 'blessed path for 90% of the common activities' (competitive-teardown-stripe-knowledge-agents)
- [Build your own company brain (How I AI, Krishnamurthy)](sources/howiai-stripe-kai-krishnamurthy.md): data-agent quality depends on pre-AI investments: tiered data catalog, blessed analytics layer, a warehouse hardened for agent query load (competitive-teardown-stripe-knowledge-agents)
- [Improving Deep Agents with harness engineering](sources/langchain-improving-deep-agents-harness-engineering.md): vendor claim: changing only prompt, tools and middleware moved the same model from 52.8% to 66.5% on Terminal Bench 2.0 (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Scaling Managed Agents: Decoupling the brain from the hands](sources/anthropic-engineering-scaling-managed-agents.md): first-party: harness assumptions about model weakness go stale as models improve; harness components must be re-tested per model (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Harness design for long-running application development](sources/anthropic-harness-design-long-running-apps.md): first-party: planner/generator/evaluator harness cost $200 vs $9 solo on one task (20x) and a harness component was removed when the model improved (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Rebuilding Devin for Claude Sonnet 4.5](sources/cognition-devin-sonnet-45-rebuild.md): first-party: one model change forced harness changes (context anxiety, parallel tools); 2x faster, 12% better after rebuild (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [We removed 80% of our agent's tools](sources/vercel-we-removed-80-percent-of-our-agents-tools.md): first-party: simplifying to one bash tool raised success 80% to 100% on five queries, tokens down 37% (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Harness Engineering: ... Eleven Systems](sources/arxiv-harness-engineering-eleven-systems.md): independent: loop sophistication does not predict benchmark performance; production harnesses invest in scaffolding for safety, reliability and integration (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [OpenAI Introduces Harness Engineering (InfoQ)](sources/infoq-openai-harness-engineering.md): vendor claim: harness = repo docs, linters, layered architecture and observability; about a million lines with no hand-written code (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Scaling Managed Agents](sources/anthropic-scaling-managed-agents.md): harness assumptions expire as models improve (context resets useful on Sonnet 4.5, dead weight on Opus 4.5) (first-party) (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Meta-Harness paper](sources/arxiv-meta-harness-optimization.md): harness code is itself searchable/optimisable (independent paper) (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Boris Cherny summary (Traces)](sources/traces-boris-cherny-light-cone-summary.md): second-hand counterpoint: scaffolding is wiped out by the next model, so harness features decay (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Accelerating Large-Scale Test Migration with LLMs](sources/airbnb-tech-llm-test-migration.md): retry loops fed with validation errors, plus choosing the right related files, beat prompt tuning; 97% of ~3.5k files migrated (research-airbnb-spotify-product-practices)
- [GraphQL Data Mocking at Scale with LLMs and @generateMock](sources/airbnb-tech-graphql-generatemock.md): schema validation plus error-fed retries make LLM mocks reliably valid (research-airbnb-spotify-product-practices)
- [From weeks to a day: how we made LLM evaluation fast enough to iterate on](sources/airbnb-tech-llm-eval-weeks-to-a-day.md): "the debt accumulates at the seams, not in the components" (research-airbnb-spotify-product-practices)
- [Beyond the model: Engineering AI infra with scientific judgement](sources/airbnb-tech-insight-miner-agent-harness.md): separate agents maintain the harness itself (update instructions for new models, review live use, reproduce bugs) (research-airbnb-spotify-product-practices)
- [The Pulse: We need to talk about migrations with AI](sources/pragmatic-engineer-migrations-with-ai.md): every successful AI migration built verification loops and kept engineers involved (research-airbnb-spotify-product-practices)
- [Context Engineering (Honk, Part 2)](sources/spotify-engineering-honk-part-2-context-engineering.md): the home-built loop failed on multi-file changes; Claude Code (todos, subagents) did about 50 migrations and most merged PRs (research-airbnb-spotify-product-practices)
- [Redesigning source control at Anthropic](sources/anthropic-redesigning-source-control-scion.md): an early internal Mythos Preview rewrote the hand-built ingestion pipeline at 20x less memory and 4x the speed with no further instructions (§What we learned). (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [How Claude Code works in large codebases: Best practices and where to start](sources/claude-code-large-codebases.md): "the harness—determines how Claude Code performs more than the model alone" (section "The harness matters as much as the model"). (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [How Cresta turned CX expertise into an agent builder on the Claude Agent SDK](sources/claude-cresta-agent-builder-evals.md): SDK chosen as "the same agentic development harness" as Claude Code, used programmatically (§intro quote, Renjie Li). (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [Office Hours: Building for the model that doesn't exist yet (Ramp, with Boris Cherny)](sources/claude-customers-ramp-office-hours.md): Ramp keeps removing scaffolding "because the model has just outgrown the harness" and builds for the model 3-6 months ahead (Rahul, mid and closing answers). (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [Building agents: When to fold subagents into your main agent loop](sources/claude-fold-subagents-into-main-loop.md): since Opus 4.5 models manage more in one loop; rigid multi-agent structures blocked migrations to newer models; Claude Code's system prompt for advanced models was cut by over 80% (three reasons section). (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [Agent harness design: 3 patterns for harnessing Claude's intelligence](sources/claude-harness-design-three-patterns.md): "agent harnesses encode assumptions about what Claude can't do on its own, but those assumptions grow stale"; context resets added for Sonnet 4.5's "context anxiety" became "dead weight" with Opus 4.5 ("The future of agent... (research-claude-resources-articles)

(research-claude-resources-articles)
- [Improving skill-creator: Test, measure, and refine Agent Skills](sources/claude-skill-creator-evals.md): if the base model passes a capability-uplift skill's evals without the skill, the skill may be retired. (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [Steering Claude Code: when to use CLAUDE.md, skills, hooks, and subagents](sources/claude-steering-claude-code.md): "two separate dials" (model and effort) control capability, while the seven methods control behaviour; each trades context cost against authority (intro; "The seven methods"). (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [Context Engineering for AI Agents Explained - a simple overview of the basics](sources/departmentofproduct-context-engineering-basics.md): agent failures "aren't necessarily model failures, but context failures" (research-department-of-product-knowledge-series)
- [Are Agent Harnesses the new "secret sauce" for Product Teams?](sources/departmentofproduct-agent-harnesses-secret-sauce.md): restates Anthropic's solo $9/20 min broken build vs harness $200/6 h working build; "the right harness for last year's model may be over-engineered for this year's" (research-department-of-product-knowledge-series)

- [How to test a new AI Model](sources/departmentofproduct-model-sense-testing.md): defines "scaffolding" (retrieval, human-in-the-loop escalation, domain checks) as what makes a model reliable in production. It credits Box's Levie, second-hand (research-department-of-product-knowledge-series)
- [Inside Devin](sources/lenny-podcast-scott-wu-inside-devin.md): "in terms of base intelligence, we're honestly basically already there"; the work is teaching real-world idiosyncrasies (Datadog, PR flow) (1:02:20) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [Why companies are becoming a series of loops | Anish Acharya](sources/lenny-podcast-anish-acharya-company-loops.md): host: across Cowork, ChatGPT Work, Cursor and Grok Bot "the underlying model is not that different ... most of it is the harness/UX" (58:31) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [How we built Grok Bot in a month | Roman Ugarte](sources/lenny-podcast-roman-ugarte-grok-bot.md): where AI seems dumb it is often "harnessed in the wrong way"; own computer plus tools raises the ceiling (36:20) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [Spec-driven development at Notion | Ryan Nystrom](sources/howiai-notion-ryan-nystrom-spec-driven.md): CI speed caps agent throughput; Stripe's 1,300 agent PRs a week cited as impossible with slow CI (42:45-44:27) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)

- [The AI paradox | Dan Shipper](sources/lenny-podcast-dan-shipper-ai-paradox.md): "every model company is starting to realize how important it is to have a harness" (25:52) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [Why humans are AI's biggest bottleneck (Alexander Embiricos)](sources/lenny-podcast-embiricos-codex-human-bottleneck.md): Codex built as model + API + harness by one product-research team; compaction for 24-hour runs needed all three layers (21:38-24:45) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [OpenAI's CPO on how AI changes must-have skills (Kevin Weil)](sources/lenny-podcast-kevin-weil-openai-cpo.md): counterpoint, "model maximalism": avoid scaffolding around today's limits because a better model arrives in two months, except for errors you can't tolerate (30:03) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [Head of Claude Code: What happens after coding is solved (Boris Cherny)](sources/lenny-podcast-boris-cherny-after-coding.md): counterpoint from the head of Claude Code: give the model tools and a goal, not workflows; scaffolding gains of 10-20% "get wiped out with the next model"; build for the model six months out (1:03:43-1:06:46) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [How Anthropic's product team moves faster than anyone else | Cat Wu](sources/lenny-podcast-cat-wu-anthropic-product-team.md): asking the model to introspect on mistakes shows "what misled it so that you can fix the harness" (53:31) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)

- [How to build AI product sense](sources/lenny-newsletter-ai-product-sense-part-1.md): "There are only a few frontier LLMs, and they're available to all product teams. Innovation is how we apply them"; tool calling is a separate skill from reasoning (Steps 5-6) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [Engineers are becoming sorcerers (Sherwin Wu, OpenAI)](sources/lenny-podcast-sherwin-wu-openai-codex.md): counterpoint: "models will eat your scaffolding for breakfast", including today's skills and file-based context; vector stores and agent frameworks already were (44:13-47:20) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)

## harness-portability: Harness portability
Whether sessions, skills and context can move between harnesses and between local and cloud without losing history or behaviour.
- [How we built OCA, our AI on-call assistant](sources/ramp-builders-how-we-built-oca.md): OCA runs inside Claude Code or Codex depending on which models perform better; switched to GPT-6 Astra (first-party) (competitive-teardown-ramp-glass)
- [Under the River](sources/shopify-engineering-under-the-river.md): harness outside the sandbox lets Shopify "swap models, runtimes, even languages on the harness side" (competitive-teardown-shopify-river)
- [Small Models, Massive Wins (Beyond the Pilot)](sources/venturebeat-beyond-the-pilot-farhan-thawar.md): "River ... switches between models"; "I don't care what harness you wanna use" (competitive-teardown-shopify-river)
- [Build your own company brain (How I AI, Krishnamurthy)](sources/howiai-stripe-kai-krishnamurthy.md): a Kai project can be backed by a different API and harness while keeping Kai's features; Kai skills follow the open skill spec (competitive-teardown-stripe-knowledge-agents)
- [Stripe Got 83% of Staff Using One AI Agent. Don't Copy Its Sales Numbers.](sources/aifounders-stripe-kai-dont-copy-sales-numbers.md): 'the skills are the durable asset'; keep them exportable from any vendor harness (competitive-teardown-stripe-knowledge-agents)
- [Use Claude Code in the cloud (Claude Code on the web docs)](sources/anthropic-claude-code-cloud-sessions.md): handoff is deliberately asymmetric: cloud to terminal via --teleport (needs clean git state, same repo, same claude.ai account), terminal to cloud only as a new session or via the Desktop app; the terminal copy is a fork that does not sync back (Move tasks between terminal and cloud) (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Scaling Managed Agents: Decoupling the brain from the hands](sources/anthropic-engineering-scaling-managed-agents.md): credentials are never visible to the harness; git tokens used at sandbox init, MCP OAuth tokens held in a vault behind a proxy (Credential handling) (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Cloud-origin agents have no 'Move to Machine' option (Cursor forum)](sources/cursor-forum-cloud-to-local-handoff.md): staff (2026-06-05) called cloud-to-local for cloud-origin sessions a 'known limitation', 'not being actively built out right now'; workaround is a local agent on the same repo or continuing in the cloud (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Claude Code deletes conversation history after 30 days by default](sources/itdaily-claude-code-30-day-transcript-deletion.md): Anthropic's stated reason is that plain-text transcripts can hold code and credentials, i.e. retention conflicts with auditability (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Agent Trace (Thoughtworks Technology Radar Vol. 34)](sources/thoughtworks-radar-agent-trace.md): vendor-neutral JSON trace record linking code ranges to contributor type (human/AI/mixed/unknown) and, per the spec's draft, to the originating conversation; works with Git, Mercurial, Jujutsu (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [codex-plugin-cc](sources/openai-codex-plugin-for-claude-code.md): a competing vendor ships a plugin that runs inside Claude Code; shows plugins as a cross-harness delegation channel. (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Run Claude Code programmatically](sources/anthropic-claude-code-headless-agent-sdk.md): `--bare` makes headless runs reproducible by skipping hooks, plugins, MCP and CLAUDE.md. (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [MCP spec 2026-07-28](sources/mcp-spec-2026-07-28-key-changes.md): stateless transport and extension mechanism; Client ID Metadata Documents replace dynamic client registration. (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Anthropic cracks down on unauthorized Claude usage by third-party harnesses](sources/venturebeat-anthropic-third-party-harness-crackdown.md): independent: Jan 2026 block of subscription OAuth outside official clients (OpenCode and others) (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Agent SDK overview](sources/anthropic-agent-sdk-overview.md): first-party: SDK runs the Claude Code binary; Claude models only; third-party products must use API keys, not claude.ai login (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Harness Engineering: ... Eleven Systems](sources/arxiv-harness-engineering-eleven-systems.md): independent: portability costs a maintained per-provider conditioning layer (cache breakpoints, thinking tiers); SKILL.md in 9 of 11 harnesses (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [AI SDK: Agents overview](sources/vercel-ai-sdk-agents-docs.md): first-party: HarnessAgent runs Claude Code, Codex or Pi behind one interface (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Omnigent launch](sources/databricks-omnigent-meta-harness-launch.md): one-line YAML change ports a custom agent across harnesses; Claude Code, Codex, Pi, OpenAI/Claude Agents SDK (vendor claim) (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Vercel AI SDK Harnesses](sources/vercel-ai-sdk-harnesses.md): HarnessAgent swaps claudeCode/codex/pi in code, sessions resumable; experimental (vendor docs, June 2026) (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Zed ACP](sources/zed-agent-client-protocol.md) and [ACP Registry](sources/zed-acp-registry.md): editor-to-agent standard; 50+ agents; Claude Code and Codex via adapters (vendor/community docs, registry 2026-01-28) (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Warp Oz](sources/warp-oz-multi-harness.md): skills, rules, environments, secrets and triggers shared across Claude Code, Codex and Warp Agent; Warp Agent only as parent (vendor claim) (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)

## human-judgment-pm-jobs: PM jobs that stay human-led

## human-relay-removed: The session or channel replaces the person as relay
On a desktop the person is the bus between the agent and everyone else: they paste context in, copy output out, brief the teammate, carry the plan to the next tool and start the morning's work. Shared, persistent designs make the session, the thread or the plan the handoff object, so the relay disappears. It matters because most of the claimed speed of shared agents comes from this one removal, not from a better model.
- [How a Typical Day of Program Manager Looks Like](sources/zalando-pmo-typical-day-program-manager.md): hour 1 is triaging email and chat into a personal tracker; hour 8 is weekly status reports, leadership updates and metrics, plus coffee chats for networking. (anecdote; research-dependency-agent)
- [Buzz: a workspace for people and agents](sources/block-eng-buzz.md): early AI use had people copying agent output into Slack and back, "making individuals faster and teams slower"; "a project becomes a conversation with code in it" (research-shared-persistent-agents)
- [We Built Every Employee at Ramp Their Own AI Coworker](sources/x-sebgoddijn-glass-article.md): a support agent hands a ticket session to an engineer instead of re-explaining it (research-shared-persistent-agents)
- [Why we built our background agent (Ramp Inspect)](sources/ramp-builders-why-we-built-background-agent.md): "every session is multiplayer. Send your session to any colleague"; prompts attributed per person (research-shared-persistent-agents)
- [Inside Stripe: how it ships fast (Orbit)](sources/youtube-notmybusiness-inside-stripe-ships-fast.md): one button hands a reviewed seven-step plan, a devbox and instructions to a Minion; engineers run three to seven projects in parallel (first-party marketing) (research-shared-persistent-agents)
- [Claude Code projects, redesigned](sources/claude-code-projects-redesigned.md): a coordinator chat scopes, delegates to parallel cloud threads and assembles, over shared project memory; single owner (research-shared-persistent-agents)
- [Ramp office hours with Anthropic](sources/claude-customers-ramp-office-hours.md): "more Inspect sessions are coming from automations than humans" (Ramp's CTO, no numbers) (research-shared-persistent-agents)

## human-review-gates: Human review gates on agent output
Where and how a human checks PM-agent output (quote checks, review before send, isolated repos). Related: [[risk-sloped-review]].
- [Why We Built Our Own Background Agent](sources/ramp-builders-why-we-built-background-agent.md): PRs open under the requesting user's GitHub identity so nobody approves their own agent's work (competitive-teardown-ramp-glass)
- [How we built OCA, our AI on-call assistant](sources/ramp-builders-how-we-built-oca.md): nothing OCA triggers merges without a human; Slack buttons gate destructive actions (competitive-teardown-ramp-glass)
- [How To Build Agents Users Can Trust](sources/ramp-builders-agents-users-can-trust.md): deterministic hard stops (dollar limits, blocklists) layered over the agent (competitive-teardown-ramp-glass)
- [How River takes security work from a fix to merge](sources/shopify-engineering-river-vulnerability-remediation.md): draft-only, human merge authority; hand off "the smallest question that an owner has to answer"; River left a human-owned branch alone (competitive-teardown-shopify-river)
- [Tobi Lütke: AI Agents, Better Decisions (Knowledge Project)](sources/fs-knowledge-project-tobi-lutke-ai-agents.md): "slop grenades", unread agent PRs that shift review load onto colleagues (competitive-teardown-shopify-river)
- [Inside Shopify's AI-first engineering playbook](sources/bvp-inside-shopifys-ai-first-engineering-playbook.md): "We still require a human PR reviewer, which is now becoming a big bottleneck" (competitive-teardown-shopify-river)
- [How Shopify builds product](sources/lenny-how-shopify-builds-product.md): every project passes GSD (Proposal, Prototype, Build, Release, Results), reviewed by directors (OK1) and senior leadership (OK2), mostly async (2023) (competitive-teardown-shopify-river)
- [Production-grade AI agents for financial compliance: Lessons from Stripe](sources/aws-stripe-compliance-agents.md): compliance agents answer sub-questions as pre-fetched research; the human reviewer answers every sub-task; 26% faster median review, >96% helpfulness (competitive-teardown-stripe-knowledge-agents)
- [Build your own company brain (How I AI, Krishnamurthy)](sources/howiai-stripe-kai-krishnamurthy.md): per-project human-in-the-loop confirmation on sensitive tools, deliberately not for everyone, because prompting on every call makes people 'press the wrong button' (competitive-teardown-stripe-knowledge-agents)
- [An Inside Look Into How This $159B Tech Company Ships So Fast](sources/youtube-notmybusiness-inside-stripe-ships-fast.md): deploys to 1% of boxes with automatic pause and rollback; mandated code review; review agent tested against past bad changes (competitive-teardown-stripe-knowledge-agents)
- [Thoughts On A Month With Devin](sources/answerai-month-with-devin.md): 'autonomy became a liability when Devin pursued dead ends instead of flagging blockers'; team found developer-driven tools like Cursor more effective for larger tasks because they allow incremental steering (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Automate work with scheduled tasks (Claude Code routines docs)](sources/anthropic-claude-code-scheduled-tasks.md): a green run status 'does not mean the work your prompt describes succeeded'; runs start in auto mode with a classifier, and stop to wait if repeated blocks occur (View runs; Permission prompts) (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Claude Tag: agent identity (concepts)](sources/anthropic-claude-tag-agent-identity.md): audit attribution differs by context: channel actions appear under service accounts; DM actions under the user (PRs still authored by the GitHub App); personal-connector work in a channel is recorded under the approving user (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Cursor Cloud Agent sessions are shared across users - act on behalf (forum bug report)](sources/cursor-forum-team-followups-act-on-behalf.md): reporter says the originating Slack prompt can be deleted, removing the audit trail while side effects remain (claim; staff reply did not address it) (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Risks and mitigations for GitHub Copilot cloud agent](sources/github-copilot-cloud-agent-risks.md): PRs are drafts a human must review and merge; the agent cannot mark them ready, approve or merge; the requester cannot approve their own agent-created PR; workflows do not run until a user with write access approves (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Minions: Stripe's one-shot, end-to-end coding agents - Part 2](sources/stripe-minions-part-2.md): every minion PR is human-reviewed; a minion gets one full CI iteration plus one retry, after which the branch goes back to a human (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Claude Tag Slack access model (Tenable Research)](sources/tenable-claude-tag-slack-access-model.md): recommends auditing bundles, scoping to minimum, keeping elevated bundles in private channels, and logging/approving channel invites (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [AWS AI coding tool decided to delete and recreate a customer-facing system, causing 13-hour outage (report)](sources/the-decoder-aws-kiro-outage.md): Amazon then added mandatory peer review for production access and says Kiro asks for authorisation by default (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Replit makes vibe-y promise to stop its AI agents making vibe coding disasters](sources/theregister-replit-saastr-response.md): Replit's fix is architectural (automatic dev/prod database separation, staging, planning/chat-only mode) not prompt-based; CEO called it 'Unacceptable and should never be possible' (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Orchestrating AI Code Review at scale](sources/cloudflare-ai-code-review-opencode.md): first-party: AI review biased to approval, critical findings block, human 'break glass' used on 0.6% of MRs (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Minions: Stripe's one-shot coding agents](sources/stripe-minions-one-shot-coding-agents.md): first-party: every minion PR is human-reviewed; CI capped at two rounds (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Choose a design pattern for your agentic AI system](sources/google-cloud-choose-design-pattern-agentic-ai.md): vendor: HITL for high-stakes, safety-critical or subjective approvals (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [How AI is transforming work at Anthropic](sources/anthropic-how-ai-is-transforming-work-at-anthropic.md): first-party self-report: more than half of engineers can fully delegate only 0-20% of work (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Designing Experimentation Guardrails](sources/airbnb-tech-designing-experimentation-guardrails.md): about 25 experiments a month escalated to stakeholders; 80% launch, 20% stopped (Jan 2021) (research-airbnb-spotify-product-practices)
- [Scaling Knowledge at Airbnb (Knowledge Repo)](sources/airbnb-tech-scaling-knowledge-knowledge-repo.md): "No piece of research should be shared without being reviewed" (research-airbnb-spotify-product-practices)
- [Eval-driven development: Lessons from evaluating GenAI at scale](sources/airbnb-tech-eval-driven-development.md): 5% of de-identified live traffic sampled daily; flagged outputs go to humans; weekly PM review (research-airbnb-spotify-product-practices)
- [Inside-Out AI: Rebuilding Airbnb Behind the Scenes and Across the Guest Experience](sources/latent-space-airbnb-al-dahle-inside-out-ai.md): every engineer must be able to explain an AI-generated PR; safety tickets stay with humans (research-airbnb-spotify-product-practices)
- [Accelerating Large-Scale Test Migration with LLMs](sources/airbnb-tech-llm-test-migration.md): Jest, lint and tsc gates per file; humans finished the last ~3% (research-airbnb-spotify-product-practices)
- [Agent-in-the-Loop: A Data Flywheel for Continuous Improvement in LLM-based Customer Support](sources/arxiv-airbnb-agent-in-the-loop.md): copilot design; humans choose replies; human and LLM audit of annotations (research-airbnb-spotify-product-practices)
- [From weeks to a day: how we made LLM evaluation fast enough to iterate on](sources/airbnb-tech-llm-eval-weeks-to-a-day.md): model hotfixes gated on no regression in expert-reviewed domains, with uncertain outputs flagged for humans (research-airbnb-spotify-product-practices)
- [Automation Platform v2: Improving Conversational AI at Airbnb](sources/airbnb-tech-automation-platform-v2.md): LLM apps sit alongside fixed workflows; sensitive claims stay on workflows (research-airbnb-spotify-product-practices)
- [Airbnb Q1 2024 earnings call](sources/airbnb-earnings-q1-2024.md): first framing was AI helping a human support agent (research-airbnb-spotify-product-practices)
- [AI's real question isn't whether AGI arrives (The Deep View: Conversations, E48, Ahmad Al-Dahle)](sources/deepview-al-dahle-airbnb.md): people who want a human are routed to one (research-airbnb-spotify-product-practices)

- [Supercharging Downstream Consumer Dataset Migrations (Honk, Part 4)](sources/spotify-engineering-honk-part-4-dataset-migrations.md): with no build-time tests, owning teams tested the 240 PRs by hand before merging (research-airbnb-spotify-product-practices)

- [Claude for the financial industry](sources/claude-guide-financial-industry.md): the work brought first is "reviewed by a senior person before it ships"; for the ten agent roles "analysts stay in the loop, reviewing, iterating on, and approving the agent's outputs before anything moves downstream" (ch. 4... - [How Anthropic secures its AI-native software development lifecycle](sources/claude-securing-ai-native-sdlc-at-anthropic.md): shadow mode for every new AI reviewer (comments need human approval until trust is earned) and red-teaming of reviewers with inserted malicious changes (§Governance). (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [Turning conversation into knowledge: how Slack builds human-agent teams](sources/claude-slack-human-agent-teams.md): the human-agent rhythm is a cycle of handoffs: agents draft, summarise, monitor, prepare; a person reviews, decides and redirects (section "Learn when to handoff tasks"). - [How Claude Tag serves as Anthropic's first responder for CI/CD failures](sources/claude-tag-ci-cd-first-responder.md): most frequent resolution is a PR "that the on-call can review, merge, and then deploy"; org-wide rule that every PR has a named human owner and every change needs approval to merge (sections "Resolution", "From monitoring... - [Building verification loops in Claude Code with skills](sources/claude-verification-loops-skills.md): in a chained loop "you only step in when something escalates back to you"; hold off on PR-wide gates while the chain is in flux ("Chained"; "On every PR"). (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [How Warp builds self-improving agents on Claude](sources/claude-warp-self-improving-agents.md): improver output goes through normal code review; "That final human step closes the loop and keeps a person in control of what actually changes." (research-claude-resources-articles)

- [How to use Claude Cowork as a Competitive Intelligence System](sources/departmentofproduct-cowork-competitive-intelligence.md): the author advises double-checking output before sharing. Browser automation was "a bit hit and miss" (research-department-of-product-knowledge-series)

- [DeepTriage: Automated Transfer Assistance for Incidents in Cloud Services](sources/arxiv-pham-deeptriage-incident-routing.md): engineers must trust recommendations; the paper frames it as transfer assistance (search summary notes top-5 recommendation matters less than top-1 only when a human corrects). - [Asynchronous Authorization (Auth0 for AI Agents)](sources/auth0-docs-asynchronous-authorization.md): steps: POST `/bc-authorize` with user id and RAR payload, receive `auth_req_id`, poll `/token`, user approves or denies, tokens issued on approval. (first-party; research-dependency-agent)

- [The Change Enablement Practice: What Changed with Change in ITIL 4](sources/easyvista-mann-itil4-change-enablement.md): the CAB "is now hard to find" in ITIL 4 guidance (author's observation). (independent; research-dependency-agent)

- [Frequently asked questions about Planner Agent](sources/microsoft-support-planner-agent-faq.md): feedback in the Loop component or comments, then Regenerate; thumbs up/down; it "may not always be able to successfully complete the task" and then gives instructions for a human. - [Explain the risk of a change request by using Now Assist for IT Service Management (ITSM)](sources/servicenow-docs-explain-change-risk.md): available only to itil users on changes assigned to them; output can be elaborated, shortened, copied, rated; no formal approval step is described.
