- [Now Assist for Strategic Portfolio Management (SPM) release notes](sources/servicenow-docs-now-assist-spm-release-notes.md): AI-identified risks are "presented to the project manager for review, allowing them to accept and add them to RIDAC or reject them"; the Demand Manager AI Specialist "Validates and converts operational demands autonomously" but is controlled-availability and "Requires approval from Servicenow". (first-party; research-dependency-agent)
- [Predictive Intelligence for Change Management](sources/servicenow-docs-predictive-intelligence-change.md): predictions shown to itil or sn_change_write users; admins configure and must train the solutions. (first-party; research-dependency-agent)
- [When DORA metrics meet governance in banking - Expert View](sources/teamtopologies-dora-metrics-governance-banking.md): restates the FCA finding that "CABs approved over 90% of the major changes they reviewed" and Accelerate's finding that external approval is negatively correlated with lead time, deployment frequency and restore time, with no correlation to change fail rate. (anecdote; research-dependency-agent)
- [Head of Growth (Anthropic): "Claude is growing itself at this point"](sources/lenny-podcast-amol-avasare-anthropic-growth.md): humans approve CASH experiments today; brand review could move into a brand-guidelines skill so human review "really decreases" (38:48) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [The Codex feature that works while you sleep](sources/howiai-claire-vo-codex-goal.md): long-running goals end in PRs and a report of what needs human review; ambiguous items labelled "needs judgment" (14:02, 18:42) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [Inside Devin](sources/lenny-podcast-scott-wu-inside-devin.md): humans step in for "the 10 or 20%" of a task on scoping, architecture or front-end checks; the human keeps "the full specification" (21:28, 25:06) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [Advanced evals: How to find (and fix) hidden AI failures in your product](sources/lenny-newsletter-advanced-evals-error-discovery.md): the evals plugin forces a human to annotate 10 traces before the agent may propose labels, "a deliberate safeguard against automation bias"; aim for about 100 (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [How tech workers are feeling in 2026](sources/lenny-newsletter-tech-workers-2026-survey.md): respondent: "I just follow Claude. I don't fully understand what I merge", a sign review is hollowing out under output pressure (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [How Devin replaces your junior engineers | Scott Wu](sources/howiai-scott-wu-devin-junior-engineer.md): every Devin change lands as a PR a human merges, with before/after screenshots and a stated confidence level (vendor demo) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [The coming AI security crisis | Sander Schulhoff](sources/lenny-podcast-sander-schulhoff-ai-security.md): per-action human approval is good security but "what people want is AIs that just go and do stuff", so he expects it to fade (1:27:24) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [What happens after coding is solved? | Fiona Fung](sources/lenny-podcast-fiona-fung-after-coding-solved.md): human code review was "a really really big bottleneck" at 8x throughput until Claude code review; humans keep deep-expertise areas; "how far do you push fully automated reviews?" is open (14:54, 1:09:13) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [Spec-driven development at Notion | Ryan Nystrom](sources/howiai-notion-ryan-nystrom-spec-driven.md): engineer still reviews agent PRs and prompts the agent to defend its change against pushback because models are sycophantic (29:59, 45:31) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [Make product management fun again with AI agents](sources/lenny-newsletter-tal-raviv-pm-agents.md): low-downside swaps for PM agents: DM me, draft not send, recommend not decide, append not modify (section "Can I keep the downside low?") (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [Building eval systems that improve your AI product](sources/lenny-newsletter-evals-hamel-shreya.md): one "benevolent dictator" domain expert, often the PM, labels pass/fail with critiques; LLM clustering must be human-validated (Phase 1) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [Zapier's CEO shares his personal AI stack](sources/howiai-zapier-wade-foster-ai-stack.md): interview agent gives yes/no/maybe plus reasoning as a second opinion and "bias check", not the decision (14:13) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [HTML is the new Markdown | Thariq Shihipar](sources/howiai-thariq-shihipar-html-specs.md): HTML plans proposed because richer formats get more human engagement in review (episode description; show notes only) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [How to do AI analysis you can actually trust](sources/lenny-newsletter-ai-analysis-you-can-trust.md): "The first pass is always a hypothesis"; mandatory verification pass for quotes, contradictions and thin evidence (Failure mode #4) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [How Claude Mythos found a 15-year-old bug in Mozilla Firefox | Brian Grinstead](sources/howiai-mozilla-mythos-bug-harness.md): humans review every fix; the patch agent's fix was right but narrow, engineers added the check in three more places; "pretty far off" from landable patches (28:22) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [The AI paradox | Dan Shipper](sources/lenny-podcast-dan-shipper-ai-paradox.md): human-plus-agent software needs approvals, a summarizing inbox, logs and fast rollback (29:34) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [Anthropic's first technical PM ... | Dianne Penn](sources/lenny-podcast-dianne-penn-evals-prds.md): delegate standardized writing (monthly business review) fully and be "a reviewer and a verifier"; who signs off matters more than who wrote it (1:01:38, 1:08:29) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [Community Wisdom: Quarterly planning and AI ...](sources/lenny-community-wisdom-quarterly-planning.md): AI outbound still needs a human reviewing every email and every CRM update (thread 5) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [How Intercom rose from the ashes ... | Eoghan McCabe](sources/lenny-podcast-mccabe-intercom-ai-bet.md): humans configure, monitor and cover edge cases for agents (42:08) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [Why humans are AI's biggest bottleneck (Alexander Embiricos)](sources/lenny-podcast-embiricos-codex-human-bottleneck.md): "the real ... bottleneck right now is validating that the code worked and writing code review"; show rendered preview before diff (35:04, 41:58) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [OpenAI's CPO on how AI changes must-have skills (Kevin Weil)](sources/lenny-podcast-kevin-weil-openai-cpo.md): support automation drafts for a human when unsure and the correction becomes fine-tuning data; 30-40 support staff for 400M+ weekly users (1:01:24) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [Why Netflix is betting on systems thinkers (Elizabeth Stone)](sources/lenny-podcast-elizabeth-stone-netflix-systems-thinkers.md): decide where AI output can be trusted versus needs review; humans stay responsible even when an agent wrote it (5:17) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [Community Wisdom: AM calls, MCP server](sources/lenny-community-wisdom-am-calls-mcp-server.md): Gong -> Claude -> Airtable insight records, each confirmed by the call host as "accurate/not AI slop" before PMs aggregate (thread 1) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [Community Wisdom: prototypes and release comms](sources/lenny-community-wisdom-prototypes-release-comms.md): Claude Code slash command drafts per-department release notes and must "await my confirmation before sending to Slack" (thread 3) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [Head of Claude Code (Boris Cherny)](sources/lenny-podcast-boris-cherny-after-coding.md): "Claude reviews 100% of pull requests. There's still a layer of human review after it" (16:52) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [Community Wisdom: How PMs are using AI coding tools](sources/lenny-community-wisdom-pms-ai-coding-tools.md): healthcare Director of Product: "The ceiling is verification ... I review more than I produce now" (thread 4) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [The AI-native startup (Dan Shipper, Every)](sources/lenny-podcast-dan-shipper-every-ai-native.md): engineers "definitely are looking at code"; staff could not do the work without knowing how to code (52:33, 53:26) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [The grief, loneliness, and burnout ... | Molly Graham](sources/lenny-podcast-molly-graham-delegating-to-ai.md): "The cost of oversight is not zero": delegating to agents keeps the mental tax with the delegator, unlike handing work to a senior human (43:49-48:42) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [How Anthropic's product team moves faster than anyone else | Cat Wu](sources/lenny-podcast-cat-wu-anthropic-product-team.md): source leak passed "two layers of human review"; multi-agent code review now gates merges at Anthropic (12:15, 1:03:04) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [The non-technical PM's guide to building with Cursor | Zevi Arnovitz](sources/lenny-podcast-zevi-arnovitz-cursor-pm.md): non-coder substitutes cross-model review (Claude, Codex, Cursor) and a "peer review" round for reading code himself (38:33-45:04) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [Community Wisdom: When AI velocity outpaces your product strategy ...](sources/lenny-community-wisdom-ai-velocity-strategy.md): Codex used as "double checker" for Claude; only one agent allowed to push to remote (thread 3) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [How I run autonomous coding agents with OpenAI Symphony + Linear](sources/howiai-alessio-fanelli-symphony-linear.md): human only at PR/preview review and rework; "you can't really stay on top of 100 new things a day" (6:02, 18:18) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [Claude Cowork 101](sources/howiai-jj-englert-cowork-101.md): per-action connector permissions (allow, block, ask) and "never send emails ... only write them as drafts" (18:47, 22:35) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [OpenClaw: The complete guide](sources/lenny-newsletter-claire-vo-openclaw-guide.md): approval steps embedded in scheduled workflows; read-only tokens as the best protection (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [Guillermo Rauch: v0 Git workflow](sources/howiai-guillermo-rauch-v0-git-workflow.md): non-engineers' changes go through branch, preview and PR review: "irresponsible to just ship it" (20:22) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [How to become a supermanager with AI](sources/lenny-newsletter-hilary-gridley-supermanager.md): a GPT encoding her feedback gives drafts "0 to 80" before she reviews "80 to 100" (Strategies 1, 4) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [How Notion's design team uses Claude Code to prototype](sources/howiai-notion-brian-lovin-prototype-playground.md): prototype repo is "YOLO merge", no code review; collisions fixed by a CLAUDE.local.md rule (40:29) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [How to build your own AI developer tools with Claude Code](sources/howiai-tenex-cj-hess-flowy.md): second model (Codex) reviews Claude's diff against the plan and diagram artifacts and caught a mockup mismatch (36:51-42:22) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [How Meta designed Muse](sources/howiai-meta-muse-alex-cornell.md): three-layer status disclosure down to raw calls and code "important from an auditing perspective. But it's only there if you need it" (6:39-8:10) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [No Figma. No Jira. No docs. How Gusto built a new product line with Claude Code](sources/howiai-gusto-eddie-kim-cofounder.md): every PR human-reviewed, median nine minutes thanks to an always-on Zoom; payroll agent stops for explicit confirmation before submitting payroll (25:59, 33:18) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [How Webflow's CPO built an AI chief of staff](sources/howiai-webflow-rachel-wolan-chief-of-staff.md): Gmail scoped to read, archive, label and draft (never send); calendar read-only; she removes power after over-granting (11:26) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [Why cultivating agency matters more than cultivating skills](sources/lenny-podcast-max-schoening-agency.md): with non-engineers the job flips to "do you understand why we can't merge this PR?"; put more effort into reviewing code (37:57) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [How to turn your AI into a world-class designer](sources/lenny-newsletter-ai-world-class-designer.md): human subtraction pass and "a human read each line of copy" (Techniques 6-8) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [Anthropic's CPO on what comes next (Mike Krieger)](sources/lenny-podcast-mike-krieger-anthropic-cpo.md): Claude Code team moved from line-by-line PR review to a second Claude reviewing plus human "acceptance testing", since PRs are larger than people can review (15:43) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [An AI state of the union (Simon Willison)](sources/lenny-podcast-simon-willison-state-of-ai.md): StrongDM's "nobody reads the code" replaced review with a 24/7 swarm of simulated users at ~$10,000/day; Willison: passing virtual QA "doesn't mean it's secure" (14:20-18:32) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [How top PMs increase their leverage with AI](sources/lenny-newsletter-pm-leverage-ladders.md): "You will always apply some level of review at the end"; the systems ladder aims to stop re-editing every output (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [I spent $20,000 on Devin in a month (Ryan Carson)](sources/howiai-ryan-carson-devin-20k-month.md): "LAN PR" skill auto-merges about 40 PRs a day after agent review and a video walkthrough, with no human QA (solo founder) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [Engineers are becoming sorcerers (Sherwin Wu, OpenAI)](sources/lenny-podcast-sherwin-wu-openai-codex.md): Codex reviews 100% of PRs; review time down from 10-15 to 2-3 minutes; human attention "from 100% ... to 30%" (15:27-18:03) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [Community Wisdom: Top Contributors Summer 2026 (product engineers pilot)](sources/lenny-community-wisdom-product-engineers-pilot.md): in a product-builder pilot, "PR reviews, design review, and QA are now the bottlenecks" (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [Community Wisdom: Keeping architecture docs up to date](sources/lenny-community-wisdom-architecture-docs-intent.md): canonical intent docs in the repo are "easy to manipulate", so agents are barred from editing them (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [Why your AI product needs a different development lifecycle (CC/CD)](sources/lenny-newsletter-cc-cd-ai-lifecycle.md): "control handoffs" designed in so humans can take back any decision, with each correction logged as eval data (CD 2, CC 4) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [Community Wisdom: Cursor for PM work](sources/lenny-community-wisdom-cursor-for-pm-work.md): "me + Cursor as a junior engineer": tickets groomed as usual, engineers PR-review every PM change (thread 2) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [Felix Rieseberg (Cowork)](sources/howiai-felix-rieseberg-cowork.md): a $19 microcontroller shows Claude's permission requests and approves them with a physical button, now an "open hardware buddy" in the desktop app (47:01-51:51) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [Prerna Kaul: FDA submissions](sources/howiai-prerna-kaul-fda-submissions.md): regulated drafting today needs weeks of review per module by ~20 specialists; the tool drafts but sign-off is not described (18:53) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [How Warp ships 2,000 PRs a month with AI factories (How I AI)](sources/howiai-warp-zach-lloyd-software-factory.md): every PR still gets human review, but the prompter may now review the agent's code; kickoff-to-PR 35 min vs PR-to-first-review 3.5 h (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [Gumroad CEO's playbook to 40x his team's productivity (How I AI)](sources/howiai-gumroad-sahil-lavingia-v0-devin.md): CEO sends his own Devin PRs to an engineer; humans "take off, decide where to go and land", and do QA (23:15) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [Why AI evals are the hottest new skill (Lenny's Podcast)](sources/lenny-podcast-hamel-shreya-evals.md): open coding of traces is "not the place for an LLM"; LLMs may cluster notes but fixes are the human's job (24:58, 35:53) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [How this PM uses MCPs to automate (How I AI)](sources/howiai-zapier-reid-robinson-mcp-pm-workflows.md): support-ticket loop proposes KB FAQs; PM reviews, edits and approves before the bot uses them (28:43) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [From skeptic to true believer: How OpenClaw changed my life (Lenny's Podcast)](sources/lenny-podcast-claire-vo-openclaw.md): host withheld email-read access from his agent because injected content could exfiltrate it (21:51) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [Spotify Honk background coding agent (InfoQ)](sources/infoq-spotify-honk.md): agents commented out failing tests to pass builds. (research-pm-agents-jobs-to-be-done)
- [We gave Claude Code to everyone at Intercom](sources/intercom-we-gave-claude-code-to-everyone.md): Claude sometimes pulls from the wrong source and users must correct it. (research-pm-agents-jobs-to-be-done)
- [Meta VP's personal agents (Lenny's Newsletter write-up of The Skip Podcast)](sources/lenny-newsletter-meta-chawla-pm-leader-agents.md): one brief dropped all source links; not rolled out everywhere, so humans check outputs. (research-pm-agents-jobs-to-be-done)
- [Make product management fun again with AI agents (Lenny's Newsletter)](sources/lenny-newsletter-tal-raviv-pm-agents.md): five-question safety checklist; start with a low-risk task. (research-pm-agents-jobs-to-be-done)
- [Introducing Custom Agents (Notion)](sources/notion-introducing-custom-agents.md): warns agents are exposed to prompt injection via content they read; credit-based spend controls. (research-pm-agents-jobs-to-be-done)
- [The sweet spot for current-generation agentic AI (Vercel)](sources/vercel-sweet-spot-agentic-ai.md): models still limited in reliability and precision; human final call, outputs approved in Slack. (research-pm-agents-jobs-to-be-done)
- [How we use Linear Agent at Linear](sources/linear-how-we-use-linear-agent-at-linear.md): Humans approve PRs, delegated issues stay human-assigned, autonomy added gradually (research-pm-agents-jobs-to-be-done)
- [How we use Claude Code today at Intercom](sources/ideas-fin-how-we-use-claude-code-today.md): PreToolUse hook blocks `gh pr create` unless the create-pr skill (which asks why the change exists) is loaded; hook blocks edits to merged PR branches (research-pm-agents-jobs-to-be-done)
- [AI is approving our pull requests (Intercom)](sources/intercom-ai-approving-pull-requests.md): the shipping engineer must monitor in production and be ready to roll back; any engineer can request human review (research-pm-agents-jobs-to-be-done)
- [Why not just ship it?](sources/ideas-fin-why-not-just-ship-it.md): Fin release rules "never knowingly ship a resolution rate regression" or increase hallucinations; decision otherwise holistic, decider not named (research-pm-agents-jobs-to-be-done)
- [Code Review for Claude Code, GA](sources/claude-code-review-ga.md): parallel find, verify, rank agents on every PR; "won't approve PRs"; substantive comments on 16% to 54% of PRs; under 1% marked incorrect; $15-25 per review (first-party) (research-shared-persistent-agents)
- [Honk part 3: feedback loops](sources/spotify-engineering-honk-part-3-feedback-loops.md): an LLM judge compares the diff with the original prompt and vetoes about a quarter of unattended sessions, mostly scope creep (research-shared-persistent-agents)
- [Intercom: AI approving pull requests](sources/intercom-ai-approving-pull-requests.md): about 19% of PRs auto-approved by risk and size; the shipping engineer stays accountable; revert rates self-reported (research-shared-persistent-agents)
- [Configuring agents in Buzz](sources/block-eng-configuring-agents-in-buzz.md): a reviewer agent deliberately from a different model family; "respond-to" sets who may direct an agent (research-shared-persistent-agents)
- [How River takes security work from fix to merge](sources/shopify-engineering-river-vulnerability-remediation.md): "hand off the decision, not the investigation": the current head, what it tried, evidence, and "the smallest question that an owner has to answer" (research-shared-persistent-agents)
- [Automated Code Review In Practice](sources/arxiv-cihan-automated-code-review-in-practice.md): 73.8% of LLM review comments resolved, but PR closure time rose from 5h52m to 8h20m (independent) (research-shared-persistent-agents)
- [AGENTOPS01-BP02 handoff and escalation (AWS)](sources/aws-agentic-lens-handoff-escalation.md): separate agent-to-human triggers (confidence, stakes, retries) from routing; mixing them causes fatigue or risk (research-shared-persistent-agents)
- [Seer: hand off to a coding agent](sources/sentry-seer-coding-agent-handoff.md): "Seer never merges on its own"; start at "Stop after Solution" to build trust (research-shared-persistent-agents)
- [Minions Part 2](sources/stripe-minions-part-2.md): after the second CI run "we send the branch back to its human operator"; all PRs human-reviewed (research-skill-rigidity-spectrum)
- [Interrupts (LangGraph)](sources/langchain-langgraph-interrupts.md): four human-gate patterns (approve/reject, edit state, review tool call, validate input) (research-skill-rigidity-spectrum)
- [Microsoft Agent Framework overview](sources/microsoft-agent-framework-overview.md): approval-required tools "pause the workflow for human review before execution" (research-skill-rigidity-spectrum)
- [Configure permissions (Claude Agent SDK)](sources/anthropic-agent-sdk-permissions.md): plan mode sends every edit to the callback, and subagents inherit it "so that handing work to one doesn't get around reviewing the plan first" (research-skill-rigidity-spectrum)
- [About protected branches](sources/github-docs-protected-branches.md): required approvals, code-owner review, stale-approval dismissal, approval from someone other than the last pusher, conversation resolution (research-skill-rigidity-spectrum)
- [Hooks (Kiro docs)](sources/kiro-hooks-docs.md): the same trigger can run a shell command (deterministic) or inject an agent prompt (advisory) (research-skill-rigidity-spectrum)
- [Orchestrate teams of Claude Code sessions](sources/anthropic-claude-code-agent-teams.md): TaskCreated/TaskCompleted hooks can block with exit 2; teammate plan approval is automatic by default, not a human gate (research-skill-rigidity-spectrum)
- [Risks and mitigations for GitHub Copilot cloud agent](sources/github-copilot-cloud-agent-risks.md): requester cannot approve own agent PR; workflows need "Approve and run" by a human (research-skill-rigidity-spectrum)
- [Agent Interaction Guidelines](sources/linear-agent-interaction-guidelines.md): "the final responsibility should always remain with a human"; delegated issue names a responsible human (research-skill-rigidity-spectrum)
- [Agent Skills (Osmani)](sources/addyosmani-agent-skills.md): "Sounds good" and "whatever you think is best" are listed as not-yes (research-skill-rigidity-spectrum)
- [Superpowers skills](sources/obra-superpowers-skills.md): no code, scaffolding or dependencies until the design doc is approved (research-skill-rigidity-spectrum)
- [Harness engineering for coding agent users](sources/fowler-bockeler-harness-engineering.md): humans run a steering loop that improves guides and sensors when issues recur (research-skill-rigidity-spectrum)
- [Large Language Models are not Fair Evaluators](sources/arxiv-llms-are-not-fair-evaluators.md): escalate to a human only where the judge's verdict is unstable across orderings (research-skill-rigidity-spectrum)
- [Knowledge (Devin docs)](sources/devin-docs-knowledge.md): every agent-proposed lesson passes through the user before it is saved (research-skill-rigidity-spectrum)
- [Atlassian Rovo MCP server: supported tools](sources/atlassian-rovo-mcp-server-supported-tools.md): delete and project-management tools are disabled by default and need an admin to enable. (user-story-mapping)
- [Atlassian Rovo MCP server: supported tools](sources/atlassian-rovo-mcp-server-supported-tools.md): confirmed verbatim: delete_jira and manage_jira are disabled by default; executeDestructive is a separate pathway 'used to apply agent-level confirmation'; updateJiraScreen 'Returns a plan by default; changes are applied only with an explicit commit'. (user-story-mapping)
- [DACI decision template (Confluence)](sources/atlassian-confluence-daci-decision-template.md): decision pages name a Driver and 'a single approver who ultimately makes the call'. (user-story-mapping)
- [Generate code from a work item in Jira (Jira Coding Agent)](sources/atlassian-jira-coding-agent-generate-code.md): always a draft PR; 'It doesn't merge pull requests' (user-story-mapping)
- [Using Jira for agentic engineering](sources/atlassian-jira-agentic-engineering-guide.md): a review status holds the transition to done until a human approves and CI passes (user-story-mapping)
- [RovoDev Code Reviewer (ICSE 2026)](sources/arxiv-rovodev-code-reviewer-icse26.md): reviewer posts comments only; humans accept or decline (user-story-mapping)

## human-thinking-skills: Skills designed to make the human think
Skills whose output is better human judgment (questions, critique, reflection prompts) rather than a deliverable, and the design rules they share. Bears on the "up-level the PM" job.
- [discernment-nudge SKILL.md](sources/anthropics-skills-discernment-nudge.md): two or three specific follow-up questions on a consequential answer; once per conversation; "silence is the right default" (research-skill-rigidity-spectrum)
- [doc-coauthoring SKILL.md](sources/anthropics-skills-doc-coauthoring.md): per section: 5-10 questions, options, user curates with reasons; reader test with a fresh Claude (research-skill-rigidity-spectrum)
- [knowledge-work-plugins PM skills](sources/anthropics-kwp-pm-plugin-skills.md): product-brainstorming: "Your job is not to generate deliverables"; four modes; named PM anti-patterns (research-skill-rigidity-spectrum)
- [Superpowers skills](sources/obra-superpowers-skills.md): brainstorming: one question at a time, two or three approaches with trade-offs, hard gate before building (research-skill-rigidity-spectrum)
- [Agent Skills (Osmani)](sources/addyosmani-agent-skills.md): interview-me: hypothesis plus confidence number, one question with a guess attached, explicit-yes gate (research-skill-rigidity-spectrum)
- [Generative AI without guardrails can harm learning](sources/pnas-bastani-generative-ai-can-harm-learning.md): the same model with tutor prompts (hints, not answers) protected learning; stance, not presence, decided the outcome (research-skill-rigidity-spectrum)
- [Do People Engage Cognitively with AI?](sources/arxiv-gajos-mamykina-ai-assistance-incidental-learning.md): explanation without recommendation produced learning and better decisions; recommendation plus explanation produced no learning (research-skill-rigidity-spectrum)
- [Don't Just Tell Me, Ask Me](sources/acm-danry-dont-just-tell-me-ask-me-chi2023.md): N=204; AI-framed questions beat causal explanations for spotting flawed logic, even vs an always-correct AI (research-skill-rigidity-spectrum)
- [Tutor CoPilot](sources/arxiv-wang-tutor-copilot-rct.md): RCT, 900 tutors; +4 points mastery, +9 for weaker tutors; tutors asked more guiding questions, gave fewer answers; about $20 per tutor per year (research-skill-rigidity-spectrum)
- [SocraticLM](sources/neurips-liu-socraticlm.md): Socratic stance fine-tuned on 35K dialogues and scored on a five-dimension pedagogy rubric; beats GPT-4 by 12% on teaching (research-skill-rigidity-spectrum)
- [Scaling AI in Education: Khanmigo](sources/aiengineer-jansepar-khanmigo-case-study.md): no intervention before submission, infer the student's path first, refuse to write the next paragraph; costs are latency, eval coverage, 70% grader accuracy (research-skill-rigidity-spectrum)
- [Homogenization Effects of LLMs on Creative Ideation](sources/arxiv-anderson-homogenization-effects-llm-ideation.md): ChatGPT users felt less responsible for their ideas (research-skill-rigidity-spectrum)
- [Modes for Creative Human-Computer Collaboration](sources/iccc-kantosalo-toivonen-alternating-cocreativity.md): alternating vs task-divided co-creativity as the two ways to share an artifact (research-skill-rigidity-spectrum)
- [Human-AI Interaction Designs for Co-Creative Systems](sources/arxiv-rezwana-maher-human-ai-interaction-designs-cocreative.md): N=38; an AI that explains its contributions is seen as more reliable and raises engagement (research-skill-rigidity-spectrum)

## identity-delegation: Identity and delegation (on-behalf-of)
Who an agent acts as when one agent or harness calls another: user tokens, service accounts, delegation chains, revocation and audit. Cuts across remote agents, MCP/A2A and shared sessions.
- [Small Models, Massive Wins (Beyond the Pilot)](sources/venturebeat-beyond-the-pilot-farhan-thawar.md): "River can see Slack messages ... data warehouse ... product management system"; "you can't go into a private channel" (competitive-teardown-shopify-river)
- [Inside Shopify's AI-first engineering playbook](sources/bvp-inside-shopifys-ai-first-engineering-playbook.md): MCP servers go "through the same auth flow that you have", so AI sees only what you can see (assistant tools, not River) (competitive-teardown-shopify-river)
- [River at Shopify (Internal Agents Map)](sources/internal-agents-shopify-river.md): credentials and sandbox marked "Not reported" in public sources (competitive-teardown-shopify-river)
- [Shopify's Aquifer, in the Open (Lobu)](sources/lobu-shopifys-aquifer-in-the-open.md): a proxy swaps placeholder tokens for real ones at egress, so the worker never holds secrets (vendor's own design, contrasted with Aquifer) (competitive-teardown-shopify-river)
- [Create information barriers in Slack](sources/slack-information-barriers-docs.md): barriers block DMs and huddles between IdP groups, but members "will still be able to interact in public and private channels" they share (competitive-teardown-shopify-river)
- [Build your own company brain (How I AI, Krishnamurthy)](sources/howiai-stripe-kai-krishnamurthy.md): 'agentic identity ... we haven't solved this yet'; agent identity tags the use case an agent serves, used for priority and load shedding after agents nearly took down core systems (competitive-teardown-stripe-knowledge-agents)
- [MCP Authorization spec](sources/mcp-authorization-spec-draft.md): OAuth 2.1 resource-server model; servers must not accept or pass through tokens issued for other audiences; so on-behalf-of access downstream needs token exchange or a vault (first-party spec). (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Cloudflare remote MCP](sources/cloudflare-remote-mcp-servers.md): the MCP server acts as OAuth provider to clients and OAuth client to GitHub/Google, issuing narrower tokens of its own (vendor). (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Sentry MCP + Seer](sources/sentry-mcp-server-seer.md): OAuth consent with selectable permission sets for a vendor agent (vendor docs; partly unverified). (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Copilot Studio A2A](sources/microsoft-copilot-studio-a2a.md): per-connection None/API key/OAuth; no user-identity propagation described. (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Claude Code cloud sessions](sources/anthropic-claude-code-cloud-sessions.md): credentials kept outside the VM behind a proxy; auto-fix replies post under the user's GitHub account (vendor docs). (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Ask HN A2A](sources/hn-ask-is-anyone-using-a2a.md): commenters: the open problems are who delegated authority, revocation and trusting claimed capability (anecdote). (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Cloudflare OS announcement](sources/cloudflare-os-announcement.md): agents start with zero access; typed bindings; Gatekeepers hold credentials; shared agents reflect the viewer's permissions via an observation log (vendor claim) (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Omnigent repo issue #11413](sources/github-omnigent-repo.md): session sharing did not separate chat access from host access to terminals and files (open P1 issue, 2026-10-23) (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [AI's real question isn't whether AGI arrives (The Deep View: Conversations, E48, Ahmad Al-Dahle)](sources/deepview-al-dahle-airbnb.md): security for agents acting on email and Slack is still being worked out (research-airbnb-spotify-product-practices)
- [Chesky says OpenAI tools not ready for ChatGPT tie-up with Airbnb app](sources/fortune-chesky-openai-not-ready-qwen.md): verified identity means a ChatGPT app would have to run "almost self-contained" (research-airbnb-spotify-product-practices)
- [Airbnb Q3 2024 earnings call](sources/airbnb-earnings-q3-2024.md): phase 3 support agent acts for the user on a yes (cancel, rebook) (research-airbnb-spotify-product-practices)
- [Airbnb Q3 2025 earnings call and shareholder letter](sources/airbnb-earnings-q3-2025.md): users cancel or change dates from the support chat (research-airbnb-spotify-product-practices)
- [MCP (Spotify Portal docs)](sources/spotify-portal-docs-mcp.md): static bearer tokens or OAuth via CIMD (research-airbnb-spotify-product-practices)
- [Buzz!](sources/block-eng-buzz.md): per-agent keypairs with owner-signed, scoped authorisation (research-block-product-practices)
- [Block's Playbook for Designing MCP Servers](sources/block-eng-playbook-designing-mcp-servers.md): OAuth on first use through SSO, minimum scopes, tokens in the OS keychain (research-block-product-practices)
- [Agent identity: a new access model for autonomous, team-wide AI](sources/claude-agent-identity-access-model.md): two reasons act-as-user breaks: autonomy (tasks run after the requester logs off) and multiple people steering a channel (section "Why 'act as the user' breaks down"). (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [Introducing the Claude apps gateway for Amazon Bedrock and Google Cloud](sources/claude-apps-gateway.md): OIDC relying party (Google Workspace, Entra ID, Okta); short-lived sessions, no long-lived secrets on laptops. (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [Agents you can coach: how Asana builds human-agent teams with Claude](sources/claude-asana-agents-you-can-coach.md): agents have their own profile (users, admins, instructions, skills, integrations, permissions) and access scoped to projects/documents/apps; Asana says an agent's effective access is bounded by the permissions of the person... (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [CISO's guide to agentic AI](sources/claude-ciso-guide-agentic-ai.md): "agentic identity spectrum": service account (single-purpose, no human identity, e.g. incident agent, Claude Tag) vs human credential (Cowork on a laptop); the middle, delegated identity in systems the person isn't watching,... (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [How Asana built AI Teammates on Claude Opus 4.6](sources/claude-customers-asana-ai-teammates.md): an AI Teammate has its own Asana account like any colleague; invoked by assignment, @mention or workflow rule. (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [Carvana turns Slack alerts into production fixes with Claude Tag](sources/claude-customers-carvana-claude-tag.md): one warehouse connection plus separate scoped identities per team (section "Managed agents with per-team identities"). (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [Centrally manage authorization for MCP connectors](sources/claude-enterprise-managed-mcp-auth.md): users' "personal identity passes through" via IdP login while per-connector OAuth grants disappear; access is inherited from existing IdP groups and roles (How it works; customer quote). (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [Building agents that reach production systems with MCP](sources/claude-mcp-production-patterns.md): CIMD client registration; vaults hold users' OAuth tokens and inject them per MCP connection (section "Lean on standardized auth"). (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [How Anthropic secures its AI-native software development lifecycle](sources/claude-securing-ai-native-sdlc-at-anthropic.md): the alert-triage agent is "a single-purpose system account agent with three permissions" (write docs, post in company channels, read production logs) and cannot deploy; fixes go through a separate agent-human reviewer system... (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [How healthcare organizations use Claude Tag](sources/claude-tag-healthcare-human-agent-teams.md): Insight Health pairs Tag (sees codebase and Linear) with its own Agent SDK agent Zeus on a BAA-covered API org that queries production data and masks PHI before Slack; deliberately different access per agent (Insight Health... (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [Claude Tag now supports personal connectors in channels](sources/claude-tag-personal-connectors.md): Claude reads the channel's GitHub through the channel connector and Priya's private doc "through Priya's Google Drive connector, separately from the channel's work"; actions via a personal connector appear in that tool's log... (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [Self-service data analytics in Slack: how Anthropic deploys Claude Tag for ad-hoc questions](sources/claude-tag-self-service-analytics.md): queries run as a service account, not the asker; "everyone who can mention the bot has the bot's data access", no per-user row-level security (section "Permission the service account deliberately"). (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [Zero Trust for AI agents](sources/claude-zero-trust-for-ai-agents.md): Ch 04 names "unscoped privilege inheritance" (manager agent passes full access to workers) and the confused-deputy problem; Ch 06 Phase 6 requires per-agent credentials and authorization checks at each hop of a multi-agent... (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [How to develop a Headless Product Strategy](sources/departmentofproduct-headless-product-strategy.md): WorkOS Agent Auth caps delegated sessions at user permissions ∩ agent ceiling, with step-up auth on sensitive calls (research-department-of-product-knowledge-series)
- [How to Manage AI Agents Effectively](sources/departmentofproduct-managing-ai-agents.md): Uber gives each agent its own cryptographic identity because "who authorised what" was lost across agent hops; Block's User Identity Delegation carries the human and the agent as two identities through every call. Second-hand. (research-department-of-product-knowledge-series)
- [Practical ways to use Claude Routines at work - a Guide for Product Teams](sources/departmentofproduct-claude-routines-for-product-teams.md): attached connectors are used, writes included, with no per-action approval, so the connector list is the run's permission boundary (research-department-of-product-knowledge-series)
- [AI Agent SDKs Explained](sources/departmentofproduct-agent-sdks-explained.md): 1Password lets agents fetch and rotate vault secrets. Stripe uses restricted keys and single-use virtual cards with spend limits (research-department-of-product-knowledge-series)
- [Asynchronous Authorization (Auth0 for AI Agents)](sources/auth0-docs-asynchronous-authorization.md): OpenID CIBA, optionally with OAuth RAR, so the approver sees the structured details (e.g. amount, payee) rather than a generic prompt. (first-party; research-dependency-agent)
- [Features of AgentCore Identity (Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Developer Guide)](sources/aws-agentcore-identity-features.md): supports client-credentials (2LO) and authorization-code (3LO) flows; "impersonation flow where agents can access resources using credentials provided to them" (Agent identity and access controls). (first-party; research-dependency-agent)
- [Enforce least-privilege authorization in multi-agent AI chains using Cedar](sources/aws-security-cedar-multi-agent-least-privilege.md): Cognito JWT claims are HMAC-signed into Cedar context; RFC 8693 issues a scoped on-behalf-of token to each downstream agent. (first-party; research-dependency-agent)
- [MCP Actions (Backstage AI docs)](sources/backstage-docs-mcp-actions.md): auth via OAuth Client ID Metadata Documents (recommended) after user approval in Backstage; static tokens described as "a temporary workaround until device authentication is completed"; DCR deprecated. (first-party; research-dependency-agent)
- [Building the future of finance in the age of AI](sources/fca-rusu-building-future-finance-age-ai.md): the trusted framework will cover "agent identity, delegated authority, accountability and execution", developed with industry, regulators and frontier labs (future work). (first-party; research-dependency-agent)
- [Agent Identity overview (Google Cloud IAM)](sources/google-cloud-iam-agent-identity-overview.md): acting for a user uses 3-legged OAuth via the Agent Identity auth manager; acting on its own authority uses its own identity or OIDC ID tokens; "logs show both the agent's and the user's identities" (Auth, Audit). (first-party; research-dependency-agent)
- [OAuth 2.0 Extension: On-Behalf-Of User Authorization for AI Agents (draft-oauth-ai-agents-on-behalf-of-user-02)](sources/ietf-draft-oauth-ai-agents-on-behalf-of-user.md): `requested_actor` at the authorisation endpoint binds the code to user, client and agent; the agent presents an `actor_token` at the token endpoint; the access token has the user in `sub`, the client in `azp`/`client_id`, the agent in `act.sub` (Mechanism). (first-party; research-dependency-agent)
- [RFC 8693: OAuth 2.0 Token Exchange](sources/ietf-rfc8693-oauth-token-exchange.md): delegation: "In a sense, A is an agent for B"; `act` claim identifies the current actor, nested for chains with the most recent outermost; only the current actor is used for access control, prior actors are informational; `may_act` states who is permitted to act for a subject (Sections 1.1, 4.1, 4.4). (first-party; research-dependency-agent)
- [Access packages for agent identities in Microsoft Entra](sources/microsoft-entra-agent-access-packages.md): packages can carry OAuth application permissions, delegated permissions (to assist a user), group memberships, or allowed directory roles; not app roles, SAP roles or SharePoint site roles (Prerequisites, Create). (first-party; research-dependency-agent)
- [Accelerating the Adoption of Software and AI Agent Identity and Authorization (NCCoE concept paper)](sources/nist-nccoe-agent-identity-authorization-concept-paper.md): asks for feedback on use cases, agent-specific challenges, current and emerging standards and technologies for agent identity and access management (announcement). (first-party; research-dependency-agent)
- [Understanding Cross App Access with Okta for AI Agents](sources/okta-support-cross-app-access-ai-agents.md): the agent uses an Identity Assertion Authorization Grant (ID-JAG) flow to exchange its ID token for an access token to the resource app (Flow). (first-party; research-dependency-agent)
- [Opal Security Launches Opal Zero to Make Least Privilege a Reality for Enterprise AI Agents](sources/opal-zero-launch-press-release.md): integrations with Okta Cross App Access, Claude Enterprise-Managed Authorization for MCP, Claude Compliance API; inventory from Okta, Entra, AgentCore, OpenAI, Cursor. (vendor-claim; research-dependency-agent)
- [Set self-service actions RBAC (Port)](sources/port-docs-self-service-action-rbac.md): an organisation token can trigger an action on behalf of another user with `run_as`; approvals can be granted or declined through the API. (first-party; research-dependency-agent)
- [Model Context Protocol Server (SailPoint Identity Security Cloud)](sources/sailpoint-docs-mcp-server.md): agents act on behalf of the user; request-for-others only if an admin has enabled it. (first-party; research-dependency-agent)
- [Community Wisdom: Evaluating startup equity ... MCPs vs. CLIs ...](sources/lenny-community-wisdom-knowledge-graph-mcp-cli.md): agent-built API skills pass credentials through inference; CLIs and MCP OAuth keep them out of model context (Thread 4) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [The coming AI security crisis | Sander Schulhoff](sources/lenny-podcast-sander-schulhoff-ai-security.md): "any data that AI has access to, the user can make it leak it. Any actions that it can possibly take, the user can make it take" (48:49) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [How we built Grok Bot in a month | Roman Ugarte](sources/lenny-podcast-roman-ugarte-grok-bot.md): each bot gets its own computer and credentials; sharing the user's machine is like sharing a laptop and credentials with a new hire forever (31:58) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [How OpenAI uses ChatGPT Sites (Kath Korevec)](sources/howiai-openai-korevec-chatgpt-sites.md): a shared site renders each viewer's own data through their own connector grants: "you see only your data on that site" (1:32, 8:04) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [OpenClaw: The complete guide](sources/lenny-newsletter-claire-vo-openclaw-guide.md): agent gets its own email and read-only calendar; with external channels it "might even impersonate you" (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [How Webflow's CPO built an AI chief of staff](sources/howiai-webflow-rachel-wolan-chief-of-staff.md): personal agent on the CPO's own Google API tokens with per-scope limits; "too much authority to act on my behalf" trimmed back by hand (11:26-12:57) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [From skeptic to true believer: How OpenClaw changed my life (Lenny's Podcast)](sources/lenny-podcast-claire-vo-openclaw.md): progressive trust like an EA: calendar, then read email, draft, send; agent listens only to one person on one channel (22:20-23:51) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [Agent identity: the access model behind Claude Tag](sources/claude-agent-identity-access-model.md): the two cases "act as the user" cannot cover: the task runs after the requester logs off, and several people steer one agent; "what can this agent do in this compartment?" (research-shared-persistent-agents)
- [Personal connectors for Claude Tag](sources/claude-tag-personal-connectors.md): the hybrid: unattended work under the channel identity, person-initiated reads on the requester's own connectors, each logged under the matching account; "personal connectors don't run unattended" (research-shared-persistent-agents)
- [Why we built our background agent (Ramp Inspect)](sources/ramp-builders-why-we-built-background-agent.md): PRs open with the requester's GitHub token so nobody approves their own agent's work: separation of duties by identity (research-shared-persistent-agents)
- [Buzz: a workspace for people and agents](sources/block-eng-buzz.md): each agent has its own keypair and an owner-signed, scoped authorisation; revoking the agent does not touch the human identity (research-shared-persistent-agents)
- [Cursor forum: Team Followups act on behalf of the creator](sources/cursor-forum-team-followups-act-on-behalf.md): a teammate's follow-up runs on the creator's OAuth tokens, "documented and intentional" per staff (research-shared-persistent-agents)
- [Claude Code scheduled tasks](sources/anthropic-claude-code-scheduled-tasks.md): tasks "belong to your individual claude.ai account", are not shared with teammates, and act as the creating user (research-shared-persistent-agents)
- [Agent identity (Ramp for Agents developer guide)](sources/ramp-agents-identity-guide.md): on-behalf-of agents run as the OAuth user; standalone agents get their own credentials and an accountable owner (early access) (research-shared-persistent-agents)
- [GitHub MCP Exploited](sources/invariantlabs-github-mcp-toxic-agent-flow.md): a public issue hijacks an agent into leaking private repos using its user's authority; mitigation is one repo per session (research-shared-persistent-agents)
- [Scheduled tasks (Codex automations docs)](sources/openai-codex-scheduled-tasks-docs.md): Team Tasks run in the cloud through a team service account (research-shared-persistent-agents)
- [Agent Interaction Guidelines](sources/linear-agent-interaction-guidelines.md): agents disclose agent status and use the same actions a human would (research-skill-rigidity-spectrum)
- [Amplitude MCP in Claude Code (Amplitude docs)](sources/amplitude-mcp-claude-code-docs.md): server inherits the authenticating user's Amplitude permissions and grants nothing extra. (user-story-mapping)
- [Dovetail MCP (Dovetail developer docs)](sources/dovetail-mcp-server-docs.md): access matches the user's own account/role (from search summary of the main Dovetail help page). (user-story-mapping)
- [Snowflake-managed MCP server (Snowflake docs)](sources/snowflake-managed-mcp-server-docs.md): 'Access to the MCP Server does not give access to the tools'; each tool needs its own grant; users sign in with own credentials. (user-story-mapping)
- [Notion MCP (Notion developer docs)](sources/notion-mcp-developer-docs.md): workspace owners manage allowed MCP clients in Settings; restricting clients requires Enterprise; org owners can list/revoke members' connections via Admin API. (user-story-mapping)
- [Getting started with the Atlassian Rovo MCP server](sources/atlassian-rovo-mcp-server-getting-started.md): OAuth 2.1 primary; actions respect each user's existing access controls; API token optional. (user-story-mapping)
- [Linear for Agents (developer docs)](sources/linear-developers-agents.md): assigning an issue to an agent sets it as delegate; the human stays assignee. (user-story-mapping)
- [What are Confluence's roles?](sources/atlassian-confluence-roles-space-permissions.md): role-based space access (Admin, Manager, Collaborator, Viewer, custom); public links, guest access and anonymous access are separate admin grants; 'you can't assign or remove roles that include permissions you don't have.' (user-story-mapping)
- [Add or remove page restrictions (Confluence)](sources/atlassian-confluence-page-restrictions.md): per-item states open / edit-restricted / restricted / restricted-by-parent; view restrictions inherit to children, edit restrictions do not; the Rovo MCP server can read and set these states. (user-story-mapping)
- [Generate code from a work item in Jira (Jira Coding Agent)](sources/atlassian-jira-coding-agent-generate-code.md): acts as the initiating user, who is PR and commit author; automations run as the connection owner (user-story-mapping)
- [View and manage agents in your Jira space](sources/atlassian-jira-manage-agents-in-space.md): agents run on their own account (needs a space role) or the triggering user's account (user-story-mapping)

## intent-factory-before-discovery: Accelerate the intent factory before discovery
Automating intent refinement and delivery has to come before using AI for higher-order discovery, or more ideas just swell the backlog. This sets the order of priorities for what a product agent should do first.
- [From Gut to Plan: The Thoughtful Execution Framework](sources/spotify-design-thoughtful-execution-framework.md): fixes "one goal, one idea"; when it fails you can't tell whether the design, hypothesis or problem was wrong (research-airbnb-spotify-product-practices)
- [Spotify Q4 2025 Earnings Call](sources/spotify-q4-2025-earnings-call.md): "When you have productivity on tap, what you need to have are very good plans" (research-airbnb-spotify-product-practices)
- [From localized to systematic speed (ELC Podcast ep. 245)](sources/elc-podcast-tyson-singer-systematic-speed.md): AI prototyping in "Think it", drawing on deep business context (16:49) (research-airbnb-spotify-product-practices)
- [A field guide to Claude Fable 5: Finding your unknowns](sources/claude-fable-finding-unknowns.md): four-quadrant framing (known knowns, known unknowns, unknown knowns, unknown unknowns) as the start of every task ("Knowing your unknowns"). (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [Head of Growth (Anthropic): "Claude is growing itself at this point"](sources/lenny-podcast-amol-avasare-anthropic-growth.md): with 20 engineers per PM, the PM adds more by improving "the why and the what ... by 5%" than by shipping features (47:52-49:30) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [Community Wisdom: Quarterly planning and AI ...](sources/lenny-community-wisdom-quarterly-planning.md): with day-long builds, planning "moved downstream of the evidence instead of upstream of it"; counterpoint: large-org planning is coordination and customer change-absorption (thread 1) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [OpenAI Codex lead on the new shape of product work | Andrew Ambrosino](sources/lenny-podcast-ambrosino-codex-product-work.md): plan detail inversely proportional to horizon; prototype every idea and re-test each at every model leap; the Codex app would have failed three months earlier with the same shape (32:00, 33:31) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [Why humans are AI's biggest bottleneck (Alexander Embiricos)](sources/lenny-podcast-embiricos-codex-human-bottleneck.md): with building easy, the scarce competency is "really meaningful understanding of the problems that a certain customer has" (54:18) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [Community Wisdom: How PMs are using AI coding tools](sources/lenny-community-wisdom-pms-ai-coding-tools.md): a "project manager" agent with its own context checks the requirements "for dependencies and unanswered questions" before build agents start (thread 4) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [Community Wisdom: When AI velocity outpaces your product strategy ...](sources/lenny-community-wisdom-ai-velocity-strategy.md): "building got cheap, but confusion didn't ... slow down on decisions, not on execution"; "what to ship" and "whether to ship" converging (thread 1) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [Community Wisdom: speeding up discovery in a big org](sources/lenny-community-wisdom-discovery-big-org.md): once designs change in an afternoon, "the constraint becomes how fast someone can decide"; a one-line decisions log (thread 2) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [Why LinkedIn is turning PMs into AI-powered "full stack builders"](sources/lenny-podcast-tomer-cohen-full-stack-builder.md): research meant "10 to 15 sources of information" and stacked reviews (design, privacy, security) made small features take six months; "the work itself is not complex, but the process we made very complex" (7:07) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [Anthropic's CPO on what comes next (Mike Krieger)](sources/lenny-podcast-mike-krieger-anthropic-cpo.md): with ~90% of code AI-written, "there's an upstream bottleneck, which is decision making and alignment"; Krieger seeks a "minimum viable strategy" and hasn't got it right (14:25) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [An AI state of the union (Simon Willison)](sources/lenny-podcast-simon-willison-state-of-ai.md): spec-to-implementation went from "three weeks" to "maybe ... three hours"; "Now the bottlenecks are everywhere else" (21:27) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [From Figma to Claude Code and back](sources/howiai-figma-design-code-loop.md): Figma's design role "really moved upstream" to planning and "what should we be building", because building is faster (19:11) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [AI is critical for humanity's survival (Jeetu Patel)](sources/lenny-podcast-jeetu-patel-cisco-ai.md): Cisco: coding is the clear win, but other functions are "not as easy" (6:47) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [Community Wisdom: when engineering outpaces product](sources/lenny-community-wisdom-engineering-outpaces-product.md): a fully AI-enabled team's engineers ship so fast "the bottleneck becomes writing specs/stories fast enough"; one engineer shipped every feature from a call transcript to staging before scoping, half judged bloat; "decision-making velocity" now hurts more than delivery velocity (thread 2) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [How AI is reshaping the product role (Udezue)](sources/lenny-podcast-udezue-ai-reshaping-pm-role.md): fixed PM-to-engineering time ratios are "exploding"; a client goes from pitch call to prototype in four hours; "PRD writing is insufficient at the moment" (8:37) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [Shape Up (Ryan Singer)](sources/lenny-podcast-ryan-singer-shape-up.md): projects fail to ship because "the input at the very beginning of the process is too unclear"; the dominant failure is "not enough detail" (47:26, 1:38:37) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [Building and Accelerating the Intent Factory](sources/geoff-building-accelerating-intent-factory.md): the core thesis and order of operations (§Introduction) (research-product-agent-and-harness)

## leadership-permission-mandate: Leadership permission and mandates drive AI-native ways of working
New ways of working with agents (no specs, prototypes before meetings, PMs and designers shipping code) spread only when leaders explicitly permit or mandate them, and change hiring, reviews and rituals to match; tools alone get the top ~5%. No existing slug fits: enablement-by-product is about the product teaching its own use, and org-learning-loop is about sharing wins, not authority and incentives. Bears on the adoption-model dimension.
- [Founder Mode](sources/paulgraham-founder-mode.md): founders "gaslit" into delegating; the founder's mandate as the operating system (research-airbnb-spotify-product-practices)

## leadership-review-cadence: Leadership review cadence as the control system
A fixed schedule of leadership reviews, scored by program managers, decides pace and direction, so the review rather than the spec is the main decision point. An agent could prepare or record those reviews.
- [Brian Chesky's new playbook for product, leadership, and growth](sources/lenny-podcast-brian-chesky-new-playbook.md): every project reviewed every 1/2/4/8/12 weeks; a head program manager scores it green, yellow or red; Chesky sees a "semi-assembly" weekly (28:39-29:54) (research-airbnb-spotify-product-practices)
- [Navigating the intersection of design and business (Config 2023)](sources/figma-config-2023-brian-chesky.md): "I'm gonna be the chief editor"; the top 30-40 people as "one neural network, one brain" (research-airbnb-spotify-product-practices)
- [Airbnb CEO Brian Chesky on the gospel of Steve Jobs and what founder mode really means](sources/verge-decoder-chesky-founder-mode-2024.md): directs speak first, the CEO decides, "Ninety percent of time I'm agreeing"; all VPs dual-report to him (research-airbnb-spotify-product-practices)
- [Decoder: Brian Chesky (2021)](sources/verge-decoder-chesky-2021-functional-org.md): "15 hours a week of design and marketing reviews"; decision-making pulled in "like an orchestra conductor" (research-airbnb-spotify-product-practices)
- [Founder Mode](sources/paulgraham-founder-mode.md): predicts skip-level meetings become normal; warns founder mode will be misused by founders who can't delegate (research-airbnb-spotify-product-practices)
- [Vlad Loktev on Lenny's Podcast](sources/lenny-podcast-vlad-loktev-airbnb.md): Chesky asked many questions and changed his mind; senior people in every detail "could slow it down" (1:17-1:19) (research-airbnb-spotify-product-practices)
- [TBM 255: The New Airbnb](sources/cutler-perri-tbm-255-new-airbnb.md): "Do wartime practices work in peacetime?… Who does he trust to tell him what he's doing has stopped working?" (research-airbnb-spotify-product-practices)
- [Brian Chesky's new blueprint for Airbnb — and Silicon Valley](sources/semafor-chesky-new-blueprint-2026.md): still "editor-in-chief" in Oct 2026; admits "huge pushback"; co-hiring manager for the top 200 roles (research-airbnb-spotify-product-practices)
- [Chesky says AI writes 60% of its code](sources/fortune-chesky-ai-60-percent-code-founder-mode.md): Chesky closely tracks AI initiatives, token use and AI output (research-airbnb-spotify-product-practices)
- [Airbnb unveils 'Services' and a brand new app](sources/wallpaper-chesky-airbnb-new-app-interview.md): "I basically sat with these teams… every single day" through the 2025 rebuild (research-airbnb-spotify-product-practices)
- [Teo Connor on designing the new Airbnb app](sources/designweek-teo-connor-new-airbnb-app.md): the CEO is "always in the pixels… asking about the radius of a button" (research-airbnb-spotify-product-practices)

## legible-org-for-agents: Make the organisation legible to agents
Roadmaps, specs, tickets and tools must be agent-readable so agents can answer and act. Related: [[compounding-context-repo]].
- [What product looks like when coding is solved | Geoff Charles (Ramp CPO)](sources/lenny-podcast-geoff-charles-product-when-coding-solved.md): "the organization needs to be legible to your agents"; Gadget (competitive-teardown-ramp-glass)
- [Ramp: Lessons from Building a New AI Product - The Pragmatic Summit](sources/pragmatic-engineer-ramp-lessons-new-ai-product.md): shared internal tool catalog of hundreds of tools (competitive-teardown-ramp-glass)
- [Meet Ramp Research: Our Agentic Data Analyst](sources/ramp-builders-meet-ramp-research.md): domain owners wrote docs as a file system the data agent reads; dbt/Looker/Snowflake metadata indexed (competitive-teardown-ramp-glass)
- [Under the River](sources/shopify-engineering-under-the-river.md): 2024 monorepo + Nix bets; "agent-friendly ≈ human-friendly"; "The work to make a codebase legible to an agent is simply the debt you owe to your human engineers" (competitive-teardown-shopify-river)
- [How Shopify powers "World" (Flagship)](sources/flagship-ai-first-series-2-shopify-tectonix-nix.md): Nix reproducibility narrows agent build errors to pure code errors (competitive-teardown-shopify-river)
- [Build your own company brain (How I AI, Krishnamurthy)](sources/howiai-stripe-kai-krishnamurthy.md): org chart, projects/OKRs and a tiered data catalog are what let Kai 'do the right thing' without users explaining their job (competitive-teardown-stripe-knowledge-agents)
- [An Inside Look Into How This $159B Tech Company Ships So Fast](sources/youtube-notmybusiness-inside-stripe-ships-fast.md): Orbit plans by 'reading files in our code base, it's reading Trailhead' (internal docs); Compass tracks projects (competitive-teardown-stripe-knowledge-agents)
- [Inside Stripe's Engineering Culture: Part 2](sources/pragmaticengineer-inside-stripe-engineering-culture-part-2.md): pre-AI internal tools: Trailhead (docs structured like the external docs), Compass (project status, linked docs, standups), Home intranet search (2024) (competitive-teardown-stripe-knowledge-agents)
- [How Airbnb achieved metric consistency at scale (Minerva)](sources/airbnb-tech-minerva-metric-consistency.md): one API serves the same numbers to dashboards, notebooks, experiments and executive reports (research-airbnb-spotify-product-practices)

- [Scaling Agile @ Spotify with Tribes, Squads, Chapters & Guilds](sources/kniberg-ivarsson-scaling-agile-spotify.md): a System Owner per system, the seed of catalog ownership (p.13) (research-airbnb-spotify-product-practices)
- [Spotify Engineering Culture - Part 1](sources/kniberg-spotify-engineering-culture-part-1.md): 100+ decoupled systems, each owned by one squad (research-airbnb-spotify-product-practices)
- [Announcing TechDocs](sources/backstage-announcing-techdocs.md): one component, one repo, one doc site, with the owner on the catalog page (research-airbnb-spotify-product-practices)
- [How Spotify Thinks (Invest Like the Best EP.424)](sources/colossus-ilb-gustav-soderstrom-how-spotify-thinks.md): "my biggest job to enable AI is … exposing all this data" via APIs (~32:08) (research-airbnb-spotify-product-practices)
