- [Initiatives (Linear docs)](sources/linear-docs-initiatives.md): Initiatives are workspace-level containers for projects tied to a shared objective; IDs like I-<n>. (user-story-mapping)
- [Documents (Linear docs)](sources/linear-docs-documents.md): Documents attach to projects, initiatives, teams, issues or cycles; same editor as issues; realtime collaboration; version history including agent edits; templates at workspace/team level. (user-story-mapping)
- [About Projects (GitHub Docs)](sources/github-docs-about-projects.md): Project = adaptable table, board and roadmap integrating issues and PRs, at user or organisation level; two-way sync with issues. (user-story-mapping)
- [Glean Enterprise Graph (product page)](sources/glean-enterprise-graph-product-page.md): entities are inferred automatically by machine learning rather than declared. (user-story-mapping)
- [Atlassian Rovo MCP server: supported tools](sources/atlassian-rovo-mcp-server-supported-tools.md): verbatim re-read: getTeamworkGraphContext returns 'all relationships and linked objects in one traversal' from Jira, Confluence, Goals/Projects/Focus Areas, people, DevOps, Loom, Compass entry points; Confluence spaces carry agent-readable 'space instructions' (getConfluenceSpaceInstructions / setConfluenceSpaceInstructions). (user-story-mapping)
- [Scopes (Teamwork Graph API)](sources/atlassian-teamwork-graph-scopes.md): 'All Teamwork Graph API scopes are read-only'; a missing scope returns success and empty rows ('fails closed rather than leaking data'), so an agent cannot tell 'no data' from 'no permission'. (user-story-mapping)
- [Work with Jira Delivery agent](sources/atlassian-rovo-jira-delivery-agent.md): documented TWG work-item context returns related PRs, commits, branches, pages and hierarchy; user summary returns work items, pages, PRs, Loom videos, projects and goals (user-story-mapping)
- [How we're evolving Jira for AI-native software development](sources/atlassian-blog-jira-ai-native-software-development.md): 'the SDLC needs to become legible to agents without becoming less accountable to humans' (user-story-mapping)

## levels-of-automation-frameworks: Levels-of-automation frameworks applied to agents
Human-factors and HCI models (Sheridan-Verplank, Parasuraman et al., Shneiderman, Horvitz, HAX) that predate LLMs and already split autonomy by task stage and separate automation from human control.
- [A model for types and levels of human interaction with automation](sources/ieee-parasuraman-sheridan-wickens-types-and-levels-of-automation.md): automate acquisition, analysis, decision and action separately; evaluate on workload, awareness, complacency, skill degradation (research-skill-rigidity-spectrum)
- [Human-Centered AI: Reliable, Safe and Trustworthy](sources/ijhci-shneiderman-human-centered-ai-reliable-safe-trustworthy.md): human control and automation are two axes; aim for high on both (research-skill-rigidity-spectrum)
- [Principles of mixed-initiative user interfaces](sources/acm-horvitz-principles-of-mixed-initiative-user-interfaces.md): act, ask or stay quiet per moment from uncertainty and expected cost/benefit (research-skill-rigidity-spectrum)
- [Guidelines for Human-AI Interaction](sources/microsoft-hax-guidelines-for-human-ai-interaction.md): 18 guidelines incl. efficient invocation, dismissal, correction, scope services when in doubt (research-skill-rigidity-spectrum)
- [smolagents: agency levels](sources/huggingface-smolagents-agency-levels.md): six-row agency table; default to coded workflow unless it falls short too often (research-skill-rigidity-spectrum)
- [Humans and Automation: Use, Misuse, Disuse, Abuse](sources/sage-parasuraman-riley-humans-and-automation-use-misuse-disuse-abuse.md): abuse = automation designed without regard to the human's remaining role (research-skill-rigidity-spectrum)

## memory-architecture: Memory as inspectable files from an offline pipeline
Agent memory built on first connection, refreshed by a periodic pipeline, read-only during sessions.
- [How We Built Glass: Vibe Coding a Product Used by 700 People](sources/x-shanebuchan-how-we-built-glass.md): 24h pipeline, write-once-read-many memory files (competitive-teardown-ramp-glass)
- [We Built Every Employee at Ramp Their Own AI Coworker](sources/x-sebgoddijn-glass-article.md): memory built from authenticated connections, 24h synthesis and cleanup (competitive-teardown-ramp-glass)
- [Tobi Lütke: AI Agents, Better Decisions (Knowledge Project)](sources/fs-knowledge-project-tobi-lutke-ai-agents.md): River "dreams" off-hours over the day's threads and rewrites skill files; per-person and per-channel memory injected at session start (competitive-teardown-shopify-river)
- [How River takes security work from a fix to merge](sources/shopify-engineering-river-vulnerability-remediation.md): the work ledger is "useful memory, but it isn't the operational truth"; each entry a claim to re-check (competitive-teardown-shopify-river)
- [How Stripe Built Kai on Deep Agents (LangChain)](sources/langchain-how-stripe-built-kai-deep-agents.md): Kai keeps session state in an S3-backed virtual filesystem; sandbox calls sync files in and out so the agent sees one persistent file environment per session (competitive-teardown-stripe-knowledge-agents)
- [Use Claude Code in the cloud (Claude Code on the web docs)](sources/anthropic-claude-code-cloud-sessions.md): only the conversation history is restored when an expired environment is reopened; running shell commands, subagents and session-scoped scheduled tasks are not (Environment expired) (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Scaling Managed Agents: Decoupling the brain from the hands](sources/anthropic-engineering-scaling-managed-agents.md): the session log is the durable store outside the context window; getEvents() allows positional slices and rewind; irreversible compaction is avoided in the store (Session as durable event store) (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Long-running agents (Cloudflare Agents SDK docs)](sources/cloudflare-agents-long-running-agents.md): state survives via setState/this.sql/scheduled tasks/fiber stash; lost: in-memory fields, timers, in-flight fetches, closures (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Claude Code deletes conversation history after 30 days by default](sources/itdaily-claude-code-30-day-transcript-deletion.md): cleanupPeriodDays defaults to 30, run on each startup; users say there is no warning or recovery; deletion keys on file modification time so backups or sync can trigger removal of active files (per GitHub discussions cited) (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [LangGraph persistence (checkpointers, threads, stores)](sources/langchain-langgraph-persistence.md): checkpointers keep thread-scoped state keyed by thread_id; stores hold cross-thread data (preferences, facts); a parent graph may not see subgraph state immediately because of checkpoint namespaces (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [The AI Agent Doom Loop: Why Your Agent Keeps Making the Same Mistake](sources/unblocked-agent-doom-loop.md): claims shared team context must be automatic, reasoned (the why), current and cross-source; CLAUDE.md-style files 'help only partly' (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Effective harnesses for long-running agents](sources/anthropic-effective-harnesses-long-running-agents.md): first-party: feature list, progress file, git history and init script as cross-session handoff memory (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Context Engineering for AI Agents: Lessons from Building Manus](sources/manus-context-engineering-lessons.md): first-party: filesystem as external context, todo recitation (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Hosting the Agent SDK](sources/anthropic-agent-sdk-hosting.md): first-party: SessionStore mirrors transcripts only; CLAUDE.md memory and working-dir artifacts need separate storage and leak across tenants by default (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Scaling Knowledge at Airbnb (Knowledge Repo)](sources/airbnb-tech-scaling-knowledge-knowledge-repo.md): topic tags, subscriptions, browse by time, author or topic (research-airbnb-spotify-product-practices)
- [AI's real question isn't whether AGI arrives (The Deep View: Conversations, E48, Ahmad Al-Dahle)](sources/deepview-al-dahle-airbnb.md): the CTO keeps "a context graph with memory", a counterpart CTO agent, and sub-agents modelled on each exec peer that review his writing (research-airbnb-spotify-product-practices)
- [Configuring Agents in Buzz](sources/block-eng-configuring-agents-in-buzz.md): agents keep core and cold memory inside the workspace (research-block-product-practices)
- [Projects redesigned: from folder to conversation](sources/claude-code-projects-redesigned.md): every thread adds to and draws from a shared project memory (e.g. release moved to Friday, why the export was dropped, who to check with before touching billing); also remembers working and communication style. (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [Agent harness design: 3 patterns for harnessing Claude's intelligence](sources/claude-harness-design-three-patterns.md): prefers model-chosen persistence (compaction, a memory folder of files) over retrieval infrastructure; Opus 4.6 Pokémon memory: 10 organised files and a learnings file versus Sonnet 3.5's 31 transcript-like files (Pattern 2,... (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [New in Claude Managed Agents: dreaming, outcomes, and multiagent orchestration](sources/claude-managed-agents-dreaming-outcomes.md): memory captures learnings per agent; dreaming "refines that memory between sessions, pulling shared learnings across agents"; can update automatically or have changes reviewed first (§Build self-improving agents with dreaming). (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [Memory for Claude Managed Agents: agents that learn across sessions](sources/claude-managed-agents-memory.md): memory mounts onto a filesystem so the agent uses bash and code execution on it; memories are files exportable and manageable by API (sections "How memory works", "Portable memories"). (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [Claude's memory works everywhere, and you decide what's in it](sources/claude-memory-everywhere.md): memory updates "as you chat" rather than by post-conversation summary; stored as a list of short files under Topics that the user can read, edit, delete, pause or reset ("Memory updates as you chat"; "See and edit"). (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [Steering Claude Code: when to use CLAUDE.md, skills, hooks, and subagents](sources/claude-steering-claude-code.md): per-method compaction behaviour (root CLAUDE.md re-read after compaction; invoked skills re-injected up to a shared budget, oldest dropped first; hooks bypass compaction) (summary table). (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [How Warp builds self-improving agents on Claude](sources/claude-warp-self-improving-agents.md): sidebar distinguishes skills (procedural, stable, changed deliberately) from memory (auto-written at inference time, always changing). (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [Zero Trust for AI agents](sources/claude-zero-trust-for-ai-agents.md): Ch 06 Phase 7 memory isolation, hash-based context integrity checks at every retrieval, source tagging, TTLs and versioned memory rollback. (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [How to build a Self-improving Product](sources/departmentofproduct-self-improving-product.md): a reflection agent rewrites one markdown memory file per product area each cycle (worked, didn't, what the team keeps rejecting) (research-department-of-product-knowledge-series)
- [Practical ways to use Claude Routines at work - a Guide for Product Teams](sources/departmentofproduct-claude-routines-for-product-teams.md): the competitor tracker keeps state between runs as a snapshot file in the repo and diffs against it each run (research-department-of-product-knowledge-series)
- [How to use /loops, /goals and other Powerful Slash Commands as a Non-Engineer](sources/departmentofproduct-loops-goals-slash-commands.md): /init writes CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md as a standing project briefing read at the start of every session (research-department-of-product-knowledge-series)
- [Community Wisdom: Evaluating startup equity ... MCPs vs. CLIs ...](sources/lenny-community-wisdom-knowledge-graph-mcp-cli.md): plain markdown vault as agent memory; members warn it turns to noise within weeks without a trusted vs captured split (Thread 3) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [OpenAI Codex lead on the new shape of product work | Andrew Ambrosino](sources/lenny-podcast-ambrosino-codex-product-work.md): users build Obsidian/Notion "mind palaces" for agents; "You shouldn't have to do that. There should be a memory feature" (47:58) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [OpenAI's Head of ChatGPT ... | Tibo Sottiaux](sources/lenny-podcast-sottiaux-chatgpt-dots.md): Dots combines two-plus years of coherent-memory research with the Codex harness and 24/7 running (15:14) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [Claude Code for product managers (Teresa Torres)](sources/howiai-teresa-torres-claude-code-pm.md): small topic context files behind index files, routed from a global CLAUDE.md; project-level CLAUDE.md holds the tag taxonomy (11:29, 28:42-30:13) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [5 OpenClaw agents run my home (Jesse Genet)](sources/howiai-jesse-genet-openclaw-agents.md): SOUL.md per agent and "decision files" to make choices stick (show notes, 13:09, 44:00) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [Community Wisdom: ... AI agents and data integrity ...](sources/lenny-community-wisdom-agents-data-integrity.md): inspectable semantic layer that the agent may update when prompted, as it learns in conversation (thread 3) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [How Grok Bot designers use AI agents ...](sources/howiai-grok-bot-designers-agents.md): after a failure, tell the bot to "memorize this" so it follows the learned script next time (39:43) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [OpenClaw: The complete guide](sources/lenny-newsletter-claire-vo-openclaw-guide.md): per-agent identity as markdown files (AGENTS, SOUL, IDENTITY, TOOLS, USER) read at every start (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [Claude Cowork 101](sources/howiai-jj-englert-cowork-101.md): a "brain" preferences file plus a generated workspace map routing Claude to the right folder and skill (7:52, 10:44) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [Build your personal AI copilot](sources/lenny-newsletter-tal-raviv-ai-copilot.md): "a transparent, curated memory that's completely under your control" in place of built-in memory (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [How Webflow's CPO built an AI chief of staff](sources/howiai-webflow-rachel-wolan-chief-of-staff.md): everything in Markdown; monthly regenerated summary of Webflow releases; each prep doc saved as a file any agent can reuse (25:16-26:35) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [Community Wisdom: ... sharing Claude Code context across a team](sources/lenny-community-wisdom-claude-context-sharing.md): shared file stores can't show who changed context, why, or what's trustworthy, or lock finished files; one team is building its own context system (thread 5) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [How to build AI product sense](sources/lenny-newsletter-ai-product-sense-part-1.md): memory "is just a text file prepended to every conversation" (AGENTS.md); put persistent context in memory and task context in retrieval, since memory costs context in every chat (Step 9) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [Community Wisdom: Managing fragmented AI usage](sources/lenny-community-wisdom-fragmented-ai-usage.md): "unified memory layer across the assistants is still absent" (thread 1) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [How I turned Claude into a self-improving PM assistant (Daniel Blum, Melio)](sources/howiai-melio-daniel-blum-pm-assistant.md): CLAUDE.md "routing brain" loads topic memory files (role, people, priorities, decisions, voice) kept locally; the morning brief saves unknown jargon to context; cloud schedules can't reach that local memory, so workflows are run manually (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [Code with Claude: The 5 biggest updates explained](sources/howiai-code-with-claude-updates.md): Anthropic's "Dreams" memory system pitched for long-term agent behaviour (show notes only) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [From skeptic to true believer: How OpenClaw changed my life (Lenny's Podcast)](sources/lenny-podcast-claire-vo-openclaw.md): manage context, not "harden memory": write to memory before compaction; hand-edit TOOLS.md because agents forget their tools (1:09:37-1:11:18) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [How Claude remembers your project (Claude Code docs)](sources/anthropic-claude-code-memory-docs.md): CLAUDE.md (human-written instructions) vs auto memory (Claude-written learnings; first 200 lines or 25KB loaded each session). (user-story-mapping)
- [Organize work with projects (Claude Cowork docs)](sources/anthropic-cowork-projects-docs.md): a dedicated project-scoped memory store persisting across sessions; archiving deletes metadata including memory but not local files. (user-story-mapping)

## meta-harness: Meta harness
A layer that runs, governs or abstracts over several harnesses.
- [Scaling Managed Agents: Decoupling the brain from the hands](sources/anthropic-engineering-scaling-managed-agents.md): harness is explicitly treated as replaceable behind stable interfaces ('brains' stateless, 'hands' = execute(name,input)->string); cited example: context resets needed for Sonnet 4.5 became unnecessary with Opus 4.5 (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [CData on Managed Agents](sources/cdata-claude-managed-agents-meta-harness.md): independent-ish: frames Managed Agents as a meta-harness and lists lock-in, memory/trace portability and reliability as trade-offs. (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Harness Engineering: ... Eleven Systems](sources/arxiv-harness-engineering-eleven-systems.md): independent: Omnigent analysed as the first meta-harness; claims harnesses are becoming importable SDKs while framework vendors ship harnesses (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [AI SDK: Agents overview](sources/vercel-ai-sdk-agents-docs.md): first-party: a general SDK adding a HarnessAgent adapter for Claude Code, Codex, Pi (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Introducing Omnigent](sources/databricks-omnigent-meta-harness-launch.md): defines the horizontal sense: a layer 'above the agents you already use' with composition, control, collaboration (vendor claim, 2026-06-13, Apache-2.0 alpha) (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [omnigent-ai/omnigent repo](sources/github-omnigent-repo.md): runner + server, 13+ harnesses, 12 sandbox providers, ~11k stars; open issues include sharing not separating chat from host access (#11413) and OIDC/Entra login failing (first-party repo, 2026-10-24) (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Contextual Policies in Omnigent](sources/databricks-omnigent-contextual-policies.md): stateful allow/deny/ask policies applied across every wrapped agent (vendor claim) (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Atlan Omnigent explainer](sources/atlan-omnigent-explainer.md): alpha OSS, Beta on Databricks; harness support tiers; advises a pilot, not a standard (vendor-biased) (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [HN Omnigent thread](sources/hn-omnigent-launch-thread.md): 15 points, 4 comments; little organic discussion found (anecdote) (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Scaling Managed Agents](sources/anthropic-scaling-managed-agents.md): Anthropic's own text calls Managed Agents 'a meta-harness' (2026-04-08), so the term predates Omnigent in first-party use (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [CodePick buyer's guide](sources/codepick-meta-harness-guide.md): term is NOT settled; horizontal (compose harnesses) vs vertical (optimise one harness's code) senses; no standard yet (independent) (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Meta-Harness paper](sources/arxiv-meta-harness-optimization.md): the vertical sense: an outer-loop optimiser over harness code (arXiv 2026-03-30) (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Daniel Vaughan: Pi as coordinator](sources/danielvaughan-meta-harness-pattern-pi.md): DIY meta-harness via `codex exec`/`claude -p`; cost fan-out ~23-25 sessions, debugging opacity, approvals bypassed in shared CI (independent practitioner) (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Garrit Franke](sources/garrit-meta-harness-parallel-agents.md), [Claude Squad](sources/github-claude-squad.md), [Conductor](sources/conductor-build-homepage.md): 'meta harness' in practice often means a local parallel-session manager (worktrees, notifications), with no governance layer (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Vibe Kanban shutdown](sources/vibekanban-shutdown.md): orchestrator UI company shut down 2026-04-10 for lack of a business model; local app continues community-maintained (first-party) (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Nx Polygraph](sources/nx-polygraph-meta-harness.md): another vendor use: agent-agnostic, repository graph + session graph (vendor claim) (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Warp Oz multi-harness](sources/warp-oz-multi-harness.md): hosted/self-hostable control plane running Claude Code, Codex and Warp Agent with shared audit and credit caps (vendor claim, 2026-05-20) (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Cloudflare Flue / Agents SDK](sources/cloudflare-flue-agents-platform.md): platform-level layering (framework / harness / runtime); does not wrap Claude Code or Codex (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Customize Claude Code with mods in TypeScript](sources/claude-code-mods.md): harness behaviour itself is replaceable; built-in features shipping as mods; plan to "pare Claude Code down to a small core" (section "Swap built-in features"). (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [How Cresta turned CX expertise into an agent builder on the Claude Agent SDK](sources/claude-cresta-agent-builder-evals.md): Conductor is "a self-improving meta-agent" that helps developers build and improve other agents (§A meta-agent that helps build the next agent). (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [Are Agent Harnesses the new "secret sauce" for Product Teams?](sources/departmentofproduct-agent-harnesses-secret-sauce.md): presents the Stanford Meta-Harness optimiser to PMs as "self-improving harnesses" (the optimiser sense of the term); calls it not production-ready (research-department-of-product-knowledge-series)
- [What is parallel AI agent coding? An in-depth guide for product teams](sources/departmentofproduct-parallel-agent-coding.md): GitHub Agent HQ as a multi-vendor agent command centre; Osmani warns that normalising agents tends to the lowest common denominator (research-department-of-product-knowledge-series)
- [Community Wisdom: sharing Claude Code skills across the org](sources/lenny-community-wisdom-sharing-skills.md): a member's company distributes a Go "meta-harness" orchestrating dozens of opencode sessions with plan/implement/review/QA roles, file-based handoff, TUI and headless CI modes (thread 1) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [How I turned Claude into a self-improving PM assistant (Daniel Blum, Melio)](sources/howiai-melio-daniel-blum-pm-assistant.md): a PM's personal Cowork/Claude Code plugin with four chained workflows (weekly prep, morning brief, open loops, self-improvement) that he says runs 70-80% of his workday (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)

## method-as-harness: Method as harness
An expert team's method (how to frame a question, pick evidence, record decisions) is wrapped around the model as a shared package, so non-experts can run reproducible, auditable work and each run improves the method.
- [Beyond the model: Engineering AI infra with scientific judgement](sources/airbnb-tech-insight-miner-agent-harness.md): Insight Miner encodes extract/embed/cluster plus hard-example mining and contrastive labelling as a shared package so text investigations are reproducible and auditable; months of work become days (research-airbnb-spotify-product-practices)

Analytics vendors' agents and MCP servers for metric Q&A and monitoring; evidence is mostly vendor claims.

## model-judge-biases: Known biases of model judges and their mitigations
Position, verbosity, self-preference and weak reasoning grading in LLM judges, and the procedural fixes (order swapping, length control, judge separation, references, escalation) that a model-judged gate needs.
- [Judging LLM-as-a-Judge](sources/arxiv-zheng-judging-llm-as-a-judge.md): position consistency GPT-4 65%, Claude-v1 23.8%; repetitive-list attack fooled two of three judges 91.3%; self-favouring +10 and +25 points; swap-and-tie, few-shot (65% to 77.5%, 4x cost), reference grading (research-skill-rigidity-spectrum)
- [Large Language Models are not Fair Evaluators](sources/arxiv-llms-are-not-fair-evaluators.md): order swap let Vicuna-13B beat ChatGPT 66 of 80; entropy across orderings triggers human review (research-skill-rigidity-spectrum)
- [LLM Evaluators Recognize and Favor Their Own Generations](sources/arxiv-llm-evaluators-favor-own-generations.md): self-preference tracks self-recognition; grade with a different model (research-skill-rigidity-spectrum)
- [Length-Controlled AlpacaEval](sources/arxiv-length-controlled-alpacaeval.md): regressing out length raised Arena correlation 0.94 to 0.98 (research-skill-rigidity-spectrum)
- [G-Eval](sources/arxiv-g-eval.md): authors flag bias toward model-written text (research-skill-rigidity-spectrum)
- [Rubrics as Rewards](sources/arxiv-rubrics-as-rewards.md): structured rubrics reduce variance across judge sizes vs Likert scoring (research-skill-rigidity-spectrum)
- [HealthBench](sources/arxiv-openai-healthbench.md): grader meta-evaluated on 60,896 physician-graded items; agreement ceiling equals expert-expert agreement (research-skill-rigidity-spectrum)
- [PaperBench](sources/arxiv-openai-paperbench.md): judge F1 ranges 0.59 to 0.84 across models; cost 0.83 F1 at $66 vs 0.84 at $830 (research-skill-rigidity-spectrum)
- [TICKing All the Boxes](sources/arxiv-tick-checklist-evaluation.md): checklists steady human raters too (0.194 to 0.256 agreement) (research-skill-rigidity-spectrum)

## onboarding-as-code: Onboarding as code: intake as a schema, approvals as policy
Scaffolder templates, promises, workload specifications, no-code modules, portal registration and data-product access requests as typed intakes, and where approval is or is not encoded beside them.
- [MCP Actions (Backstage AI docs)](sources/backstage-docs-mcp-actions.md): `scaffolder:*` actions let an agent create software from templates (multi-server example). (first-party; research-dependency-agent)
- [Writing Templates (Backstage Software Templates)](sources/backstage-docs-writing-templates.md): "Each `Step` is `JSONSchema` with some extra goodies for styling"; steps are a series of actions with `id`, `if`, `each`, `action`, `input`, and outputs referenced as `steps.$id.output.*` (Parameters, Steps). (first-party; research-dependency-agent)
- [Open Data Contract Standard (ODCS)](sources/bitol-odcs-open-data-contract-standard.md): the contract is YAML and "platform agnostic", so a request can be checked against it before submission (Principles). (first-party; research-dependency-agent)
- [Provision no-code infrastructure (HCP Terraform)](sources/hashicorp-terraform-no-code-provisioning.md): platform teams mark a private-registry module version "No-code Ready"; users supply variables without defaults, name the workspace, choose a project and apply method; types validated. (first-party; research-dependency-agent)
- [Requesting access to a data product (Immuta)](sources/immuta-docs-request-access-data-product.md): `POST /api/data-product/{id}/request` (and `/request/masking-exception`) with a Request-app personal access token; 201 returns the hydrated request. (first-party; research-dependency-agent)
- [Dev Portal MCP server (Kong Konnect)](sources/kong-docs-dev-portal-mcp-server.md): modes: public read-only, authenticated read-only, authenticated read-write; OAuth 2.0 with PKCE for clients that support discovery. (first-party; research-dependency-agent)
- [Developer self-service and application registration (Kong Dev Portal)](sources/kong-docs-dev-portal-self-service.md): Konnect Portal Management v3 API creates and approves developers, creates applications, registers them to APIs, manages forms and publications; custom registration forms per portal. (first-party; research-dependency-agent)
- [Promises (Kratix reference)](sources/kratix-docs-promises-intro.md): a Promise bundles dependencies, an API for requesting it, workflows (Promise and Resource lifecycles, each with `configure`/`delete`) and destination rules (Definition, Workflows). (first-party; research-dependency-agent)
- [Access packages for agent identities in Microsoft Entra](sources/microsoft-entra-agent-access-packages.md): policy fields define who can request ("All agents"), approval stages and approvers, expiry and extension; packages can be created via Microsoft Graph and PowerShell. (first-party; research-dependency-agent)
- [Port MCP server: overview and installation](sources/port-docs-remote-mcp-server.md): controls: `x-read-only-mode` hides write tools; `x-allowed-actions-to-run` allowlists actions (empty blocks all). (first-party; research-dependency-agent)
- [Set self-service actions RBAC (Port)](sources/port-docs-self-service-action-rbac.md): permissions managed in UI or Terraform; per-action approval with specific users/teams as approvers, any-one or all must approve; runs wait until approved. (first-party; research-dependency-agent)
- [Score: developer-centric workload specification](sources/score-dev-workload-specification.md): "a developer-centric and platform-agnostic workload specification"; resource dependencies declared, resolved by the platform (home page). (first-party; research-dependency-agent)

## one-job-per-agent: One job per agent
Scoping an agent to one defined job (with human in the loop) for consistency and evals. In tension with [[single-agent-many-skills]].
- [Harbor: Stripe's AI-assisted prototyping tool](sources/stripe-harbor-ai-prototyping.md): Stripe: 'keep agents specialized (on research, coding, or browser-native tools) while exposing them to capabilities in other systems' (competitive-teardown-stripe-knowledge-agents)
- [12-Factor Agents, factor 10](sources/humanlayer-12-factor-agents-small-focused-agents.md): first-party: small focused agents (about 3-10 steps) because LLMs lose focus as context grows; scope grows only as quality holds (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Measuring Agents in Production](sources/arxiv-measuring-agents-in-production.md): independent: 68% of deployed agents execute at most 10 steps before human intervention; reliability is the top challenge (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Orchestrating AI Code Review at scale](sources/cloudflare-ai-code-review-opencode.md): first-party: seven narrow specialist reviewers plus a coordinator beat one big prompt; 'what not to flag' per specialist (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Don't Build Multi-Agents](sources/cognition-dont-build-multi-agents.md): reconciliation note: its objection is to splitting interdependent work across parallel agents, not to bounded single-job agents (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [1,500+ PRs Later (Honk, Part 1)](sources/spotify-engineering-honk-part-1-1500-prs.md): multi-agent setup for planning, generating and reviewing PRs (research-airbnb-spotify-product-practices)

## one-roadmap-functional-org: One roadmap, functional org
The whole company works from one roadmap with functional teams instead of divisions, so priorities are global and few. It sets where a planning agent's artifact lives and who owns it.
- [Brian Chesky's new playbook for product, leadership, and growth](sources/lenny-podcast-brian-chesky-new-playbook.md): about 10 divisions folded into a functional org; no separate guest and host teams, because separate teams build "separate roadmaps that go in separate directions" (22:23, 41:48) (research-airbnb-spotify-product-practices)
- [Navigating the intersection of design and business (Config 2023)](sources/figma-config-2023-brian-chesky.md): "If it's not on the roadmap, it can't ship and it must be on one roadmap"; only about 10% of roadmap items kept (research-airbnb-spotify-product-practices)
- [Airbnb CEO Brian Chesky on the gospel of Steve Jobs and what founder mode really means](sources/verge-decoder-chesky-founder-mode-2024.md): "all functions roll up to me"; functional orgs are slow to start, but "if it gets on the roadmap, we put the weight of the company behind it" (research-airbnb-spotify-product-practices)
- [Decoder: Brian Chesky (2021)](sources/verge-decoder-chesky-2021-functional-org.md): 10-11 divisions cut to homes plus experiences after a 25% layoff; "the entire company was on one roadmap… Decision-making was faster" (Nov 2021) (research-airbnb-spotify-product-practices)
- [Vlad Loktev on Lenny's Podcast](sources/lenny-podcast-vlad-loktev-airbnb.md): "all org charts suck"; functional orgs create "too many dependencies"; reorganising "is rarely the solution" (57:30) (research-airbnb-spotify-product-practices)
- [TBM 255: The New Airbnb](sources/cutler-perri-tbm-255-new-airbnb.md): asks whether the late-2010s GM model, fuelled by cheap money, was the real problem (research-airbnb-spotify-product-practices)
- [Airbnb's new app for 'services' is getting shot down by critics](sources/fortune-airbnb-services-app-critics.md): the CFO says Experiences sat on "the back burner" through a "multi-year pause" before the 2025 re-plan (research-airbnb-spotify-product-practices)
- [Teo Connor on designing the new Airbnb app](sources/designweek-teo-connor-new-airbnb-app.md): Airbnb "focuses the whole company on a single product calendar" (research-airbnb-spotify-product-practices)

## opportunity-to-code-chain: Opportunity → problem → goal → intent → plan → code
A stage chain for product work, drawn by a Stripe engineer, in which agents today own the lower stages (intent research, plan, code, review) and people own the upper ones (opportunity, problem, goal) through customer conversations. It gives the strategy a spine: where each agent sits, where hand-offs and artifacts are, and where captured context must feed in.

- [Building and Accelerating the Intent Factory](sources/geoff-building-accelerating-intent-factory.md): Geoff's eight-step Stripe/Ramp loop starts at informal intent and runs to staged release; Stripe's chain adds the three human stages above intent (opportunity, problem, goal) that the loop leaves implicit (competitive-teardown-stripe-knowledge-agents)

- [AI didn't write our SDK. It changed how we built it.](sources/stripe-ai-didnt-write-our-sdk.md): between intent and code, agents draft specs that humans review as GitHub issues before implementation (competitive-teardown-stripe-knowledge-agents)

## org-context-grounding: Agents work when grounded in organisation context
Successful PM agents read the organisation's own data (docs, tickets, calls, code); thin context yields generic output. Related: [[compounding-context-repo]], [[harness-over-model]].
- [Meet Ramp Research: Our Agentic Data Analyst](sources/ramp-builders-meet-ramp-research.md): grounding in dbt, Looker and Snowflake metadata plus domain-owner docs (competitive-teardown-ramp-glass)

## org-learning-loop: One person's win becomes everyone's baseline
Skills, prompts and corrections made by one employee propagate to the team so the organisation learns once. Overlaps with [[compounding-context-repo]] (product context) but is about workflow/skills and shared sessions.
- [We Built Every Employee at Ramp Their Own AI Coworker](sources/x-sebgoddijn-glass-article.md): principle 2 and Dojo, 350+ skills (competitive-teardown-ramp-glass)

- [Superpowers: How I'm using coding agents](sources/fsck-jesse-vincent-superpowers.md): skills mined from a book and about 2,249 past memory files (research-skill-rigidity-spectrum)

## outcome-measurement-gap: Nobody can yet measure PM-agent outcomes
Time-saved claims are self-reported; no one publishes decision-quality or outcome measures. An opening for a harness that bakes in measurement.
- [Shopify's River shows why agent context costs more (Magica)](sources/magica-shopify-river-agent-context-cost.md): names the missing evidence: resolution time, rollback rate, retention, infrastructure cost against a baseline (competitive-teardown-shopify-river)
- [How River takes security work from a fix to merge](sources/shopify-engineering-river-vulnerability-remediation.md): "PR count and green-branch count measure motion, not remediation"; measure items reaching fixed, rejected or escalated (competitive-teardown-shopify-river)
- [Meet Stripe's Knowledge AI Platform](sources/stripe-meet-knowledge-ai-platform.md): Kai's outcome numbers are within-person usage comparisons (Kai weeks vs non-Kai weeks; power vs low users), not controlled tests (competitive-teardown-stripe-knowledge-agents)
- [Emily Glassberg Sands on Latent Space](sources/latentspace-emily-sands-stripe.md): Sands (Oct 2025): 'I have a really hard time understanding impact. Like I don't quite know what statistic to look at' (competitive-teardown-stripe-knowledge-agents)
- [Chesky says AI writes 60% of its code](sources/fortune-chesky-ai-60-percent-code-founder-mode.md): 60% AI-written code, up to 60% faster concept-to-launch, 45% of support resolved by AI; all company-reported, no method given (research-airbnb-spotify-product-practices)
- [Beyond the CLI: Agentic AI for async workloads and non-developers](sources/dx-airbnb-beyond-the-cli-airchat.md): gains measured with a vendor's (DX) TrueThroughput, a survey of AI-authored share and self-reported time saved (research-airbnb-spotify-product-practices)
- [Airbnb Q1 2026 earnings call and shareholder letter](sources/airbnb-earnings-q1-2026.md): the same 60% is "coauthored with AI" in the letter and "written by AI" on the call; never defined (research-airbnb-spotify-product-practices)
- [Airbnb (ABNB) Q2 2026 earnings call transcript and shareholder letter](sources/airbnb-earnings-q2-2026.md): outcomes counted as "features and improvements" shipped (+~80%) and concept-to-launch time (up to −60%) (research-airbnb-spotify-product-practices)
- [Airbnb Q4 2024 earnings call](sources/airbnb-earnings-q4-2024.md): Feb 2025 baseline: "some productivity gains", no step change yet; 30% plausible in a few years (research-airbnb-spotify-product-practices)
- [Airbnb says AI now writes 60% of its new code](sources/techcrunch-airbnb-ai-writes-60-percent-code.md): press repeats 60% without saying what is counted (research-airbnb-spotify-product-practices)
- [Beyond Winning: Spotify's Experiments with Learning Framework](sources/spotify-engineering-experiments-with-learning.md): learning rate varies 16-76% by team; used to triage testing bandwidth (research-airbnb-spotify-product-practices)
- [Spotify Q3 2026 Earnings Call](sources/spotify-q3-2026-earnings-call.md): lines of code and PRs up ~100%, but features per six-month cycle treated as the real signal; no count given (research-airbnb-spotify-product-practices)
- [The Platform PM role at Spotify (DX ep. 50)](sources/dx-podcast-nils-loodin-platform-pm-spotify.md): time-to-first-PR replaced by "time to a meaningful PR" (research-airbnb-spotify-product-practices)
- [The Design Productivity Blueprint](sources/spotify-design-productivity-blueprint.md): designer productivity measured by routine-task time, bottlenecks and design-system adoption (research-airbnb-spotify-product-practices)
- [1,500+ PRs Later (Honk, Part 1)](sources/spotify-engineering-honk-part-1-1500-prs.md): 60-90% migration time saving claimed with no method (research-airbnb-spotify-product-practices)
- [Spotify Q1 2026 Earnings Call](sources/spotify-q1-2026-earnings-call.md): productivity tracked by features, "definitions of done" and bets-board bets, said to be "doubling"; no figures (research-airbnb-spotify-product-practices)
- [AI Changed How Spotify Builds… Quality at Higher Velocity](sources/spotify-engineering-quality-at-higher-velocity.md): rework metric rebuilt; no rise found; PR size and complexity rising with unclear meaning (research-airbnb-spotify-product-practices)
- [AiKA hub](sources/spotify-portal-aika-hub.md): 6,000+ hours saved over 20 months, no method (research-airbnb-spotify-product-practices)
- [How Block is becoming the most AI-native enterprise (Lenny's Podcast)](sources/lenny-podcast-block-dhanji-goose.md): 8-10 h/week self-reported; 20-25% of manual hours saved from an unpublished formula (research-block-product-practices)
- [Block Q4 2025 prepared remarks](sources/block-q4-2025-earnings-prepared-remarks.md): the only metric for the cut is code shipped per engineer, up 40%+ (research-block-product-practices)
- [Q1 2026 Shareholder Letter](sources/block-q1-2026-shareholder-letter.md): throughput up 2.5x and post-change incidents down 70%+, credited jointly to AI and reliability work (research-block-product-practices)

(research-claude-resources-articles)
- [Measure Claude Code's impact with contribution metrics](sources/claude-code-contribution-metrics.md): the metric is activity (PRs, lines), not outcomes; Anthropic concedes PRs are "an incomplete measure of developer velocity" and positions them as a proxy ("How we're shipping at Anthropic"). (research-claude-resources-articles)

- [A conversation with Seth Hain about Epic's internal AI adoption](sources/claude-customers-epic-internal-adoption.md): monitoring draft acceptance: 100% unedited use and 0% use are both signs something is wrong (answer on clinical trust). (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [Office Hours: Asynchronous coding and the end of the IDE with Spotify](sources/claude-customers-spotify-office-hours.md): 75%+ improvement in PR frequency and 73% AI-authored PRs claimed; connecting PRs to work items, A/B tests and user value is "what we're trying to build right now" (ROI segment). (research-claude-resources-articles)

(research-claude-resources-articles)

(research-claude-resources-articles)
