## overreliance-and-deskilling: Overreliance and deskilling
AI assistance breeds automation bias and erodes human skill unless the design works against it; the effect grows as the AI improves. Matters because every "up-level the human" job in the project is fighting this default.
- [To Trust or to Think](sources/arxiv-bucinca-cognitive-forcing-functions.md): cognitive forcing designs cut overreliance vs explainable AI (N=199) but were least liked and helped high need-for-cognition people most (research-skill-rigidity-spectrum)
- [The Impact of Generative AI on Critical Thinking](sources/microsoft-research-lee-genai-critical-thinking-chi2025.md): 319 workers, 936 examples; confidence in GenAI predicts less critical thinking, task self-confidence more; thinking shifts to verification, integration, stewardship (research-skill-rigidity-spectrum)
- [Generative AI without guardrails can harm learning](sources/pnas-bastani-generative-ai-can-harm-learning.md): unrestricted GPT-4 +48% on practice, -17% on the unassisted exam; GPT Tutor +127% practice and most harm removed (research-skill-rigidity-spectrum)
- [How People Can Create and Destroy Value with Generative AI](sources/bcg-how-people-create-and-destroy-value-with-gen-ai.md): 758 consultants; +40% quality inside the frontier, 23 points worse outside; training made it worse (research-skill-rigidity-spectrum)
- [Falling Asleep at the Wheel](sources/hbs-dellacqua-falling-asleep-at-the-wheel.md): 181 recruiters; a 75%-accurate AI beat an 85% one because people kept checking the weaker tool (research-skill-rigidity-spectrum)
- [Endoscopist deskilling risk after exposure to AI](sources/lancet-budzyn-endoscopist-deskilling-after-ai.md): ADR in non-AI colonoscopies 28.4% to 22.4% within three months of AI; OR 0.69 (research-skill-rigidity-spectrum)
- [When combinations of humans and AI are useful](sources/arxiv-vaccaro-when-human-ai-combinations-are-useful.md): 100+ experiments; combinations averaged worse than the better party alone; losses on decision tasks, gains on creation (research-skill-rigidity-spectrum)
- [Your Brain on ChatGPT](sources/arxiv-kosmyna-your-brain-on-chatgpt.md): 54-person EEG preprint; lowest ownership and inability to quote own essay in the LLM group; weak evidence (research-skill-rigidity-spectrum)
- [Does the Whole Exceed its Parts?](sources/arxiv-bansal-does-the-whole-exceed-its-parts.md): explanations raised acceptance of AI answers including wrong ones and added no complementary gain (research-skill-rigidity-spectrum)
- [Explanations Can Reduce Overreliance](sources/arxiv-vasconcelos-explanations-can-reduce-overreliance.md): N=731; engagement is a cost-benefit choice; explanations help when they make checking cheaper (research-skill-rigidity-spectrum)
- [In Search of Verifiability](sources/arxiv-fok-weld-in-search-of-verifiability.md): explanations help only when they enable verification; most tasks resist cheap verification (research-skill-rigidity-spectrum)
- [Humans and Automation: Use, Misuse, Disuse, Abuse](sources/sage-parasuraman-riley-humans-and-automation-use-misuse-disuse-abuse.md): 1997 taxonomy: misuse (overreliance), disuse (ignored after false alarms), abuse (automation designed without regard to the human's role) (research-skill-rigidity-spectrum)

## ownership-inference: Inferring who owns what, then having a person confirm
Owner and expert inference from commit history, incident routing to owning teams, and the inferred-then-confirmed pattern commercial catalogues use. Related: [[stale-records-mislead-agents]].
- [Identifying Source Code File Experts](sources/arxiv-cury-identifying-file-experts.md): "First Authorship" correlates most positively with knowledge and "Recency of Modification" most negatively (abstract); ML gives higher precision, linear techniques higher recall. (independent; research-dependency-agent)
- [Automated Code Review Assignments: An Alternative Perspective of Code Ownership on GitHub](sources/arxiv-lulla-codeowners-review-assignments.md): declared owners' collaboration behaviour "is similar to traditional ownership metrics" (abstract), so commit-derived and declared ownership tend to agree where both exist. (independent; research-dependency-agent)
- [Nudge: Accelerating Overdue Pull Requests Towards Completion](sources/arxiv-maddila-nudge-overdue-pull-requests.md): actor identification decides who the blocker is; the authors list dependencies among PRs and developer availability as future work. (first-party; research-dependency-agent)
- [In Search of Socio-Technical Congruence: A Large-Scale Longitudinal Study](sources/arxiv-mauerer-socio-technical-congruence.md): the method doubles as "who should be talking to whom" inference from code. (independent; research-dependency-agent)
- [DeepTriage: Automated Transfer Assistance for Incidents in Cloud Services](sources/arxiv-pham-deeptriage-incident-routing.md): team recommendation from incident text and metadata, 82.9% F1 on real Azure incidents (abstract). (first-party; research-dependency-agent)
- [Service Detection](sources/opslevel-docs-service-detection.md): for repository-based detections, OpsLevel reads recent commit history, matches contributors to known users, and suggests their teams, aggregating contributions per team (hover shows the breakdown). (first-party; research-dependency-agent)
- [OpsLevel releases recommended service owners to optimize service management efficiency](sources/opslevel-recommended-service-owners.md): "The recommendations are based on the top three contributors to that service."; a tooltip shows recent contribution frequency so the user can judge. (first-party; research-dependency-agent)

## platform-as-a-product: Platform as a product, and its evidence
The platform-engineering doctrine (self-service, golden paths, thinnest viable platform, interaction modes) and what the independent evidence says it delivers, including the DORA 2024 finding that platforms raise reported productivity and cut throughput and stability.
- [How Platform Teams Can Avoid the Ticket Factory Trap](sources/builtin-mahajan-ticket-factory-trap.md): causes include stakeholders treating platforms as support services, and metrics that reward closed tickets over outcomes. (anecdote; research-dependency-agent)
- [Platform Engineering Maturity Model](sources/cncf-platform-engineering-maturity-model.md): Investment L3 "As product": funding based on expected value to customers, product management and UX included, chargeback may be used (Investment aspect). (independent; research-dependency-agent)
- [CNCF Platforms White Paper](sources/cncf-tag-app-delivery-platforms-white-paper.md): "A platform exists to serve the requirements of its users"; include product managers early (Attributes; Challenges). (independent; research-dependency-agent)
- [DORA Report 2024 (Accelerate State of DevOps)](sources/dora-accelerate-state-of-devops-2024.md): platform use improves productivity and performance but platform implementation needs "careful implementation focused on developer independence" (findings list). (independent; research-dependency-agent)
- [Capabilities: Platform engineering](sources/dora-capability-platform-engineering.md): assign a product manager focused on developer experience; map critical user journeys such as "spinning up a new service" (User-centred section). (independent; research-dependency-agent)
- [What I Talk About When I Talk About Platforms](sources/fowler-bottcher-what-i-talk-about-platforms.md): "Platform is a product, and needs a long-lived and stable product team tasked with both build and run"; platforms also include documentation, consulting, support and evangelism. (anecdote; research-dependency-agent)
- [Platform engineering and internal developer portals: a multivocal literature review](sources/frontiers-anjum-platform-engineering-mlr.md): scorecards, a core portal governance mechanism, have "no peer-reviewed empirical evidence of effectiveness" despite commercial adoption. (independent; research-dependency-agent)
- [Trial mode – GOV.UK Notify](sources/govuk-notify-trial-mode.md): go-live is a checklist ("Make your service live" tasks) plus a request; Notify checks the service meets its terms of use and responds "by the end of the next working day". (first-party; research-dependency-agent)
- [DevOps Benchmarking Study 2023](sources/humanitec-devops-benchmarking-2023.md): "93% of top performers use a platform built and maintained by a platform team" following a "Platform as a Product approach" (Executive summary). (vendor-claim; research-dependency-agent)
- [Accounting Versus Physics – Rewiring Organizations for Improvement](sources/itrevolution-prugh-accounting-versus-physics.md): platform teams are named as one of the moves that cut coordination cost (body). (anecdote; research-dependency-agent)
- [Driving enterprise software delivery](sources/jpmorganchase-driving-enterprise-software-delivery.md): standardising on a common toolchain to avoid "tool sprawl"; platform meant to be "friction-less" and "invisible to our developers". (first-party; research-dependency-agent)
- [Developer Velocity: How software excellence fuels business performance](sources/mckinsey-developer-velocity.md): the four strongest drivers are tools, culture, product management and talent management; "best-in-class tools are the top contributor", yet "only 5 percent of executives" ranked tools in their top three enablers. (vendor-claim; research-dependency-agent)
- [Investigation into Verify](sources/nao-investigation-into-verify.md): HMRC did not adopt Verify for all services "in part because Verify cannot deal with business customers or agents acting on behalf of others"; the NAO links this to its shared-services finding that departments "felt the central standardised solution offered did not meet their specific needs" (para 1.13). (independent; research-dependency-agent)
- [2023 State of DevOps Report Finds Platform Engineering Unlocks DevOps Success in the Enterprise](sources/perforce-puppet-state-of-devops-2023-platform-engineering.md): top platform-team priorities: raising awareness of capabilities (47%), setting realistic expectations for the team's role (44%), tracking trends and feature requirements (37%) (press release). Evidence: vendor survey. (vendor-claim; research-dependency-agent)
- [Puppet's 2024 State of DevOps Report Reveals Security is Strengthened by Platform Engineering](sources/perforce-puppet-state-of-devops-2024-platform-engineering.md): 52% say a product manager is crucial to platform team success (press release). Evidence: vendor survey. (vendor-claim; research-dependency-agent)
- [How Spotify measures the value of Backstage](sources/spotify-backstage-measuring-backstage-roi.md): converts the cycle-time and PR-activity gains into "3 FTEs for a team of 10 developers", an internal ROI framing a platform team might copy. (first-party; research-dependency-agent)
- [How We Use Golden Paths to Solve Fragmentation in Our Software Ecosystem](sources/spotify-engineering-golden-paths.md): the path is "opinionated and supported"; leaving it is allowed, but "then you will not have the same support". (first-party; research-dependency-agent)
- [Platform as a Product in a 300-Year-Old Bank](sources/syntasso-natwest-platform-as-product-300-year-old-bank.md): marketplace model separating providers from consumers, with eight interface factors; component principles "product-scoped, self-serve, operationally owned". (vendor-claim; research-dependency-agent)
- [Key Concepts (Team Topologies)](sources/teamtopologies-key-concepts.md): platform teams provide services that speed up stream-aligned teams; "The TVP approach creates platforms that provide just enough capability without unnecessary complexity"; X-as-a-Service means one team provides and another consumes with minimal interaction (page sections on team types and interaction modes). (independent; research-dependency-agent)
- [Banking at scale: a blueprint for delivery transformation using Team Topologies](sources/teamtopologies-pujar-banking-at-scale.md): a platform group formed from chapter leads (Java, Azure, .NET, Cloud) owning DevOps and test automation; enabling teams of agile coaches, project managers and change-execution staff. (anecdote; research-dependency-agent)
- [Google DORA issues platform engineering caveats](sources/techtarget-pariseau-dora-2024-platform-engineering-caveats.md): platform gains follow a J-curve (early gains, a dip, recovery as the platform matures) "provided they listen to developer feedback" (article body, citing the report). (independent; research-dependency-agent)
- [A decade of cloud native at ING: lessons learned and what comes next](sources/techzine-nardiello-ing-decade-cloud-native.md): each capability needs "an owner, a clear contract, semantic versioning, a lifecycle, a reliability target, and a cost-per-unit metric". (first-party; research-dependency-agent)
- [Lloyds Bank reviews tech and engineering personnel in reorg](sources/theregister-lloyds-tech-engineering-reorg.md): since 2022 Lloyds has used a Platform approach bringing tech and business teams together around shared goals, aiming at a "standard, agile way of working"; the next stage, Platform 3.0, means more investment in tools and automation (body). (independent; research-dependency-agent)
- [Mapping out Agile transformation at TBC Bank](sources/thoughtworks-tbc-bank-agile-transformation.md): re-alignment of tribes and squads to product domains and decoupled teams as the fix. (vendor-claim; research-dependency-agent)

## platform-onboarding-friction: Onboarding to an internal platform is seldom plug and play
Intake, prioritisation, funding, access, environments, data agreements, assurance evidence, conformance, agreements and the cascade to other platforms; the staged process a product team goes through, where it stalls, and the absence of published lead times.
- [A Case Study of Onboarding in Software Teams: Tasks and Strategies](sources/arxiv-ju-onboarding-software-teams.md): hindrances include "unclear or outdated documentation", information overload, and waiting on other teams for reviews (findings). (independent; research-dependency-agent)
- [How JPMorgan Chase built a data mesh architecture to drive significant value to enhance their enterprise data platform](sources/aws-jpmc-data-mesh-enterprise-data-platform.md): consumers find data in a catalogue and request it; the owning domain decides, which the post says "minimizes the consumption team's wait time" (no timings given). (first-party; research-dependency-agent)
- [How Platform Teams Can Avoid the Ticket Factory Trap](sources/builtin-mahajan-ticket-factory-trap.md): teams "build workarounds", fuelling shadow IT, when the platform feels like bureaucracy. (anecdote; research-dependency-agent)
- [Infosys insurance customer case study (Backstage developer portal)](sources/cncf-infosys-insurance-backstage.md): "Onboarding time for new developers reduced by 40%" (Impact). Vendor claim, no method. (vendor-claim; research-dependency-agent)
- [Platform Engineering Maturity Model](sources/cncf-platform-engineering-maturity-model.md): Interfaces L1 "Custom processes": capabilities "mainly provided through manual requests", provisioning relies on manual intervention and person-to-person knowledge (Interfaces aspect). (independent; research-dependency-agent)
- [CNCF Platforms White Paper](sources/cncf-tag-app-delivery-platforms-white-paper.md): documentation, onboarding and "golden path" templates are an attribute; self-service means obtaining capabilities "with minimal manual steps" (Attributes). (independent; research-dependency-agent)
- [Capabilities: Platform engineering](sources/dora-capability-platform-engineering.md): pitfalls named "Build it and they will come", "Ivory tower" (drives shadow IT), "Ticket-ops", "Big bang" release and "One-size-fits-all" ("golden cage") (Common pitfalls). (independent; research-dependency-agent)
- [Escape ticketing hell with a shift to self-service platforms](sources/equalexperts-smith-escape-ticketing-hell.md): a task "that takes minutes to complete" can wait days or weeks in a queue; Dutch bank: 11 weeks for repository access (body). Evidence: anecdote from consulting engagements. (anecdote; research-dependency-agent)
- [Interagency Guidance on Third-Party Relationships: Risk Management](sources/fed-fdic-occ-third-party-risk-guidance-2023.md): "Relying solely on experience with or prior knowledge of a third party is not an adequate proxy for performing appropriate due diligence" (Section C.2), so each new use repeats work. (first-party; research-dependency-agent)
- [FedRAMP 20x](sources/fedramp-20x-overview.md): replaces static yearly manual assessments; "Security should be continuously enforced, monitored, and reported—not staged for a point-in-time audit." (first-party; research-dependency-agent)
- [FINOS Common Cloud Controls (CCC)](sources/finos-common-cloud-controls.md): aim is a common framework instead of each bank's bespoke cloud-risk interpretation (FINOS blog estimates Tier 1 banks run 15,000-20,000 active controls; search result, not this page). (first-party; research-dependency-agent)
- [What I Talk About When I Talk About Platforms](sources/fowler-bottcher-what-i-talk-about-platforms.md): the platform "must provide services that do not require tickets to be raised and work to be assigned". (anecdote; research-dependency-agent)
- [Consumer-Driven Contracts: A Service Evolution Pattern](sources/fowler-robinson-consumer-driven-contracts.md): strict whole-schema binding forces consumers to redeploy in lockstep with the provider, burdening the enterprise "with services". (anecdote; research-dependency-agent)
- [Cloud Security: Federal Authorization Program Usage Increasing, but Challenges Need to Be Fully Addressed (GAO-24-106591)](sources/gao-cloud-security-fedramp-challenges-2024.md): agencies sponsoring providers "that were not fully prepared, including incomplete documentation"; inconsistency among third-party assessment organisations (3PAOs) (Highlights). (independent; research-dependency-agent)
- [Trial mode – GOV.UK Notify](sources/govuk-notify-trial-mode.md): new services start in trial mode: send only to yourself and team members, up to 50 emails and 50 texts a day, no letters (Trial mode limits). (first-party; research-dependency-agent)
- [Provision no-code infrastructure (HCP Terraform)](sources/hashicorp-terraform-no-code-provisioning.md): auto-apply is the default; manual apply requires an operator to confirm; module upgrades notify existing workspaces rather than auto-upgrading. (first-party; research-dependency-agent)
- [DevOps Benchmarking Study 2023](sources/humanitec-devops-benchmarking-2023.md): developers who depend on Ops for simple tasks produce "ticket ops when developers need" help; top performers create feature or PR environments (83.6%), deploy to dev or staging (93%) and assign resources via golden paths (85%) themselves; 53% can bootstrap a new app in under two hours (Executive summary). (vendor-claim; research-dependency-agent)
- [NAB uses CAST to keep its cloud apps in check](sources/itnews-nab-cast-cloud-controls.md): the old default "is no"; CAST changed the question to "Does it comply with CAST?" (first-party; research-dependency-agent)
- [Episode 3: The Quest for Accelerated Delivery (DevOps Enterprise Summit 2016)](sources/itrevolution-nationwide-does16-accelerated-delivery.md): "Work requests required" went from 100% to 0% after moving to self-managed internal cloud provisioning, with patching and configuration initiated by users rather than operations (results slide). (first-party; research-dependency-agent)
- [Developer self-service and application registration (Kong Dev Portal)](sources/kong-docs-dev-portal-self-service.md): "Developer sign ups and application creation require admin approval by default."; portal-level auto-approve overrides per-API settings. (first-party; research-dependency-agent)
- [Building a world-class platform for software engineers](sources/mit-tr-jpmorgan-world-class-engineering-platform.md): frames cumbersome processes and burnout as the problem to remove for engineers; no onboarding metric. (first-party; research-dependency-agent)
- [Investigation into Verify](sources/nao-investigation-into-verify.md): "GDS and the Cabinet Office did not mandate the use of Verify at an early stage. Departments were able to continue using other identity verification systems" (para 1.13); 11 of the 19 services using Verify also offered alternative online routes (para 1.12). (independent; research-dependency-agent)
- [Onboarding to the National Record Locator (NRL) v3.0](sources/nhs-england-nrl-onboarding-guidance.md): "You cannot proceed to DOS Stage 1 without these prerequisites in place"; "Timelines vary depending on the complexity of your integration and the completeness of submitted evidence" (Stage 0; Timings). (first-party; research-dependency-agent)
- [DevEx: What Actually Drives Productivity](sources/noda-devex-what-actually-drives-productivity.md): cognitive load from poorly documented code and systems; eBay's DevEx team fixed "tooling and documentation gaps", removed manual steps and streamlined "cross-domain team interactions" (eBay case). (independent; research-dependency-agent)
- [2023 State of DevOps Report Finds Platform Engineering Unlocks DevOps Success in the Enterprise](sources/perforce-puppet-state-of-devops-2023-platform-engineering.md): the need to raise awareness and set expectations implies consumers struggle to find and understand platform offerings. (vendor-claim; research-dependency-agent)
- [Puppet's 2024 State of DevOps Report Reveals Security is Strengthened by Platform Engineering](sources/perforce-puppet-state-of-devops-2024-platform-engineering.md): organisations average 3 internal self-service platforms, so a product team onboards to several, each with its own route in. (vendor-claim; research-dependency-agent)
- [2023 Project to Product State of the Industry Report](sources/planview-project-to-product-state-of-industry-2023.md): "5% of respondents have transitioned to a full self-service model for internally consumed capabilities"; 8% still run execution paths through SLAs with functional areas (p. 17). (vendor-claim; research-dependency-agent)
- [2025 State of Internal Developer Portals](sources/port-state-of-internal-developer-portals-2025.md): 94% are dissatisfied with self-service tools; 6% very satisfied. (vendor-claim; research-dependency-agent)
- [Add details to demands (Demand Management)](sources/servicenow-demand-management-add-details.md): demands are submitted through the service catalog form or the Demand Management app; selecting a portfolio auto-populates the stakeholder list; resource assignments inform approval only when the Resource Management Workspace is active. (vendor-claim; research-dependency-agent)
- [How Backstage Made Our Developers More Effective — And How It Can Help Yours, Too](sources/spotify-engineering-backstage-made-developers-more-effective.md): onboarding measured as time to tenth pull request; over 60 days before, 20 days after (body). First-party, no baseline dates. (first-party; research-dependency-agent)
- [Platform as a Product in a 300-Year-Old Bank](sources/syntasso-natwest-platform-as-product-300-year-old-bank.md): the older central model described as "Safety through tickets". (vendor-claim; research-dependency-agent)
- [A decade of cloud native at ING: lessons learned and what comes next](sources/techzine-nardiello-ing-decade-cloud-native.md): self-service without product discipline becomes "a YAML vending machine (or worse)"; the goal is that "the recommended way is also the easiest way". (first-party; research-dependency-agent)
- [The all-in-one trust management platform (Enterprise)](sources/vanta-enterprise-trust-management.md): "Manage vendor onboarding and security reviews in one place"; a healthcare customer (Vibrent Health) says vendor security assessments took "50 hours per vendor", reduced to a few hours a week (testimonial). (vendor-claim; research-dependency-agent)

## pm-ai-usage-surveys: What surveys say about PMs' AI use
Self-selected, mostly vendor-run surveys of where PMs use AI and what they save; directional only.
- [Airbnb Q4 2025 earnings call and shareholder letter](sources/airbnb-earnings-q4-2025.md): ">80% of engineers are now using AI tools" (Chesky, Feb 2026) (research-airbnb-spotify-product-practices)
- [Coding Is No Longer the Constraint](sources/spotify-engineering-coding-no-longer-constraint.md): 99%+ of engineers use AI weekly, 94% say more productive, PR frequency +76% (Spotify, Jun 2026) (research-airbnb-spotify-product-practices)
- [The 2026 State of AI Agents Report](sources/claude-2026-state-of-ai-agents.md): 500+ technical leaders (engineering leaders, IT executives), late 2025; respondents are technical, not PMs (Foreword, Survey methodology). (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [Building AI agents for the enterprise](sources/claude-building-agents-enterprise-cowork.md): cites Anthropic Economic Index (Sept 2025): 40% of US employees report using AI at work, up from 20% in 2023 (opening). (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [How people are using Claude Cowork](sources/claude-how-people-use-cowork.md): category shares from 1.2M sampled sessions, 600,000+ organisations, May 11-31 2026, 20-category taxonomy ("What the data shows", "How we measured"). (research-claude-resources-articles)
- ["I'm incapable of doing my job without AI"](sources/howiai-monday-amir-klein-second-brain.md): Monday.com ranks its 90 PMs by AI tool usage (an internal leaderboard, not a survey) (34:16) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [How tech workers are feeling in 2026](sources/lenny-newsletter-tech-workers-2026-survey.md): 5,332 working respondents (47% PMs): 82% at least moderately better at their job; burnout up from 44.7% to 55.7%; top fear is more work for same pay (51%), job loss to AI only 22% (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [What's in your stack: The state of tech tools in 2025](sources/lenny-newsletter-tech-stack-2025-survey.md): Jan 2025 baseline: 90% ChatGPT, 35% Claude, 24% Gemini, 17% Cursor (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [Head of Claude Code (Boris Cherny)](sources/lenny-podcast-boris-cherny-after-coding.md): Lenny's informal X polls: ~70% of engineers and PMs enjoy work more since AI, ~10% less; designers 55% / 20% (44:59) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [OpenAI's Head of Design (Ian Silber)](sources/lenny-podcast-ian-silber-openai-design.md): OpenAI internal surveys: engineers 10-100x, designers not; Lenny's workforce survey finds designers the unhappiest role (0:00, 3:18) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [State of Product 2026 webinar and event pages (Atlassian)](sources/atlassian-state-of-product-2026-webinar-event.md): Report: half save 10-60 minutes a day ('up to 2 hours' is the top bucket); reactive, short-term work; many feel burnt out (single wave); 84% concerned their products won't succeed in market. (research-pm-agents-jobs-to-be-done)
- [AI tools are overdelivering: results from our large-scale AI productivity survey](sources/lennys-newsletter-ai-tools-overdelivering-results.md): Top PM AI uses: writing PRDs 21.5%, mockups/prototypes 19.8%, communication 18.5%; user research 4.7%, roadmap ideas 1.1%. Largest demand gap is user research (+27.2 points); prototyping desired use rises 19.8% to 44.4%. (research-pm-agents-jobs-to-be-done)
- [AI tools are overdelivering: results from our large-scale AI productivity survey](sources/lennys-newsletter-ai-tools-overdelivering-results.md): 63% of PMs and 83% of founders report saving 4+ hours/week; over 70% of PMs and founders (combined) report quality gains; designers, the most sceptical group, 47.5% save 4+ hours; engineers' top use is writing code (51% current). More than half of all responde (research-pm-agents-jobs-to-be-done)
- [Inside Atlassian's State of Product 2026: key takeaways](sources/mindtheproduct-atlassian-state-of-product-2026-takeaways.md): 80% of teams do not involve engineers in ideation, problem definition or roadmap creation; 49% lack time for strategic planning and roadmap development (Atlassian vendor survey, 700 manager-level respondents US/DE/FR plus 521-PM AI survey). (research-pm-agents-jobs-to-be-done)
- [AI in Product Management: What 379 Product Managers Revealed About the New Reality](sources/productboard-ai-in-product-management-report.md): Largest time savings for presentations, PRDs, competitive research and roadmap creation; about 4 hours saved per task on average; 98% have changed or plan to change team structures; top rising skills data literacy 58% and customer-insight synthesis 54%. (research-pm-agents-jobs-to-be-done)
- [Product Focus Industry Survey Report 2026](sources/productfocus-industry-survey-2026.md): 677 respondents, 40 countries. (research-pm-agents-jobs-to-be-done)
- [The State of Product Management Report 2026 (ProductPlan with Product-Led Alliance)](sources/productplan-state-of-product-management-2026.md): 'Over 60% of prioritization frameworks are overridden by leadership escalations' (marketing page; report gated). (research-pm-agents-jobs-to-be-done)
- [The State of AI for Product Managers 2026](sources/productside-state-of-ai-for-pms-2026.md): 4 in 5 PMs use AI regularly but only 1 in 4 have a strategy to show for it. (research-pm-agents-jobs-to-be-done)
- [State of AI in Product Management 2026](sources/uxcam-state-of-ai-in-product-management-2026.md): 99% use AI and 70% spend 5+ hours a week with it (search/page figures as reported). (research-pm-agents-jobs-to-be-done)
- [Product Manager Practices for Delegating Work to Generative AI](sources/arxiv-pm-delegating-work-to-genai.md): 62% of 885 Microsoft PMs use GenAI daily; self-report matches telemetry only moderately (rho 0.37); top barrier is output quality (47%) (research-pm-agents-jobs-to-be-done)

## pm-job-stable-methods-change: The PM job is stable; how it is done is changing
Surveys and practitioners agree the core PM jobs (discovery, shaping, spec, prioritization, comms, metrics) persist; agents change who or what performs the sub-tasks. Frames which jobs to build job/persona agents for.
- [The Future of Software Engineering Isn't What You Think](sources/medium-al-dahle-future-of-software-engineering.md): deciding what to build and why stays scarce as coding becomes cheap (research-airbnb-spotify-product-practices)
- [Spotify Q4 2025 Earnings Call](sources/spotify-q4-2025-earnings-call.md): "engineering practices, product practices and design practices will change" (research-airbnb-spotify-product-practices)
- [Product management on the AI exponential](sources/claude-pm-on-the-ai-exponential.md): the traditional playbook assumes what's possible at project start holds at the end; exponential model gains break that, so the PM's job becomes creating clarity in ambiguity and identifying "the handful of true... (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [How to become "AI fluent"](sources/departmentofproduct-ai-fluency.md): Zapier's rubric marks manual-only work and dismissing AI as "unacceptable" for every role, product included (research-department-of-product-knowledge-series)
- [AI's third era: the rise of persistent AI coworkers](sources/lenny-podcast-tara-seshan-persistent-coworkers.md): PM core (eigenquestion, sharp hypothesis, fast test, feedback loop) unchanged; execution "trappings" falling away; EMs, engineers, designers and data scientists now all run this loop (9:19) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [The Codex feature that works while you sleep](sources/howiai-claire-vo-codex-goal.md): "outcomes, not outputs" becomes a technical skill: PMs must write goals with verifiable finish lines for agents (26:29-28:03) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [Product manager is an unfair role. So work unfairly.](sources/lenny-newsletter-tal-raviv-unfair-role.md): "the great flattening": fewer IC PMs own more, and AI raises what one PM is expected to handle (introduction) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [Anthropic's first technical PM ... | Dianne Penn](sources/lenny-podcast-dianne-penn-evals-prds.md): hiring loop unchanged for three years; user research moves from pixels to model transcripts: "sweat the tokens as much as you sweat the pixels" (40:04, 42:32) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [OpenAI's CPO on how AI changes must-have skills (Kevin Weil)](sources/lenny-podcast-kevin-weil-openai-cpo.md): in early 2025 even OpenAI's CPO would "recognize" his day job from five years earlier (53:52) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [Why half of product managers are in trouble (Nikhyl Singhal)](sources/lenny-podcast-nikhyl-singhal-half-of-pms.md): 12-24 months of chaos, then the role settles, like the hardware-to-internet PM shift (49:37-51:08) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [This CPO regrets that product management exists (Tom Verrilli)](sources/lenny-podcast-tom-verrilli-whatnot-pm.md): core PM skills are durable, but five years of rewarding "storytelling, alignment, strategy" built "product theater" that AI exposes (47:21-48:57) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [How Anthropic's product team moves faster than anyone else | Cat Wu](sources/lenny-podcast-cat-wu-anthropic-product-team.md): Claude Code PMs trade multi-quarter roadmap alignment for goal-setting, a repeatable ship process and cross-functional frameworks; timelines cut from six months to days (5:03-8:59) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [The design process is dead: Jenny Wen](sources/lenny-podcast-jenny-wen-design-process-dead.md): research, mocks and prototypes all still happen; mocking fell from 60-70% to 30-40% of time, pairing with engineers rose to 30-40% (17:58) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [All of the Lenny & Friends Summit talks are now online!](sources/lenny-newsletter-summit-talks-online.md): "Nobody has it figured out"; Atlassian's Yehoshua: "it depends"; Anthropic's Ami Vora: "We don't think anyone knows the answer" (trend 2) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [Building AI product sense, part 2](sources/lenny-newsletter-ai-product-sense-part-2.md): Meta's PM loop changed for the first time in five years to test product sense with AI in real time (intro) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [How top PMs increase their leverage with AI](sources/lenny-newsletter-pm-leverage-ladders.md): "the PM job drifted toward coordinating and aligning people. That version of the role is fading"; execs now expect AI to "complete entire tasks" (intro) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [How to build AI product sense](sources/lenny-newsletter-ai-product-sense-part-1.md): two AI PMs "spend most of our days in coding agents for non-technical tasks" (Step 3) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [How AI is reshaping the product role (Udezue)](sources/lenny-podcast-udezue-ai-reshaping-pm-role.md): core PM value unchanged ("de-risking the product delivery process" and maximising value); PMs freed to invest in customer insight (4:59) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [Community Wisdom: Pivoting to AI PM, how AI changed our product development cycles](sources/lenny-community-wisdom-ai-product-dev-cycles.md): "a PM's core responsibilities haven't changed—PMs just have new tools" (thread 1) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [Community Wisdom: Prototyping vs. writing PRDs](sources/lenny-community-wisdom-prototyping-vs-prds.md): "your job ... isn't writing PRDs ... it's not building prototypes either"; the PRD exists for better engineer conversations (thread 1) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [Cowork plugins (including Product Management plugin)](sources/anthropic-cowork-plugins-product-management.md): PM plugin packages spec writing, roadmap prioritization and progress tracking as skills; research preview, no outcomes stated. (research-pm-agents-jobs-to-be-done)
- [Product development in the agentic era](sources/anthropic-product-development-agentic-era.md): PM job shifted from alignment work (meetings, status reports, ticket backlogs) toward product craft. (research-pm-agents-jobs-to-be-done)
- [How Block is becoming the most AI-native enterprise (Lenny's Podcast)](sources/lenny-podcast-block-dhanji-goose.md): org-structure change boosted productivity more than AI tools (speaker claim). (research-pm-agents-jobs-to-be-done)
- [Roles aren't converging—they're expanding | Tamar Yehoshua (Atlassian CPO)](sources/lenny-podcast-tamar-yehoshua-roles-expanding.md): "the job of a PM is really the same as it always was... It's how we do it that's changed" (02:30). (research-pm-agents-jobs-to-be-done)
- [Marty Cagan interview (Modern CTO)](sources/moderncto-marty-cagan-2026.md): bottleneck moved from building to deciding. (research-pm-agents-jobs-to-be-done)
- [Ten things I brought back from the Lenny & Friends Summit 2026](sources/productmanagementsociety-ten-things-lenny-summit.md): 'rowing vs steering' framing of PM role. (research-pm-agents-jobs-to-be-done)
- [An Introduction to Outcome-Driven Innovation](sources/customerthink-outcome-driven-innovation-intro.md): The job, not the product, is the unit of analysis; a job map captures all customer needs (importance/satisfaction ratings not described on this page). (research-pm-agents-jobs-to-be-done)
- [Summary: Continuous Discovery Habits (Evan Samek Substack)](sources/evansamek-continuous-discovery-habits-summary.md): Continuous discovery minimum: weekly customer touchpoints by the team building the product, running small research activities toward a desired outcome; unit is the product trio. (research-pm-agents-jobs-to-be-done)
- [Clay Christensen's Milkshake Marketing](sources/hbs-christensen-milkshake-marketing.md): Customers 'hire' products for a job; segmenting by product category or demographics misses the purchase trigger. (research-pm-agents-jobs-to-be-done)
- [Intercom on Jobs-to-be-Done (book announcement)](sources/intercom-jobs-to-be-done-book.md): JTBD covers switching behavior, real competitors, product scope, identifying the core job and Job Stories; says it is not a step-by-step guide. (research-pm-agents-jobs-to-be-done)
- [Des Traynor on JTBD Radio](sources/jtbd-radio-des-traynor.md): Traynor: the customer isn't the fundamental unit of analysis; 'a job is more like a verb' is Bob Moesta's line, which Traynor endorses. (research-pm-agents-jobs-to-be-done)
- [Getting to a team-based approach to continuous discovery (Teresa Torres)](sources/mindtheproduct-torres-team-based-continuous-discovery.md): Continuous discovery: weekly customer touchpoints by the team building the product, small research activities, in pursuit of a desired outcome; product trio as unit. (research-pm-agents-jobs-to-be-done)
- [How to Build High-Functioning Teams (Pragmatic Institute)](sources/pragmatic-institute-high-functioning-teams.md): 37 product management and product marketing activities, each completed and handed off; Pragmatic's framework page arranges them as 37 boxes in 7 categories, including Market Problems and Win/Loss Analysis. (research-pm-agents-jobs-to-be-done)
- [More valuable, less protected](sources/reforge-more-valuable-less-protected.md): Spec now more important because building is cheap; speed amplifies the cost of a wrong direction. (research-pm-agents-jobs-to-be-done)
- [The AI Productivity Paradox](sources/svpg-ai-productivity-paradox.md): the fix is the existing product model applied with AI, not a new role (research-pm-agents-jobs-to-be-done)
- [How AI will impact product management](sources/lenny-how-ai-will-impact-product-management.md): the PM as orchestrator; keep soft skills, use AI to amplify hard skills (research-pm-agents-jobs-to-be-done)

## pm-persona-role-expansion: PM and adjacent personas are expanding or blurring
Evidence on how PM, designer, engineer, founder-PM and PMM roles overlap or expand with AI; bears on persona-based agents.
- [Brian Chesky's new playbook for product, leadership, and growth](sources/lenny-podcast-brian-chesky-new-playbook.md): PM's inbound work merged with product marketing's outbound work; program work moved to program managers; a smaller, more senior group that manages "by influence" (06:47-08:31) (research-airbnb-spotify-product-practices)
- [Navigating the intersection of design and business (Config 2023)](sources/figma-config-2023-brian-chesky.md): "we got rid of the classic product management function… We combined product management with product marketing" (research-airbnb-spotify-product-practices)
- [Airbnb CEO Brian Chesky on the gospel of Steve Jobs and what founder mode really means](sources/verge-decoder-chesky-founder-mode-2024.md): senior PMs became product marketers, most others program managers; product marketing is "product management minus program management plus some outbound marketing" (research-airbnb-spotify-product-practices)
- [Vlad Loktev on Lenny's Podcast](sources/lenny-podcast-vlad-loktev-airbnb.md): the change was "a little overblown" but "very liberating"; PMs who are also good marketers are "a rare skill set" (1:23-1:26) (research-airbnb-spotify-product-practices)
- [TBM 255: The New Airbnb](sources/cutler-perri-tbm-255-new-airbnb.md): asks how anyone grows into a senior-only PM role (research-airbnb-spotify-product-practices)
- [Airbnb Q1 2026 earnings call and shareholder letter](sources/airbnb-earnings-q1-2026.md): design and engineering managers are "going back to coding or using" Claude Code (research-airbnb-spotify-product-practices)
- [The Future of Software Engineering Isn't What You Think](sources/medium-al-dahle-future-of-software-engineering.md): the "engineer-product thinker"; the product/engineering line "may disappear entirely" (research-airbnb-spotify-product-practices)
- [Inside-Out AI: Rebuilding Airbnb Behind the Scenes and Across the Guest Experience](sources/latent-space-airbnb-al-dahle-inside-out-ai.md): organise teams around outcomes and missions, not features (research-airbnb-spotify-product-practices)
- [What Happens When a Public Company Goes All In on AI](sources/a16z-owen-jennings-block-all-in-on-ai.md): "All of our product managers are shipping PRs"; fewer PMs per roadmap, more overall (research-block-product-practices)
- [Jack Dorsey: Every Company Can Now Be a Mini-AGI](sources/sequoia-dorsey-every-company-mini-agi.md): "product person" folded into the IC builder role; DRIs own strategy and roadmap (research-block-product-practices)
- [From Hierarchy to Intelligence](sources/block-from-hierarchy-to-intelligence.md): no PM among the three roles; "No product manager decided to build either solution" (research-block-product-practices)
- [Growth Manager, Activation & Habituation (Cash App)](sources/block-careers-growth-manager-activation.md): a growth role that "blurs growth and product", owns roadmap and experiments, uses Claude Code or Goose (research-block-product-practices)
- [Cameron Worboys: Inside an AI-native design org](sources/dive-club-cam-worboys-ai-native-design-org.md): "even product managers are coding stuff"; roles blur to who can ship (research-block-product-practices)
- [Square Global Head of Product (Product School)](sources/productschool-willem-ave-square-org-design-ai-agents.md): the DRI must "synthesize product technology and business" across the whole arc (research-block-product-practices)
- [Gumroad's customer support team ships code with Claude](sources/claude-customers-gumroad-support-ships-code.md): the founder predicts artists, writers and engineers will be "promoted to directors, editors, and product managers" (Looking forward). (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [Inside Rakuten's plan to turn every employee into a builder with Claude Managed Agents](sources/claude-customers-rakuten-every-employee-builder.md): PM Shoko Sakamoto builds multi-cloud FinOps pipelines and stakeholder dashboards and sets up ambient observability agents "all by herself" (Galileo answer). (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [How a non-technical project manager built and shipped a stress management app with Claude Code in six weeks](sources/claude-nontechnical-pm-ships-app.md): he now commits code releases and ships features at Mythical Games, and a small internal team there delivers work "entirely through Claude" ("Founder mode at work"). (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [Product management on the AI exponential](sources/claude-pm-on-the-ai-exponential.md): roles blend: designers ship code, engineers make product decisions, PMs build prototypes and evals. (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [Running an AI-native engineering org](sources/claude-running-ai-native-engineering-org.md): "Our PMs code a lot now"; engineers take on content and design; hiring indexes on creative builders with product sense and deep systems experts, less on raw throughput (Team makeup). (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [How to Build Powerful Internal AI Productivity Tools](sources/departmentofproduct-internal-ai-tools-ramp-glass.md): an emerging "internal AI specialist" role at OpenAI, Figma, Replit and Ramp (second-hand) (research-department-of-product-knowledge-series)
- [How to "vibe code"](sources/departmentofproduct-vibe-coding.md): three team scenarios; the author leans to designer-led, with PMs overseeing several squads "including eventually, autonomous AI teams" (research-department-of-product-knowledge-series)
- [What is parallel AI agent coding? An in-depth guide for product teams](sources/departmentofproduct-parallel-agent-coding.md): claim that PMs, as "mini orchestrators", could judge parallel agents' output and run feature variants as experiments (research-department-of-product-knowledge-series)
- [Claude Design is here](sources/departmentofproduct-claude-design.md): reads model-native design tools as "closing the gaps between each of the traditional product disciplines" (research-department-of-product-knowledge-series)
- [Head of Growth (Anthropic): "Claude is growing itself at this point"](sources/lenny-podcast-amol-avasare-anthropic-growth.md): five engineers now produce like 15-20, squeezing PM and design; Anthropic hires more PMs and makes engineers the PM for any project of two engineering weeks or less (43:04-45:00) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [AI's third era: the rise of persistent AI coworkers](sources/lenny-podcast-tara-seshan-persistent-coworkers.md): role boundaries dissolve but someone stays DRI for user value and quality (42:48) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [How we restructured Airtable's entire org for AI | Howie Liu](sources/lenny-podcast-howie-liu-airtable-reorg.md): PMs must become "hybrid PM prototyper" with design sense; every EPD role "minimally good at the other two"; AEs SE-fluent (55:00-1:12:06) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [Why every company now needs to think and operate like a lab team | Josh Woodward](sources/lenny-podcast-josh-woodward-labs-team.md): Google Labs piloted a builder job ladder before rolling it out across Google; PMs adapt fastest in builder pilots (36:14, 49:49) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [How tech workers are feeling in 2026](sources/lenny-newsletter-tech-workers-2026-survey.md): designers and researchers most anxious; research "democratized, not to other roles but to AI"; early-career ICs most destabilized (27%) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [What happens after coding is solved? | Fiona Fung](sources/lenny-podcast-fiona-fung-after-coding-solved.md): PMs and designers check in code on Claude Code; PMs "no longer bottlenecked" on engineering; design and data science next (8:16, 1:00:23) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [Zapier's CEO shares his personal AI stack](sources/howiai-zapier-wade-foster-ai-stack.md): merging job families is "one of the harder culture tasks"; "only builders" is overstated for 2025 (37:40) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [OpenAI Codex lead on the new shape of product work | Andrew Ambrosino](sources/lenny-podcast-ambrosino-codex-product-work.md): role = "the average of where you're working", but removing the PM role is "a terrible idea": "you can use Excel, but you cannot work on the finance team"; ICs manage agents (21:38-30:40) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [The AI paradox | Dan Shipper](sources/lenny-podcast-dan-shipper-ai-paradox.md): a "lightly technical" ex-PM runs Every's Spiral app and ships faster than almost anyone; full-stack designers as "superheroes" (1:08:40) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [How Intercom rose from the ashes ... | Eoghan McCabe](sources/lenny-podcast-mccabe-intercom-ai-bet.md): future orgs as "a medley of humans and agents", leaders in IC roles configuring and monitoring agents (42:08) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [Why humans are AI's biggest bottleneck (Alexander Embiricos)](sources/lenny-podcast-embiricos-codex-human-bottleneck.md): "compressing the talent stack": designers land PRs, a product marketer edits strings and docs from Slack (44:24-50:28) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [Why Netflix is betting on systems thinkers (Elizabeth Stone)](sources/lenny-podcast-elizabeth-stone-netflix-systems-thinkers.md): PMs, designers, data scientists get further before engineering is needed; finance and content stakeholders generate hypotheses from data; but not everyone should ship to production (3:44-9:52) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [Why half of product managers are in trouble (Nikhyl Singhal)](sources/lenny-podcast-nikhyl-singhal-half-of-pms.md): PMs spread to other functions as "agents of change"; engineers become "more PM-y" (1:09:20-1:15:35) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [OpenAI's CPO on how AI changes must-have skills (Kevin Weil)](sources/lenny-podcast-kevin-weil-openai-cpo.md): ~25 PMs, deliberately PM-light; predicts ML/research roles on every product team (48:11, 57:36) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [Head of Claude Code (Boris Cherny)](sources/lenny-podcast-boris-cherny-after-coding.md): "maybe a 50% overlap" between PM, eng and design on his team; the PM does more coordination, planning and forecasting; predicts "builder" replaces "software engineer" (42:46-43:06) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [OpenAI's Head of Design (Ian Silber)](sources/lenny-podcast-ian-silber-openai-design.md): roles blurrier but still distinct "hats" at scale; still values a PM who rallies teams and sharpens the problem space (18:12-21:26) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [This CPO regrets that product management exists (Tom Verrilli)](sources/lenny-podcast-tom-verrilli-whatnot-pm.md): ~21 PMs for $8B+ GMV, mapped to six-monthly problems not teams; engineers and designers as DRIs; rising "engineering manager light" role (9:10, 15:28, 43:07) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [Community Wisdom: How PMs are using AI coding tools](sources/lenny-community-wisdom-pms-ai-coding-tools.md): where org processes exist "for audit reasons", a PM can't do product work without separate project-management support (thread 2) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [The AI-native startup (Dan Shipper, Every)](sources/lenny-podcast-dan-shipper-every-ai-native.md): "allocation economy": management skills held by ~8% of workers become universal as everyone manages agents (50:33) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [How Anthropic's product team moves faster than anyone else | Cat Wu](sources/lenny-podcast-cat-wu-anthropic-product-team.md): engineers with product taste ship from Twitter feedback to release in a week with no PM; nearly all PMs ship code; designers were front-end engineers (16:15-17:54) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [The grief, loneliness, and burnout ... | Molly Graham](sources/lenny-podcast-molly-graham-delegating-to-ai.md): "everyone in the world is a manager now", including ICs who chose not to manage; managing agents uses the same skills as managing people (46:30) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [How Grok Bot designers use AI agents ...](sources/howiai-grok-bot-designers-agents.md): designer turns "shower thoughts" into interactive prototypes without first going through a PM or engineer (25:59-30:21) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [Everyone's an engineer now | Guillermo Rauch](sources/lenny-podcast-guillermo-rauch-v0.md): Vercel's most effective people combine design and engineering; translation-type specialisms disappearing (17:52-22:22) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [From managing people to managing AI: Julie Zhuo](sources/lenny-podcast-julie-zhuo-managing-ai.md): Sundial dropped planned PM hires; everyone is a "builder" and engineers own product definition (14:42-17:01) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [The design process is dead: Jenny Wen](sources/lenny-podcast-jenny-wen-design-process-dead.md): designers "becoming more PM shape ... engineering shaped"; she implements polish in code (46:26, 18:57) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [Becoming an AI PM: Aman Khan](sources/lenny-podcast-aman-khan-becoming-ai-pm.md): 2024 three-way split: platform, AI-product and "AI-powered" PMs (8:09) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [Adam Mosseri: AI is a tailwind for authenticity](sources/lenny-podcast-adam-mosseri-product-staff.md): Instagram moved in 2026 from ~13-person specialist teams to pods of 4-6 generalist engineers plus one "product staff" (PM doing some design, data science and research with internal AI tools); smallest pods have no designer, data scientist or researcher (2:33, 5:57) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [Why LinkedIn is turning PMs into AI-powered "full stack builders"](sources/lenny-podcast-tomer-cohen-full-stack-builder.md): Full Stack Builder title and ladder; APM program replaced by Associate Product Builder (Jan 2026); pods assembled per quarter; a user researcher became a growth PM (14:55, 35:58, 42:57) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [No Figma. No Jira. No docs. How Gusto built a new product line with Claude Code](sources/howiai-gusto-eddie-kim-cofounder.md): no PM on the team; "everybody was kind of a product manager" (13:27) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [Why cultivating agency matters more than cultivating skills](sources/lenny-podcast-max-schoening-agency.md): wants designers and PMs who understand agent loops as material, "not a cog in the delivery mechanism" (8:53-10:14) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [All of the Lenny & Friends Summit talks are now online!](sources/lenny-newsletter-summit-talks-online.md): summit consensus that roles are "expanding, not disappearing"; Ramp's Geoff Charles: "PMs will become GMs" (trend 4) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [How Amplitude built an internal AI tool](sources/howiai-amplitude-wade-chambers-moda.md): role-swapping exercises across engineers, designers and PMs (show notes only) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [The rise of the professional vibe coder (Lazar Jovanovic)](sources/lenny-podcast-lazar-jovanovic-vibe-coder.md): engineer, designer and PM roles "converging"; "we're all becoming product managers on steroids" (47:48, 1:04:54) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [Community Wisdom: How AI is changing product operating models](sources/lenny-community-wisdom-ai-operating-models.md): PMs and designers branch POCs off main instead of handing over PRDs and Figma; another org bars PMs from production code (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [Community Wisdom: Top Contributors Summer 2026 (product engineers pilot)](sources/lenny-community-wisdom-product-engineers-pilot.md): product-engineer pilot: "what we managed to deliver like this in 2 months would have taken us 10"; fixed trio replaced by fluid 1-2 engineer teams (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [Community Wisdom: when engineering outpaces product](sources/lenny-community-wisdom-engineering-outpaces-product.md): "aspire to shift some PM responsibility to engineers"; hire product intuition into EMs (thread 2) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [How AI is reshaping the product role (Udezue)](sources/lenny-podcast-udezue-ai-reshaping-pm-role.md): "shipyard team" of six capabilities (PM, eng, design, research, data/ML, PMM) collaborating hourly, with sales/support as "tendrils" (12:58-16:19) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [How to ship like a startup (Figma Slides)](sources/lenny-newsletter-figma-slides-ship-like-startup.md): "Everyone is a part-time PM"; engineers in design syncs; handoffs as live pairing (lesson 5) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [Quests, token leaderboards, and a skills marketplace (How I AI)](sources/howiai-sendbird-john-kim-adoption-playbook.md): new "AI engineer for internal operations" role; JDs rewritten to lower tenure and select for curiosity, agency, energy (14:56, 35:05) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [Community Wisdom: Building without clear PM requirements](sources/lenny-community-wisdom-building-without-pm-requirements.md): "product owns the why and what, eng owns the how" — does the line hold "now that building is becoming a shared capability through AI"? (thread 1) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [How 80,000 companies build with AI (Lenny's Podcast)](sources/lenny-podcast-asha-sharma-loop-not-lane.md): "the loop, not the lane": ~500 touchpoints per launch drive full-stack builders, even in 50-year-old enterprises (11:05-14:21) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [Gumroad CEO's playbook to 40x his team's productivity (How I AI)](sources/howiai-gumroad-sahil-lavingia-v0-devin.md): "making design more about product, making engineering more about architecture" (34:14) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [Marty Cagan on AI in product management (airfocus)](sources/airfocus-cagan-ai-product-management.md): Cagan: the delivery-process product-owner role is easy for an AI assistant to dent; product leaders 'need to drive this whole discussion' (P2). 'Theater' is not on this page (see svpg-product-management-theater). (research-pm-agents-jobs-to-be-done)
- [How AI turns product managers back into builders](sources/atlassian-ai-turns-pms-into-builders.md): Prototyping as a PM job in the founder-PM persona (P3). (research-pm-agents-jobs-to-be-done)
- [The bottleneck keeps shifting: what AI is changing about how we build (Gamma interview)](sources/atlassian-bottleneck-keeps-shifting-gamma.md): Gamma co-founder Jon Noronha: ~1 PM to 4 engineers (article sets it against a 1:10 rule of thumb); half of Gamma's PMs and designers commit code; Noronha calls his job 'context wrangler'. - [The Definitive Chief Product Officer Job Description (LaunchNotes)](sources/launchnotes-cpo-job-description.md): CPO collaborates with the C-suite, is measured on KPIs, shapes the roadmap, manages PMs and designers (board communication and product ops not on the page). - [AI tools are overdelivering: results from our large-scale AI productivity survey](sources/lennys-newsletter-ai-tools-overdelivering-results.md): Founders report highest satisfaction, with productivity and decision support as top use (32.9%); designers use AI most for research synthesis (22.3%) and content (17.4%). - [What does product operations do? (Parallel HQ)](sources/parallelhq-what-does-product-operations-do.md): Product ops covers processes, tools and data: standardises workflows and documentation, manages tool standardisation, keeps a single source of truth for the roadmap, maintains metrics/feedback/usage data. - [Product launch checklist for product marketers (Product School)](sources/productschool-launch-checklist-product-marketers.md): Checklist addressed to PMMs; launch timing named as a PMM decision; positioning, messaging, tiering and pricing listed without named owners; no source settles who breaks ties. (research-pm-agents-jobs-to-be-done)
- [More valuable, less protected](sources/reforge-more-valuable-less-protected.md): Prototyping, once dependent on engineering, is now open to PMs and designers; PMs now distribute context so teams decide without roadmap gatekeeping. (research-pm-agents-jobs-to-be-done)
- [The Era of the Product Creator](sources/svpg-era-of-the-product-creator.md): Product creators are those actively shaping the product and tackling product risks, whatever their title; non-creator PMs will be left behind; succeeding alone will be the rare exception. ## policy-enforcement-fail-open: Agent policy layers that fail open
Policy layers enforce only at the seams they hook, and gaps (errors, unparsed actions, internal tools, sub-agents) have defaulted to allow. In a regulated setting, whether a control fails open or closed matters as much as what it expresses. Our coined label.
- [How Airbnb Guardrailed Its AI Customer Support Agent (QCon San Francisco 2026 abstract)](sources/qconsf-2026-airbnb-guardrails-support-agent.md): input sanitisation plus classifiers on user input and agent drafts; became a centralised AI risk platform (research-airbnb-spotify-product-practices)
- [Automation Platform v2: Improving Conversational AI at Airbnb](sources/airbnb-tech-automation-platform-v2.md): reusable parallel guardrails, including tool guardrails that block invalid listing updates (research-airbnb-spotify-product-practices)
- [MCP (Spotify Portal docs)](sources/spotify-portal-docs-mcp.md): the Actions Registry doesn't enforce permissions; each tool must check (research-airbnb-spotify-product-practices)
- [Adversary Mode (goose docs)](sources/goose-docs-adversary-mode.md): the reviewer agent allows the call if it errors, and is off by default (research-block-product-practices)
- [goose Extension Allowlist (docs)](sources/goose-docs-extension-allowlist.md): no env var means no restriction (research-block-product-practices)
- [Running auto mode in production](sources/claude-auto-mode-in-production.md): the classifier "does not eliminate risk"; in a red-team set the miss rate fell from 12% to 7%, and broad allow-rules such as `python:*` are set aside in auto mode because they would bypass the classifier (companion:... (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [Customize Claude Code with mods in TypeScript](sources/claude-code-mods.md): sec-default stops user mods overriding permission deny rules, but admins who load their own mods first must add sec-default back or lose its restrictions (enterprise section). (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [Inference hooks: inline data loss prevention for Claude Enterprise](sources/claude-enterprise-inference-hooks.md): "Customize failure-policy tolerance, timeouts" lets each org choose what happens when the DLP server is slow or down; the post does not state the default ("Ways to use inference hooks"). (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [Steering Claude Code: when to use CLAUDE.md, skills, hooks, and subagents](sources/claude-steering-claude-code.md): prompted "never do this" rules fail under pressure, in long sessions, ambiguity or prompt injection; real guardrails are hooks (PreToolUse exit code 2) and permissions, with managed settings for org-wide enforcement ("When to... (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [Zero Trust for AI agents](sources/claude-zero-trust-for-ai-agents.md): Ch 02 "impossible, not tedious" test: friction controls (rate limits, extra hops, SMS MFA) fail against patient agentic attackers; Ch 05 cites fail-closed matching for unrecognised commands. (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [MCP Actions (Backstage AI docs)](sources/backstage-docs-mcp-actions.md): action attributes `destructive`/`readOnly` are hints clients may use to ask for confirmation; defaults are "conservative" and should be set explicitly (Action attributes). Per secondary docs, the registry does not enforce permissions; each action handler must (search summary, see Could not verify). (first-party; research-dependency-agent)
- [Decision: Remark and administrative fine, Swedbank AB (FI Ref. 22-18430)](sources/fi-swedbank-change-management-sanction.md): it "had been possible for employees to assess, decide on, and implement the change in question without control measures or involvement from persons higher up within the organisation" despite first-, second- and third-line review of the change process (bank's statement, 2.2.2). (first-party; research-dependency-agent)
- [The coming AI security crisis | Sander Schulhoff](sources/lenny-podcast-sander-schulhoff-ai-security.md): guardrails are bypassable by determined attackers and "quite likely to make you overconfident in your security posture" (1:27:24) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [omnigent-ai/omnigent issues and discussions on shared-session identity, audit evidence and enterprise authorisation (#2150, #5670, #10359, #11493, discussions #5931 and #1133)](sources/github-omnigent-identity-audit-issues.md): The nearest thing to adopter testimony: outside teams evaluating Omnigent for multi-user pilots describe exactly the gaps a regulated audit setting would hit. (research-runtime-patterns-follow-up-round)
- [omnigent-ai/omnigent security advisories and policy-bypass issues](sources/github-omnigent-security-advisories.md): The strongest evidence found on how Omnigent's governance layer behaves under attack. (research-runtime-patterns-follow-up-round)
- [CVE-2026-62676: omnigent Shell-Command Parser Fails Open, Allowing Policy Bypass](sources/securelayer7-cve-2026-62676-omnigent.md): An independent security firm's write-up of Omnigent's first published guardrail CVE. (research-runtime-patterns-follow-up-round)
- [Hooks reference (Claude Code)](sources/anthropic-claude-code-hooks-reference.md): a timed-out hook "doesn't block the tool call"; exit 1 is non-blocking; "If your hook is meant to enforce a policy, use exit 2" (research-skill-rigidity-spectrum)
- [Configure permissions (Claude Agent SDK)](sources/anthropic-agent-sdk-permissions.md): checks in `canUseTool` are "silently bypassed" for auto-approved tools (research-skill-rigidity-spectrum)
- [Guardrails (OpenAI Agents SDK)](sources/openai-agents-sdk-guardrails.md): with parallel guardrails, the agent may already have run tools before the tripwire fires (research-skill-rigidity-spectrum)
