## process-artifacts-as-coordination: Process artifacts as the coordination layer
Decision logs, assumption registers, task lists, checklists and change folders are what let several people and agents hold one quality bar over days or weeks. Their content is judgment; their structure is where deterministic gates attach.
- [Dependency Management in Large-Scale Agile: A Case Study of DevOps Teams](sources/aisel-stray-moe-aasheim-dependency-management-devops-teams.md): nine of the 20 mechanisms are synchronisation artefacts (Abstract). (independent; research-dependency-agent)
- [Coordinating Knowledge Work in Multi-Team Programs: Findings from a Large-Scale Agile Development Program](sources/arxiv-dingsoyr-coordinating-multi-team-programs.md): the master plan began as a spreadsheet and was replaced about a year in by Jira because of two problems: no overview at that size, and "it was difficult to know what the latest version of the spreadsheet was" (§Impersonal mode). All process descriptions, guidelines and checklists lived in a mandatory wiki. (independent; research-dependency-agent)
- [Define dependencies between work with plans in Jira](sources/atlassian-jira-plans-dependencies-lesson.md): the Dependencies report shows all dependencies in a plan as a visual matrix to spot bottlenecks, filterable by parent, epic, space, team, sprint or dependency type; lines "will turn red if there are conflicting dates" (lesson body). (vendor-claim; research-dependency-agent)
- [Nine things a (technical) program manager does](sources/balter-nine-things-technical-program-manager.md): item 7: "Everything (and I do mean everything) is documented, discoverable, and socialized"; the TPM surfaces pending decisions and makes sure decision-makers have what they need. (anecdote; research-dependency-agent)
- [How to manage dependencies with Jira Align](sources/eficode-manage-dependencies-jira-align.md): views include the dependency list ("the to-do list for teams and leaders"), the Program Board with colour-coded planning issues, Team Room and Program Room, and five further views: Grid/Matrix, Wheel Map, Analytics Map, Team, and Program or Increment Status. (vendor-claim; research-dependency-agent)
- [Challenges and success factors for large-scale agile transformations: A systematic literature review](sources/jss-dikert-large-scale-agile-transformations.md): "High-level requirements management largely missing in agile" (12% of cases) and "Gap between long and short term planning" (14%) (Table 11). (independent; research-dependency-agent)
- [3.10 – RAID Log (Overview & Template Guide)](sources/lga-raid-log-guidance-sds.md): "The RAID Log is the single place to record and manage Risks, Assumptions, Issues, and Dependencies" (§1); monthly pack includes "Top 10 RAID items", new and closed counts, a "dependency heatmap" and a one-page narrative of decisions needed (§6). (first-party; research-dependency-agent)
- [Track dependencies in Delivery Plans - Azure Boards](sources/microsoft-azure-devops-track-dependencies-delivery-plans.md): green/red icons on cards and black/red lines on the plan; best practice is to check dependency status in sprint planning and reviews (§Best practices). (vendor-claim; research-dependency-agent)
- [All-in-One PI Planning Template](sources/miro-humana-coach-all-in-one-pi-planning-template.md): boards included are PI Calendar, multi-ART PI Planning Agenda, Solution Board, team areas, Program Board, Program Risk ROAM Board (resolved, owned, accepted, mitigated) and ART Confidence Vote (1-5). (anecdote; research-dependency-agent)
- [Onboarding to the National Record Locator (NRL) v3.0](sources/nhs-england-nrl-onboarding-guidance.md): stage outputs are artefacts (app ID and non-production credentials, test evidence, conformance certificate, signed connection agreement). (first-party; research-dependency-agent)
- [SAFe® Program Dependency Board Retrospective – PI Planning and Execution](sources/scaledagile-yeret-program-dependency-board-retrospective.md): proposes a "deeper learning" retrospective on the board after PI planning, discussed at a Scrum of Scrums or ART leadership forum, often leading to re-running Value Stream Identification (VSI) (body). (anecdote; research-dependency-agent)
- [Soon time for one of Europe's largest PI planning events](sources/sebgroup-europes-largest-pi-planning.md): the planning event is the coordination layer; "greater transparency and a better understanding of interdependencies" reported as an effect. (first-party; research-dependency-agent)
- [A taxonomy of inter-team coordination mechanisms in large-scale agile](sources/sintef-berntzen-inter-team-coordination-taxonomy.md): tools and artefacts are one of the three mechanism classes; the TOPS framework characterises each mechanism as technical, organisational, physical and social. (independent; research-dependency-agent)
- [Banking at scale: a blueprint for delivery transformation using Team Topologies](sources/teamtopologies-pujar-banking-at-scale.md): live dependency trackers, QBRs and squad health dashboards; work tracked in Azure Boards as Epic, Feature, User Story, Task. (anecdote; research-dependency-agent)
- [Lloyds Bank reviews tech and engineering personnel in reorg](sources/theregister-lloyds-tech-engineering-reorg.md): product teams each had their own Jira instance ("somewhat siloed"); consolidation into a single view makes work visible across teams so it can be assigned and linked (body, anonymous source). (independent; research-dependency-agent)
- [Coordination Challenges in Large-Scale Software Development: A Case Study of Planning Misalignment in Hybrid Settings](sources/tse-bick-planning-misalignment-dependency-awareness.md): recommends aligning planning activities across levels to improve dependency awareness and in turn coordination (abstract). (independent; research-dependency-agent)
- [Context Graphs: AI's Trillion-Dollar Opportunity](sources/foundationcapital-context-graphs.md): defines a context graph as decision traces (inputs, policy version, exceptions, precedents, approver) captured at decision time; no data offered (research-skill-rigidity-spectrum)
- [Documenting Architecture Decisions](sources/nygard-documenting-architecture-decisions.md): ADRs exist so rotating contributors neither blindly accept nor blindly reverse past decisions; six to ten developers found them useful (research-skill-rigidity-spectrum)
- [Design Docs at Google](sources/industrialempathy-design-docs-at-google.md): design docs serve consensus, knowledge spread and organisational memory; revisited a year or two later (research-skill-rigidity-spectrum)
- [Assumption Testing](sources/producttalk-torres-assumption-testing.md): each assumption test logged with six fields including pre-set success criteria and how the team acted (research-skill-rigidity-spectrum)
- [Orchestrate teams of Claude Code sessions](sources/anthropic-claude-code-agent-teams.md): shared task list with dependency blocking and file-locked claiming; docs admit task status can lag (research-skill-rigidity-spectrum)
- [MetaGPT](sources/arxiv-metagpt.md): structured PRD, then design, then task handoffs; full role team 4.0 executability vs 1.0 for a lone engineer agent (research-skill-rigidity-spectrum)
- [Agent interaction (Linear)](sources/linear-developers-agent-interaction.md): agent runs as sessions on issues with typed elicitation activities and a checklist plan humans can watch (research-skill-rigidity-spectrum)
- [OpenSpec](sources/github-openspec-readme.md): per-change folder (proposal, spec deltas, design, tasks) archived into canonical specs (research-skill-rigidity-spectrum)
- [The 2020 Scrum Guide](sources/scrumguides-scrum-guide-2020.md): Definition of Done gives everyone a shared understanding of what is complete; no Definition of Ready in the guide (research-skill-rigidity-spectrum)
- [An insider look at Amazon's culture and processes](sources/aboutamazon-insider-look-working-backwards.md): PR/FAQ review minutes circulated after each meeting; document stays live after approval (research-skill-rigidity-spectrum)

## process-governance-load: Process governance as a dependency: gates, evidence and waiting
Change advisory, architecture review, security, privacy, model risk, third-party risk, filings and audit as gates a product team must satisfy; how they actually operate (the gate that never says no, the gate that was skipped) and what they cost.
- [Challenges of Adopting SAFe in the Banking Industry – A Study Two Years after its Introduction](sources/arxiv-tengstrand-safe-banking-challenges.md): a "Banking specific" category: "G1. External rules and regulations complicate transformations"; and "A1. Difficult to adapt existing internal processes to the agile development practices" (Table 1). (independent; research-dependency-agent)
- [How JPMorgan Chase built a data mesh architecture to drive significant value to enhance their enterprise data platform](sources/aws-jpmc-data-mesh-enterprise-data-platform.md): the stated goal is to make data easy to share while keeping appropriate control in a regulated industry (introduction). (first-party; research-dependency-agent)
- [CNCF Platforms White Paper](sources/cncf-tag-app-delivery-platforms-white-paper.md): platforms aim to lower security, regulatory and functional risk through governance; "secure by default" builds compliance and validation in from organisational rules (Why platforms; Attributes). (independent; research-dependency-agent)
- [Build-Run Teams and Segregation of Responsibility](sources/curvelogic-hawkins-build-run-segregation.md): "SoR makes it hard to do bad things by making it hard to do anything." Strong segregation by department is effective but heavyweight and prone to rubber-stamping. (anecdote; research-dependency-agent)
- [DORA Report 2024 (Accelerate State of DevOps)](sources/dora-accelerate-state-of-devops-2024.md): unstable priorities reduce productivity and raise burnout; the effect is "highly resistant to mitigation" (findings list). (independent; research-dependency-agent)
- [Capabilities: Streamlining change approval](sources/dora-capability-streamlining-change-approval.md): external approval (a CAB or senior manager) hurts delivery performance; centralised CABs "add delay and error" because approvers are far from the change (Overview). (independent; research-dependency-agent)
- [Accelerate: State of DevOps 2019](sources/dora-state-of-devops-2019.md): "formal change management processes that require the approval of an external body such as a change advisory board (CAB) or a senior manager for significant changes have a negative impact on software delivery performance"; respondents were "2.6 times more likely to be low performers" (p. 50, "Heavyweight change process"). (independent; research-dependency-agent)
- [The Change Enablement Practice: What Changed with Change in ITIL 4](sources/easyvista-mann-itil4-change-enablement.md): product-focused organisations should embed change enablement in product teams rather than keep change-specific job titles (author's reading). (independent; research-dependency-agent)
- [Final Report on EBA Guidelines on outsourcing arrangements (EBA/GL/2019/02)](sources/eba-guidelines-outsourcing-arrangements.md): para 58: inform competent authorities "in a timely manner" or engage in supervisory dialogue about planned outsourcing of critical or important functions (p. 38); para 60: document the assessments and ongoing monitoring results. (first-party; research-dependency-agent)
- [Escape ticketing hell with a shift to self-service platforms](sources/equalexperts-smith-escape-ticketing-hell.md): self-service workflows keep "automated guardrails and audit trails", visualised in a platform portal, so control is kept without the queue. (anecdote; research-dependency-agent)
- [Regulation (EU) 2022/2554 on digital operational resilience for the financial sector (DORA)](sources/eu-dora-regulation-ict-risk-third-party.md): Art. 28(4): before contracting, assess whether the arrangement supports a critical or important function, whether supervisory conditions are met, all relevant risks including concentration risk (Art. 29), due diligence on the provider, and conflicts of interest. (first-party; research-dependency-agent)
- [Implementing technology change](sources/fca-implementing-technology-change.md): firms with governance established for more than a year had a lower proportion of change-related incidents; firms managing change risk continuously within day-to-day project management had higher success rates than those using periodic or ad hoc approaches (Findings: governance). (first-party; research-dependency-agent)
- [Computer Software Assurance for Production and Quality System Software; Guidance for Industry and Food and Drug Administration Staff; Availability](sources/fda-computer-software-assurance-notice-2025.md): "software testing alone is often insufficient to establish confidence that the software is fit for its intended use" (I. Background). (first-party; research-dependency-agent)
- [Interagency Guidance on Third-Party Relationships: Risk Management](sources/fed-fdic-occ-third-party-risk-guidance-2023.md): due diligence covers "a. Strategies and Goals; b. Legal and Regulatory Compliance; c. Financial Condition; d. Business Experience; e. Qualifications and Backgrounds of Key Personnel...; f. Risk Management; g. Information Security; h. Management of Information Systems; i. Operational Resilience; j. Incident Reporting and Management Processes; k. Physical Security; l. Reliance on Subcontractors; m. Insurance Coverag... (first-party; research-dependency-agent)
- [Supervisory Guidance on Model Risk Management (SR 11-7, attachment)](sources/federalreserve-sr-11-7-model-risk-guidance.md): vendor products are in scope: "Banks are expected to validate their own use of vendor products" and should require vendors to provide developmental evidence (Validation of Vendor and Other Third-Party Products, p. 15). (first-party; research-dependency-agent)
- [Decision: Remark and administrative fine, Swedbank AB (FI Ref. 22-18430)](sources/fi-swedbank-change-management-sanction.md): remediation included building "a functionality in the system in question to ensure compliance with the change management process" and more extensive mandatory annual training (2.2.2). (first-party; research-dependency-agent)
- [Cloud Security: Federal Authorization Program Usage Increasing, but Challenges Need to Be Fully Addressed (GAO-24-106591)](sources/gao-cloud-security-fedramp-challenges-2024.md): estimated authorisation costs "ranged anywhere from tens of thousands to millions of dollars"; OMB had not issued guidance on which costs to track (Highlights). (independent; research-dependency-agent)
- [HealthCare.gov: Case Study of CMS Management of the Federal Marketplace (OEI-06-14-00350)](sources/hhs-oig-healthcare-gov-case-study.md): "poor coordination between policy and technical work, resistance to communicating and heeding warnings of 'bad news,' and reluctance to alter plans"; staff became "path dependent" (Executive summary; Lessons). (independent; research-dependency-agent)
- [When do we need to do a DPIA?](sources/ico-when-do-we-need-a-dpia.md): DPIA framed as a planning tool, e.g. deciding "what proportionate security measures should be implemented" and as "a reminder that UK GDPR-compliant contracts need to be in place with any processors". (first-party; research-dependency-agent)
- [The IIA's Three Lines Model: An update of the Three Lines of Defense](sources/iia-three-lines-model-2020.md): "First line roles are most directly aligned with the delivery of products and/or services to clients of the organization and include the roles of support functions. Second line roles assist with managing risk." (Principle 3, p. 5) (first-party; research-dependency-agent)
- [CBA pushing to production more often, with fewer incidents](sources/itnews-cba-production-more-often-fewer-incidents.md): a "4x increase in the velocity of the cyber reviews". (first-party; research-dependency-agent)
- [Episode 3: The Quest for Accelerated Delivery (DevOps Enterprise Summit 2016)](sources/itrevolution-nationwide-does16-accelerated-delivery.md): problem framed as "Water-SCRUM-Fall": "Teams waiting for work due to 'discrete' planning processes" (slide 5); moved from readiness-based to time-based releases. (first-party; research-dependency-agent)
- [Driving enterprise software delivery](sources/jpmorganchase-driving-enterprise-software-delivery.md): capabilities "must have compliance checks, security scans and threat modeling built in from the start"; "shifting extreme left on our security and compliance focus, right from the design phase". (first-party; research-dependency-agent)
- [Challenges and success factors for large-scale agile transformations: A systematic literature review](sources/jss-dikert-large-scale-agile-transformations.md): functions beyond development that interface with it included "infrastructure and operations", "legal", "security", "customer services" and "finance"; "The full benefits of the transformation could not be attained unless the entire organization was set to work along the same paradigm" (4.2.9). (independent; research-dependency-agent)
- [3.10 – RAID Log (Overview & Template Guide)](sources/lga-raid-log-guidance-sds.md): roles (§3.1) are a RAID owner who updates before gateways and monthly reporting, theme leads who own entries, and an SRO/programme board who approves escalations; cadence (§3.2) is weekly triage, monthly board review, gateway reviews. - [Delivering large-scale IT projects on time, on budget, and on value](sources/mckinsey-delivering-large-scale-it-projects.md): "every additional year spent on the project increasing cost overruns by 15 percent" (body). (vendor-claim; research-dependency-agent)
- [ING's agile transformation](sources/mckinsey-ing-agile-transformation.md): legal, finance and operational risk "are not part of a squad per se, as they need to be independent, but a squad can call on them"; regulators "were at times worried that agile meant freedom and chaos" (Schlatmann). - [Building a world-class platform for software engineers](sources/mit-tr-jpmorgan-world-class-engineering-platform.md): the platform "abstracts controls by automatically factoring in the relevant workflows and processes"; audits save engineers "several days and weeks of effort" (body). - [Speed to Market (D) Working Group, Virtual Meeting, April 23, 2026 (draft minutes, Attachment 1)](sources/naic-speed-to-market-wg-minutes-april-2026.md): a commissioner-facing filing metrics report built from SERFF data "did not meet the Spring National Meeting deadline and remains in process" (item 2); the uniform transmittal document is "a holdover from pre-SERFF paper filings" and may be retired (item 2). - [The challenges in implementing digital change](sources/nao-challenges-implementing-digital-change.md): recommends reviewing business-case approval to "remove the incentives to state with full confidence those things which are still unknown" and to be "clear on what risks represent 'unknown unknowns'" (Recommendation b). - [Framework to review programmes (Update April 2021)](sources/nao-framework-to-review-programmes.md): under cost and schedule (Question 6), "Does the programme schedule reflect dependencies on activities managed within and outside the programme?" and whether the critical path has been assessed as achievable (p.11 of 36). - [Onboarding to the National Record Locator (NRL) v3.0](sources/nhs-england-nrl-onboarding-guidance.md): Stage 2 requires clinical risk management documents (DCB0129/DCB0160), a hazard log, information-governance confirmation and security architecture where required; "NHS England will review submitted evidence and may request clarification or updates". - [Change Advisory Boards Don't Work](sources/octopus-change-advisory-boards-dont-work.md): auditability matters more to regulators than the review format; pull requests with branch protection or logged pipeline approvals can provide it (author's view; advises seeking legal advice). (anecdote; research-dependency-agent)
- [Puppet's 2024 State of DevOps Report Reveals Security is Strengthened by Platform Engineering](sources/perforce-puppet-state-of-devops-2024-platform-engineering.md): 43% report a dedicated security and compliance team on their platform; 51% say platform teams enforce software and tool versions for security updates. - [2023 Project to Product State of the Industry Report](sources/planview-project-to-product-state-of-industry-2023.md): system data: "Completed code commonly idles for 3+ months before it's released"; "30-40% of end-to-end delivery time is spent on software testing and release activities", with bottlenecks "in the junctions where work from multiple contributors converges" (p. 18). - [Pulse of the Profession 2018: Success in Disruptive Times](sources/pmi-pulse-of-the-profession-2018.md): "9.9% of every dollar is wasted due to poor project performance", down from 13.5% in 2013; "champions" waste 1.4% versus 29.1% for "underperformers" (report body, Champions comparison). - [The Scrum@Scale Guide](sources/scrumatscale-guide-scrum-of-scrums.md): the Executive Action Team is "accountable for removing impediments that cannot be removed by members of the Scrum of Scrums" and must be made of people "empowered, politically and financially, to remove them" (§Executive Action Team). (independent; research-dependency-agent)
- [Add details to demands (Demand Management)](sources/servicenow-demand-management-add-details.md): "Demand managers analyze business demands, approve demands, and create projects and enhancements"; demand tasks gather effort, cost, risk and benefit estimates "needed for a business case" (body). (vendor-claim; research-dependency-agent)
- [Platform as a Product in a 300-Year-Old Bank](sources/syntasso-natwest-platform-as-product-300-year-old-bank.md): principles include reviewed and traceable changes, Git as source of truth, reconciliation to prevent drift, "governable". (vendor-claim; research-dependency-agent)
- [When DORA metrics meet governance in banking - Expert View](sources/teamtopologies-dora-metrics-governance-banking.md): one engineer's documented path for a single line of code: "It required 3 different Jiras, a change ticket, and 81 individual steps just to get the paperwork created and approved" (Morgan Stanley example). ## product-artifact-primitives: Native PM artifact objects and project containers across platforms
What each platform treats as its first-class product-work objects (idea, initiative, project, space, spec, insight, document, skill) and how a 'project' is bounded. Matters for deciding whether a product meta-harness defines its own primitives or maps onto existing ones.
- [Spotify Rhythm: How we create focus](sources/kniberg-spotify-rhythm.md): the bets board was a Google Sheet open to all; cascading company, product and tribe boards (slides 13-16) (research-airbnb-spotify-product-practices)
- [From Gut to Plan: The Thoughtful Execution Framework](sources/spotify-design-thoughtful-execution-framework.md): tree shipped as PDF, Figma and MURAL templates (research-airbnb-spotify-product-practices)
- [Scorecards: Creating Alignment Throughout the Process](sources/spotify-design-scorecards-alignment.md): Understand It Brief and Scorecard templates with fail, success and surpass levels (research-airbnb-spotify-product-practices)
- [Projects redesigned: from folder to conversation](sources/claude-code-projects-redesigned.md): project library collects files you add and artifacts Claude produces. (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [Claude Cowork and chat are now one Claude](sources/claude-cowork-chat-unified.md): Claude Docs and Claude Slides launched (beta, paid plans), Claude Design available inside conversations; artifacts live at one shareable link, editable directly or by commenting to Claude, exportable to PowerPoint or PDF... (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [How the product designer who built Claude Design uses it](sources/claude-design-designer-workflow.md): HTML as the universal medium for decks, one-pagers, emails, animations, and "designs that are also their own editors" ("Make it alive"). (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [How to use Claude Projects and Skills to Monitor your Product's Health](sources/departmentofproduct-claude-projects-product-health.md): a Project (instructions, knowledge files, history) is the PM's standing container; filename prefixes stand in for structure (research-department-of-product-knowledge-series)
- [Frequently asked questions about Planner Agent](sources/microsoft-support-planner-agent-faq.md): the agent is an assignee on Planner tasks; output lives in Loop components inside the plan. (first-party; research-dependency-agent)
- [Claude Duet is beautiful. I still forgot to use it](sources/howiai-claire-vo-claude-duet-review.md): Duet's primitives are task lists (user's and agent's), first-class artifacts carried over from the Claude account, and Slack-style channels; "we're all trying to decide what the primitives are for agents" (3:07-4:38) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- ["I'm incapable of doing my job without AI"](sources/howiai-monday-amir-klein-second-brain.md): a Monday.com PM keeps one chat-app project per workstream as a "second brain", seeded with kickoff decks and PRDs and fed back its own outputs (0:14, 17:04) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [HTML is the new Markdown | Thariq Shihipar](sources/howiai-thariq-shihipar-html-specs.md): throwaway micro-UIs to edit parts of a plan; comments and annotations on HTML plans (18:16, 30:16; show notes only) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [How to build your PM second brain](sources/lenny-newsletter-pm-second-brain-chatgpt.md): one ChatGPT/Claude Project or Gemini Gem per initiative, instructions plus files, as the PM's working container (Step 1, Appendix) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [How OpenAI uses ChatGPT Sites (Kath Korevec)](sources/howiai-openai-korevec-chatgpt-sites.md): Sites hosts Codex-built web artifacts with storage, co-editors and deploy; used for DevDay keynote slides and throwaway personal tools (1:32, 9:46) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [Claude Cowork 101](sources/howiai-jj-englert-cowork-101.md): Cowork project = folder plus shared memory across chats, project instructions and a context panel (15:35-17:43) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [How to build your own AI developer tools with Claude Code](sources/howiai-tenex-cj-hess-flowy.md): Flowy renders agent-written JSON as editable flowcharts and mockups; edits save back for the agent to read (10:44, 30:26) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [Anthropic's CPO on what comes next (Mike Krieger)](sources/lenny-podcast-mike-krieger-anthropic-cpo.md): Claude.ai primitives (projects, Artifacts, styles, conversations) "should all just be exposed to an MCP" so the agent can write back to project knowledge (56:25-58:00) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [Felix Rieseberg (Cowork)](sources/howiai-felix-rieseberg-cowork.md): "live artifacts" refresh from connectors and reuse connector OAuth; target pain is re-updating a deck weekly per audience (23:46-25:51, 33:57) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [Teamwork Graph glossary (Atlassian developer docs)](sources/atlassian-teamwork-graph-glossary.md): Object = single item of data (Jira work item, Confluence page, Google Drive file); each belongs to an object type that defines structure, properties and possible relationships. (user-story-mapping)
- [Teamwork Graph object types (Atlassian developer docs)](sources/atlassian-teamwork-graph-object-types.md): Queryable API object types named on the page: Jira work items and Users. (user-story-mapping)

- [Atlassian Rovo MCP server: supported tools](sources/atlassian-rovo-mcp-server-supported-tools.md): Jira read: work items, projects, boards, sprints, filters, dashboards, comments, changelogs, worklogs, statuses, versions, components. Write: create/edit/transition work items, comments, links, versio (user-story-mapping)
- [What is a Jira space (formerly project)](sources/atlassian-jira-space-definition.md): 'A Jira space is a collection of related work items' for a product, team, service or project; items carry a space key prefix (e.g. GDT-1). (user-story-mapping)
- [What is a Confluence space](sources/atlassian-confluence-space-definition.md): A space is a container for creating, storing and collaborating on work tied to a team, shared project or initiative; examples: a knowledge base, or a space per launch or campaign. (user-story-mapping)
- [What is an idea (Jira Product Discovery docs)](sources/atlassian-jira-product-discovery-ideas.md): Idea = basic unit of work in a JPD space; fields such as goals, team, priority score, impact. (user-story-mapping)
- [Working with databases (Notion API docs)](sources/notion-api-databases-data-sources.md): Database = container holding data sources and views; does not carry the schema in current API versions. (user-story-mapping)
- [Notion MCP supported tools](sources/notion-mcp-supported-tools.md): Search (up to 50 results), connector search across Slack/Drive/GitHub, memory search over saved agent memories. (user-story-mapping)
- [Projects (Linear docs)](sources/linear-docs-projects.md): Project = 'a grouping of issues that have a clear outcome or planned completion date'. (user-story-mapping)
- [Initiatives (Linear docs)](sources/linear-docs-initiatives.md): Initiatives are workspace-level containers for projects tied to a shared objective; IDs like I-<n>. (user-story-mapping)
- [Documents (Linear docs)](sources/linear-docs-documents.md): Documents attach to projects, initiatives, teams, issues or cycles; same editor as issues; realtime collaboration; version history including agent edits; templates at workspace/team level. (user-story-mapping)
- [Linear for Agents (developer docs)](sources/linear-developers-agents.md): Agents can be @mentioned, assigned issues, comment, and collaborate on projects and documents; installed agents are not billable users. (user-story-mapping)
- [Connect a coding agent to Spark via MCP (Productboard support)](sources/productboard-mcp-server-spark.md): Beta, included with Spark-enabled workspaces at no extra cost; admins enable it under Settings > MCP Server and choose roles. (user-story-mapping)
- [Add features to your hierarchy (Productboard support)](sources/productboard-product-hierarchy.md): Hierarchy: Product > Component > Feature > Subfeature. Features can be imported from spreadsheet, Jira or Zapier. (user-story-mapping)
- [Build on Dovetail (docs)](sources/dovetail-build-on-dovetail.md): Three options: MCP server, REST API (default 200 requests/min per workspace), CLI 'dt' for bulk import from Notion, Confluence, Google Drive and files (no sync after import). (user-story-mapping)
- [github/spec-kit (README)](sources/github-spec-kit-readme.md): Workflow: /speckit-constitution (once per project), then per feature /speckit-specify, -plan, -tasks, -implement, -converge. Runs as skills in the agent's chat. (user-story-mapping)
- [Spec-Driven Development (spec-kit spec-driven.md)](sources/github-spec-kit-spec-driven.md): Each feature lives in specs/<NNN-branch-name>/ with spec.md, plan.md, research.md, data-model.md, contracts/, quickstart.md, tasks.md ([P] marks parallel tasks). (user-story-mapping)
- [About Projects (GitHub Docs)](sources/github-docs-about-projects.md): Project = adaptable table, board and roadmap integrating issues and PRs, at user or organisation level; two-way sync with issues. (user-story-mapping)
- [What are projects? (Claude Help Center)](sources/anthropic-claude-projects-support.md): Project = self-contained workspace: knowledge base (documents, text, code), custom instructions, own chat history; memory mentioned only for a beta version. (user-story-mapping)
- [How Claude remembers your project (Claude Code docs)](sources/anthropic-claude-code-memory-docs.md): Locations: managed policy (e.g. /Library/Application Support/ClaudeCode/CLAUDE.md), user, project (./CLAUDE.md or ./.claude/CLAUDE.md), local (CLAUDE.local.md). (user-story-mapping)
- [Organize work with projects (Claude Cowork docs)](sources/anthropic-cowork-projects-docs.md): Project holds: description (Dispatch reads it to choose a project for a task), folders (one or more local), instructions, links, linked Chat projects, memory. (user-story-mapping)
- [Glean Enterprise Graph (product page)](sources/glean-enterprise-graph-product-page.md): Enterprise Graph = relationships among people, projects, teams, products and processes, plus indexed content metadata; personal graphs infer the tasks and projects behind a person's activity. (user-story-mapping)
- [Relationships (Teamwork Graph)](sources/atlassian-teamwork-graph-relationships.md): four relationship kinds (canonical, activity, logical, inferred); logical ones like AtlassianUserCreatedDocuments unify Confluence pages and external documents under one edge. (user-story-mapping)
- [PRD template (Confluence)](sources/atlassian-confluence-prd-template.md): Atlassian's PRD is a page template whose Options table holds user story, importance and 'Jira issues' as embedded links via /jira; no typed PRD-to-work-item relationship, no JPD or Home link. (user-story-mapping)
- [Atlassian MCP enhancements blog](sources/atlassian-blog-mcp-enhancements-jpd.md): July 2026 blog claims agents can find a JPD idea and link it to a delivery issue, but the supported-tools page names no JPD tool. (user-story-mapping)
- [Open-Inspect README](sources/github-open-inspect-background-agents.md): the session is 'the core unit of work'; it stores messages, events, 'Artifacts | PRs created, screenshots captured', participants and sandbox state; no project object, grouping is by repository, environment and team; Linear holds the project mapping. - [Why We Built Our Own Background Agent (Ramp Builders)](sources/ramp-builders-why-we-built-our-own-background-agent.md): Inspect's unit is the session (own SQLite DB, shareable by URL) and its output is the PR with before/after screenshots; no spec, PRD, project or folder concept described. - [Link an idea to a Jira work item (JPD)](sources/atlassian-jpd-link-idea-to-work-item.md): idea shows a Delivery progress bar from linked work items (user-story-mapping)

## product-coherence-over-automation: Product coherence can suffer from over-automation
Warnings that agent-driven shipping produces incoherent 'additive' products without a human holding the whole.
- [Open Source AI Won. Now What?](sources/medium-al-dahle-open-source-ai-won.md): the "blinking cursor" empty chat box is a design problem, not a model problem (research-airbnb-spotify-product-practices)
- [Airbnb says AI now writes 60% of its new code](sources/techcrunch-airbnb-ai-writes-60-percent-code.md): Chesky says chatbot design "does not work for travel or e-commerce" (research-airbnb-spotify-product-practices)
- [Airbnb Q3 2025 earnings call and shareholder letter](sources/airbnb-earnings-q3-2025.md): travel AI needs rich visual UI, not just text (research-airbnb-spotify-product-practices)
- [Airbnb Q4 2023 earnings call and shareholder letter](sources/airbnb-earnings-q4-2023.md): goal is an adaptive interface, "like the ultimate concierge" (research-airbnb-spotify-product-practices)
- [Lessons from scaling Spotify (Gustav Söderström)](sources/lenny-podcast-gustav-soderstrom-scaling-spotify.md): chose an Apple-like centralised model so one app doesn't "ship the org chart" (36:03-41:50) (research-airbnb-spotify-product-practices)
- [Office Hours: Building the case for leaders who ship with DoorDash](sources/claude-customers-doordash-office-hours.md): user-facing features need cross-functional buy-in; product/ship/design review now friction; Andy asks "do we even need to have product review?" (learnings answer). (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [How to build a Self-improving Product](sources/departmentofproduct-self-improving-product.md): metric-chasing agents risk wins that harm the experience (Netflix autoplay), "AI optimized product slop" (research-department-of-product-knowledge-series)
- [DESIGN.md Explained](sources/departmentofproduct-design-md-explained.md): "consistency gets easier but coherence gets harder"; finished-looking AI output suppresses critique. (research-department-of-product-knowledge-series)
- [How do AI coding agents work?](sources/departmentofproduct-ai-coding-agents-explained.md): once engineering capacity stops being the constraint, the risk is "feature slop" and feature discovery becomes the bottleneck. (research-department-of-product-knowledge-series)
- [How tech workers are feeling in 2026](sources/lenny-newsletter-tech-workers-2026-survey.md): "I can do more, faster, but not better"; respondents report focus and judgment suffering (Takeaway 4) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [How we built Grok Bot in a month | Roman Ugarte](sources/lenny-podcast-roman-ugarte-grok-bot.md): built a separate app rather than a tab in Cursor to avoid "shipping your org chart"; "unshipped" thinking traces, memory views and debug tools before launch (9:20, 19:21) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [OpenAI Codex lead on the new shape of product work | Andrew Ambrosino](sources/lenny-podcast-ambrosino-codex-product-work.md): product people play "zone defense" so a full team doesn't have to review code for product coherence; models "usually increase complexity" and should get better at deleting code (29:00, 40:07) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [The AI paradox | Dan Shipper](sources/lenny-podcast-dan-shipper-ai-paradox.md): non-technical staff now open PRs, moving pressure to whoever merges: keep "a coherent whole" and decide "what do we delete?" (50:25-51:55) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [Why Netflix is betting on systems thinkers (Elizabeth Stone)](sources/lenny-podcast-elizabeth-stone-netflix-systems-thinkers.md): designers build templates and design systems so non-designers don't ship "Frankensteins"; deep design still gets time for top priorities (15:14, 20:51) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [OpenAI's Head of Design (Ian Silber)](sources/lenny-podcast-ian-silber-openai-design.md): "Just do less"; build composable primitives so the product stays "one cohesive, simple thing" when engineers ship thousands of PRs (29:32-32:08) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [How Anthropic's product team moves faster than anyone else | Cat Wu](sources/lenny-podcast-cat-wu-anthropic-product-team.md): "We're sacrificing product consistency": overlapping features, confused new users, users on a treadmill; /powerup onboarding added against prior principle (25:42-27:57) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [Community Wisdom: When AI velocity outpaces your product strategy ...](sources/lenny-community-wisdom-ai-velocity-strategy.md): legal-tech founder-PM slows to protect discovery and avoid a "Frankenstein product" (thread 1) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [The design process is dead: Jenny Wen](sources/lenny-podcast-jenny-wen-design-process-dead.md): when anyone can build anything, "you need to point them towards something"; Claude misses the design system (8:02, 23:04) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [Becoming an AI PM: Aman Khan](sources/lenny-podcast-aman-khan-becoming-ai-pm.md): Betty Crocker "add an egg": leave users knobs rather than automate the job away (39:37) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [Why cultivating agency matters more than cultivating skills](sources/lenny-podcast-max-schoening-agency.md): the amount of software rose in 12 months but not its quality; merged roles risk losing specialists (6:42, 14:22) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [All of the Lenny & Friends Summit talks are now online!](sources/lenny-newsletter-summit-talks-online.md): "It's never been easier to build something nobody wants"; "The output is not the product" (Saarinen) (trend 3) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [No Figma. No Jira. No docs. How Gusto built a new product line with Claude Code](sources/howiai-gusto-eddie-kim-cofounder.md): "at any given time there was always something wrong with it in production" while the team chipped away behind a flag (21:07) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [Anthropic's CPO on what comes next (Mike Krieger)](sources/lenny-podcast-mike-krieger-anthropic-cpo.md): downstream bottleneck: "how do we make sure that we're still building something coherent and packaging it up" (15:43) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [Microsoft CPO (Aparna Chennapragada)](sources/lenny-podcast-aparna-chennapragada-microsoft.md): more ideas and prototypes need editorial taste "otherwise you just have Frankenstein product" (24:31) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [Community Wisdom: What to do when non-PMs start shipping](sources/lenny-community-wisdom-non-pms-shipping.md): even with unlimited engineering "you still need some discipline to create coherent products" (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [Community Wisdom: when engineering outpaces product](sources/lenny-community-wisdom-engineering-outpaces-product.md): transcript-driven features judged half bloat; risk of "3 slightly different versions of the same feature because it was easier to build a new one" (thread 2) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [Someone Behind the Software (Karri Saarinen, Linear)](sources/linear-saarinen-someone-behind-the-software.md): changes are mostly additive and agent-made changes average the product (essay, read); losing learning from struggle is from his summit talk (PMS write-up, secondhand) [re-check 2026-10-24]. (research-pm-agents-jobs-to-be-done)
- [Marty Cagan interview (Modern CTO)](sources/moderncto-marty-cagan-2026.md): "product management theater" (title without control over what is built); one-click AI PRDs speed up a bad process; the avoid-thinking remark is from the PMS write-up [re-check 2026-10-24]. (Single decision owner and editing-as-a-job are in the PMS write-up, not here) [re-check 2026-10-24]. (research-pm-agents-jobs-to-be-done)

## program-failure-causes: Why large programmes fail: dependencies, integration and late discovery among the causes
Independent and auditor evidence on large-IT-programme overruns and their named causes, including unrecorded interdependencies, legacy integration and components arriving too late; and the caution that priority churn ranks higher.
- [Why Your IT Project May Be Riskier Than You Think](sources/flyvbjerg-budzier-it-project-riskier.md): "The average overrun was 27% — but that figure masks a far more alarming one ... Fully one in six of the projects we studied was a black swan, with a cost overrun of 200%, on average, and a schedule overrun of almost 70%" (The True IT Pitfall). (independent; research-dependency-agent)
- [HealthCare.gov: Case Study of CMS Management of the Federal Marketplace (OEI-06-14-00350)](sources/hhs-oig-healthcare-gov-case-study.md): "Most critical was the absence of clear leadership, which caused delays in decisionmaking, lack of clarity in project tasks, and the inability of CMS to recognize the magnitude of problems as the project deteriorated" (Executive summary). (independent; research-dependency-agent)
- [The Rise and Fall of the Chaos Report Figures](sources/ieee-software-eveleens-verhoef-chaos-figures.md): reproduces Standish's series (successful/challenged/failed): 1994 16/53/31; 1996 27/33/40; 1998 26/46/28; 2000 28/49/23; 2004 29/53/18; 2006 35/46/19; 2009 32/44/24 (Table 1). (independent; research-dependency-agent)
- [Why Software Fails](sources/ieee-spectrum-charette-why-software-fails.md): common factors include "Unrealistic or unarticulated project goals", "Badly defined system requirements", "Poor reporting of the project's status", "Unmanaged risks", "Poor communication among customers, developers, and users", "Inability to handle the project's complexity", "Stakeholder politics" and "Commercial pressures" (list). (independent; research-dependency-agent)
- [Delivering large-scale IT projects on time, on budget, and on value](sources/mckinsey-delivering-large-scale-it-projects.md): "large IT projects run 45 percent over budget and 7 percent over time, while delivering 56 percent less value than predicted"; "17 percent of IT projects go so bad that they can threaten the very existence of the company"; total cost overrun $66 billion (body). (vendor-claim; research-dependency-agent)
- [The challenges in implementing digital change](sources/nao-challenges-implementing-digital-change.md): "Despite 25 years of government strategies and countless attempts to deliver digital business change successfully, our reports show a consistent pattern of underperformance" (Summary para 7); causes include "shifting business requirements; over-optimism; supplier performance; and lack of capability" (para 2). (independent; research-dependency-agent)
- [Pulse of the Profession 2018: Success in Disruptive Times](sources/pmi-pulse-of-the-profession-2018.md): primary causes of failed projects (select up to 3), in the report's chart order: change in organisation's priorities, change in project objectives, inaccurate requirements gathering, inadequate vision or goal, inadequate/poor communication, opportunities and risks not defined, inaccurate cost estimates, poor change management, inadequate sponsor support, resource dependency, inaccurate task time estimate, inexperi... (vendor-claim; research-dependency-agent)

## project-taxonomy: How 'project' is defined
Initiative/project/epic/space taxonomies across tools and conventions.
- [Projects redesigned: from folder to conversation](sources/claude-code-projects-redesigned.md): a project = goal + repo or context + configured environment, connectors, plugins, instructions and model; work is "longer than one reply and has more than one part" (sections "Threads do the work", "Context builds over time"). (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [How to use Claude Projects and Skills to Monitor your Product's Health](sources/departmentofproduct-claude-projects-product-health.md): either one Project, or five function-owned sub-Projects plus a master; the master is fed by pasting each sub-Project's summary by hand (research-department-of-product-knowledge-series)
- [Claude Cowork 101](sources/howiai-jj-englert-cowork-101.md): "a project is a folder on your computer"; "a skill is literally like a file" (6:20, 9:23) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [Initiatives (Linear docs)](sources/linear-initiatives-docs.md): Initiatives are curated groups of projects tied to a company objective; sub-initiatives allowed; projects can be collected by filters; initiative health on track/at risk/off track from updates; documents attach via a Resources pro (user-story-mapping)
- [Create a space (Confluence)](sources/atlassian-confluence-create-a-space.md): a space is 'a container ... for work related to a shared project or initiative' with a purpose of Collaboration, Knowledge base or Custom, one owner and a permissions scheme; it is a third 'project'-like container beside Jira spaces and Atlassian Home projects. (user-story-mapping)

## prototyping-agents-limits: Prototyping agents and their limits
Prompt-to-prototype tools let PMs build quickly but break down as complexity grows and need engineering handoff.
- [Reflexive AI usage is now a baseline expectation at Shopify](sources/x-tobi-reflexive-ai-usage-memo.md): "AI must be part of your GSD Prototype phase"; the prototype phase "should be dominated by AI exploration" (Apr 2025) (competitive-teardown-shopify-river)
- [Harbor: Stripe's AI-assisted prototyping tool](sources/stripe-harbor-ai-prototyping.md): Harbor prototype animation shipped 'nearly one-for-one'; prototypes became inputs to reviews; next step is live data and prototype-scoped databases (competitive-teardown-stripe-knowledge-agents)
- [Protodash (How I AI, Owen Williams)](sources/howiai-stripe-protodash-owen-williams.md): gets '90% of the way most of the time ... it will make slop'; taste and craft stay with designers (competitive-teardown-stripe-knowledge-agents)
- [GraphQL Data Mocking at Scale with LLMs and @generateMock](sources/airbnb-tech-graphql-generatemock.md): a design URL plus an LLM produce realistic demo data; over 700 mocks merged in months (research-airbnb-spotify-product-practices)

- [How Spotify Thinks (Invest Like the Best EP.424)](sources/colossus-ilb-gustav-soderstrom-how-spotify-thinks.md): a prototyping phase (Figma, increasingly generative AI) before each bets cycle surfaces conflicts between bets (~16:26) (research-airbnb-spotify-product-practices)

- [From localized to systematic speed (ELC Podcast ep. 245)](sources/elc-podcast-tyson-singer-systematic-speed.md): bottlenecks outside R&D (legal, licensing) limit speed (32:12) (research-airbnb-spotify-product-practices)

- [How to turn your AI into a world-class designer](sources/lenny-newsletter-ai-world-class-designer.md): models default to predictable, committee-like design and "love to add more, but rarely take away"; seed strings and critics push past it (Techniques 1, 6) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)

## public-by-default-agent-work: Public-by-default agent work and its costs
Agent sessions that are visible to the whole organisation by default (no DMs, no private mode), so others learn by watching and the transcripts can be mined; and the costs of that default: questions not asked, sensitive data in open threads, channel membership as access control, regulated walls. Matters for the trust-privacy-defaults and agent-interface choices.
- [Learning on the Shop floor](sources/x-tobi-learning-on-the-shop-floor.md): River "does not respond to direct messages"; "Asking for help feels different when the whole company can see the question" (competitive-teardown-shopify-river)
- [Under the River](sources/shopify-engineering-under-the-river.md): "Every conversation with River becomes a public Slack transcript, open by default to other Shopify employees" (competitive-teardown-shopify-river)
- [River's reaction to the Shop floor post](sources/x-tobi-river-reaction-to-shop-floor-post.md): "Some questions that would have been asked in a DM just don't get asked"; also an "honesty pressure" on agent and user (competitive-teardown-shopify-river)
- [Small Models, Massive Wins (Beyond the Pilot)](sources/venturebeat-beyond-the-pilot-farhan-thawar.md): River refuses private channels too: "you can't go into a private channel and say, 'Hey, River, help me build'" (competitive-teardown-shopify-river)
- [Quick](sources/shopify-engineering-quick.md): the same default for artifacts: all sites open to all employees, no owners (competitive-teardown-shopify-river)
- [Shopify's River shows why agent context costs more (Magica)](sources/magica-shopify-river-agent-context-cost.md): Slack's CPO: a boundary for "genuinely sensitive work"; "psychological safety should determine where openness stops" (competitive-teardown-shopify-river)
- [Shopify Just Showed the Agent Stack](sources/adaptordie-shopify-river-agent-stack.md): "A pricing conversation may need a tighter audience" (competitive-teardown-shopify-river)
- [Hacker News: River submissions and comments](sources/hn-shopify-river-discussion.md): one-line anecdote: the way people speak to agents wouldn't be "kosher in a company slack" (competitive-teardown-shopify-river)
- [The Transparency Paradox (Bernstein)](sources/asq-bernstein-transparency-paradox.md): broad visibility can breed hiding; privacy zones raised output 10–15% (independent; factory setting) (competitive-teardown-shopify-river)
- [Create information barriers in Slack](sources/slack-information-barriers-docs.md): chat-tool walls don't stop interaction in shared channels, so a channel-native agent inherits that gap (competitive-teardown-shopify-river)
- [Tenable on Claude Tag](sources/tenable-claude-tag-slack-access-model.md): in channel agents, public-channel join policy effectively governs access to the agent's credentials; new members see scrollback (competitive-teardown-shopify-river)
- [Agents you can coach: how Asana builds human-agent teams with Claude](sources/claude-asana-agents-you-can-coach.md): Bose argues one-on-one agent use hides the prompt and back-and-forth from reviewers, so they cannot align on or revise the instructions. (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [Lessons from Anthropic on building effective human-agent teams](sources/claude-building-effective-human-agent-teams.md): Lesson 1: "if it's not written down and accessible, it doesn't exist" for agents; channels default public within the org; a handful of workspace-level boundaries instead of per-item sharing; private DMs and personal-connector... (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [How the Claude Code team does code review](sources/claude-dev-claude-code-team-code-review.md): review's second job, building shared understanding, is now covered by Claude-written explainers on demand and by "our culture of defaulting to working on open Slack channels" (§Sharing context across the team). (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [Turning conversation into knowledge: how Slack builds human-agent teams](sources/claude-slack-human-agent-teams.md): "Agents can only learn from what they can see"; default channels to public and go private on purpose; "A private channel is a blind spot for every agent that reports on it" (sections "Treat your conversation history", "Default... (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [Claude Tag now supports personal connectors in channels](sources/claude-tag-personal-connectors.md): "Anything Claude posts is visible to everyone in the channel"; the requester chooses review mode (see the reply before it posts) or auto mode (posts unless Claude judges content sensitive) (intro, §Using personal connectors). (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [Self-service data analytics in Slack: how Anthropic deploys Claude Tag for ad-hoc questions](sources/claude-tag-self-service-analytics.md): keep the agent in shared channels and work in threads, not DMs, so threads are a reviewable record (section "Claude Tag threads become the new meeting"). (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [Automating Dependency Updates in Practice: An Exploratory Study on GitHub Dependabot](sources/arxiv-he-dependabot-exploratory-study.md): volume of bot-originated requests drives configuration to suppress them. (independent; research-dependency-agent)
- [How Devin replaces your junior engineers | Scott Wu](sources/howiai-scott-wu-devin-junior-engineer.md): host: "hiding your AI use is kind of the worst thing you can do"; Wu: public use transfers knowledge to the agent and educates the humans (24:01-24:56) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [How Warp ships 2,000 PRs a month with AI factories (How I AI)](sources/howiai-warp-zach-lloyd-software-factory.md): factory work starts in public Slack threads others can join; Lloyd credits this with spreading power-user habits across a power-law team (41:27) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [River's reaction to the Shop floor post](sources/x-tobi-river-reaction-to-shop-floor-post.md): "Some questions that would have been asked in a DM just don't get asked"; public-only as "an honesty pressure"; written by the agent (research-shared-persistent-agents)
- [The transparency paradox (Bernstein, ASQ 2012)](sources/asq-bernstein-transparency-paradox.md): broad visibility bred hiding and a "show" for observers; privacy zones raised defect-free output 10-15% for five months; one factory, 2009 (independent) (research-shared-persistent-agents)
- [Building effective human-agent teams (Slack CPO)](sources/claude-slack-human-agent-teams.md): "Agents can only learn from what they can see"; "a private channel is a blind spot"; psychological safety, not secrecy, sends work to DMs (research-shared-persistent-agents)
- [Tenable on the Claude Tag access model](sources/tenable-claude-tag-slack-access-model.md): channel membership becomes the IAM boundary; new members see prior scrollback (independent) (research-shared-persistent-agents)
- [How I AI: Stripe Minions (Kaliski)](sources/howiai-stripe-minions-kaliski.md): a public "robots" channel 76 people follow; "we pair prompt"; open-by-default chosen per person for coding runs while Kai sessions stay private (research-shared-persistent-agents)
- [Shopify River and agent context (Magica)](sources/magica-shopify-river-agent-context-cost.md): no like-for-like comparison of shared versus private agents has been published (research-shared-persistent-agents)
- [Don't Disturb Me](sources/arxiv-wessel-dont-disturb-me-bots.md): noise is the central harm of bots in PRs; information overload disrupts communication and workflow (independent, 2021) (research-shared-persistent-agents)
- [Meta-Analysis of Digital Surveillance of Workers](sources/msr-ravid-digital-surveillance-meta-analysis.md): monitoring is stressful whatever its form; only transparent, purposeful, less invasive monitoring improves attitudes (independent) (research-shared-persistent-agents)

## red-team-stance: Structured critique as a procedure
Fixed rituals for open critique (premortem, silent-read reviews) that a PM agent can run or prompt.
- [Performing a Project Premortem](sources/hbr-klein-project-premortem.md): assume the project failed and list reasons; supporting research is thin (about 30% more reasons generated, not better accuracy, per secondary critiques) (research-skill-rigidity-spectrum)
- [An insider look at Amazon's culture and processes](sources/aboutamazon-insider-look-working-backwards.md): silent reading, senior attendees speak last, most PR/FAQs not approved (research-skill-rigidity-spectrum)
- [LLM-Powered Devil's Advocate](sources/acm-chiang-llm-powered-devils-advocate-iui2024.md): advocates arguing against the AI's recommendation promoted appropriate reliance without raising workload; interactive ones rated higher (research-skill-rigidity-spectrum)
- [The bar raiser program](sources/metaview-bar-raiser-program.md): independence from the deadline and written answers to objections matter more than the veto; no outcome data exists (research-skill-rigidity-spectrum)
- [How we built our multi-agent research system](sources/anthropic-multi-agent-research-system.md): no runtime critic; LLM judge is offline; critique is aimed at the agent's own prompts and tools (research-skill-rigidity-spectrum)

## regulatory-drivers-of-process: Regulation prescribes the record and the independence, not the meeting
What regulators and laws (FCA, PRA, Federal Reserve, OCC, EBA, EU DORA, ICO, NAIC, FDA, GAO) actually require of a change, a model, a third party or a dependency map, and how that drives internal process in regulated firms.
- [Accelerate: State of DevOps 2019](sources/dora-state-of-devops-2019.md): segregation of duties is "often required by regulatory frameworks" (footnote cites PCI DSS and the NIST RMF); can be met by peer review recorded in a change management system with authenticated approval events (pp. 48-49, "Implementing segregation of duties"). (independent; research-dependency-agent)
- [Final Report on EBA Guidelines on outsourcing arrangements (EBA/GL/2019/02)](sources/eba-guidelines-outsourcing-arrangements.md): para 61: "Before entering into any outsourcing arrangement, institutions and payment institutions should: a. assess if the outsourcing arrangement concerns a critical or important function...; b. assess if the supervisory conditions for outsourcing ... are met; c. identify and assess all of the relevant risks...; d. undertake appropriate due diligence on the prospective service provider...; e. identify and assess... (first-party; research-dependency-agent)
- [DORA Dry Run exercise: summary report (ESA 2024 35)](sources/esas-dora-dry-run-register-of-information.md): two-step assessment: technical integration checks (file formats, naming) then data quality and validation checks; individual feedback was passed back through national authorities (pp. 3-4). (first-party; research-dependency-agent)
- [Regulation (EU) 2022/2554 on digital operational resilience for the financial sector (DORA)](sources/eu-dora-regulation-ict-risk-third-party.md): Art. 9(4)(e): "documented policies, procedures and controls for ICT change management ... based on a risk assessment approach ... in order to ensure that all changes to ICT systems are recorded, tested, assessed, approved, implemented and verified in a controlled manner"; the change process "shall be approved by appropriate lines of management". (first-party; research-dependency-agent)
- [Implementing technology change](sources/fca-implementing-technology-change.md): good practice includes estate discovery to understand dependencies before designing change, especially with legacy systems, and contractual visibility of third-party changes (Good practices). (first-party; research-dependency-agent)
- [Computer Software Assurance for Production and Quality System Software; Guidance for Industry and Food and Drug Administration Staff; Availability](sources/fda-computer-software-assurance-notice-2025.md): "Medical device manufacturers have expressed a desire for greater clarity regarding the Agency's expectations for software validation ... manufacturers have also expressed a desire for a more iterative, agile approach for validation" (I. Background). (first-party; research-dependency-agent)
- [Interagency Guidance on Third-Party Relationships: Risk Management](sources/fed-fdic-occ-third-party-risk-guidance-2023.md): life cycle "Planning; Due Diligence and Third-Party Selection; Contract Negotiation; Ongoing Monitoring; Termination", with Governance covering oversight, independent reviews, documentation and reporting (Final guidance, Section C-D). (first-party; research-dependency-agent)
- [Supervisory Guidance on Model Risk Management (SR 11-7, attachment)](sources/federalreserve-sr-11-7-model-risk-guidance.md): "The range and rigor of validation activities conducted prior to first use of a model should be in line with the potential risk presented by use of the model. If significant deficiencies are noted ... use of the model should not be allowed or should be permitted only under very tight constraints" (Validation section, p. 10). (first-party; research-dependency-agent)
- [Decision: Remark and administrative fine, Swedbank AB (FI Ref. 22-18430)](sources/fi-swedbank-change-management-sanction.md): the change "should have been assessed and approved by Swedbank's Change Advisory Board (CAB) ... since the change was being made outside of the bank's so-called service window. This was not done" (2.1.2, p. 4); FI found a violation of the requirement on internal control (2.2.3). (first-party; research-dependency-agent)

(independent; research-dependency-agent)
- [When do we need to do a DPIA?](sources/ico-when-do-we-need-a-dpia.md): Article 35(1) requires the DPIA "prior to the processing"; Article 35(3) makes it mandatory for systematic and extensive profiling with significant effects, large-scale special category or criminal offence data, and large-scale systematic monitoring of public areas. (first-party; research-dependency-agent)
- [Speed to Market (D) Working Group, Virtual Meeting, April 23, 2026 (draft minutes, Attachment 1)](sources/naic-speed-to-market-wg-minutes-april-2026.md): future roadmap includes "rule sharing between states and industry-facing features that would advise insurers of potential objections before submission"; industry-facing features not expected in 2026 (item 3). - [SS1/23 – Model risk management principles for banks](sources/pra-ss1-23-model-risk-management-principles.md): deterministic "decision-based rules or algorithms that are not classified as a model" but have material bearing on decisions should be considered for the MRM framework (Principle 1.1(b), p. 11). (first-party; research-dependency-agent)
- [When DORA metrics meet governance in banking - Expert View](sources/teamtopologies-dora-metrics-governance-banking.md): banks must implement change management, but the processes are manual and slow to keep pace; a regulator reported significant findings about the bank's CAB. ## risk-review-as-classification: Risk review as a specification and classification problem
Risk advisory works as classification against a known taxonomy, with a curation path for novel risks. That makes a risk agent tractable to build and straightforward to evaluate with SME labels.
- [Risk-Aware Product Decisions in A/B Tests with Multiple Metrics](sources/spotify-engineering-risk-aware-product-decisions.md): the rule maps every outcome to a decision, so anyone can read a shipping recommendation (research-airbnb-spotify-product-practices)

## risk-sloped-review: Human review sloped to risk
How much human review agent output gets depends on how risky it is. Where that line sits is a key harness and governance design choice, especially in regulated organisations.
