## rules-vs-judgment-encoding: Encoding standards as rules vs as reasons and judgment
How skills, rule files and model specs choose between fixed rules, scripts and checks on one side and explained criteria and judgment on the other, and which steps practitioners make rigid. Matters for which PM-skill standards become hard gates and which stay as guidance.
- [The Change Enablement Practice: What Changed with Change in ITIL 4](sources/easyvista-mann-itil4-change-enablement.md): change is treated as a complexity spectrum from business-as-usual (standard changes) to business continuity (emergency practices), with guidance matched to each. (independent; research-dependency-agent)
- [When do we need to do a DPIA?](sources/ico-when-do-we-need-a-dpia.md): "high risk" is a higher threshold than "risk"; the guidance recommends erring on the side of caution when in doubt. (first-party; research-dependency-agent)
- [Skill authoring best practices](sources/anthropic-skill-authoring-best-practices.md): match specificity to "fragility and variability": high, medium and low freedom; narrow bridge vs open field (research-skill-rigidity-spectrum)
- [skill-creator SKILL.md](sources/anthropics-skills-skill-creator-skill-md.md): all-caps ALWAYS/NEVER and "super rigid structures" are "a yellow flag"; explain the why (research-skill-rigidity-spectrum)
- [Claude's new constitution](sources/anthropic-claude-new-constitution.md): judgment with reasons by default; rules only as hard constraints; a box-ticking rule can generalise badly (research-skill-rigidity-spectrum)
- [docx SKILL.md](sources/anthropics-skills-docx.md): low-freedom end: exact unpack, edit, validate commands with XSD script gates, still with reasons (research-skill-rigidity-spectrum)
- [frontend-design SKILL.md](sources/anthropics-skills-frontend-design.md): taste encoded as persona, five named AI-default clusters to avoid, and plan-review-critique (research-skill-rigidity-spectrum)
- [Superpowers skills](sources/obra-superpowers-skills.md): mandatory invocation, an "iron law" and rationalisation tables where the model is tempted to skip discipline (research-skill-rigidity-spectrum)
- [Superpowers: How I'm using coding agents](sources/fsck-jesse-vincent-superpowers.md): Cialdini persuasion principles in skill wording; pressure-scenario tests replaced quizzes (research-skill-rigidity-spectrum)
- [vercel-labs/agent-skills](sources/vercel-labs-agent-skills-repo.md): 70 impact-ranked rules with incorrect/correct examples; thin skills fetch a central rule list each run (research-skill-rigidity-spectrum)
- [awesome-cursorrules](sources/patrickjs-awesome-cursorrules.md): roughly 210 always-on rule files of bare imperatives; newer files encode stance ("warn once, then comply") (research-skill-rigidity-spectrum)
- [knowledge-work-plugins PM skills](sources/anthropics-kwp-pm-plugin-skills.md): PM skills hold all standards as prose criteria; no script or schema gate (research-skill-rigidity-spectrum)
- [Agent Skills (Osmani)](sources/addyosmani-agent-skills.md): "the judgement moves out of your head and into checks"; CONSTRAINTS.md with chosen numbers and diff watch (research-skill-rigidity-spectrum)
- [Harness engineering for coding agent users](sources/fowler-bockeler-harness-engineering.md): guides vs sensors x computational vs inferential; skills appear as both inferential guides and sensors (research-skill-rigidity-spectrum)
- [12-Factor Agents factors 2 and 8](sources/humanlayer-12-factor-agents-own-your-control-flow.md): model proposes a tool intent, code decides continue, pause or approve by tool risk (research-skill-rigidity-spectrum)
- [Claude Skills are awesome](sources/simonwillison-claude-skills-bigger-than-mcp.md): loose instructions plus a validator script for the hard limit (Slack GIF size) (research-skill-rigidity-spectrum)
- [Using LLM-as-a-Judge](sources/hamel-llm-as-judge-guide.md): criteria drift: experts find their standard while grading, so rubrics are grown from critiques (research-skill-rigidity-spectrum)
- [Inside the Development Workflow of Claude Code's Creator](sources/infoq-claude-code-creator-workflow.md): deterministic PostToolUse format hook takes a class of errors out of model judgment (research-skill-rigidity-spectrum)

## scoped-governance-containers: Governance scoped to a project or workspace
Policy (default model, allowed tools, human-in-the-loop rules, data back end, even which harness) set once by a project owner and applied to everyone working in that project, rather than per user or org-wide. Matters for governance and trust defaults.
- [Build your own company brain (How I AI, Krishnamurthy)](sources/howiai-stripe-kai-krishnamurthy.md): "projects are primarily a governance mechanism"; owners set default model, tool policies, HITL; HR has a separately backed secure project; projects of 5 to 500 people (competitive-teardown-stripe-knowledge-agents)
- [Meet Stripe's Knowledge AI Platform](sources/stripe-meet-knowledge-ai-platform.md): domain-owned custom Kai agents load a team's skills and data sources by default (competitive-teardown-stripe-knowledge-agents)
- [Agent identity: a new access model for autonomous, team-wide AI](sources/claude-agent-identity-access-model.md): distinct identity per private channel, shared workspace identity for public channels; memory and access stay inside boundaries (section "How identity boundaries work"). (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [How Notion ships and scales agents with Claude Managed Agents](sources/claude-customers-notion-managed-agents.md): every agent starts private and must be shared explicitly, with chat-only, trigger and edit permission levels; the review agent is managed by a few people, the investigator by many (same answer). (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [How healthcare organizations use Claude Tag](sources/claude-tag-healthcare-human-agent-teams.md): Tag can be off by default, enabled only in approved channels, DMs disabled, connectors scoped per channel; "access bundles" give a channel its codebase and tracker while EHR and clinical systems stay unreachable (intro bullets). (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [Understanding Cross App Access with Okta for AI Agents](sources/okta-support-cross-app-access-ai-agents.md): access is a directional managed connection between a requesting app and a resource app. (first-party; research-dependency-agent)
- [Community Wisdom: Using AI to accelerate a team's velocity](sources/lenny-community-wisdom-ai-team-velocity.md): one Claude Project per larger feature initiative, shared with CS, PMM and marketing for handoffs (thread 1) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [What a harness is and how to build one with Claude Agent SDK](sources/howiai-claire-vo-agent-sdk-harness.md): "How to encode specific permissions into a harness" (show notes; details not available) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [Community Wisdom: ... sharing Claude Code context across a team](sources/lenny-community-wisdom-claude-context-sharing.md): Obsidian dropped for "too little governance around what agents can do to the data (without a human in the loop)" (thread 5) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [Quests, token leaderboards, and a skills marketplace (How I AI)](sources/howiai-sendbird-john-kim-adoption-playbook.md): pre-vetted app template with auth and environments, "fully compliant", plus a weekly CTO/engineering/Infosec task force; quests show a risk rating (9:51-14:56) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [View and manage agents in your Jira space](sources/atlassian-jira-manage-agents-in-space.md): agents are members of a space with a role; private spaces grant nothing without one (user-story-mapping)

## shared-persistent-sessions: Shared, persistent, multi-user agent sessions
Agent sessions that outlive one person's laptop: shared with teammates, running in a deployed runtime, resumable or event-driven. Raises identity (who is the agent acting as), permission-leakage, durability and cost questions that local sessions avoid.
- [Building Laminar: Ramp's Managed Agents Platform](sources/ramp-builders-building-laminar.md): async-by-default, always-open sessions with HITL approvals, steering and multiplayer; session state in Postgres decoupled from sandboxes; cloud workers so 'laptop goes to sleep' no longer matters (first-party) (competitive-teardown-ramp-glass)
- [Why We Built Our Own Background Agent](sources/ramp-builders-why-we-built-background-agent.md): every Inspect session is multiplayer, prompts attributed per person, state synced across Slack, web, extension, PR and hosted VS Code (first-party) (competitive-teardown-ramp-glass)
- [Under the River](sources/shopify-engineering-under-the-river.md): Aquifer session = append-only Postgres event log; harness and sandbox disposable; idle "session cells" rehydrate on any host; "Cells die, sandboxes die, machines die. The conversation doesn't." (Part III) (competitive-teardown-shopify-river)
- [River floods Shopify chart](sources/x-tobi-river-floods-shopify-chart.md): "wrote in the same thread" links 61,680 (Mar) → 171,853 (Sep 2026), the only published multiplayer metric (self-reported) (competitive-teardown-shopify-river)
- [We gave AI agents a mobile dev environment](sources/shopify-engineering-remote-dev.md): each River session claims a warm Mac plus Android VM, destroyed after use; tasks start from Slack or run overnight; Live Preview links shareable (competitive-teardown-shopify-river)
- [Shopify: Building River (ZenML)](sources/zenml-llmops-shopify-river-durable-infrastructure.md): Postgres event-log session, harness outside the sandbox, idle "session cells" restart anywhere (competitive-teardown-shopify-river)
- [Case Study: Shopify River (Wallfacer)](sources/wallfacer-case-study-shopify-river.md): "the resume mechanism and the audit record are the same artifact" (competitive-teardown-shopify-river)
- [Hacker News: River submissions and comments](sources/hn-shopify-river-discussion.md): practitioners compare River to Managed Agents and say "we built something similar" (competitive-teardown-shopify-river)
- [Meet Stripe's Knowledge AI Platform](sources/stripe-meet-knowledge-ai-platform.md): Kai sessions are cloud-hosted and long (one hit 932 turns) but single-user; context is 'locked in'; sharing and multi-person artifacts are on the roadmap (competitive-teardown-stripe-knowledge-agents)
- [Stripe's AI minions ship 1,300 PRs weekly from a Slack emoji (How I AI)](sources/howiai-stripe-minions-kaliski.md): minions run in a public Slack 'robots' channel watched by 76 people: open-by-default observation and 'pair prompting' (competitive-teardown-stripe-knowledge-agents)
- [Harbor: Stripe's AI-assisted prototyping tool](sources/stripe-harbor-ai-prototyping.md): Harbor shares artifacts, not sessions: one published snapshot per URL, anchored comments that re-resolve after agent rewrites, remix into a copy (competitive-teardown-stripe-knowledge-agents)
- [Thoughts On A Month With Devin](sources/answerai-month-with-devin.md): the Slack-based chat and visible environment setup were polished; the unreliability was in the agent (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Use Claude Code in the cloud (Claude Code on the web docs)](sources/anthropic-claude-code-cloud-sessions.md): cloud sessions keep running after the laptop closes and can be steered from mobile; sharing is Private or Team visibility, and 'recipients see the latest state when they open the link, but their view doesn't update in real time' (Share sessions) (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Automate work with scheduled tasks (Claude Code routines docs)](sources/anthropic-claude-code-scheduled-tasks.md): scheduled tasks 'belong to your individual claude.ai account. They are not shared with teammates'; everything they do through GitHub/connectors 'appears as you' (Create a scheduled task) (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Claude Tag: agent identity (concepts)](sources/anthropic-claude-tag-agent-identity.md): channel sessions use connectors, repos and plugins an admin applied to the channel/workspace/org, and 'everyone in the channel gets the same capability, regardless of who asks' (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Scaling Managed Agents: Decoupling the brain from the hands](sources/anthropic-engineering-scaling-managed-agents.md): first design ran session, harness and sandbox in one container, making it a 'pet'; decoupling into session (durable log), harness (loop) and sandbox (hands) lets any piece fail or be replaced (Decoupling) (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Self-hosted environments (Claude Code cloud sessions on your infrastructure)](sources/anthropic-self-hosted-environments.md): control plane (queue, session stream, claude.ai UI) stays Anthropic-hosted; runners execute sessions; 'Anthropic stores the session transcript so you can resume the session from another supported surface' (What stays on your infrastructure) (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Self-hosted environments (Claude Code cloud sessions on your infrastructure)](sources/anthropic-self-hosted-environments.md): a runner locks to one owner (a user account or a Claude Tag agent) at a time so checked-out code never mixes between owners; minimum fleet size equals active owners (Runner lifecycle) (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Long-running agents (Cloudflare Agents SDK docs)](sources/cloudflare-agents-long-running-agents.md): agents are 'durable identities, not always-on processes': wake on HTTP, WebSocket, RPC, alarm or inbound email, hibernate after about 2 minutes idle; eviction can occur at any point (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Cloud-origin agents have no 'Move to Machine' option (Cursor forum)](sources/cursor-forum-cloud-to-local-handoff.md): related thread reports local to cloud handoff failing for GitLab repos with 'Background composer not found' (search snippet only) (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Cursor Cloud Agent sessions are shared across users - act on behalf (forum bug report)](sources/cursor-forum-team-followups-act-on-behalf.md): the reporter claims a session runs with the initiating user's OAuth identity for Jira, GitHub and Slack while its prompt surface is not bound to that user; follow-ups via Slack thread or the shared web URL run as the initiator (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [The $47K agent loop: why logging, monitoring and max_tokens all failed to stop it](sources/devto-47k-agent-loop.md): argues enforcement should be deterministic, pre-call and per-run (cost, iterations, wall clock) with an external kill switch, separate from the agent (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Risks and mitigations for GitHub Copilot cloud agent](sources/github-copilot-cloud-agent-risks.md): identity: commits are authored by Copilot with the requesting developer as co-author, signed ('Verified'), each linked to its session log; logs and audit events available to admins (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Risks and mitigations for GitHub Copilot cloud agent](sources/github-copilot-cloud-agent-risks.md): only users with write access can trigger the agent and comments from others never reach it; pushes confined to one branch (the PR branch or a new copilot/ branch) (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Open-Inspect (ColeMurray/background-agents) README](sources/github-open-inspect-background-agents.md): a Durable Object per session holds SQLite, a WebSocket hub and event stream; clients are web, Slack, GitHub, Linear, webhooks; presence indicators and prompts attributed to authors in git commits (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)

The default is shadow' (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)

## single-agent-many-skills: One agent with many skills, not many agents
Consolidate to one agent and one conversational surface, extended by skills and tools.

- [Introducing Glass. Make your entire company smarter](sources/ramp-introducing-glass.md): "one single agent" with pre-built connectivity (competitive-teardown-ramp-glass)

## skill-improvement-loops: How skills and agent instructions get better
The mechanisms by which a skill, prompt or instruction file changes over time: static, curated from human corrections, driven by an eval, or rewritten by the agent itself; and the signal each depends on.
- [How Intercom uses Claude Code today](sources/ideas-fin-how-we-use-claude-code-today.md): a SessionEnd hook classifies each transcript's gaps (missing skill, missing tool, repeated failure, wrong info) and opens a pre-filled GitHub issue: traces to standards (research-shared-persistent-agents)
- [How I AI: Stripe Kai (Krishnamurthy)](sources/howiai-stripe-kai-krishnamurthy.md): telemetry sorts about 2,000 skills into about 50 used daily, 100-150 by sub-org and a long tail; a pipeline says which to promote into the default context (research-shared-persistent-agents)
- [Remote Dev (Shopify)](sources/shopify-engineering-remote-dev.md): the "Jev" classifier tags every mobile River conversation by outcome and feeds failures to an LLM that proposes improvements (research-shared-persistent-agents)
- [The Knowledge Project: Tobi Lütke on AI agents](sources/fs-knowledge-project-tobi-lutke-ai-agents.md): River's repeated failure to pick unit tests became an ML test-selection model, saving about 30 minutes per task; nightly "dreaming" rewrites skill files (research-shared-persistent-agents)
- [Building Laminar](sources/ramp-builders-building-laminar.md): a bespoke session-debug UI because "building great agents requires you to read the traces" (research-shared-persistent-agents)
- [Automating SKILL.md Generation via Interaction Trajectory Mining](sources/arxiv-hao-skillmd-trajectory-mining.md): mined skills are readable but don't transfer; "readability does not imply transfer" (research-shared-persistent-agents)
- [Bugbot now self-improves with learned rules](sources/cursor-bugbot-learning.md): online rule promotion from live review feedback replaced offline-only experiments (research-shared-persistent-agents)
- [Agentic Context Engineering](sources/arxiv-agentic-context-engineering.md): names brevity bias and context collapse in whole-file rewrites; incremental deltas from generate/reflect/curate roles; +10.6% on AppWorld without labels (research-skill-rigidity-spectrum)
- [Dynamic Cheatsheet](sources/arxiv-dynamic-cheatsheet.md): self-curated memory took GPT-4o on Game of 24 from 10% to 99%; limits: self-curation without labels, persisted errors, weak-model gains small, tokens 370 to 1,831 (research-skill-rigidity-spectrum)
- [Reflexion](sources/arxiv-reflexion.md): stored verbal reflection between trials; 91% vs 80% on HumanEval; needs a feedback signal (research-skill-rigidity-spectrum)
- [Voyager](sources/arxiv-voyager-skill-library.md): ever-growing library of verified executable skills; transfers to new worlds; 15.3x faster milestones (research-skill-rigidity-spectrum)
- [GEPA](sources/arxiv-gepa-reflective-prompt-evolution.md): prose diagnosis of trajectories beats RL by 6% average with up to 35x fewer rollouts; still eval-driven (research-skill-rigidity-spectrum)
- [DSPy](sources/arxiv-dspy.md): prompts compiled against a metric; bootstrapped demonstrations beat expert-written by 5-46% (research-skill-rigidity-spectrum)
- [autoresearch](sources/github-karpathy-autoresearch.md): fixed evaluator file, one mutable work file, human edits only program.md; ~100 experiments overnight (research-skill-rigidity-spectrum)
- [Knowledge (Devin docs)](sources/devin-docs-knowledge.md): agent proposes a Knowledge item from chat corrections; user edits, saves or dismisses; Knowledge migrating to Skills (research-skill-rigidity-spectrum)
- [Claude Code /insights](sources/vincentqiao-claude-code-insights.md): transcript analysis with friction categories and proposed CLAUDE.md lines; third-party description only (research-skill-rigidity-spectrum)
- [TICKing All the Boxes](sources/arxiv-tick-checklist-evaluation.md): Self-TICK checklist self-refinement +7.8% absolute (research-skill-rigidity-spectrum)
- [A Survey of Self-Evolving Agents](sources/arxiv-survey-self-evolving-agents.md): what/when/how taxonomy; intra- vs inter-test-time; scalar vs textual feedback (research-skill-rigidity-spectrum)

## skill-standards: Skill standards
(Section created by research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy; please refine.)
- [AI steering experiments (Stripe)](sources/stripe-ai-steering-experiments.md): modular, progressively disclosed skills beat a monolithic skill by ~10% on Stripe's eval suite and used fewer tokens (competitive-teardown-stripe-knowledge-agents)

## skill-supply-chain-security: Skill supply chain security
Third-party skills and plugins carry malware, prompt-injection and credential risks; whether a private marketplace with review is needed.
- [Plugin security and trust](sources/anthropic-claude-code-plugin-security.md): plugin hooks/monitors/MCP run outside the sandbox with user privileges (first-party). (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [ToxicSkills (Snyk)](sources/snyk-toxicskills-study.md): 3,984 skills: 36.82% any issue, 13.4% critical, 76 malicious (vendor claim). (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [MalSkills](sources/arxiv-malskills.md): 400 confirmed malicious of 150,108 skills across 7 registries (independent). (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [ClawHavoc](sources/thehackernews-clawhavoc-341-malicious-skills.md): 341 of 2,857 ClawHub skills malicious (independent reporting). (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [CSA: agent context poisoning](sources/csa-skill-md-context-poisoning.md): scanners miss natural-language payloads; hidden Unicode tags (independent). (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Agent skills at enterprise scale](sources/paypal-agent-skills-at-enterprise-scale.md): fail-closed validation + human review. (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [Vercel skills](sources/vercel-skills-sh-open-skills-ecosystem.md): public directory scanned by Snyk. (research-agent-runtime-patterns-taxonomy)
- [How We Red-Teamed Our Own AI Agent](sources/block-eng-red-teamed-own-ai-agent.md): a poisoned shareable recipe was the winning vector; recipe instructions are now shown on load (research-block-product-practices)
- [Customize Claude Code with mods in TypeScript](sources/claude-code-mods.md): mods "aren't sandboxed" and run with Claude Code's access; install only from trusted sources (opening). (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [Stripe deploys Claude Code to 1,370 engineers with zero-configuration enterprise rollout](sources/claude-customers-stripe-claude-code-rollout.md): random JavaScript packages on corporate laptops were unacceptable; the signed binary bypassed the npm dependency chain ("Claude Code enables zero-friction adoption"). (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [Claude Marketplace: plugins and connectors, products and agents, and service partners](sources/claude-marketplace.md): no listing review, signing, permissions or admin allow-listing is described; the absence is the finding. (research-claude-resources-articles)
- [Practical Agent Skills for Product Teams](sources/departmentofproduct-practical-agent-skills.md): a popular PM newsletter offers one download bundling skills from 10 repos, one of them a collection of 1,000+ skills, with no warning about review, pinning or scanning (research-department-of-product-knowledge-series)
- [Community Wisdom: Vibe coding as a team sport](sources/lenny-community-wisdom-vibe-coding-team-sport.md): supply-chain attacks are "a huge risk right now when everyone is building software on their desktop"; vet dependencies, store credentials to limit exposure (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [Guillermo Rauch: v0 Git workflow](sources/howiai-guillermo-rauch-v0-git-workflow.md): star ratings added so users can tell vetted skills; skills as prompt-injection vector (9:08, 10:26) (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)
- [OpenClaw: The complete guide](sources/lenny-newsletter-claire-vo-openclaw-guide.md): install skills only from the official bundle or known developers; read SKILL.md first (research-lennys-newsletter-archive)

## spec-becomes-prototype-and-evals: The spec is replaced by prototype plus evals
Some teams swap the PRD for a problem statement, a working prototype and evals.
- [AI didn't write our SDK. It changed how we built it.](sources/stripe-ai-didnt-write-our-sdk.md): a two-day prototype moved a scope decision weeks earlier; agents draft specs reviewed as GitHub issues before implementation (~20 lint rules) (competitive-teardown-stripe-knowledge-agents)
- [Protodash (How I AI, Owen Williams)](sources/howiai-stripe-protodash-owen-williams.md): engineers worked from a designer's prototype PR: 'just use the prototype as the source of truth' (competitive-teardown-stripe-knowledge-agents)

- [Beyond the CLI: Agentic AI for async workloads and non-developers](sources/dx-airbnb-beyond-the-cli-airchat.md): "no more long requirement docs": short concept brief, then 5-10 high-fidelity prototypes, smaller pods (research-airbnb-spotify-product-practices)

- [Cameron Worboys: Inside an AI-native design org](sources/dive-club-cam-worboys-ai-native-design-org.md): prototypes set direction faster than documents; Friday demos; design crits deleted (research-block-product-practices)

## stale-records-mislead-agents: Stale process records become wrong instructions
Once agents read decision records as instructions, an outdated record misleads them; record sets need freshness controls.
- [Agent READMEs: An Empirical Study of Context Files for Agentic Coding](sources/arxiv-chatlatanagulchai-agent-readmes.md): files evolve through small incremental additions rather than deletions (median addition 57 words for Claude Code files, per search summary), so accumulated instructions are rarely pruned. (independent; research-dependency-agent)
- [Learning from Change: Predictive Models for Incident Prevention in a Regulated IT Environment](sources/arxiv-kapel-ing-change-incident-prediction.md): labels depend on manual linking of incidents to changes; the IT Product field is only about 50% populated and release data covers 23.1% of changes; the most influential features are free-text change descriptions, CI name, assignment group and support offering (SHAP). (first-party; research-dependency-agent)
- [Automated Detection of Typed Links in Issue Trackers](sources/arxiv-luders-automated-detection-typed-links.md): Relate links are often confused with other types, suggesting people use them when the relationship is unclear; repositories differ significantly by how and by whom they are used (abstract), so training data from one tracker transfers badly. (independent; research-dependency-agent)
- [Beyond Duplicates: Towards Understanding and Predicting Link Types in Issue Tracking Systems](sources/arxiv-luders-beyond-duplicates-link-types.md): custom link types proliferate per repository; Composition links form trees 97.7% of the time while General Relation links show higher transitivity (abstract), i.e. link semantics vary by type and by team. (independent; research-dependency-agent)
- [Automated Code Review Assignments: An Alternative Perspective of Code Ownership on GitHub](sources/arxiv-lulla-codeowners-review-assignments.md): the paper does not measure decay; practitioner and patent sources assert ownership files go stale without measuring it (search results), a gap. (independent; research-dependency-agent)
- [System Model (Backstage Software Catalog)](sources/backstage-system-model.md): all of these relations are declared by hand in descriptor files; nothing on the page reconciles them with runtime reality (this filer's observation; see thereliabilityengineering-service-catalog-already-wrong). (first-party; research-dependency-agent)
- [DORA Dry Run exercise: summary report (ESA 2024 35)](sources/esas-dora-dry-run-register-of-information.md): "Out of the 947 registers that passed the data integration checks and were analysed, 6.5% successfully passed all data quality checks, while 50% of the remaining registers failed less than five data quality checks" (Executive summary, p. 4). (first-party; research-dependency-agent)
- [Regulation (EU) 2022/2554 on digital operational resilience for the financial sector (DORA)](sources/eu-dora-regulation-ict-risk-third-party.md): Art. 8(6): "maintain relevant inventories and update them periodically", and also whenever a major change occurs (paraphrase). (first-party; research-dependency-agent)
- [Supervisory Guidance on Model Risk Management (SR 11-7, attachment)](sources/federalreserve-sr-11-7-model-risk-guidance.md): SR 11-7 (issued jointly with the OCC as Bulletin 2011-12) is why any US bank feature that touches a quantitative model, including a vendor model or an AI component, picks up a model-risk dependency: validation before first use, scaled to risk, by people independent of the developers, recorded in a firm-wide model inventory. (first-party; research-dependency-agent)
- [Two data-backed ways to resolve incidents faster](sources/firehydrant-two-ways-resolve-incidents-faster.md): the benefit assumes the service record and its owner are correct; the post does not test accuracy. (vendor-claim; research-dependency-agent)
- [About code owners](sources/github-docs-about-code-owners.md): lines with invalid syntax are skipped; users or teams that don't exist or lack write access "are not assigned as owners"; files over 3 MB are not loaded at all (Errors, Limits). (first-party; research-dependency-agent)
- [Agent Identity overview (Google Cloud IAM)](sources/google-cloud-iam-agent-identity-overview.md): "Deleting an agent doesn't remove the IAM bindings that reference its principal"; a redeployed agent gets a new principal needing new grants (Lifecycle). (first-party; research-dependency-agent)
- [Splitting the Organization and Integrating the Code: Conway's Law Revisited](sources/herbsleb-grinter-conways-law-revisited.md): the integration plan assumed components would be ready on schedule; they were not (section 4.1.1). (independent; research-dependency-agent)
- [NAB uses CAST to keep its cloud apps in check](sources/itnews-nab-cast-cloud-controls.md): about 5,000 changes across 120 applications in one month (April 2019), many minor tweaks that had previously gone unrecorded; "100 percent" of activity now logged in ServiceNow; CMDB updated nightly with service maps. (first-party; research-dependency-agent)
- [Coordination in Large-Scale Software Development: Helpful and Unhelpful Behaviors](sources/microsoft-research-coordination-large-scale-development.md): "Work items I depend on are changed without my knowledge": 67% occasionally or more; "My team has problems deciding which team has responsibility for a work item": 47% agree (Table 2). (independent; research-dependency-agent)
- [The challenges in implementing digital change](sources/nao-challenges-implementing-digital-change.md): "Departments typically do not have a good understanding of their IT estate and its interdependencies, and legacy systems are often poorly understood because of their age. This can add to the time, risk and cost" (para 2.18). (independent; research-dependency-agent)
- [Service Detection](sources/opslevel-docs-service-detection.md): detection runs continuously from Git, Datadog, PagerDuty, New Relic, OpsGenie, deploy and custom events; close alias matches are proposed as Merge rather than duplicate Register. (first-party; research-dependency-agent)
- [OpsLevel releases recommended service owners to optimize service management efficiency](sources/opslevel-recommended-service-owners.md): before the feature, teams asked in Slack or checked org charts that could be out of date, producing "orphaned services". (first-party; research-dependency-agent)
- [New Vulnerability in GitHub Copilot and Cursor: How Hackers Can Weaponize Code Agents](sources/pillar-security-rules-file-backdoor.md): poisoned rules persist across sessions and survive forks because rule files are copied between projects. (independent; research-dependency-agent)
- [50% of engineers lack trust in the data they rely on most](sources/port-state-of-idp-2025-metadata-trust.md): "53% of organizations do not update their metadata repositories more than once per week"; only 6% of engineers update asset metadata manually daily. (vendor-claim; research-dependency-agent)
- [2025 State of Internal Developer Portals](sources/port-state-of-internal-developer-portals-2025.md): 50% of teams lack trust in the data quality of their central system of record; 3% find their metadata repository completely trustworthy; 53% update software-asset metadata no more than once a week. (vendor-claim; research-dependency-agent)
- [llms.txt adoption rises 8.8x but 97% of files get zero AI requests](sources/ppcland-llms-txt-adoption-zero-requests.md): a published-but-unread file is unmaintained by design; nobody notices when it drifts (inference from the zero-request finding). (independent; research-dependency-agent)
- [SS1/23 – Model risk management principles for banks](sources/pra-ss1-23-model-risk-management-principles.md): / legible-org-for-agents: inventory must hold findings from validation including "the dates when those indicators were last updated", outstanding remediation, "the names of individuals responsible for validation, the dates when validation was last performed, and the frequency of future validation" (Principle 1.2(c)(iii)-(iv), p. 12). (first-party; research-dependency-agent)
- [SAP LeanIX Application Portfolio Management](sources/sap-leanix-application-portfolio-management.md): "Maintain data accuracy with guided best-practice templates and quality seals that keep your inventory current" (product page). (vendor-claim; research-dependency-agent)
- [CMDB Health KPIs and metrics](sources/servicenow-cmdb-health-kpis-metrics.md): Staleness counts configuration items (CIs) not updated within a rule's Effective Duration; the base system rule "sets the Effective Duration time to 60 days" (§Correctness). Stale relationships are those where "the parent CI or the child CI is a stale CI" (§Relationships). (vendor-claim; research-dependency-agent)
- [Your service catalog is already wrong](sources/thereliabilityengineering-service-catalog-already-wrong.md): "Every service catalog is declared by hand and drifts from reality within weeks"; "In practice the gap opens within about two weeks, and it compounds" (author's experience, no data). (anecdote; research-dependency-agent)
- [Coding agents love decision records](sources/duncandavidson-coding-agents-love-decision-records.md): agent kept an obsolete abstraction an ADR marked mandatory; agents bloated ADRs when asked to update them (research-skill-rigidity-spectrum)
- [Stale docs are prompt injection you wrote yourself](sources/codeminer42-stale-docs-prompt-injection.md): CI structure and drift checks, AI code-vs-record review and human attestation; 24 code comments pointed to the wrong record before controls (research-skill-rigidity-spectrum)

## standard-form-spectrum: The form a standard takes
How a quality bar is written down: completeness checklist, rubric of criteria needing judgment, exemplars and references, explained principles, or left as unencoded taste; and how the form changes what a model or human judge can do with it.
- [A systematic review of validity evidence for checklists versus global rating scales in simulation-based assessment](sources/medu-ilgen-checklists-vs-global-rating-scales.md): 45 studies; inter-rater reliability equal (0.81 checklist vs 0.78 rating scale) but rating scales more internally consistent (0.92 vs 0.66) and reusable across tasks; use both (research-skill-rigidity-spectrum)
- [TICKing All the Boxes](sources/arxiv-tick-checklist-evaluation.md): generated yes/no checklists raised judge-human agreement 46.4% to 52.2% and human inter-rater agreement 0.194 to 0.256 (research-skill-rigidity-spectrum)
- [Rubrics as Rewards](sources/arxiv-rubrics-as-rewards.md): four rubric rules (expert-grounded, comprehensive with pitfalls, importance-weighted, self-contained); holistic reading of checkable items beat fixed weighted sums; reference-grounded rubrics beat reference-free (35.9% vs 32.0%) (research-skill-rigidity-spectrum)
- [HealthBench](sources/arxiv-openai-healthbench.md): 262 physicians wrote 48,562 weighted (-10..+10) criteria for 5,000 conversations; model grader F1 0.709, matching physician-physician agreement; Consensus subset keeps only majority-agreed criteria (research-skill-rigidity-spectrum)
- [PaperBench](sources/arxiv-openai-paperbench.md): weighted rubric trees with pass/fail leaves for partial credit; "multiple weeks per paper" to write with the author; judge F1 0.83 at ~$66 per paper (research-skill-rigidity-spectrum)
- [Judging LLM-as-a-Judge](sources/arxiv-zheng-judging-llm-as-a-judge.md): a reference exemplar cut judge math-grading failures 70% to 15% vs 30% for chain-of-thought (research-skill-rigidity-spectrum)
- [Prometheus](sources/arxiv-prometheus-fine-grained-evaluation.md): evaluator performs best given both a score rubric and a reference answer; 0.897 Pearson with humans on 45 custom rubrics (research-skill-rigidity-spectrum)
- [G-Eval](sources/arxiv-g-eval.md): one-line criterion expanded by the model into evaluation steps; 0.514 Spearman on summarisation (research-skill-rigidity-spectrum)
- [Check-Eval](sources/arxiv-check-eval.md): second checklist-generation evaluator reporting higher human correlation than G-Eval (research-skill-rigidity-spectrum)
- [Prompting best practices (Use examples effectively)](sources/claude-platform-prompting-best-practices-examples.md): examples are "one of the most reliable ways to steer ... format, tone, and structure"; 3-5, relevant, diverse, tagged (research-skill-rigidity-spectrum)
- [Define success criteria and build evaluations](sources/claude-platform-define-success-and-evaluations.md): rubric lines as checkable statements with a consequence; several rubrics per criterion; grading ladder code, LLM, human (research-skill-rigidity-spectrum)
- [Graders (OpenAI API docs)](sources/openai-graders-guide.md): rubric in the grader prompt with step-by-step instructions and many examples, numeric range and pass threshold (research-skill-rigidity-spectrum)
- [frontend-design SKILL.md](sources/anthropics-skills-frontend-design.md): taste encoded as persona, a few hard rules, named anti-patterns and a forced-choice process; no rubric, no exemplars (research-skill-rigidity-spectrum)
- [Claude's new constitution](sources/anthropic-claude-new-constitution.md): explained principles over rules because rules "can be applied poorly in unanticipated situations"; few hard constraints; priority order (research-skill-rigidity-spectrum)
- [3 Principles for Designing Agent Skills](sources/block-eng-3-principles-agent-skills.md): "write a constitution, not a suggestion" as an explicit-constraint list beside scripted binary checks (research-skill-rigidity-spectrum)
- [Taste for Makers](sources/paulgraham-taste-for-makers.md): fourteen criteria of good design that need judgment to apply and are acquired by practice (research-skill-rigidity-spectrum)
- [Human Factors of Flight-Deck Checklists](sources/nasa-degani-wiener-flight-deck-checklists.md): the checklist as a designed artifact shaped by regulator, manufacturer, airline culture and production pressure (research-skill-rigidity-spectrum)

(research-claude-resources-articles)
- [How to build the ultimate Product Dashboard that generates stakeholder updates on demand](sources/departmentofproduct-product-dashboard-stakeholder-updates.md): pick data points, a format (Slack, email, voice-cloned audio) and an audience (C-suite, users, team), get a draft (research-department-of-product-knowledge-series)
